Sports.title: Ballon d'Or judge who put Lionel Messi 3 places above Lamine Yamal explains controversial list
Sports.content:
Ballon d'Or judge who put Lionel Messi 3 places above Lamine Yamal explains controversial list

The Ballon d'Or ceremony took place on Monday night with Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe all in the top three

View 3 Images Lionel Messi placed above Lamine Yamal in the judge's list (Image: John Todd/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

A Ballon d'Or judge heralded Lionel Messi's "abnormal" World Cup performance as the justification for placing him third in his rankings, three places above Barcelona successor Lamine Yamal. Australian journalist Daniel Garb, who has been his country's judge for the trophy since 2018, was pleased that Harry Kane won the title but believed Messi should've placed higher.

‌



‌



Garb said that this year's voting process was "the most difficult it has ever been" because it was a World Cup year. He told Football360: "In my experience, a World Cup or a Euros usually separates one or two players from the rest. This time the World Cup made it more complicated."

‌



The journalist's top two performers at the tournament were Messi and Rodri, but their club seasons prevented them from collecting another Ballon d'Or. Garb placed Kane and Kylian Mbappe in his top two, and while the latter had a slightly better World Cup, he put Kane first due to his impressive campaign with Bayern.

‌



He sadded: "Goals aren't the only thing we base it on, and they’re not the only thing Kane does. He drops deep, he helps build the play and he creates for others. He's much more than a finisher, and he did it for England as well as Bayern over the course of the calendar season.

"The World Cup is what made me doubt it. Kane didn’t have his greatest tournament, scoring six goals as England finished third. Mbappe won the Golden Boot with 10 goals in eight games. In the end, a gap of 15 goals was just too much. If Kane had scored five to 10 fewer, Mbappé probably wins it."

Garb was also impressed by Messi for his domestic season as well as his World Cup campaign, adding: "That’s why Messi was third on my ballot. His World Cup was abnormal again. He finished second in the Golden Boot race with eight goals and second to Rodri for the Golden Ball, carrying Argentina to a final they lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. And yes, it’s MLS, but he still did it domestically."

‌



Despite Yamal winning the World Cup at just 19 and cleaning up for Barcelona, he dropped all the way to sixth on Garb's list. "Lamine Yamal finished third overall, and he made history with a third straight Kopa Trophy, but I had him sixth. Yamal didn’t do anything wrong. I just felt the players above him had either greater output or greater World Cups, and as brilliant as he is, that elevated them," explained Garb.

View 3 Images Lamine Yamal finished third overall, but won the Kopa trophy (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He placed Yamal's new Barca team-mate, Rodri, above him in fourth due to him winning the Golden Ball at the major tournament, with Garb claiming he "didn’t play enough club football to be my winner."

‌



Kane's Bayern team-mate Michael Olise was placed fifth due to his assists record, with this statistic the one that "stood out above everything else" to the Australian juror. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Erling Haaland, Pau Cubarsi and Jude Bellingham rounded out the top 10 for Garb as he hailed the Georgia international the most out of this quartet.

He added: "The name I keep coming back to is Kvaratskhelia, and you’d love to see Georgia get into a big tournament while they’ve got him in the team."

‌

Sports.title: Eddie Howe gave clear response when asked about Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe gave clear response when asked about Man Utd job

Eddie Howe left no room for doubt when he was asked about potentially taking over as the manager of Manchester United

View 3 Images Eddie Howe is the reported frontrunner to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Eddie Howe was not tempted by the Manchester United job when asked about it in January. But the manager has since left Newcastle United and is the frontrunner to take over should Michael Carrick be sacked as expected.

‌



‌



United's defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday seemed like the final nail in Carrick's coffin. This season, the Englishman's squad have tasted Premier League victory just once - a 5-2 drubbing of newly-promoted Ipswich Town - and faced the Cherries on the back of a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

‌



The manager's seat was already too hot to handle pre-match, but after falling 3-0, he exited the Old Trafford turf to applause from fans, who seemed to have accepted that this was his final game in charge. No decision has been made yet on Carrick's future, with crisis talks taking place on Monday. However, it is anticipated that he will depart one way or another.

‌



If and when he does leave, the hunt for a successor will be on. And as things stand, it is former Magpies boss Howe who is leading the way, according to reports. Howe is currently unattached after leaving St James' Park in July. Yet he made his stance crystal clear when asked about taking over at United earlier this year - albeit his circumstances have changed significantly.

Why Bruno Fernandes was at Carrington as Michael Carrick crisis talks took place READ MORE :

At Newcastle, Howe orchestrated two Champions League qualifications and ended their 70-year domestic trophy drought, lifting the 2024/25 Carabao Cup.

View 3 Images The English boss was revered during his time with the Magpies (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

His CV was already a glittering one from his two spells at Bournemouth, where he guided them to Premier League stability and oversaw three promotions in five seasons from League Two to the top flight.

‌



When Ruben Amorim was sacked by United in January, Howe, comfortably at the helm of Newcastle, was asked whether he could be tempted to leave the club for the vacant role at Old Trafford, as well as Chelsea's post after the exit of Enzo Maresca.

A reporter posed the question: "In the last week, you have been linked with the Chelsea job and the Manchester United job. Is there anything that would tempt you away from Newcastle United?"

‌



He replied: "No… Not at this current time. I am very happy at the moment and hopefully that stays for a long time. Absolutely nothing has changed from my perspective. I am one hundred per cent here."

View 3 Images Howe shut down the suggestion in January (Image: Getty)

However, almost seven months later, he was zero per cent there. Howe stepped down as Newcastle boss, citing personal exhaustion. Squad turnover and behind-the-scenes tension also likely contributed to his resignation.

‌



It was Carrick who was eventually made United boss permanently, after he took over as interim in January and oversaw a third-place Premier League finish. Liam Rosenior was appointed by Chelsea and sacked after 106 days in the job, with Xabi Alonso now installed.

But the free agent Howe now finds himself linked with United once more, with Carrick on the brink. Perhaps his stance has changed now that he's out of a job?

Sports.title: 'I saw Harry Kane score his first ever goal - his rise to Ballon d'Or has been remarkable'
Sports.content:
It was January 22 2011. It's fair to say that not many eyes of the football world were on Brisbane Road as Leyton Orient welcomed Sheffield Wednesday for a League One clash.

The O's were bidding to claim a scalp of one of English football's fallen giants and move themselves up the third division table. A week earlier, they had handed a professional debut to Harry Kane, a 17-year-old youth prospect who had joined on loan from Tottenham.

Kane came on as a 73rd-minute substitute in a 1-1 draw at Rochdale, and boss Russell Slade had seen enough to throw him in from the start against the Owls.

After Ben Chorley had fired Orient ahead from the penalty spot, Kane doubled their advantage, turning home a Dean Cox free-kick to notch his first-ever professional goal. The hosts ran out 4-0 winners and the rest, as they say, is history.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

I was in the away end that day. While someone so tender in years clearly had something about them to be mixing it in professional men's football, I can't say as I left the ground thinking I had seen a player who would go on to win the Ballon d'Or.

Kane's journey is one born out of perseverance, hard work and sheer bloody-mindedness. He scored five goals in 18 appearances in that Orient loan spell. Creditable, but not sparkling.

‌



In the following couple of years he would join Millwall, Norwich and Leicester on loan while biding his time to force his way into the Tottenham first team. Across those three spells, he scored 11 goals in 47 appearances.

Compared to the form Michael Owen and Wayne Rooney showed in their formative years, it was hard to see Kane reaching the heights they did, let alone going on to become his country's record goal scorer.

And now officially recognised as the best player in the world.

View 3 Images Kane has gone on to become England's record goal scorer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Things started to click for Kane at Spurs in the 2014-15 season. After being blooded by Tim Sherwood the previous year, he flourished under Mauricio Pochettino notching 31 goals in all competitions.

An England debut came against Lithuania in March 2015, replacing Rooney in the second half and scoring 80 seconds later - a sign of things to come with the Three Lions on his chest.

As well as that maiden strike at Brisbane Road, I've also been privileged enough to see a huge number of Kane's 91 England goals in the flesh.

I was in Naples to see him go past Rooney as the Three Lions' all-time top goal scorer in March 2023. I speculated to a friend of mine, who had also been present for both goals, whether we were the only two people that could say that. There can't be many.

‌



Kane's move to Bayern Munich has taken him to another level and should serve as a shining example for English players considering moving abroad to one of Europe's juggernauts.

His 156 goals for Bayern have come in just 159 games and have propelled him into another stratosphere - one in which he can challenge for, and win, the Ballon d'Or.

View 3 Images Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday night

It is all the more remarkable given how he has adapted his game in recent years, regularly dropping into his own half to start attacks and almost invariably getting on the end of them to put the ball in the net.

‌



Kane is such an intelligent footballer, adept with both feet and would slot into any side in world football and be among their best midfielders.

That is why he will go on for years to come yet. At 33, you might think he is approaching the twilight of his career. But his dedication is such that he is in remarkable shape and shows no signs of slowing down.

Don't be surprised if there are more Ballons d'Or in his future. And hopefully a pot or two with England to boot.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe forced into China apology after sponsors cut ties over Mao Zedong meme
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe forced into China apology after sponsors cut ties over Mao Zedong meme

Kylian Mbappe has lost at least three major sponsors in China after seemingly referring to Mao Zedong as a dictator during an appearance on an online chat show

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe has seen a number of endorsement deals cancelled (Image: Soccrates Images, Getty Images)

Kylian Mbappe has apologised after three companies in China have cut ties with the Real Madrid sensation as a result of appearing to have described Mao Zedong as a dictator. Drinks manufacturer Dongpeng, dairy company Mengniu and cheesemaker Milkground announced on Tuesday they had ended deals with the Frenchman.

‌



‌



Each also explained that they reject "any words and actions that hurt national sentiment" in a scathing message. While the companies failed to give any further reasoning for their decision, it comes after footage emerged online of Mbappe seemingly being questioned on "The Bridge" - a French online chat show.

‌



In the clip, Mbappe was asked about his favourite meme of himself, and the star replies that it was "a video someone made of a guy...I think he was a Chinese dictator" before the footage showed a doctored image depicting Mbappe's face on the blue-suited figure of Mao Zedong, the country's communist leader from 1949 until 1976.

‌



Football fans online playfully refer to the star - who is said to overshadow many of his team-mates and even the sides he plays for - as a dictator, and memes portraying him as Mao or other authoritarian leaders are widely circulated across social media.

Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or 2026 as top 30 rankings confirmed with Kylian Mbappe second READ MORE :

The Associated Press was immediately unable to contact Mbappe's representatives for comment. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun responded to the controversy by stating that "words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Social media platform RedNote also entered the fray, releasing a statement confirming it had maintained a content partnership with Mbappe that ended on December 31, 2024, and that it would "remove related promotional materials."

The platform likewise expressed its opposition to "any conduct that hurts national sentiment." By Tuesday, Mbappe's RedNote account had ceased accepting new followers.

‌



The French football star had previously been the face of multiple advertising campaigns throughout China, endorsing products ranging from electrolyte drinks to milk and cheese.

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe had a number of sponsorship deals in China (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

‌



FOLLOW OUR REAL MADRID FB PAGE! Latest news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In one Dongpeng advert, Mbappé delivers a slogan in Chinese, while a commercial for Mengniu features him alongside Argentine football legend Lionel Messi.

‌



Chinese social media was already flooded with criticism aimed at the footballer. The hashtags "Dongpeng ends partnership with Mbappe" and "Several brands end partnerships with Mbappe" rocketed straight to the top of Weibo's trending charts.

Meanwhile, "Football fans boycott Mbappe" also gathered substantial momentum, with countless users expressing their anger at his comments or calling on him to keep away from China.

‌



Now, Mbappe has issued an apology for his words. He said: "During a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry."

Sports.title: Why Bruno Fernandes was at Carrington as Michael Carrick crisis talks took place
Sports.content:
Why Bruno Fernandes was at Carrington as Michael Carrick crisis talks took place

Bruno Fernandes was at Manchester United's training ground on Monday despite the players having a day off following their defeat to Bournemouth

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes arrived at Carrington on Monday as crisis talks went on (Image: Getty)

Bruno Fernandes arrived at Carrington on Monday for treatment as his Manchester United team-mates enjoyed a day off. The captain's appearance added to the intrigue as boss Michael Carrick teeters on the edge of being sacked following a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

‌



‌



United's season went from bad to worse on Sunday. Heading into a bout with the Cherries, they had only one Premier League win to their name and had just been hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League.

‌



Skipper Fernandes was far from pleased with the tactical performance against the Italian side and spoke out about his manager in a post-match interview. He was dropped to the bench for the Bournemouth game and was not substituted on, though Carrick put this down to a pure footballing decision, refusing to relate it to his outburst.

‌



Alas, a Fernandes-less United were no match for Marco Rose's side at Old Trafford and fell 3-0. Boos rang out at full-time and chants were aimed at the owners. Manager Carrick is now facing what seems like insurmountable pressure and will likely struggle to keep his job.

On Monday, crisis talks took place between the club's top brass at Carrington and conference calls were reportedly staged with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairmen Avram and Joel Glazer. But Fernandes was in the building too, as was Carrick.

View 3 Images Fernandes didn't play a minute against Bournemouth (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

According to the Daily Mail, Fernandes was at the training ground to undergo pre-planned treatment. Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte, who are all sidelined, joined him.

‌



This came less than 24 hours after he was dropped by Carrick and in the wake of the 3-0 loss, his cryptic social media activity perhaps hinted at some discontent. Fernandes' Instagram account liked a post with the caption: "Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care."

Carrick's comments, however, hinted that the benching was just tactical. He said post-match on Sunday: "He's fit and available, but we decided to pick the team that we did today. Unfortunately for everyone, we didn't manage to get the right result."

‌



The manager was also at Carrington on Monday and arrived in the afternoon to watch the Under-21s against Hull City as the crisis talks were ongoing in the background. It's unknown if he was spoken to by chief executive Omar Berrada or director of football Jason Wilcox.

‌



Carrick was also present at the training complex bright and early on Tuesday morning, as his players reported back after Monday's off day, as per usual. It is not yet clear whether Carrick will keep his job.

View 3 Images Carrick arrived at Carrington on Tuesday morning in his training gear (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

‌



Regardless, the 45-year-old was emotional after the Cherries beat his side and he said when asked if he expects to be sacked: "I totally understand the situation.

"I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I'm carrying on as normal. I love this place and I'll always do what I feel is going to be best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything, really. That's kind of it, I'm not expecting either way.

Article continues below

"I take the responsibility, of course. I've said that and I accept the responsibility, whatever's going to happen results-wise, whether we win, lose, or draw. I'm in this position because I respect the position that I'm in and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say?"

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher reveals Jason Tindall concern as Eddie Howe emerges as Man Utd favourite
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher reveals Jason Tindall concern as Eddie Howe emerges as Man Utd favourite

Eddie Howe has emerged as a frontrunner for the Manchester United job if Michael Carrick is sacked, but Jamie Carragher has raised a concern over the former Newcastle manager

View 3 Images Jason Tindall is Eddie Howe's trusted assistant (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher believes that Eddie Howe is the best man for the Manchester United job, even though he has concerns about his assistant Jason Tindall.

‌



‌



Michael Carrick remains United boss for the time being, having survived crisis talks with the club's hierarchy on Monday. But his position remains uncertain after replacements were discussed following a miserable start to the season.

‌



Former Newcastle boss Howe is one of the candidates being considered, along with ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann and ex-Chelsea and Tottenham boss Antonio Conte. Howe is available, having left Newcastle in July after nearly five years at the helm.

‌



The 48-year-old is interested in the role and would likely demand to bring in a new backroom staff if he were appointed. That group would include Tindall, who has been Howe's assistant throughout his managerial career.

Eddie Howe's first Man Utd demand clear after job offer collapsed at 11th hour READ MORE :

Howe has compared their relationship to that of a "married couple", but Tindall's animated presence on the touchline, where he has clashed with rival coaches and the fourth official, has made him a divisive figure. He is therefore a reservation for Carragher.

‌



"It’s not going to get any easier. So, I think you’d almost need a manager who knows the Premier League right now," Carragher said on The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet.

"But this is just a point, because I have waxed lyrical about Eddie Howe when he was at Newcastle United. I’d love him as the England manager. And when I said yesterday on Sky, probably Eddie Howe right now, I thought if Liverpool were looking for a manager, I wouldn’t want Eddie Howe.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Jamie Carragher has given his take on Eddie Howe (Image: The Overlap Fan Debate)

‌



"I think I’d want Eddie Howe, but I wouldn’t want Jason Tindall on the side of the pitch. I don’t know the guy, and they might work together brilliantly, and they obviously do. They’ve got a great combination.

"Eddie Howe’s a sensible, respected guy, and he loves him. He has him as part of his team, but I don’t think as a Liverpool supporter I’d want him to run up and down a touchline, and I don’t think Manchester United’s supporters would either.”

‌



United are 16th in the Premier League following their 3-0 thrashing by Bournemouth on Sunday. Carrick has won just two of his 12 matches so far this season after being made permanent boss in the summer on the back of an impressive spell as interim manager.

‌



View 3 Images Jason Tindall has become a divisive figure

Howe led Newcastle to Champions League qualification on two occasions while winning the Carabao Cup in 2024/25, the club's first domestic trophy in 70 years. He stepped down in the summer after a disappointing campaign finished with the Magpies in 12th place.

‌



Carragher added: "I’m a massive fan of Eddie Howe and should be the next England manager, and he’s the best English coach out there. Is he this big, glamour name? No.

"And would he be the guy who could get Manchester United back to winning titles or European Cups? Most people would say no. But where United are right now, you need somebody who knows the Premier League."

Sports.title: Man Utd's 7 biggest social media tantrums as Bruno Fernandes joins Sancho and Garnacho
Sports.content:
Man Utd's 7 biggest social media tantrums as Bruno Fernandes joins Sancho and Garnacho

Bruno Fernandes has taken out his Manchester United frustrations on social media, but he's far from the first player to do so

View 8 Images Bruno Fernandes appears to have taken a sly jab at Manchester United on social media (Image: Getty)

Bruno Fernandes seems to have vented his frustration on social media after being dropped for Manchester United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth. Yet the club concerningly has a rich recent history of their stars spitting dummies out online.

‌



‌



United are in a rut. Under Michael Carrick, their season has started abysmally and they have just one Premier League win to their name. They're out of the Carabao Cup after losing to Brighton and their most recent European venture saw them battered 4-1 by Como.

‌



On Sunday, they needed to show some spine against the Cherries but lost 3-0 in the latest damning result of the season. But skipper Fernandes played no part. He had spoken out against his boss in the week and was dropped to the Old Trafford bench - though Carrick insisted this was purely a sporting decision.

‌



United perhaps could have used their Portuguese talisman as they were humiliated by Marco Rose's side, but Fernandes was an unused substitute. In the wake of the loss, his social media activity - liking a specific post - is being treated as him passive-aggressively throwing his toys out of the pram.

Jamie Carragher picks who must replace Michael Carrick as next Man Utd manager READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes hints he DOESN'T CARE about Man Utd after Michael Carrick snub READ MORE :

But the 32-year-old father of two is not the first United star to use social media as a vessel for public agitation and he won't be the last. Mirror Football takes a look at seven times United players and those associated with them have thrown online tantrums in recent years.

Bruno Fernandes (2026)

To be specific, the benched captain's official Instagram account liked a reel that has the caption: "Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care." This occurred not long after Sunday's loss.

‌



View 8 Images Fernandes liked the reel (Image: Instagram)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



In the reel, a Sisyphus-esque rock monster is depicted protecting a city from a giant boulder. The citizens then turn on him, at which point he lets the boulder he was holding back destroy the city in its entirety.

Fernandes might just be a fan of the animation, or maybe the reel's backing tune, Macarena. However, it's still likely that this cryptic bit of online activity represents how he's feeling at this current stage.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo's brother (2025)

Just last year, some more social media rumblings caused a stir at United - though this time it wasn't a player directly creating them. Under Ruben Amorim, the promising Kobbie Mainoo had had his minutes cut down dramatically.

Amorim made it clear he wasn't part of his plans, despite having shown potential in United's midfield and for England at Euro 2024. Fans disagreed, but the Portuguese coach stood firm. Mainoo requested a loan move away last summer, but this never materialised. He must have been frustrated, though it was not he who took action. It was his half-brother, Jordan Mainoo-Hames.

‌



View 8 Images Mainoo's half-brother Jordan uploaded the pictures online (Image: Instagram/@jxrdan)

During a match against none other than Bournemouth in December 2025, Mainoo's brother was snapped in the Old Trafford stands wearing a plain black t-shirt with "FREE KOBBIE MAINOO" on it in large, white writing. He immediately uploaded these pictures to his Instagram account and both he and Mainoo came under scrutiny.

‌



Amorim responded quite diplomatically, saying: "It was not Kobbie that wore the t-shirt. He is not going to start because of the t-shirt or go to the bench because of it. He is going to play if he is the right player to play." Eventually, Amorim was given the boot and Mainoo returned to first-team contention.

Alejandro Garnacho (2024)

Like Fernandes, ex-United star Alejandro Garnacho found himself in hot water after liking specific posts with his official account. In April 2024, the Argentine was hauled off at half-time during a match away at… Bournemouth. Who knew the Cherries could cause such head loss?

‌



View 8 Images Ten Hag clashed with Garnacho (Image: Getty)

The game ended 2-2 and Garnacho was visibly annoyed with manager Erik ten Hag for taking him off. So much so that on X, his account liked two posts by fan content creator Mark Goldbridge.

‌



One post read: "Ten Hag subtly blaming Garnacho in the post-match press conference... Not a good look throwing a 19-year-old under the bus who has actually delivered for you this season." The other branded the substitution as "a joke."

Garnacho later unliked these posts and Ten Hag confirmed that he had apologised. He was eventually frozen out under Amorim before being sold to Chelsea in August 2025 for £40million. He is currently on loan at Aston Villa.

‌



Jadon Sancho (2023)

Perhaps the most infamous and damaging outburst on this list came from Jadon Sancho. In September 2023, the winger, who had cost United £73m just two years earlier, was completely excluded from Ten Hag's squad that travelled to Arsenal for a 3-1 defeat.

The player was not injured and Ten Hag stated that he was not selected because of his performance in training. This angered the Englishman, who took to X and damningly stated: "Please don't believe everything you read!

‌



View 8 Images Sancho claimed he was being used as a scapegoat (Image: Getty)

"I will not allow people saying things that was entirely untrue. I have conducted myself in training very well this week... I have been a scapegoat for a long time which isn't fair!"

‌



Sancho pinned this post to the top of his profile for a week before deleting it. He refused Ten Hag's demand to make an internal and public apology, was banned from using the club's facilities and shipped out on loan to Borussia Dortmund four months later.

The two did draw a line under the feud when he returned, but the truce was short-lived: Sancho was loaned out to Chelsea then Villa before his United contract expired this summer. He is still without a club at 26.

‌



Jesse Lingard and his brother (2022)

Both Jesse Lingard and his brother Louie Scott had a pop in 2022. That January, the attacker had sought a move to Newcastle after falling out of favour with interim boss Ralf Rangnick. However, the move was blocked and in a press conference, Rangnick said Lingard was absent from an FA Cup tie against Middlesbrough because he'd asked for days off to "clear his mind."

View 8 Images Lingard's brother did not think he was given a proper farewell (Image: Getty)

‌



The player immediately contradicted this by posting on Twitter (now X): "The club advised me to have time off due to personal reasons! But my headspace is clear and I'll always be professional when called upon and give 100 per cent."

An acrimonious departure soon followed the February 2022 public spat, as Lingard's contract expired. United beat Brentford 3-0 in the final home game of the season and whilst Juan Mata, Nemanja Matic and Edinson Cavani all made farewell appearances, Lingard did not.

‌



He was an unused substitute and left months later for Nottingham Forest. Lingard's brother did not take kindly to this and posted on his Instagram story: "20 years of blood sweat and tears, four domestic trophies, three cup final goals, not even a farewell. No wonder it's Conference League next year."

Anthony Martial (2022)

Rangnick seemingly attracted online controversy in 2022 and Lingard and his brother were not the only ones who felt aggrieved - so did Anthony Martial. In January, Rangnick named his team to face Aston Villa and Martial was nowhere to be seen.

‌



View 8 Images Martial vented online (Image: Getty)

Asked why, the manager stated: "He didn't want to be in the squad. He would have been in the squad normally, but he didn't want to and that was the reason why he didn't travel with us yesterday."

‌



Martial, like Lingard, then directly batted this back online, stating on his Instagram story: "I will never refuse to play a match for Man United. I've been here for seven years and I never disrespected and will never disrespect the club and the fans."

Rangnick quickly chalked this interaction down to miscommunication and he wasn't kept on after a short spell as interim boss. Martial left the club in 2024 and is currently a free agent after spells at AEK Athens and Monterrey.

‌



Sergio Romero's wife (2020)

Two years before Rangnick's discord, the wife of goalkeeper Sergio Romero made her feelings crystal clear on social media. The Argentine shot-stopper was third-choice at United in the summer of 2020 and sought an exit.

View 8 Images Romero's partner was not best pleased (Image: John Peters)

Article continues below

Everton reportedly launched a deadline-day loan bid, but United refused the deal. Romero's wife, Eliana Guercio, was furious and she tore into the club on Instagram. The goalkeeper was effectively frozen out for the entire season until his contract expired in the summer of 2021. He then headed to Italian side Venezia.

His wife posted: "Sergio Romero worked hard for his club. Last trophy they won, they lifted it with him. He helped the team reach four finals/semi-finals and then he was left on the bench only to lose them all. It is time for them to return the opportunity and let him go. RESPECT FOR ONCE!"

Sports.title: Carrick to remain in charge of Man Utd for Chelsea trip
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their game against Chelsea on Saturday.

The under-pressure United head coach was thought to be on the brink after Sunday's crushing 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth but he and the players are being given the chance to turn the current situation around.

United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, were at Carrington discussing Carrick's future on Monday. It is understood they had already been considering alternatives for the head coach role.

However, Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision has been taken to give him at least one more match. Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are among the contenders to replace him if he is sacked.

Following the trip to Chelsea, United face Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Analysis: It is delaying the inevitable for Carrick

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett:

"I'm staggered. We all expected this to be the end for Carrick. The mood music around the club, the reaction of the supporters at Old Trafford - they clearly thought it was the end.

"It's a real surprise. I'm not sure this does anything for his standing. This isn't a vote of confidence. It doesn't feel like Man Utd are saying, 'He's our man, we're sticking with him'.

"I felt for Carrick going onto the training pitch today and trying to coach and work with Bruno Fernandes, who publicly criticised his tactics. How can Carrick be among that group and for it to be successful and harmonious?

"It's an impossible situation for Carrick and feels like it's delaying the inevitable."

Sports.title: Are Chelsea back? Have Man Utd weathered early-season storm?
Sports.content:
Sky Sports columnist Laura Hunter analyses the big talking points from the sixth round of Women's Super League matches, bringing you closer to the key stories at the heart of the women's game. Plus: Vote on the topics you want covered next week.

Are Chelsea back in business?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's Super League match between Crystal Palace and Chelsea

It's been a long time since Chelsea entered a domestic campaign as underdogs. The bookies might have had them as favourites to win the WSL title before a ball was kicked but most hardened observers chose Man City as the more likely champions. The market appeared to be hedging their bets on history.

While I still believe Man City are the team to beat, Chelsea's start to the season cannot be ignored. After seven played they are top by virtue of goal difference, with a perfect record since their opening day draw with Aston Villa. City and Chelsea's results in a head-to-head count are actually identical - but of course the nip and tuck is more nuanced than that.

Chelsea's win from behind to beat Crystal Palace at the weekend, without Keira Walsh or Lauren James, was a deliberate show of strength. And an indication of Sonia Bompastor's intent to balance her squad between priorities. The Blues host Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Are they equipped to sustain such momentum? The numbers suggest they are well placed to compete with Man City. Chelsea are the league's top scorers, best chance creators and have conceded the fewest goals against. Dig a bit deeper into the data and their improved output presents the picture of a team revitalised.

It may have taken two years, but Bompastor has finally got her wish. The Frenchwoman always wanted her side to have greater technical control but was struggling to get the arrangement right, especially in midfield. At long last, Chelsea are a team with an identifiable attacking style, based on the principles of progressive, possession-orientated football.

The system relies heavily on high-advancing full-backs, who are dynamic enough to stretch the pitch in possession and make it more compact when the ball is lost. Ellie Carpenter and Katie McCabe are perfect for the role.

Carpenter is the WSL's best in class when it comes to two-way influence. She ranks as the league's highest-performing defender in terms of goals scored (3), shots taken (17), touches in the opposition box (49) and open-play crosses (40). She and McCabe have generated 17 chances for team-mates apiece.

In central areas, the introduction of Lexi Potter has encouraged a higher role for Keira Walsh and the combination has meant Chelsea are able to dictate tempo with greater success and variation. Aesthetically, Chelsea are a better watch, but crucially, with more reliable end product.

Melvine Malard was an inspired signing in the summer, boasting four WSL goals from four starts so far, matched by the consistency of James. Goals are coming from elsewhere, too, as the intensity of Chelsea's midfield press continues to generate high turnovers and therefore opportunities for lesser-known scorers. Walsh and Sjoeke Nusken have bagged four between them.

Such consistency of delivery is enough to excite even the most skeptical of spectators. And Bompastor must take credit too, making two changes at half-time against Palace to turn the result on its head.

No doubt Chelsea in a relentless rhythm spells danger for the competition. Only time will tell if such an uptick means they remain close chasers of Man City - or have in fact managed to overtake them.

Are Man Utd in better shape than first thought?

Man City won 3-0 home and away in the derby last season. It was the least competitive that fixture had been for some time. And there was plenty to suggest a similar pattern would repeat itself this term, given City's perfect start and United's patchy evolution under Eva Olid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Man United against Man City in the Women's Super League

But Olid's side have turned a corner in recent weeks. Now on a four-game unbeaten streak, the Spaniard's possession-led approach is starting to take recognisable shape.

Against Charlton last Sunday, United completed 700 passes with an accuracy of 88.7 per cent. Both club record high figures in a WSL game. This week, they went toe-to-toe with the league's pass-masters and boasted an equal share of the ball, landing more accurate passes overall and a higher amount in the opposition half. Few sides are technically capable of doing that to City.

"If you want to see the progression of this United team, this is a great example of it," said Sky Sports' Izzy Christiansen on co-comms at Leigh Sports Village. United were breaking lines with the frequency of a side who had been modelled on this tactical plan for years.

Jess Park in particular was outstanding, involved prolifically in the build-up phase. She is the glue. The ball-carrier, but also the player with the cognitive ability to play in a way that accepts responsibility for being at the heart of every attack. Importance is placed on Ella Toone too.

Such numbers represent more than baby steps. It's evidence that United's squad, fairly modest in size, can produce the systematic style Olid prefers while also getting results. To be the first to take points off City is a triumph in itself. They have jumped into fourth in the table as reward.

Of course there are many more layers to this approach and Olid is relying on key contributors to make it work consistently. But major ground has been broken over the past six weeks. The manager is clearly enthused: "How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time, the progression has been massive."

Sports.title: Brundle's verdict on 'outstanding' Antonelli and Piastri 'pain' in 2026 cars
Sports.content:
Given that Red Bull and Ferrari, and from time to time McLaren, have undoubtedly closed down the pace advantage enjoyed by Mercedes in the first half of the season, it was looking possible that Kimi Antonelli might win the World Championship perhaps not fully in the style he would have wanted.

His Austin qualifying and race performances demolished that concern in the most comprehensive way.

From seemingly nowhere, he produced a stormer of an initial time in the third and final top-10 shootout to secure pole position and deny Max Verstappen's Red Bull and the two Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, all of whom had seemed likely to beat him. It was his seventh pole of the season but his first since Spa back in the summer eight races ago, and therefore very timely.

Antonelli was 'simply outstanding'

Kimi produced a perfect start and opening lap to comfortably lead, while the slow-starting Verstappen had to fend off the Ferraris. His pace, consistency, and tyre management thereafter was simply outstanding.

Both Red Bull drivers, Verstappen and Isack Hadjar, had impressively made it through to Q3 having used only one set of soft tyres up to that point. This would give Max on the front row two brand new sets of soft tyres for the race, surely a significant advantage? As it turns out, not so, as they didn't last particularly well, forcing Max to pit first of everyone on Lap 13 of 56, and clearly now on a two-stop strategy.

Mercedes didn't panic or respond, they trusted their data and instincts, and their championship-leading driver, to babysit his tyres at sufficient pace to make only one pit stop on Lap 24.

With fresh tyres Max was inevitably very fast, and it initially appeared that he would be able to make up the extra 20 seconds he must spend in the pitlane for his second stop on Lap 31. But he couldn't clear the traffic with much ease. With his radio failing for the second time, but not before he would castigate his team for not moving his team-mate on a different run plan out of the way much sooner, he ended up a fairly disgruntled third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

I did the post-race interviews and Max did though beam a nice smile when I complimented him on his overtake of Lando Norris up into Turn 1. It was pure Verstappen, just as he looked highly likely to lose a position to Leclerc, he converted that into an overtake of the McLaren with a stunning and controlled slice while extremely late on the brakes.

It didn't do him much good in the end though because after Leclerc's own first stop on Lap 15, and having already been awesome on the opening lap of the race, he was mighty fast all the way to the chequered flag for a very well-earned second place.

Ferrari had led all three practice sessions and so their qualifying had been a relative disappointment, but Hamilton too was rapid in the closing stages and would finish fourth just a second behind Verstappen. Another lap and he'd have joined his team-mate Leclerc on the podium.

Norris did a fine job in fifth, having pitted on Lap 16 but then changing to a one-stopper, stretching his hard compound tyres a full 40 laps. In the end, he ran out of grip and slipped from second place, but it was good while it lasted.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Piastri struggling with 2026 cars and Russell's 'harsh' penalty

Oscar Piastri in the sister McLaren had another disappointing race, lacking front-running pace from relatively early on and finishing 52 seconds behind the winner. Oscar simply can't seem to gel with the 2026 cars and it's painful to witness after his stellar run last year.

Piastri's struggles would heavily impact another driver having a season to forget in the shape of George Russell. On the opening lap Russell was both attacking Hadjar's slow-starting Red Bull and defending from Piastri. He ran wide at the Turn 12 hairpin at the end of the back straight and rejoined, marginally ahead of Piastri. The Stewards looked at all the camera angles and data and decided that Russell had gained a lasting advantage off the track by not losing a place to Piastri, but given it was the opening lap and the proximity of other cars, they served him half the normal 10-second penalty in mitigation. I thought that was harsh, George felt somewhat more strongly about it.

Taking his five-second penalty at the first pit stop put him behind Piastri, and despite very solid initial pace on fresh tyres he simply couldn't find a way past the young Aussie and finished a full 54 seconds behind his winning team-mate in eighth place. Ouch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Another 11th for Audi!

Liam Lawson drove very well again for two points at Racing Bulls in ninth and Pierre Gasly grabbed the final point for Alpine in 10th, the position he started.

Nico Hulkenberg finished 11th and just out of the points - that's Audi's 10th race this year when just missing out. That's a torment which revives bad memories for me, back when points only went down to sixth place, I had a spate of dragging some reluctant machine past all the accidents and unreliability to finish a point-less seventh.

Antonelli's supreme victory ensures he will be the youngest ever F1 world champion by over three years, usurping Sebastian Vettel. And the first Italian F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, despite such motorsport passion and history in that country.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli looks ahead to Mexico as he moves to brink of a title win

Verstappen is now out of championship contention, incredibly for the first time since 2020. Russell and Hamilton would have to win every race until the end of the year, with Antonelli not showing up, for them to be champion. It's a case of when, and not if.

Austin put on at great show at COTA, a combined 460,000 fans had all the usual great views along with live music, fun fairs, and many other attractions, and a spectacular hospitality suite and infinity pool at the very top of the already high first corner. The lucky few were transported over the track in gondolas on ski-slope-style pylons and cables, I'm impressed by how F1 keeps developing as a full experience, even though the race didn't turn out to be a classic.

Next up, Mexico.

MB

Sports.title: Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test late due to neck injury
Sports.content:
Steve Smith has been ruled out of Australia's third Test decider against South Africa in Cape Town after it was confirmed late on Tuesday morning that the batter had not fully recovered from a neck injury.

Australia gave the 37-year-old a chance to prove his fitness ahead of the Test match, which would have seen Smith return to Cape Town for the first time since the infamous 'Sandpapergate' scandal at Newlands in 2018.

Smith appeared to injure himself during his first spell at the crease during Australia's second Test defeat to South Africa in Gqeberha, in which the hosts levelled the series 1-1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Smith appeared to suffer the injury during Australia's second Test defeat against South Africa

The former skipper subsequently dropped down the batting order in the second innings, as Pat Cummins' side went on to suffer an innings and 31-run defeat.

Ahead of the third Test, Smith had complained of neck stiffness during Australia's pre-match training session and was due to undergo a fitness test ahead of Tuesday's match.

He was later seen walking around Newlands with a large plaster stuck to his neck.

Cummins said that their star batter had been working to overcome the injury early on Tuesday morning, but confirmed at the toss that Smith would be one of four changes to the Australia XI.

"He had a little try this morning," Cummins told SuperSport. "But he wasn't happy with how his neck was feeling, so we had to look elsewhere."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Africa drew level in the series after their innings and 31-run win in Gqeberha

Smith, who received 12-month suspension for his role as Australia's captain in the ball-tampering scandal, has had a lean tour of South Africa.

His top score of 28 came during Australia's first innings in Gqeberha, with Smith having made 25 and 27 during the opening Test in Durban.

Cameron Green returns to the side and slots in at No 4 in place of Smith. Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Nathan Lyon also come into the starting XI.

Beau Webster, Scott Boland and Nic Maddinson miss out, while Matt Renshaw opens for Australia in Maddinson's place.

Australia won the toss and elected to field first, with Cummins stating he was hopeful his batters can bounce back after South Africa's bowlers kept them to a first-innings score of 99 in the second Test.

"We've got some guys really well placed," Cummins said. "They've been here working hard the last couple of weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pat Cummins confirmed that Scott Boland would miss the third Test despite taking five wickets in Gqeberha

"A couple of injuries they're coming back from and are now 100 per cent. It's exciting, it's a huge opportunity and everyone's itching to get out there."

Sports.title: Carabao Cup: Arsenal should unleash Dowman as Liverpool-Chelsea clash
Sports.content:
It's time to unleash Dowman

Fleetwood Town vs Arsenal - Tuesday, kick-off at 8pm live on Sky Sports Football

It's time for Mikel Arteta to unleash Max Dowman regularly for Arsenal.

The talented 16-year-old is hardly the new kid on the block anymore. In the last round of the Carabao Cup, Dowman dazzled against Ipswich Town with a man-of-the-match display and is expected to be the creative fulcrum of the Arsenal attack again against Fleetwood Town.

But having largely been held back by Arteta this season, here comes the teenager's first real chance since his breakthrough to become an Arsenal regular.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Carabao Cup third round clash between Ipswich and Arsenal.

The point where Arteta releases the shackles off Dowman and puts him in as one of his key stars is an important moment not just for Arsenal, but for English football as well. This is a diamond player, a rare gem that eventually needs to shine.

With all the Ballon d'Or talk this week, it is worth remembering that Lamine Yamal was unleashed by both Barcelona and Spain without hesitation. Does Dowman need that same treatment?

Bukayo Saka's injury has opened the door now for Dowman to play week in, week out for Arsenal. But not just as a rotational option, Dowman could really challenge Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze for a starting spot, given the pair are yet to show the consistency required since joining Arsenal.

Is this the period where Dowman's career accelerates?

Sam Blitz

Savage's Posh revival faces stern Bradford test

Bradford City vs Peterborough United - Tuesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+

Robbie Savage is slowly turning Peterborough United around, and now has the chance to make some history.

The former Wales and Leicester City midfielder left National League club Forest Green Rovers in early October to join the struggling League One side, and has taken five points from his first four games in charge.

He promised attacking football, and Posh have scored seven goals since.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet League One match between Bromley and Peterborough United.

To reach the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 1992, they must unlock a watertight Bradford City defence that has conceded just five times in 12 league games.

Under new boss Michael Duff, who took over from Graham Alexander just four days after Savage was appointed, Bradford haven't conceded a goal in four matches, but three have ended 0-0. They have netted just 10 times in League One this season, yet sit third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet League One match between Oxford United and Bradford City.

Bradford, finalists in 2013, are attempting to boost the attendance by offering tickets for just £5, setting the stage for a bumper crowd as they look to keep their own cup hopes alive.

David Richardson

In the battle of the Basques, how strong will Iraola and Alonso go?

Liverpool vs Chelsea - Wednesday, kick-off 8pm live on Sky Sports Main Event

It will be intriguing to see just how strong Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso go with their lineups at Anfield on Wednesday night, with both Basques facing huge Premier League games on the weekend, albeit for different reasons.

Liverpool are currently in the middle of a run of four home games in a row and will head into the Chelsea clash bouncing after three straight wins, so will the Reds head coach look to prioritise the visit of champions Arsenal to Anfield on Super Sunday, or would another victory help maintain the feelgood factor around the club right now?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carabao Cup match between Liverpool and Tottenham.

Either way, one player certain to start the tie against the club he began his career at is young Reds forward Rio Ngumoha, who shone against Villarreal in the Champions League last week, before playing the final 13 minutes of Sunday's 2-0 win against Brighton.

As for the visitors, Alonso will be looking for a reaction from his players after Saturday's "awful" 2-0 loss to Tottenham, as Gary Neville described their display at the Bridge. But, again, where will the Chelsea manager's priorities lie with hugely important league games against Man Utd, Sunderland and Leeds on the horizon?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Carabao Cup match between Chelsea and Leeds.

Alonso, who will be without the suspended Cole Palmer after his sending off against Spurs, will surely want to freshen things up at Anfield, but as Paul Merson told Sky Sports: "If they get beat by Liverpool and Man Utd this week, then Chelsea are in big trouble. You'd be seriously thinking they'd be lucky to get Champions League this season. And that can't happen. Whatever happens, that can't happen."

Rich Morgan

Man City-Brighton double-header presents big chance for Hurzeler

Man City vs Brighton - Wednesday, kick-off 7.30pm live on Sky Sports+

Manchester City and Brighton meet twice this week, once in the cup and once in the league. It's a chance for Fabian Hurzeler to prove that Brighton can consistently mix it with the best teams in the division after faltering at Liverpool at the weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the third round Carabao Cup match between Man City and Norwich City.

For all the club's progress, and the never-ending stream of compliments about Hurzeler's progressive style of play, he is missing the tangible evidence to cement Brighton as the Premier League's great disruptors. The EFL Cup presents the perfect opportunity to do that.

Brighton are unbeaten in four games against Man City (W2, D2) - their best ever run against such usually-dominant opposition. Hurzeler's brand of high-intensity football is exactly the style City tend to find most unsettling, so the visitors should arrive to the Etihad full of confidence.

They're perfectly capable of causing an upset to dispatch of the holders.

Laura Hunter

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the third round of the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton.

Europe has helped, not hindered - but can Villa and Bournemouth also balance cup run?

Bournemouth vs Aston Villa - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+

Europe is usually viewed as a hindrance to domestic form, but it has been a positive thus far for Aston Villa and Bournemouth.

Both teams started slowly this season. Villa had not scored a goal in the Premier League until the 2-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest on September 12, while their first league win came a week later at Tottenham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Manchester City.

Unai Emery's men kicked into gear with a 3-2 win against Club Brugge earlier in September and have now gone seven games unbeaten across all competitions since beating Coventry City in the last round of the Carabao Cup.

Bournemouth are a similar story. It was a slow start under Marco Rose, but their performances in the Europa League have ignited the new era.

They had to wait until October 18 for a first win in the top flight but they now come into this game against Villa full of confidence after beating AC Milan and Manchester United across a four-game winning streak.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Bournemouth in the Premier League.

After starting slowly, the two teams are beginning to flex their muscles and are showcasing why they are regarded as two of the best run clubs in the division. However, how they balance this Carabao Cup tie will be the ultimate test for their squad depth.

Can they juggle European football, the priority that is the Premier League and a cup run? We'll find out on Wednesday.

Patrick Rowe

Fulham finding form as Palace and Sage face Carabao Cup reckoning

Fulham vs Crystal Palace - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+

When Fulham and Crystal Palace first met in early September, both managers were under pressure after losing their opening two Premier League games. Ahead of Wednesday's Carabao Cup meeting, however, the balance of power has shifted dramatically.

Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham have found momentum at precisely the right time, winning back-to-back league games against Hull and Coventry.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Fulham’s match against Crystal Palace in the Premier League.

Oscar Bobb's late winner at the CBS Arena was another sign of a side growing in resilience, while consecutive clean sheets suggest they are beginning to find the defensive stability that eluded them earlier in the season.

The crisis has not disappeared, but Arbeloa has bought himself breathing room via 'Arbeloa-ball'.

Pierre Sage, meanwhile, is facing an altogether different reckoning at Palace.

Consecutive defeats to Brighton and Newcastle, conceding seven goals without reply, have exposed a team desperately short of defensive organisation and confidence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of the future Premier League stars making their mark in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Palace have shipped 19 league goals, the division's worst record, and Sage's insistence that the problems are not tactical will do little to silence the growing discontent among supporters.

Wednesday offers Fulham a chance to deepen Palace's crisis. For Sage, it risks becoming another step towards the exit.

William Bitibiri

Can the Bees make it three in a row?

Sunderland vs Brentford - Wednesday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+

Given their contrasting form this season, Brentford will be confident heading to the Stadium of Light this week. Not only that, they also have a decent pedigree in recent Carabao Cup campaigns.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Hull City’s match against Brentford in the Premier League.

They have reached the quarter-finals in three of the last five seasons, including the last two - and were knocked out by the eventual winners in 2024/25 (Newcastle) and 2025/26 (Man City). Finalists Chelsea knocked them out in their other quarter-final appearance in 2021/22.

Of course, Keith Andrews will be hoping to go one better this season - but they have Sunderland to beat first.

The Black Cats have been eliminated in six of their last eight League Cup fourth round ties - the most recent in 2021/22 - and are struggling to find the magic touch they had last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United.

But form doesn't always translate onto the pitch and knockout football is a different beast altogether. At home, Sunderland will feel they are a match for anyone - and will not want to get stung again on Wednesday.

Charlotte Marsh

Can Toffees or Magpies lay down a marker before PL rematch?

Everton vs Newcastle - Thursday, kick-off 7.45pm live on Sky Sports+

The Carabao Cup often gives teams a chance to rotate their squad in order to remain fresh for the upcoming Premier League games. That is less likely to be the case here. Instead, it could act as a preview of their league meeting on Monday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Everton.

Everton’s paper-thin squad has already been rocked by the illness of Jack Grealish and the concussion of Jarrad Branthwaite. Whether he likes it or not, David Moyes will have to go to the well with the exact same group and just pray for no more knocks.

Newcastle’s options have also been rather depleted, but they do have the advantage when it comes to strength in depth, aided greatly by the return of Anthony Elanga during the league win over Crystal Palace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Newcastle United.

The thirst for silverware on Tyneside may encourage Matthias Jaissle to put out a relatively strong team as the Magpies look to regain the title they won two years' ago under Eddie Howe.

If these two do line up strongly, then perhaps as important as progression in the cup is the opportunity to lay down a marker before they meet again on Merseyside a mere 96 hours later.

Callum Bishop
