Sports.title: Hamilton reveals the area where he's 'lost out' to Leclerc
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has revealed he's "lost out" to Charles Leclerc through the set-up of his Ferrari car in recent races.

Hamilton was outqualified by Leclerc at the United States Grand Prix and was unable to match his team-mate's impressive pace in the race on his way to fourth, while Leclerc finished second behind race-winner Kimi Antonelli.

At the previous race in Singapore, Hamilton looked strong in qualifying until Q3 when he was beaten by Leclerc, and a similar pattern occurred in Austin where the seven-time world champion topped final practice, only to qualify fifth.

"I lost a lot of points in the last five races or so," Hamilton, who is one point behind second-placed George Russell in the Drivers' Championship, told Sky Sports F1.

"I think it has come from set-up, not perfect, the set-up. That's something I really have to get on top of. That's where I have lost out. Performance-wise I feel like I've been driving well and the last [race] stint [in Austin] was good. The first two stints there was nothing I could do about that.

"Definitely lots to take away. The team did a great job to bring an upgrade. Charles got a second place. We have got good performance. Hopefully when we go to Mexico, we can improve on where we have gone wrong on that setup."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Ferrari continued to be the benchmark team in most corners at the Circuit of the Americas but lacked straight-line speed compared to Mercedes and Red Bull.

But, Hamilton was unhappy with the car's low-speed balance in the first two stints of the Grand Prix which put him out of the podium fight.

"I lost so much time. I couldn't turn the car in the low-speed particularly - Turn 1, Turn 11, Turn 12, Turn 13, 14, 15. Massive understeer so the [other] cars pulled away when I was adjusting my settings," he said.

"By the time we got to the last stint, we got closer to the balance but we should have started with that balance at the beginning. Lots of learnings. The team did a great job with pit stops and strategy."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton revealed that his Ferrari had 'massive' understeer, which cost him a fourth-place finish at the United States Grand Prix

Could Leclerc have won United States GP?

Leclerc qualified fourth but had a superb start by overtaking Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen in the first sector, only for Verstappen to overtake the Ferrari driver at the end of the first lap.

Ferrari opted for a two-stop strategy with Leclerc which saw him charge past Verstappen and Lando Norris, who did a one-stop race, in the closing stages but he ultimately finished 13 seconds behind Antonelli.

Leclerc believes his qualifying position cost him a chance at victory but even if he had less traffic to contend with in the race, Antonelli was "just too quick".

"If you look at FP1, FP2 and FP3, we were very strong. If you look at qualifying, at the end of the day in Q3, it was extremely difficult to bring the tyres up to temperature, and we probably lost a shot at the victory there," said Leclerc.

"But Kimi was very strong, so, as a whole weekend, I think we're just not robust enough."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton topped final practice in Austin from Max Verstappen

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur believes Leclerc could have won the race in different circumstances.

"The race went well - the racing went well, the pace was OK, we were aggressive with the strategy because we had to overtake," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"Overall, if we missed something it was the last two laps in Q3. That was the most important laps of the weekend and that's where we had the issue.

"Overall, I want to take the positive of the weekend that the pace was there from FP1 to the last lap of the race. Without the VSC it would have been a double podium but let's try to do a better qualifying in Mexico and win the race."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Can Ferrari win another race in 2026?

Five rounds remain in the 2026 season with the Mexico City Grand Prix up first this weekend, where altitude will be a factor given the track is 2,200m above sea level.

The performance of the Ferrari power unit at altitude will dictate if they can challenge for victory at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, which features lots of twisty corners which the SF-26 should enjoy.

"It's such fine margins, and it also depends on what the upgrade plans of the others are in upcoming races. But the feeling with the car is getting better and better," said Leclerc.

"These cars are very specific and unique, and I feel like, over the last two or three races, I've unlocked something again in terms of driving, and particularly setup with my driving. Just both together, we've taken a step forward, and I just feel much more comfortable with the car.

"I hope that this will result in a win soon. Whether it's in Singapore or in Austin, we were quite close, so I'm confident that we'll have a shot to win a race before the end of the season."

Formula 1 next heads south for the second leg of The Americas triple header with the Mexico City Grand Prix this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

Sports.title: Carrick given chance to save job as he stays for Manchester United’s game at Chelsea
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has been given the chance to save his job by turning Manchester United’s results around, with the head coach remaining in place for Saturday’s visit to Chelsea.

The decision by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, can be viewed as a surprise given United’s dire form.

Sunday’s abject 3-0 league home defeat by Bournemouth followed Wednesday’s equally dire 4-1 reverse at Como in the Champions League.

Carrick’s side have won twice in 12 games and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Brighton. United are 16th in the Premier League, a point above the relegation zone.

Yet Wilcox, who has driven the retaining of Carrick, wants to give the 45-year-old a chance to transform form and results. Whether Carrick could survive another poor performance and result at Stamford Bridge is in the balance.

United host Roma in the Champions League three days later, then Aston Villa in the league the following Saturday. Carrick’s reprieve may also be a move to allow time for Wilcox to secure a replacement should the decision be taken to sack him.

United will have to pay Newcastle about £3m in compensation if they want Eddie Howe. He is Wilcox’s prime candidate if a change is made and wants the job. When he left Newcastle in July a deal was struck on the remaining terms of his contract which means the club would be due compensation.

View image in fullscreen Eddie Howe is the preferred choice of Manchester United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

United would also have to pay Newcastle a minor sum for Howe’s staff, headed by his assistant, Jason Tindall.

Manchester United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, has been pushing the case of Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach.

Sports.title: Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph a glorious riposte to celebrity fawning of ceremony | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
Well, there’s something new. Football: now available in new, genuinely heartwarming flavour.

There was a lovely moment at London’s Palladium theatre, with the clock creeping towards 11pm at the end of a startlingly shrill and bloated evening of never-ending awards and never ending award-related excitement.

Not just for Harry Kane, who is now the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or winner, and in the process placed indelibly in that lineage of elite footballers. But also, frankly, for anyone watching, as Kane stood on stage gazing a little shyly at his golden orb, and kicked off his speech by thanking everyone, paying tribute to everyone, everywhere, then finally cracking into tears and a strangled croak as he thanked his parents for sacrifices made, his wife for always being there, and even, in slightly jarring vibe-shift from the warm honeyed tone, José Mourinho.

Even Kane’s biggest advocates will rarely claim their man is one of a kind, sui generis, in the mode of the Ronaldo-Messi godhead. But Kane is exactly this in his own admirably humble way.

Not just an exceptional footballer, the best, most deserving men’s player in the world this year, a European golden boot, scorer of 89 goals since August 2025, Bundesliga champions, World Cup semi-final captain, model of extreme professionalism and care. He’s also quite clearly the nicest man, if not just in football, then possibly the world.

Or at least it felt like that as he walked off in that very dear and tender way, the centre of the world in that moment, but also just keen to get off the stage and let everyone get on with clearing up.

It would be wrong to say Kane’s victory in the final vote of the night redeemed the grotesqueness of the ceremonies itself. There was a roomful of hugely deserving winners here. But Kane hits particularly hard.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas and Harry Kane pose with their trophies at the end of the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards ceremony in London. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

And the Ballon d’Or is, let us be clear, a horrendous event, albeit a supremely popular horrendous event. There was the usual pomp around the ceremony, staged this year at a fancy theatre close to Oxford Circus.

This isn’t sport. It’s celebrity culture, red carpet fawning, the worship of images and people, and fame. Football isn’t supposed to be cocooned this way, to send the message that there are barriers and ropes and special people. Yeah, well, good luck with that.

The night kicked off with French Montana in spotless white tuxedo performing on an open-air double-decker bus. He definitely speaks, clearly, carried well, seemed enthusiastic. If it all goes south from here, the evidence suggests French Montana could, at the very least, get a job as a London tour bus operator.

View image in fullscreen French Montana performs during Ballon d’Or award ceremony in London. Photograph: Rasid Necati Aslim/Anadolu/Getty Images

Before long Thierry Henry and Kate Scott glided on stage, half an hour late, to add a little deft and easy charm to a furious schedule of pots and prizes.

View image in fullscreen The hosts of the ceremony: Kate Scott and Thierry Henry. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

And the awards came thick and fast. The Spain manager, Luis de la Fuente, won coach of the year. “I hope in the future I will become in English better,” were his first words at the lectern, throwing his hat in the ring for a disastrous pension-padding six months at Manchester United two years from now.

There was a lovely moment as Burna Boy came on to present the Socrates award for charitable works to Bukayo Saka. He was asked if there were footballers who had inspired his love for the game. At which point he looked at Thierry Henry and said, “definitely, one of them’s standing right there”, and of course he said it in his Burna Boy voice, looking Thierry deep in the eyes so smooth and deep, just almost an impossibly sexy moment.

View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka delivers his speech after accepting the Sócrates award from Burna Boy. Photograph: Jeff Spicer/Uefa/Getty Images

The Ballon d’Or can be unintentionally hilarious at times like these. There were just so, so many video tributes, so much excitingly portentous music. This is a stage where everyone happening at every moment is very clearly the most important thing ever to happen, superseded only by the next thing to happen on that stage, and then the thing after that.

The degree of fawning is startling at first, but glazed by familiarity before long. At one point Cristiano Ronaldo appeared very briefly in a fact-cut big-screen montage and the crowd shrieked a song, clutched its hand to its fevered throat, collapsed into the aisles in sheer priapic excitement.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although by the time the original Ronaldo emerged onstage at 10.44pm, there was a sense of the genuinely vertiginous company Kane was about to join. Ronaldo read out the name inside the envelope, and the hall collapsed into cheers and yells and roars as Kane appeared onstage.

And yes the Ballon d’Or is a fundamentally silly thing on its own terms. As a concept it jars with the basic concept of team sport, promoting instead the opposite of sport, the opposite of team culture, the modern disease of fawning parasocial engagement with star names.

In many ways the world would be a better place if the Ballon d’Or was simply abolished, as an example to all who pore over reels and clips and the imagined qualities of their celebrity paramours.

But it is also fascinating, unignorable, and endlessly moreish. All the more so this time. Kane as the Ballon d’Or 2026 is a genuinely fine, uplifting, instructive moment in the spotlight.

It is always tempting to talk about the journey these players make. Everyone has a backstory. Most footballers come from adversity. Kane has this, in his own way, 16 years into a professional career, which has names like Leyton Orient, Millwall, Leicester and Norwich on the timelines. He was unexceptional as a junior, didn’t stand out as particularly skilful or big or outstanding in his numbers. He played as a holding midfielder for a bit while Spurs decided what to do with him.

Kane worked relentlessly. He was Millwall young player of the year 2012, fitting bookend to the Ballon. He made it because he simply refused to go away, to stop working, honed instead the deeper skills in his quiver, the purity of his shooting, the range of his passing long and short

And Kane is exceptional in other ways. Without ever peacocking around promoting his brand, without really trying he remains the most likable, authentic, role-model-ish modern-day England player. For a man who never talks big or acts big he has a happy knack of becoming the key player wherever he goes. Perhaps Kane has become cool now. He has always been likable, with that mild-mannered air of a kindly Victorian chimney sweep with a hamster in his waistcoat watch pocket. In the Bayern years, Kane has become leaner, more glossed and handsome, jawline, tan, iconic Vampire hairline.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane celebrates after scoring a penalty against Paris Saint-Germain in last season’s Champions League. Photograph: Christophe Ena/AP

Mainly he expresses a common confusion about what talent really is. Talent isn’t simply moments. Talent is also application, focus, craft, the ability to work, to make others better.

And yet his elite career has also been oddly grudging. Somehow the idea has always been out there that Kane is undeserving of these accolades, despite his own mildness and humility, his obvious team qualities, his relentless delivery of goals, effort, leadership. It is a genuinely odd conclusion given the opposite is so manifestly true, that this is an entirely uplifting story of overachievement, of hard work and applied intelligence, as opposed to the kind of talent that just needs to be flame-throwered in the right direction.

It is undeniably true that Kane’s levels can drop dramatically when he can’t perform at his full physical capacity. There have been moments where it has been tempting to wonder if he’s gone far enough as England’s captain in the last few years, if his body and his talent deserve a little care.

Well, that just shows how wrong you can be.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage given more time by Crystal Palace but remains under pressure
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage has been given more time to turn around Crystal Palace’s fortunes but remains under huge pressure and could be dismissed if they lose to Tottenham on Saturday.

The Frenchman’s position was in serious doubt after another poor performance in the 2-0 defeat to Newcastle at the weekend. That followed a 5-0 thrashing against Brighton when Sage was warned that he could be dismissed if results did not improve quickly.

But with Palace set to travel to Craven Cottage to face Fulham in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening before their trip to Spurs in the Premier League, the club’s chair, Steve Parish, has decided not to act given the tight turnaround in Palace’s schedule. However, Sage – who attended the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Monday evening – is understood to have been left in no doubt that the meeting with Spurs on Saturday is crucial to his future.

Palace are 17th and have conceded 19 goals in eight Premier League matchesthis season – the highest in the division. But, it is understood, Sage retains the support of his squad, with two leading players having sent him messages saying that they still have faith he can turn things around.

Palace’s hierarchy are said to be split over whether to fire the former Lens manager after only 12 games in charge, with some in favour of bringing in Thomas Frank or Sean Dyche to steady the ship. Rob Edwards, the former Wolves manager, has also been mentioned as a potential contender.

There is sympathy for Sage at boardroom level given that Axel Disasi – who was signed on loan from Chelsea to replace key defender Maxence Lacroix – has only just returned from a three-match suspension. There were also signs of improvement in the 2-2 Europa League draw at Besiktas in midweek, with Sage believed to have been delighted with Jean-Philippe Mateta’s response since returning from injury. The France striker is in the final year of his contract but failed in an attempt to have it ruled invalid by an independent Premier League tribunal and Fifa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There are concerns about Ismaïla Sarr, however, who missed the defeat to Newcastle after a recurrence of the groin injury that ruled him out earlier in the season. The Senegal forward has made no secret of his disappointment after Palace rejected a bid from Liverpool in the summer and Sage needs last season’s player of the year back on the pitch if they are to recover from a poor start to life after Oliver Glasner.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé has apologised for his “ill-judged” comment about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which has led to brands in China dropping the Real Madrid forward. In China jokes about Mao, the founding leader of the People’s Republic of China who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” the drinks company Dongpeng said in a statement earlier on Tuesday, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappé”.

Adverts showing AI-generated images of the 27-year-old France captain drinking a Dongpeng sports drink were regularly shown in China during this year’s World Cup.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward, who has been hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media. Mbappé is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. “With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappé,” Mengniu said in a statement. “Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photo-shopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures.

“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” the Frenchman said in a statement.

“Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappé” was the top-trending topic on the Chinese social media site Weibo. One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks … crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable”. Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappé’s image from their energy drink bottles.

View image in fullscreen Two Chinese brands have ended deals with Kylian Mbappé after he allegedly referred to Mao Zedong as a ‘Chinese dictator’. Photograph: Karwai Tang/WireImage

Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappé’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people” and “have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people”.

Mbappé in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator, in an interview with the French sports newspaper L’Equipe. “There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. “Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people – well, I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life,” he said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In a statement released on Tuesday morning, La Liga condemened Mbappe’s remarks. It read: “La Liga deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.”

Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there. The former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s vice-president and current president, Lai Ching-te, sparking fury on Chinese social media. Beijing claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

The Houston Rockets general manager, Daryl Morey, posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.

Sports.title: ‘The wind goes in all directions’: Fleetwood prepare wet welcome for Arsenal at Highbury
Sports.content:
The headlines around Fleetwood Town are rarely about what happens on the pitch. Noteworthy elements include Jamie Vardy’s celebrated status as a former player, a partnership signed with a team in Uzbekistan and the owner Andrew Pilley resigning in 2023 after being convicted of fraud, for which he was jailed for 13 years. There is often something noteworthy going on in relation to the Fylde coast club.

It is no different this week, although this time football is taking centre stage as Arsenal head to Highbury Stadium on Tuesday for a Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against the League Two side. There is no link to the Gunners’ former home in Islington and the ground is a world away from what the visitors are used to, its capacity a fraction of the Emirates Stadium. The Championship side Sheffield United were deservedly beaten there in the previous round, unable to cope with their opponents or the conditions, but the Cod Army anticipate a sterner test from Mikel Arteta’s aristocrats.

Even against the Blades, the ground was less than half full but Tuesday will bring the venue’s biggest football attendance; the only other time it has sold out was for a fireworks display. The capacity is 5,300 and the stadium has four parking spaces, leaving Arsenal representatives to find alternatives on the street.

Fleetwood have a loyal local fanbase and occasions such as this can aid growth. Since the draw they have sold about an extra 200 season tickets to supporters keen to guarantee a place at the best show in town.

“It’s definitely the biggest game we’ve hosted, the Premier League champions at Highbury,” the club legend and assistant coach Nathan Pond says. “I think it’s just going to be a special night for everyone involved at the club.”

View image in fullscreen Fleetwood Town’s manager, Matt Lawlor. Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images

Pilley was the driving and financial force behind the club’s rise from non-league to a decade in League One, from which they were relegated in 2024. He handed the reins to his son Jamie, and some feel Pilley Sr’s absence has left a hole.

Away from high-profile managers including Uwe Rösler, Graham Alexander, Charlie Adam, Scott Brown and Joey Barton, a long-term project was growing in the background. Rösler and Barton were close to leading Fleetwood into the Championship, losing play-off semi-finals in 2016-17 and 2019-20 respectively. Defeat at Exeter last Saturday left the club 18th in League Two.

Matt Lawlor, the head coach since January, is an under‑the‑radar figure considering the names of some of his predecessors. He is a local who spent his playing career in non-league, representing Bamber Bridge for much of it. Lawlor has progressed from hard‑as-nails midfielder to impressive coach, spending time working for Manchester United’s foundation before joining Fleetwood’s respected academy. Regarded as a firefighter, he took charge for caretaker/interim spells at Fleetwood and their Irish sister club, Waterford, in between being part of the staff under Adam and Pete Wild, whom he succeeded.

At academy level, the club is aiding the careers of players and coaches. Bournemouth’s James Hill came through the ranks and the sale of Josh Feeney to Aston Villa in 2021 funded improvements that allowed the youth set-up to gain category two status. Three staff members have moved to Premier League clubs in recent months.

View image in fullscreen Fleetwood players celebrate during the recent 2-0 home win over Rotherham. Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images

Fleetwood tried to establish global links beyond Waterford. In 2015, they announced their short‑lived partnership with Lokomotiv Tashkent, as part of which players were invited from Uzbekistan to Fleetwood for trial. They founded Fleetwood United in Dubai in 2021 but sold the club in 2024.

In South Africa they created Western Cape Fleetwood Football Club in 2021 and partnered with Hout Bay United Football Community a year later but are no longer involved with either project.

Fleetwood’s training ground, opened by Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016, is regarded as one of the best facilities in the EFL. The club make money from hosting touring youth teams there, as part of which matches against local academy and grassroots teams – including Fleetwood’s – are offered.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The training ground is open to the public, meaning fans can sit at the cafe and take in a session before chatting with the players about all and sundry, but mainly football. “The fans do come down quite a lot and interact with staff and players, which I think is important for a community football club like ourselves,” Pond says.

“There’s no barriers between us. I think that’s really important for the club we’ve come from, to maintain those things. Some of the loyal fans who come down to the training ground every now and then and go to every game, they’ve got an understanding and they’ve had conversations with the players. After a bad result, there’s no malice in it because they know the character of the lads.”

Being on a peninsula could make conditions interesting for Arsenal, with wind and rain predicted in the wake of Storm Boelo. “You can play the first half [against] the wind, come out for the second half and still be against it,” Pond says. “It goes in all directions.”

Pond made 498 appearances for Fleetwood across seven divisions between 2003 and 2018 before returning to be part of the coaching staff. His teammates in the Conference Premier included Vardy.

“I meet people on the street, people who know I used to play for Fleetwood,” Pond says. “The first question they ask is: ‘Did you play with Vardy?’ Even on the Vardy documentaries, Fleetwood gets a mention. He’s put us in the limelight.”

They are back there, for one night at least.

Sports.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
José Mourinho had already done the por qué?, the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists.

He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out.

“We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of us cried because Thibaut couldn’t play,” Mourinho said. Plenty might have felt like it, more reason to be fearful. But the coach called Andriy Lunin, the substitute goalkeeper so serious that he bought a roll of artificial turf and spent the pandemic diving round the living room of his flat, and told him this was his moment: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench, so go on.” As for the rest of them, the manager told them nothing changes: the plan remains in place. By the time they headed back to the dressing room, “Fucking get in!” echoing along the Camp Nou corridor, so it had proved.

Thirteen years later, Mourinho was back in Barcelona for a clásico and he had guided Madrid to a 2-1 win. It wasn’t supposed to be like this, or maybe it was. Barcelona, the team who had won nine in a row, banging in 4.3 goals per game, had been beaten by Madrid, the team who had lost twice already and, truth be told, were mostly just not very good. The night it could have been all over, the title race done when it’s not even in November, was instead the night it finally started. “If you leave here nine points behind, it’s very heavy psychologically; if it’s six, it’s more balanced; if it’s three, that’s different,” Mourinho said.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho returned to where it all began to continue his unbeaten streak against Barcelona. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP

This was different, and so is the season now. Counting the clásicos all those years ago, Mourinho racked up his sixth consecutive meeting with Barcelona without defeat, and there had been no parked bus, nor many lumps kicked. They didn’t just desperately hang on, although there was a moment when Dean Huijsen saved a shot with his face. Nor had they just waited for a moment, resisting and then robbing it, even if João Cancelo did insist: “That’s Madrid; they don’t have many chances but they score them.” The final shot count said 18-10 to Barcelona, and possession was 62% Barcelona’s.

“The way we won is important: you can win luckily or by defending a lot. But we won with calmness and totally deservedly. We did it by being organised, concentrated and having the courage to come out from the back,” Mourinho said. And if that might have been pushing it a little – and, let’s face it, the analyses might be different had Lunin not made an astonishing save from Gerard Martín or Lamine Yamal’s second-half shot not faded just past the post – he had a point.

Barcelona were not at their best. They had been hurried and imprecise, Rodri telling his teammates to lower their “pulse rate” as they came out for the second half. Lamine Yamal somehow missed an extraordinary chance just before the break. And when they did tighten the screw in the second half, they couldn’t break the wall. Xavi Espart was forced off, yet another injury at the back, the failure to sign a centre-back in the spotlight again. Yet this was still a faster, more aggressive, tighter Madrid than anyone expected. Asked to define it, Lunin went for “discipline and attitude”. And if that is partly about occasion, the least you can ask for, it’s more than you sometimes get.

View image in fullscreen Andriy Lunin stepped up for Real Madrid in the absence of the ill Thibaut Courtois. Photograph: Jose Breton/AP

Besides, it was also more than that. More than Marc Cucurella getting under Lamine Yamal’s skin, although he certainly succeeded. They went for the space beyond Barcelona’s full-backs: superb in his first clásico, aged 19, Yan Diomandé – the left winger – got more touches than any Madrid player, and protected his full-back as well. But it was more than that, too. More than the wonderful winning goal, a flash of inspiration with Jude Bellingham going all Nureyev, the ball flitting between his feet and Gabriel Jesus’s legs, pirouetting to release Eduardo Camavinga. This was a team with an idea and a victory that vindicated their manager, some kind of resurrection.

Before the game, Rodri said that one of Madrid’s tricks is to convince you that they’re not that good, but insisted he wouldn’t fall into that trap. Still he felt that plan particularly. Pedri did too. Bellingham dealt with Rodri, Bernardo Silva with Pedri. Pressed and tired too, according to Hansi Flick, neither truly took control. The inclusion of Arda Güler and Silva – the surprise in the middle, starting his first league game in six weeks – underlined an intention for Madrid to keep the ball when they could. They actually had a midfield, which was new. From the back they tried to build, draw Barcelona in. And if a time came when they had to wait, to put bodies in before the ball, well, they would do that too. Six times Barcelona shots were blocked. At least twice more, shots were taken from their toes. At the other end, meanwhile, Madrid attacked with an intent and an incision that probably drew the clearer chances: the xG showed 1.19 v 1.94.

Thank you for your feedback.

Victory puts Madrid three points behind Barcelona and, Federico Valverde claimed, “will give us a kickstart”. It has taken 10 weeks but it’s game on. Hay liga, as they like to say. There is league. There is Madrid, too. Something has shifted, starting in Rome, where 70 dreadful minutes gave way to 20 pretty good ones, another inexplicable comeback actually having something of an explanation, too. The changes were impossible to ignore. Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer the partnership in the middle, Valverde going to right-back instead. Güler playing. Diomandé playing. And, yes, Vinícius Júnior not playing. “I’m not stubborn; I can change,” Mourinho said. Madrid have won five in succession now; something was seen that night, a way ahead. They’ve won every game since Vinícius was suspended, facile and perhaps even cruel though that may be to say. And since Mourinho grew a beard, if you believe in that kind of thing.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé celebrates the goal that leaves Real Madrid only three points behind Barcelona in the league. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

Before the clásico, Mourinho had said it wasn’t fair to compare his team, a side in construction and a long way from the finished product, to Barcelona. He insisted that he was still getting to know his players; he hadn’t been there long, after all. After the clásico, he admitted: “We have improved, we can’t hide that.” The idea has shifted, almost like it was an epiphany: “I’ve learned something about the middle of the pitch; I have learned that a mixture is better, that it is better to have a combination of qualities than two players of similar characteristics.” In short, Tchouaméni and Valverde doesn’t work. There needs to be some football in there somewhere, and so a shift started. Sunday came as a kind of confirmation, a hope, an identity emerging.

“The best Madrid is born at the Camp Nou,” ran the headline in El País. “Madrid are here now,” AS’s cover said. “I won’t let them have their heads on the moon; if we win this and then don’t win at the Sardinero, it won’t mean much,” Mourinho said, but this was a start, not just an end in itself. At full time, Mourinho headed on to the pitch and shook Lunin’s hand as all around players embraced. High in the north-east corner, Madrid’s fans stayed and sang. Back home, Courtois was watching. He had “a horrible night” on Saturday, they said, but now he was feeling a little better. They all were.

Sports.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation
Sports.content:
England abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1.

Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee.

Thorpe was seen asking the referee to come over before instructing his players to leave the field. One of England’s assistant coaches subsequently told the referee: “We are reporting racism”, adding that the team did not want to continue playing.

When another official approached to discuss the next steps, the assistant coach reiterated that England’s players did not want to resume the match. He also said a player was upset by the incident. Footage later showed heated exchanges between members of the coaching teams, with representatives from each side saying they were seeking to protect their players.

“Fifa is aware of an incident at the Under-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland,” said a spokesperson for world football’s governing body. “The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.”

The spokesperson said the official reports were being collected and that the matter would be referred to Fifa’s independent disciplinary committee, which would decide on any further action.

The Football Association has not commented, but is understood to be waiting for more information. It is said to be taking the matter seriously and providing support to players and staff. The Football Association of Ireland has been contacted for comment.

The inaugural Under-15 World Cup involves 189 countries and territories. Games are played in an eight-a-side format on smaller pitches, with two 20-minute halves.

England, who had won their three previous matches against Cambodia, Montenegro and Nicaragua, faced Zimbabwe later on Monday, while Ireland were due to play Cambodia. Only the group winners will progress to the top-tier competition this week, with the rest of the teams divided into separate tiers depending on where they finished.

Before the tournament, Fifa described it as “unrivalled in scale or ambition”. More than 3,000 players are taking part in 950 matches, with each team playing a minimum of nine games. Arsène Wenger, Fifa’s chief of global football development, described it as giving “players from across the world the chance to compete, to learn and to grow”.

Sports.title: Police called to Florida soccer game after parents say three-year-old benched for being too good
Sports.content:
Police were called after a dispute involving the parents of a three-year-old player at a soccer game in Florida over the weekend.

The boy’s parents can be heard on police body cameras saying their son, Nevada, had been kicked out because he was too good at soccer and was embarrassing the other children. However, an organizer at the game said Nevada had pushed other children and his parents had become argumentative when their son was taken out the game.

In police body camera footage the organizer of the event, who works for i9 Sports, a youth sports group, can be heard saying Nevada’s parents had caused a disturbance.

“The kid is good. He’s great. Really good,” the organizer says in the footage. “He’s very advanced compared to the other ones, so he’s scoring a lot of goals. But he’s pushing the kids ... So, I try to tell him, don’t push; we want to play without pushing, right?”

Nevada’s parents posted a clip of their son at the event in which he can be seen dribbling around older children with ease. The video has since gone viral. Nevada cannot be seen pushing any other children in the footage posted by his parents.

“They’re mad at my son because he actually plays soccer. They’re literally kicking him out of this place because he’s good at soccer,” his mother says in the body camera footage. “First, they said he’s not passing, but nobody’s catching the ball when he’s passing.”

The i9 Sports worker told police they were willing to give Nevada’s parents a refund if they left.

“I just want him out. Immediately,” the organizer told police. “Just give me their names so I can give them their refund.”

The Winter Park Police Department said the family agreed to leave the event and no one was arrested.

“The family stated the game was over and they were leaving. The family was cooperative with the officers,” the department wrote in a statement on its website. “No one was arrested, trespassed, or forced to leave the park.”

i9 Sports said it was reviewing the incident and had contacted Nevada’s family.

“We are aware of concerns being shared regarding an incident at a local i9 Sports program, and we take them very seriously,” i9 Sports said in a statement. “The respectful treatment and well-being of every child and family matter deeply to us. We have reached out to the family and have begun a review that includes speaking with those involved. While we work to understand the circumstances, we will not speculate or share unverified information. We appreciate everyone who has brought their concerns to our attention.”

One officer appeared to want to see more of Nevada though. “I kind of want to see him play. I bet he’s good,” he can be heard saying to another officer on body camera.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick given more time at Man United and will be in charge for Chelsea game
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick given more time at Man United and will be in charge for Chelsea game

Michael Carrick is set to be given time to turn things around as Manchester United manager.

He is expected to be on the touchline at Stamford Bridge on Saturday as his side take on Chelsea, live on talkSPORT.

4 Carrick appeared to be waving goodbye at Old Trafford on Sunday as fans chanted his name - but he has not been sacked after the loss to Bournemouth Credit: Getty

Carrick appeared destined for the sack after losing 3-0 at home to Bournemouth on Sunday, but he is staying on.

Man United's chiefs were at Carrington on Monday, with Carrick also present, however, he was there to watch at academy game.

And the club legend arrived at the training ground again on Tuesday, with the decision clearly made to give him more time.

The Red Devils' training will take place as usual in the build-up to the clash with Chelsea, with focus on preparing the team.

The manager and players will have the chance to show there is still hope with a response on the pitch on Saturday.

United have not won any of their last eight games in all competitions, going on a miserable run that seemed to spell the end of Carrick.

But after cutting an emotional figure at Old Trafford, where fans sang his name from the stands, he remains boss.

'I'm a little bit concerned'

Reacting to the news, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said: "It feels like a stay of execution for Michael Carrick.

"The message coming out of the club this morning is business as usual. Michael reported for training and is taking training.

"Everyone at the club is focused on preparing the team for Saturday...it will be fascinating to see how the players react to this.

4 Carrick has managed to keep his role and will be on the touchline at Stamford Bridge when his side face Chelsea on Saturday Credit: Getty

"I'm a little bit concerned as a United fan whether they can turn it around on the back of those two performances against Como and Bournemouth.

"Do the players have it in then to go to to Stamford Bridge and produce a performance worthy of the shirt? On the evidence of what we have seen in the last few weeks, I would say no.

"But Carrick stays and we will see what happens."

Carrick's chaotic week

Carrick has kept his job despite back-to-back heavy losses to Como in the Champions League and Bournemouth in the Premier League.

He had also dropped captain Bruno Fernandes in a bold decision in the league clash after the skipper criticised his tactics.

The manager went on to keep Fernandes as an unused substitute in a decision that led to some backlash coming his way.

4 Carrick's side have not won in their last eight games and he has seemingly fell out with Fernandes, but he has kept his role for now Credit: Getty

But after all of that happened over the span of just a few days, Carrick has managed to survive and remains in charge.

The decision comes after Carrick remained defiant and clarified his waves to the Old Trafford crowd were not a farewell.

"I take the responsibility, of course," he admitted on Sunday. "I accept the responsibility. I respect the position I am in. The responsibility is mine. What else can I say right now?

"I totally understand the situation. I am not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I always do what I feel is best for this football club.

"Whatever decision is made on anything really, that's kind of it. I am not expecting anything."

Chelsea vs Man United: Live on talkSPORT

Carrick wasn't expecting anything and he was right to, as nothing has happened and he remains in charge this weekend.

4 Carrick will be in the United dugout as his side face Chelsea, live on talkSPORT Credit: Getty

And you can follow all of the action from Chelsea vs Man United, which kicks off at 12:30pm, live on talkSPORT on Saturday.

Sports.title: Galatasaray vs Fenerbahce descends into mass brawl as stars wrestled to the ground
Sports.content:
Galatasaray vs Fenerbahce descends into mass brawl as stars wrestled to the ground

The Intercontinental derby between Turkish giants Galatasaray and Fenerbahce descended into total chaos post-match.

Galatasaray won the game 2-1 before the rival players began to fight on the pitch, with some even wrestling on the ground.



3 Total chaos broke out in Istanbul on Sunday as Galatasaray and Fenerbahce players clashed following the full-time whistle Credit: Getty

3 Brown and Bardakci even ended up rolling on the ground fighting after the former got his rival into a headlock Credit: Getty

Viral footage showed the full, brutal clash that began with Gala captain Abdulkerim Bardakci having to hold his teammates back.

Fenerbahce's Kerem Akturkoglu was involved in a confrontation at full-time and that sparked a brawl that spiralled out of control.



Akturkoglu was separated from his beef, but ex-Arsenal midfielder Matteo Guendouzi then started another argument.

Guendouzi, who was involved in another fight in the Champions League in August, scuffled with a member of Gala staff, which then led to almost every player on the pitch rushing over.



Multiple staff members and stadium security were also involved, as different breakaway clashes began.

Alongside the huge group involved in the main scuffle, English defender Archie Brown fought with Bardakci.



The Fenerbahce left-back was on the outskirts of the brawl when Bardakci confronted him and the pair got into it, with Brown quickly getting his rival into a tight headlock.

Staff and security tried to break them up, but they both ended up falling over, rolling on the ground before being surrounded.

Further clashes then began around them as they were finally separated amid the crazy scene on the pitch.

The brawl continued into the tunnel too, with Guendouzi seen chasing a rival before fighting continued on the touchline.



3 Staff members from both teams and stadium security were involved as the mass brawl exploded on the pitch Credit: Getty

How did the match play out?

Fenerbahce's Akturkoglu, Guendouzi and Brown were key to the chaos after their side were beaten in the derby.

They were left fuming by the 2-1 loss to their rivals, which saw them drop down to fifth in the Turkish Super Lig.

Victor Osimhen scored two to lead Galatasaray to victory, with Irfan Can Kahveci's goal not enough to inspire a comeback.



Gala remained top of the table after picking up their seventh win in their opening nine league games.

There were seven yellow cards shown by the referee during the match, including to ex-Premier League stars N'Golo Kante, Davinson Sanchez and Nelson Semedo.

Rafael Leao and Milan Skriniar were also booked in a game that ended up reaching boiling point after the final whistle.

The opening two months of the Premier League season has been a tumultuous period for both of the Manchester clubs both on and off the pitch.

Manchester City are sat at the top of the Premier League table eight games in to the new season but have been found guilty of 114 charges relating to breaching the league's financial regulations over a nine year period from 2008 - a verdict which the club is appealing.

Meanwhile Manchester United are struggling desperately on the pitch, with the club currently sat just one point above the relegation zone with only one win in the league so far this season.

With City expected to be on the receiving end of an enormous points deduction should their guilty charge be upheld, relegation seems all but inevitable to some.

All of the above brings the distinct possibility that both Manchester clubs could be relegated from the Premier League this season, which talkSPORT BET have priced up at 40/1, which can be added straight into your bet slip here.

All the noise around Manchester City's guilty verdict doesn't appear to be affecting them on the pitch.

The news broke during the extended international break leaving lots of time for the footballing world to voice their opinions on the matter and what they believe the punishment should be for such an unprecedented case.

But in their first game back, Enzo Maresca's side went to Anfield to take on a Liverpool side who had finished as Premier League runners up behind Manchester City on two occasions during the time period in question relating to City's charges.

An amplified hostile atmosphere was there to greet Man City in the match, but City did their talking on the pitch as they romped to a 3-0 win.

The Cityzens, who have won six of the last nine Premier League titles, have won seven of their eight matches in the league this time around, and currently sit top of the table on goal difference ahead of defending champions Arsenal.

On the other side of the city, Manchester United are currently sat 16th in the Premier League table and without a win across their last eight matches in any competition, with just two wins in 12 in the entire campaign.

Recent results, in particular their 4-1 loss to Champions League debutants Como which was followed four days later by a 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth in the league, have left manager Michael Carrick under considerable pressure for his job.

The former Red Devils midfielder only became the team's manager on a permanent basis in the summer after impressing as caretaker boss last season, finishing as high as third in the table.

However, this season has been an entirely different story, with players attacking the board and the manager after disagreeing with summer transfer business and game tactics, it seems the club are imploading from within slightly.

Relegation would have seemed unthinkable for both clubs in recent times, but it's now a very real threat for two of English football's most successful clubs, the only two English teams ever to win a continental treble, for very different reasons.

For Man City, playing outside the Premier League next season would mark their first season outside the top flight since their promotion from the second tier in 2002, while for United, it would bring an end 50 consecutive years in the top division of English football.

Sports.title: Harry Kane Premier League transfer prediction made after England captain wins Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Will Harry Kane, the newly-crowned 2026 Ballon d'Or winner, return to the Premier League before retirement?

Tim Sherwood and Ally McCoist have stated differing assessments on whether or not the world's best footballer could be set for one final stint in the league where his career catapulted.



2 Kane has won the biggest individual prize in world football after a stunning year with England and Bayern Credit: Getty

Kane beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the prestigious Ballon d'Or gong on Monday night, joining Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen as the English winners.

The 33-year-old totalled 68 goals and assists for Bayern Munich last season and then banked seven contributions as England captain at the 2026 World Cup.

With 73 international and club goals, Kane also won the Gerd Muller Trophy on a memorable night at the London Palladium.



talkSPORT understands that he is set to sign a new three-year deal at Bayern that will keep him at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

Will Kane return to the Premier League?

However, there has long been talk over a potential return to Premier League football as he is second in the all-time scoring standings with 213 goals, all of which he scored for Tottenham.



Kane made his first start in the league in April 2014 under his former Spurs boss Sherwood, who hinted to talkSPORT Breakfast that he will come back but only three clubs are viable options for him.

"I think when he comes back, he's going to come back to a team he thinks can win," he explained. "He's used to winning trophies now, he's enjoying his time over there at Bayern.



"I don't think he comes back to a team that he thinks can't win, so it narrows it down. He's not going to go to Chelsea, he's not going to go to Arsenal, so where is he actually going to end up?

"It's probably not going to be Man City, so you're only looking at Liverpool, Man United and possibly Tottenham.

"I mean, Tottenham have got more chance of winning something at the moment, as you look at it, than Man United certainly have."

2 Kane is an all-time Premier League great, but Sherwood and McCoist have different opinions on whether he will come back Credit: Getty



While Sherwood may have more of an insight into Kane's thinking, and was in attendance at his Ballon d'Or after-party, McCoist isn't certain of a Premier League comeback.

It would mean that Alan Shearer remains as the all-time top scorer on 260 goals, a record that may never be beaten.

"I hope so, but I'm not sure. I'd be leaning towards no," McCoist said.

"The thing is, I can see him... the decision now might be similar to the one that he had at Tottenham, in terms of, 'Do I move, or do I stay?'



McCoist then added: "I'm not inside his head but you can tell when you watch him, listen to him, he is as happy as Larry where he is right now, how that club and those supporters, and that country have taken to him.

"I can see him finishing his career there, I really can. I think he loves the place and they love him."

Sports.title: EFL star spotted celebrating with Harry Kane in lavish Ballon d’Or afterparty
Sports.content:
Harry Kane headed straight to an exclusive London nightclub to celebrate his historic Ballon d'Or win on Monday evening.

After picking up the prestigious award, he held a lavish after party alongside some of his old teammates and good friends.

4 Kane partied alongside his family and friends in an exclusive London nightclub after winning the Ballon d'Or Credit: Instagram

4 A packed dancefloor full of Kane's ex-teammates saw sparkler-topped champagne bottles carried through the crowds Credit: Instagram

Kane became the first Englishman to lift the trophy since Michael Owen in 2001 and he celebrated in worthy style.

A video circulating around social media shows the England captain holding his drink to the sky and dancing.

He was flanked by his parents, his brother and wife Kate, who joined him for the celebrations, along with some familiar faces.

A few of his former Tottenham teammates were present in the club, as sparkler-topped champagne bottles were held aloft.

Among those on the packed dancefloor was Matt Doherty, who now plays for Sheffield United in the Championship, Eric Dier and Ben Davies.

The trio all played for Spurs at the same time and clearly became good friends, with Dier playing at Bayern with Kane too.

James Maddison was also pictured with his Three Lions pal at the party and was able to get his hands on the Ballon d'Or.

Ex-Tottenham manager Tim Sherwood was also at the party celebrating with his former player.

After dancing the night away, Kane was up bright and early to return to Germany for training with Bayern, being interviewed outside his hotel in the early hours ahead of his flight.

Kane will potentially play in the DFB Pokal second round against Magdeburg on Wednesday, two days after his win.

4 Kane toasted the crowd as he celebrated, with plenty of his old teammates joining him after his Ballon d'Or success Credit: Instagram

What has Kane said on his Ballon d'Or win?

Speaking about his success, Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday morning: "A special night, just trying to take it all in really.

"It feels like a dream. Thank you everyone for all the love and support, I really felt it. From social media, here in London and in the theatre last night.

"Thank you very much and this one's for all of us."

Kane had thanked Bayern Munich, Tottenham and England in his speech at the London Palladium on Monday night.

He also shouted out Bayern boss Vincent Kompany, who is currently in hospital after collapsing following training on Friday.

His first words as he stepped on to the stage and claimed the Ballon d'Or were: "I'm almost speechless.

4 Kane thanked his old club Spurs, current club Bayern and England before dancing the night away at the nightclub Credit: instagram @madders

"Thank you to France Football, to the Ballon d'Or for putting on this amazing event.

"Being here in London has made it extra special. It looked like a good omen for me tonight so thank you very much.

“Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was really tough this year, some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my teammates, some world-class players in the room tonight."

Sports.title: Fleetwood vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: ‘Excited’ Cods eye huge Carabao Cup shock at Highbury
Sports.content:
Fleetwood Town will be eyeing a huge Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal tonight, live on talkSPORT.

The Premier League champions take on League Two opposition in the fourth round of this season's competition, in what will be the first-ever meeting between the two sides.



4 Goals from Ezri Konsa and Gabriel gave Arsenal victory over Everton on Saturday Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's side beat Ipswich 4-2 to reach this stage, while Fleetwood are targeting another upset after a 1-0 win over Championship outfit Sheffield United in the previous round.

Arsenal head into the tie days after a 2-0 win over Everton that moved them joint-top of the Premier League with Manchester City.

This capped off a strong week for the Gunners, who also clinched a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich in the Champions League.



Meanwhile, Fleetwood have struggled since their last Carabao Cup outing, losing six of nine games to leave them 18th in League Two.

But cup ties are famously unpredictable, and the Cods will look to bring their best as they welcome Arsenal to Highbury Stadium - the same name as the visitors' iconic old north London home.



Fleetwood vs Arsenal live commentary

This Carabao Cup fourth round tie will take place on Tuesday, October 27.

Kick-off at Highbury Stadium is scheduled for 8pm.

talkSPORT will have live coverage of the game, with Adrian Durham presenting the action in Lancashire.



Commentary will come from Joe Shennan and former Fleetwood manager and ex-Liverpool midfielder Charlie Adam.

4 Fleetwood's Highbury Stadium will play host to Arsenal, which has a capacity of just 5,327

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.



Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

The match has also been selected for live television broadcast on Sky Sports.

Coverage on Sky Sports Main Event is scheduled to get underway at 7.30pm.



4 Max Dowman has been used sparingly this season, but boasts two Carabao Cup goals Credit: Getty

Fleetwood vs Arsenal team news

Arteta is expected to rotate his Arsenal side, with a Premier League clash against Liverpool also on this week's agenda.

This could see Max Dowman handed a start, with the teenage sensation grabbing a brace in the third round win over Ipswich.

Meanwhile, the likes of Declan Rice, Riccardo Calafiori, Martin Odegaard and Gabriel could all be rested, giving Cristhian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi a chance of minutes.



Injury-wise, Arsenal will be without Bukayo Saka against Fleetwood, with Arteta confirming he is facing 'weeks' out after picking up a quad injury against Bayern Munich.

Meanwhile, William Saliba continues his recovery along with Christos Tzolis, while Viktor Gyokeres could be in line to start again.

As for Fleetwood, striker Lewis McCann is unavailable through suspension, having been booked twice already in the Carabao Cup this term.

Kane Thompson-Sommers is among the other Cods stars missing out on the Arsenal visit through injury, while summer signing Andy Cannon is fit to make his return after almost two months out.



4 Matt Lawlor was appointed Fleetwood's permanent manager in January Credit: Getty

Fleetwood vs Arsenal: What has been said?

Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor urged his side to embrace one of the biggest nights in the club’s history, as they look to pull off a huge upset against Arsenal.

Looking ahead on Monday, he said: “The champions are coming to town and they’re coming to our patch.

“The players need to be excited by it, not overawed by it. The respect is through the roof, but the fear can’t be through the roof.



“We’ve earned a game like this. We’ve had to go through round upon round of tough games, and none of them were easy. To get to where we are, we deserve that.”

The draw for Carabao Cup quarter-finals will take place on Wednesday.
