Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes tipped to leave Manchester United: ‘It’s coming to an end’
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has been predicted to leave Man United as part of a dressing room clear-out amid his clash with Michael Carrick.

Fernandes slammed Carrick's tactics last week before liking a social media post in what appeared to be a dig at the manager.

3 Fernandes has been tipped to leave Man United amid the club's struggles and his clash with manager Carrick Credit: Getty

He was dropped for United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday, remaining as an unused substitute despite the score.

The Red Devils captain's relationship with the club appears to be fractured, with Carrick on the brink of being sacked too.

So, what's next for Fernandes? Will he work things out at Old Trafford if Carrick goes? Or could he end up leaving the club?

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda thinks the best thing for both parties is for him to depart in the coming transfer windows.

Fernandes tipped to leave Man United

Sepulveda admitted to Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist on talkSPORT Breakfast: "In my personal opinion, I think it's coming to an end.

"And I really think that's the best for both because I think first of all, Manchester United must organise their own dressing room.

"Even for Bruno Fernandes, I think the best for both is to, let's say, break this relationship, find a solution, because I think that kind of organisation that Man United needs to make a step back, to make two steps forward, starts with cleaning the dressing room.

"I think that a player like Fernandes nowadays, it's better to not be there, even for him, because I think that Fernandes is in a team that is more established, fighting for big things.

"Even for him, it could be much better, because yesterday, for example, it is what it is, but Bruno Fernandes, the position that he had in the Ballon d'Or [27th], for example, it doesn't reflect the player that he is, the numbers that he has.

"And if he plays for another team, I'm sure that Bruno Fernandes easily can be in the top ten players of the world."

3 Fernandes, who finished 27th in the Ballon d'Or on Monday, should be part of United's dressing room clear-out, according to Sepulveda Credit: Getty

Where could Fernandes go if he leaves?

Host Stelling then tipped Fernandes for a move to Saudi, not long after he rejected a £700,000-a-week move in summer 2025.

The idea of a return to his home country was also floated, but Sepulveda can't see either of those moves happening.

He said: "No [I can't see him back in Portugal], at the end of his career yes, but you're talking about a player in his prime.

"You mention Saudi, but what I know from Bruno, his priority will not be Saudi, he is not that kind of player looking for financials.

"If a big club comes with the right project, I think he will prefer to stay in a big club in Europe instead of getting millions."

Is Fernandes the problem?

As well as assessing Fernandes' future at Man United and his next move, Sepulveda also discussed the midfielder's issues.

3 Fernandes would prefer to stay at a big club in Europe - but will his personality impact interest from those European giants? Credit: Getty

He believes that his personality simply doesn't match Man United's current troubles and that he has become a 'problem', with that potentially impacting interest from other big clubs.

"I think the quality of the player is undebatable," Sepulveda said. "I don't think there's one person that will say Fernandes is not an amazing player, probably the best player of Man United.

"The thing is, Bruno is let's say, a special person outside the pitch, he has a huge personality and I think that huge personalities can sometimes be a negative point for him in his career.

"Even in his future, because, to be honest, from the reputation that this kind of midfielder has in the industry, you can look at other clubs that are interested in the transfer of Bruno Fernandes...

"Of course, Man United is a huge team, but the teams that nowadays fight for the Champions League, these teams are not interested in the player [Fernandes] with these kinds of numbers, so this is where there must be a reason for that and I think that reason is his behaviour outside the pitch and in the dressing room.

"Fernandes is that kind of player that if things are positive, if the team is winning, he's a massive contribution to the team.

"But if things are not well, like the way Man United is now, I think sometimes he could be a problem."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick is STAYING: Man United decide against wielding axe after day of crisis talks - with under-pressure boss taking training today ahead of trip to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is staying as Manchester United head coach after being given the chance to turn the club’s season around.

Carrick will remain in charge for Saturday’s trip to Chelsea after Old Trafford bosses decided not to sack him.

The 45-year-old took charge of a first-team training session at Carrington on Tuesday morning despite intense speculation over his future.

Carrick arrived at the complex shortly before 8am dressed in a club tracksuit, and oversaw training as usual as the players returned after a day off.

He had also turned up at Carrington on Monday but was there to watch United’s Under-21s play in a behind-closed-doors game against Hull City alongside his No2 Steve Holland and Under-18s coach Darren Fletcher.

He stayed for three hours before leaving with his son Jacey, a member of United’s Under-18s.

Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington to take training on Tuesday morning with his fate still up in the air - but the club have decided to keep him as manager

Bruno Fernandes - dropped for the Bournemouth game after criticising the manager's tactics - stops outside training, before news broke that Carrick was staying

Director of football Jason Wilcox drives into Carrington today after spending Monday discussing Carrick's future

Carrick’s job has been hanging by a thread after losing half of his 12 games this season.

United have made their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years, and have failed to win in eight games for the first time since 2015.

Carrick was visibly emotional after the defeat to Bournemouth when the fans gave him a rousing show of support while directing their fury at the Glazers, Ratcliffe, Wilcox and the players.

The former United midfielder appeared to say farewell to supporters afterwards, although he later insisted that was not the case.

It followed a heartfelt five-minute monologue to reporters at the start of his pre-match press conference on Friday, two days after he approached the travelling fans in Como to apologise for a 4-1 defeat.

After playing away in Spain and Italy over the last fortnight, United have a free week because they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton and are not in action again until Saturday’s trip to Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick takes Manchester United training despite mounting fears over his job as club bosses weigh up under-fire manager's future in Carrington summit
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has arrived at Manchester United's Carrington training ground this morning with his bosses giving him the vote of confidence despite huge pressure surrounding his job.

Carrick took training today with the players reporting back to the club's HQ after Monday's scheduled day off following Sunday's disastrous 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth.

United take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with Carrick set to remain in post by the weekend.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at the club's Carrington training ground yesterday where they held conference calls with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Berrada and Wilcox were pictured arriving this morning after Carrick, alongside a number of players including rogue captain Bruno Fernandes.

Daily Mail Sport understands Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe have been mooted as potential replacements but, for now, Carrick's job is safe.

Michael Carrick is pictured arriving at Manchester United training before 8am on Tuesday

Carrick was in the dark over his future but he has survived, and will take the Chelsea game

Carrick was also at the training ground on Monday to watch a behind-closed-doors game against Hull City while Berrada and Wilcox discussed his future in another part of the complex. It is not known if the 45-year-old spoke to them during his three hours there.

Jamie Carragher this morning suggested United could be 'broken' and said Carrick is 'not at the level they really need'.

On The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet, Carragher said: 'Were we looking at a broken football club , in terms of the players, your captain being on the bench? There was no way in the world Michael Carrick was ever bringing him on, no matter what would have happened in that game, he was never coming on.

'It's been up and down for Man United. It's been worse than that, shall we say. But that to me felt almost as bad as it's been at different times because of that complete nothing on the pitch.

'Bruno Fernandes sitting there on the bench, your best player, PFA Player of the Year last year.... Michael Carrick really probably not at the level Manchester United need in the dugout, and losing 3-0, and it could have been five or six.'

If United decide to change head coach again, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann – both currently out of work and able to take over immediately – are the leading candidates after bookmakers stopped taking bets on Carrick being sacked.

Although Howe is available after leaving Newcastle in the summer, it's understood that United would still owe his old club around £3million in compensation as well as having to pay off Carrick and his coaching staff.

Technical director Jason Wilcox discussed Carrick's future in another part of the complex

United CEO Omar Berrada is pictured arriving at Carrington with the situation stuck in limbo

Carrick brought Lisandro Martinez on against Bournemouth but left Bruno Fernandes out

Carragher says Howe is the 'sensible' appointment to get United away from the Premier League's relegation zone. They currently sit 16th after eight rounds of games.

'I'm a massive fan of Eddie Howe and should be the next England manager, and he's the best English coach out there,' he said. 'Is he this big, glamour name? No. And would he be the guy who could get Manchester United back to winning titles or European Cups? Most people would say no.

'But where United are right now, you need somebody who knows the Premier League, really, because I'm not saying you're going to get relegated, but there's a good chance you're going to be in the bottom three by the time we get to an international break because of the fixtures.'

Sports.title: 'What the f*** are you doing? Stick a firework up their a**e!': Wayne Rooney launches f-word rant about Man United players letting down close friend Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney has launched a furious tirade at the Man United players who have let down his friend and ex-team-mate Michael Carrick. United's abject 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after their 4-1 demolition at Como has seen the crisis club plumb new depths but the manager has been given the chance to fight on and turn the season around, as reported by Daily Mail Sport's Chris Wheeler. The apparent lack of effort for Carrick, the fans and the club that United's highly-paid stars are delivering has enraged club legend Rooney, 41. 'At least I ran and worked hard and put myself about for the team,' he said on The United Stand. 'I don't think the players have got a leg to stand on. What's not fair is the performances they're giving. 'I was a player who could score a goal, had a bit of ability but at least I f***ing ran and worked hard, put myself about for the team even when it's going tough. These players are not doing that. 'I'd love to go in that dressing room. I'd love to go in that dressing room, f***ing sit them all down and say "what the f*** are you doing? What type of performance do you think this is? Do you think you deserve to wear that shirt?" Put a f***ing firework up their a**e because they're f***ing not doing anything. Wayne Rooney has hammered the Man United players who have let down Michael Carrick Carrick's United have endured an abysmal start to the season and lost 3-0 to Bournemouth 'You could see the pain and anger in the fans' faces when the players are walking around a football pitch. Martinez when Rayan just ran around him... when they're just not getting to the ball it's so frustrating.' Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the game and refused to bring on the club captain in the wake of his midweek interview moaning about the team's tactics. Rooney namechecked Fernandes and Marcus Rashford as two individuals who should be stepping up with the beleaguered club struggling. He went on: 'These players have had some top class managers and they've just absolutely pulled the wool over their eyes. They're not running, they're not working, they're selfish. 'Bruno got off that bus with his hood up trying to hide away from it. Be front and centre. Go and stand up. You questioned the manager, go and show yourself. 'Where's Rashford now? Things get tough, where's Rashford? You need to play through a pain barrier, you need to be ready to give everything for the club and they're not doing that.' Supporters in the Stretford End gave Carrick a warm reaction, singing his chant and applauding him off the pitch on Sunday before turning on the players to boo. Rooney is pleased they're seeing through the squad, who are 'not fit to wear the shirt'. Rooney took aim at Bruno Fernandes for 'walking in with his hood up' on Sunday after being dropped by Carrick for his insubordination He added: 'I was really pleased they clapped Michael off the pitch, it was almost a sympathy clap when they've done that and turned on the players. 'They're not fit to wear that shirt at the minute. I don't think they ever will be but they're getting paid enormous amounts of money. The least you can do is work. Show that it means something. Show that you care. That's why the fans have switched on them. 'It's so annoying and frustrating and disappointing that these players are going to get away with it again. Michael Carrick has won five Premier League titles and the Champions League. He knows how to win at this club, albeit as a player, he knows what the standards are and you've got these players walking all over him.' Rooney's former team-mate Gary Neville has also been scathing in his criticism of the Man United players, accusing them of being unprofessional. 'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned him for a few months. They have they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though. He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players. 'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them. 'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. 'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or disrespect row: French superstars Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele fail to stand to shake humble winner's hand - as it's revealed just how close vote was
Sports.content:
French football superstars Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele have been accused of disrespecting Harry Kane after failing to stand to shake his hand before he won the Ballon d'Or – the prize for the world's best footballer – on Monday night. Humble hero Kane posted last night saying: 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise.' But Real Madrid striker Mbappe had backed himself before the ceremony saying: 'I always think I'm the best [player in the world] but everyone has their own opinion. Maybe it's a good year for this.' In footage from the London Palladium, Kane, 33, can be seen greeting Mbappe and Paris Saint-Germain star Dembele in the theatre, while they pay little attention to him. Both French players stay firmly in their seats as Kane crouches to grasp their hands – with Mbappe in particular looking elsewhere before the Englishman grabs his attention. Kane would go on to win the award, beating Mbappe by fewer than 41 points – a tighter margin than the last close race in 2024 between Rodri and Vinicius Jnr – the director of the Ballon d'Or organisation revealed. In 2025 the gap between first and second was 321 points as Dembele triumphed. Full voting breakdowns are not released until Saturday, October 31. In footage from the ceremony, Mbappe also does not stand up to congratulate Kane when he is announced as the winner. Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele both failed to stand to shake Harry Kane's hand at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London on Monday night. Source: X/Kyks98 Mbappe is seen with Kane and Barcelona superstar Rodri at Monday's ceremony Dembele, last year's winner, finished seventh in the rankings behind third-place Lamine Yamal, Rodri, Lionel Messi and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. French outlet RMC report there were 'tensions' among a number of players including Dembele, who was forced to wait an hour at his hotel before departing for the Palladium and there were no refreshments or barriers set up when he arrived. The ceremony was also delayed. Dembele later complained about a 30-minute wait to leave the venue when vans and buses could not reach the red carpet to pick VIPs up afterwards. Meanwhile, Kane's England team-mate Jude Bellingham - who also plays alongside Mbappe at Real Madrid - sent a classy message to the newly-crowned Ballon d'Or winner. He wrote on Instagram: 'Congratulations skip!' with a love heart and a goat emoji. After the ceremony, Kane headed to Cirque le Soir in Soho. Wife Kate Goodland and his parents Patrick and Kim were among those celebrating his crowning as the world's best footballer. Still kitted out in his tuxedo having arrived directly from the glitzy London Palladium ceremony, the 33-year-old was filmed bopping at the back of the room while sparkler-filled champagne bottles made their way through the packed dance-floor in wild scenes of jubilation. Kane, ever the diligent professional, made sure to go easy on the booze while others around him indulged. He was seen wearing a stunning £1million Rolex Daytona watch at the ceremony and still looked sharp in the nightclub. Kane raised his shot glass of champagne to the friends and family celebrating his Ballon d'Or win in Cirque le Soir in Soho on Monday night as the afterparty took off Harry Kane and his wife Kate Goodland shared a kiss after he won the striker award (left) and Ballon d'Or (right) on Monday night He is back in Bayern Munich training today and ensured he stuck to small measures of booze despite his career-defining triumph. The London ceremony capped a chaotic evening for football's top individual prize. Profiles of at least three 'winners' were published on their website before the ceremony had begun – proclaiming Kane, Mbappe and Yamal as the victors separately. A statement from the organisers read: 'Portraits of some Ballon d'Or nominees, prepared by Ballondor.com, were inadvertently published online. These articles had been written in advance for each of the nominees, in the event of a victory. 'They reveal nothing about the podium, which remains, to this day, unknown to everyone.' In France, there are suggestions that Champions League winners PSG, Dembele's club, sabotaged themselves by failing to orchestrate a voting bloc for one player. Dembele, Kvaratskhelia, Achraf Hakimi, Vitinha, Ferran Torres, Joao Neves, Willian Pacho, Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos all ranked in the final top 30 list. England captain Kane plants a kiss on the trophy after being crowned the world's best player Kane wore a rare Rolex Daytona - said to be worth around £1m - at the ceremony Jude Bellingham, who plays alongside Mbappe at Real Madrid, sent a classy message England captain Kane, often hailed for his humble attitude, used a 12-minute winner's speech to thank a long list of people from his life and career – right from his former Leyton Orient manager Russell Slade to current boss Vincent Kompany and his wife Kate. 'Wow. Wow, wow, wow,' Kane said. 'First of all... I'm almost speechless. Luckily I have this list here! 'Thank you again to France Football, for the Ballon d'Or, for putting on this amazing event. Being here in London as well has made it extra special. It looked like a good omen today, so thank you very much. 'Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was very tough this year, some of the incredible players I was up against. Some of my team-mates and some of the world-class players that are in the room tonight.' He later added: 'I want to give out a shout out to some of my coaches who have helped me along the way. If I've forgotten anyone, I'm really sorry. 'Bradley Allen, Chris Ramsey, John McDermott, Alex Inglethorpe, Tim Sherwood. Ryan Mason, Kenny Jackett, Russell Slade, Harry Redknapp, Mauricio Pochettino, Jose Mourinho, Antonio Conte. Roy Hodgson, Gareth Southgate and, of course, my two managers Vinnie and Thomas (Tuchel) now.

'All of you have played a big role in my development, all at different stages in my life. Without each and every one of you, I wouldn't be standing here today. For sure, I learned lots, and when you surround yourself with the best people, the best coaches, it only enhances you as a person and a player.' Sports.title: Michael Owen involved in awkward Ballon d'Or exchange...as he is forced to tell reporter that he is a previous winner of the award!
Sports.content:
Michael Owen was involved in an awkward exchange at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London last night – with a questioner who appeared not to know the former England striker is a previous winner of the award.

The ex-Liverpool and Real Madrid star was stopped on his way to the ceremony by a journalist, who proceeded to baffle him by asking: 'What was the best standing in the Ballon d'Or when you were active?'

Owen hesitated before saying, 'Well I won it in 2001.'

The now floundering journalist, who was reporting for Norwegian channel TV2 Sport, attempted to salvage the exchange by quickly muttering, 'you did right.'

Owen was the last Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or until last night when Three Lions skipper Harry Kane lifted the trophy at the London Palladium.

Owen won the award at the age of 23, beating likes of Raul, Oliver Kahn and David Beckham to win the accolade and become the fourth Englishman to be crowned the world's best player.

He really just asked Ballon d'Or winner Michael Owen “What was your best standing in the Ballon d'Or” 😂😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/t6EBLe1JSb — Football Hub (@FootbalIhub) October 26, 2026

Owen attended the awards last night where he saw Harry Kane follow in his footsteps as an English winner

Until last night Michael Owen was the last Englishman to be awarded the Ballon d'Or, winning it in 2001

The striker won the gong off the back of a stellar season with Liverpool in which he netted 24 goals and registered eight assists in 46 appearances across all competitions and lifting the UEFA Cup, League Cup and FA Cup.

He then added a Community Shield and UEFA Super Cup to his trophy haul in the following summer, helping to make the Reds the first English side to win five major trophies in a calendar year.

Owen has previously admitted that he was unaware of the magnitude of his achievement until he moved to Spain in 2004. Speaking to talkSPORT in 2023, Owen said: 'When Gerard Houllier phoned me and said, "You’ve won the Ballon d’Or", I’m like "What’s that, gaffer?"

'I didn’t know what the award was. I never did because I never even knew what it was. Back in those days it was never in our press.'

'When I played for Real Madrid, it’s like an MBE, it follows you. Whenever they mention your name it’s Ballon d’Or winner.

'Abroad it is so big, and it’s only just cottoned on here for the last five or ten years.It’s so much bigger in other countries, in foreign countries. It quickly sunk in how big it was."

Sports.title: MICHAEL OWEN: I was wrong about Harry Kane, he is England's best ever striker - and he wasn't even born with a finisher's instinct! Here's how Ballon d'Or winner became the greatest player in the world
Sports.content:
Harry Kane was crowned the best player in the world on Monday night at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. He is the first Englishman for 25 years to win the most prestigious individual award in football, and who better to explain how the Chingford boy rose to the very top than the previous winner from these shores, Michael Owen.

Originally published in June when Kane was breaking records and adding to his enormous 73-goal season at the World Cup, this is what the 2001 Ballon d'Or winner had to say about his 2026 counterpart.

The older I get, the more I realise I was wrong about strikers – and Harry Kane is an example of why I have changed my mind. When I was young, I thought the great goalscorers were simply born that way. I believed finishing was instinct. You either had it or you didn't. I probably thought that about myself.

Now this might sound ridiculous given everything Harry has achieved, but I don't think he was born to become the player he is today. That, as much as anything, is why I love him. That is why, without hesitation, I call him England's greatest-ever striker.

Some players arrive with gifts that simply can't be taught. Electric pace. Extraordinary balance. Harry's greatest gift isn't physical, it's mental. Many years ago, I spent time with him filming a striker's masterclass at Tottenham. Listening to him talk about practice, repetition and the tiny details of finishing, you quickly realised none of this had happened by accident. He has built himself.

Alan Shearer was similar, and Harry has exactly that mentality. Relentless. Obsessive. Totally convinced that if they work harder than everyone else, they will become better than everyone else.

Harry Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or on Monday night, is England's greatest ever striker, but he wasn't born to be the player he is today

Some players arrive with gifts that simply can't be taught. Electric pace. Extraordinary balance. Harry's greatest gift isn't physical, it's mental

I have watched Lionel Messi over the years, Kylian Mbappe now, footballers who make you leap out of your seat because they can do things nobody else can. Harry has never been that player for me – and yet he is the best finisher in world football, no doubt.

Left foot, right foot, headers, volleys, penalties, first-time finishes, strikes from distance. Whatever you ask of him, he delivers. He combines something that very few strikers ever manage – incredible power without sacrificing accuracy. Robbie Fowler was like that. He could absolutely leather a ball and still find the corner. Harry does exactly the same. For me, nobody does it better. With that, his temperament is just off the scale. He is never flustered.

I know he missed a penalty against Croatia in the opening game, but if we've got a penalty in a World Cup final, I don't want anyone else taking it other than Harry Kane. He's got nerves of steel. I love his single-mindedness. I love his longevity. I love that he never gets injured. And I love that his game has got better and better. Even at 32, he won't be thinking he can rest on what he has achieved. This comes back to my point about his elite mindset and the work he puts in.

The longer I've been retired, the more I've analysed the game and coached youngsters, the more I appreciate the craft of goalscoring. It's why I always tell parents not to rush talented young strikers into older age groups. Everyone gets excited when a 10-year-old is scoring for fun and wants to move him up three age groups. That's wrong. Making things harder for a striker and giving them one chance a game is not the way to improve. Let him dominate. Let him have six or seven chances every game. That's how you discover what works for you.

MY TOP 5 ENGLAND STRIKERS 1. Harry Kane. Lethal. Our best ever, and he isn't done yet. 2. Wayne Rooney. I played with Wayne and he was, talent-wise, outrageously gifted. 3. Jimmy Greaves. My Dad told me all about him. 'Pure class' he said, and that's good enough for me. 4. Geoff Hurst. He scored a hat-trick in a World Cup final, and that's the stuff of dreams. 5. Gary Lineker. My idol as a kid. He was Mr Dependable for England in the big games at World Cups.

I knew very early in my career that I preferred dinking it over a goalkeeper rather than going around him. You only discover those preferences by repeating the same situations hundreds and thousands of times. Eventually they become instinct. Drop a ball in front of me now, even at my age, and I'd still know exactly what finish to use because I've rehearsed those situations for decades.

Harry has done the same and that's why his finishing looks effortless. It isn't talent alone. And even though he knows, and we know, what finish he is likely to apply, can defenders and goalkeepers do anything about it? Can they hell!

My one gripe with Harry is the move to Bayern Munich. I said it at the time and I haven't changed my mind. I understand the benefits, and England will hopefully see that in the next few weeks. His all-round game is so mature, the way he comes into midfield and starts attacks as well as finishing them. But in terms of his career, he is better than the Bundesliga.

I have watched the league more now because of Harry, and beyond Bayern it is very ordinary. Week after week he is playing for a team that dominates possession, dominates territory and creates chance after chance. Of course he scores goals.

In terms of his career, he is better than the Bundesliga. I have watched the league more now because of Harry, and beyond Bayern it is very ordinary

For me, Kane has eclipsed Wayne Rooney (right) as the greatest English striker ever

But I still think becoming the Premier League's all-time leading scorer would have been the greater achievement. He would have deserved that. He'd also have had his pick of clubs once his Tottenham contract expired. Manchester United would have moved heaven and earth to sign him. He should probably have gone to Manchester City before Erling Haaland signed.

Winning Bundesliga titles with Bayern was never going to define his greatness because Bayern almost always win them. Had Bayern won the Champions League, perhaps we'd view it differently, but they haven't.

None of this changes how I feel about Harry Kane. He's a wonderful footballer, an outstanding captain and a brilliant human-being. More importantly, he's an example. An example that you don't always have to be born as Lionel Messi, Pele or Diego Maradona.

Sometimes, the greatest players are the ones who simply refuse to stop improving.

Sports.title: The Lionesses big night out! Hannah Hampton stuns on the red carpet as she leads England's Women in supporting Harry Kane at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London
Sports.content:
The Lionesses big night out! Hannah Hampton stuns on the red carpet as she leads England's Women in supporting Harry Kane at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London

Hannah Hampton led the way as the Lionesses dazzled on the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or, with England's women's team throwing their support behind Harry Kane.

Three Lions skipper Kane was crowned the new king of football at London's Palladium on Monday night, with the Bayern Munich star seeing off Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal for the sport's top prize.

Kane was supported by his wife Katie at the biggest night of the year, which saw singer Jorja Smith perform on stage, while Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner was also in attendance.

So too were England's Lionesses, with goalkeeper Hampton stunning in a plunging deep V black gown as she joined her Chelsea team-mates Veerle Buurman, Manaka Matsukubo and Melvine Malar.

Hampton was nominated for women's goalkeeper of the year, but finished fourth behind winner Cata Coll, runner up Ann-Katrin Berger and third-place Ayaka Yamashita.

Meanwhile. fellow England and Chelsea star Lucy Bronze wore a high neck burgundy rouched at the waist gown.

Manchester City's Alex Greenwood, who is engaged to former footballer Jack O'Connell, made the top 30 women's footballers in the world, placing 26th, and wore a black satin corset style dress with a matching clutch bag on the red carpet.

Hannah Hampton stunned at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London on Monday night

The Lionesses star wore a plunging V neck dress as she posed with her Chelsea team-mates

Hampton swapped the pitch for full glamour on the red carpet alongside Manaka Matsukubo

Arsenal star Alessia Russo placed in the top 10, finishing ninth, and donned a graceful high collar neckline full-length black gown.

The night was all about Kane, who became the first England player in 25 years to win football's most prestigious individual prize - following in the footsteps of Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane, who scored 73 goals in all competitions last season, has been widely lauded following his London triumph, with Prince William leading tributes for the England captain.

'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or!' William wrote in a post on Instagram. 'What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Kane and the Prince have worked together on mental health campaigns and in William's role as official patron of the FA, which he moved into in July 2024 after serving as president for 18 years. And he was also by Kane's side at one of his lowest moments when England lost the Euro 2024 final against Spain.

Monday was a joyous moment for the former Leytonstone-born player, who was joined on the red carpet at the Palladium by wife Kate. 'Wow, wow, wow,' he said as he stepped up to accept the trophy.

Alex Greenwood of Manchester City was ranked the 26th best women's player on the planet

Lucy Bronze (left) and Alessia Russo (right) also hit the red carpet for the big awards night

'I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special - it made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me.'

England manager Thomas Tuchel said Kane 'deserved' to be 'formally recognised' for his talent. With 125 caps, Kane is England's record appearance-maker and his 91 goals in those games make him the national team's all-time top goalscorer.

'Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon D'Or!' Tuchel said 'I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

'To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader. I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches.'

Former England players Wayne Rooney, John Terry and Gary Neville were among Kane's well-wishers on Instagram while former Tottenham strike partner Heung-min Son wrote: '@harrykane deserved more then anyone huge congratulations my partner.'

Lionesses goalkeeper Hampton is sharing more of her glamourous life, having previously given fans a glimpse into her thrill-seeking summer, jetting off to the crystal clear waters of Zanzibar

Hampton went swimming with turtles in Zanzibar and also shared a picture of her wearing the jersey of her former club, Villarreal

The Wembley Arch was also lit up in Kane's honour with a message of congratulations.

Indian cricket legend Virat Kohli was quick to say he was 'really happy' for Kane.

'Harry, my friend, you deserve every bit of this award for your resilience, hard work and honesty with which you've carried yourself through all these years playing football at the top,' he wrote.

'Really happy for you. God bless you and your family. They must all be very proud of you, as you would be of your own journey. My best wishes always. Congratulations.'

Ridgeway Rovers, the youth club where Kane started his career, posted: 'One of our own! From everyone at Ridgeway Rovers we are so proud to see one of our own win the Ballon D'or. An incredible achievement from a true champion!'

England's talisman has largely been seen as the most humble winner of the Ballon d'Or after years of posturing for the award by the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Vinicius Jnr. And Kane himself wrote: 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise.'

Sports.title: Why Mikel Arteta is so impressed by Ceadach O'Neill, Arsenal's prolific 18-year-old vying for his first-team debut against Fleetwood - and how he's justifying Gunners' new recruitment drive
Sports.content:
There's a good reason why Arsenal are especially keen for Ceadach O'Neill to be a success story.

The 18-year-old, who is vying to make his competitive debut in the Gunners' Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night, is the first rising star to emerge from their raid on Scottish and Northern Irish academies, which began in 2024 and was influenced by Brexit rules.

If the teenager can either make a name for himself at Arsenal, or one day be sold for a worthwhile fee, the club's recruitment pivot to a UK strategy will have paid dividends.

And Mikel Arteta likes what he sees. So do Northern Ireland, for whom O'Neill made his senior debut in June. And so do the Republic of Ireland, but we'll come back to that.

O'Neill was involved in the Gunners' pre-season preparations, featuring in friendlies against Girona and Real Betis in August, as well as scoring in a behind-closed-doors fixture against MK Dons. He was also on the bench for Arsenal’s 3-0 Champions League victory over Lille earlier this month.

This followed a fruitful 2025-26 campaign where he finished as the club’s top goalscorer in the academy with 18 goals in 30 games across three age-group levels.

The 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill is vying to make his competitive debut in Arsenal's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night

The attacking player (right) has taken part in first-team training alongside Bruno Guimaraes, Declan Rice and Andre Harriman-Annous

The versatile forward typically operates on either wing or as a false nine and with Bukayo Saka sidelined and Christos Tzolis still making his way back from injury, Arsenal are not blessed with options out wide.

O’Neill's profile is an exciting one. He's 5ft 11in with tight dribbling skills and constantly looks to take opponents on and get into goalscoring positions. He's also two-footed, reflected by his ability to play off both flanks.

O’Neill’s long-term position remains a work in progress, though, Arsenal having also played him as an attacking midfielder.

Born in Kilrea, County Londonderry, O’Neill made his senior debut for Linfield in the Irish Premiership aged just 15 against Ballymena United in November 2023. Weeks later he was on trial at Arsenal, and travelled to Brazil with the Under 16s in December 2023 for the Flamengo Adidas Cup – a baptism of fire for a teenager trying to win a contract.

O’Neill impressed in the tournament before officially joining the Gunners in March 2024, later signing his first professional contract with the club in April 2025.

He has flourished ever since and become the embodiment of Arsenal's bid to tap into the best talents across the UK borders, bringing in other young prospectsfrom Scotland and Northern Ireland after Brexit made it harder to sign players from Europe.

Callan Hamill, 17, signed an agreement in the summer of 2024 which allowed him stay at Scottish Premiership side St Johnstone while also splitting his time with Arsenal, before officially joining in July 2025.

The versatile forward typically operates on either wing or as a false nine and with Bukayo Saka sidelined and Christos Tzolis still out, Arsenal are not blessed with options out wide

Evan Mooney, 18, moved from St Mirren in February 2026 for a fee the Scottish club described as ‘substantial... with potential for significant future add-ons and a sizeable sell-on clause’. As for Northern Ireland, Daniel McCarron, 16, joined from Dungannon Swifts in July 2026.

The Gunners’ pivot to the UK stems from Brexit. Before these rules changes, English clubs could recruit eligible 16 to 18-year-olds from EU countries.

After Brexit, that was no longer allowed. So non-EU Northern Ireland and Scotland were seen as fertile areas for Arsenal to explore further. For example, Arsenal are having to wait for Victor Ozhianvuna to turn 18 in January 2027 before he officially joins them from Shamrock Rovers due to him coming from EU member, the Republic of Ireland.

Most academy prospects have enough to worry about when it comes to whether they will make the grade or not. Yet O’Neill has had other matters to navigate too – the tug of war between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland over his international allegiance.

Having represented Northern Ireland at youth level, he earned his first two senior caps in friendlies against Guinea and France in June 2026.

But that summer, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) approached him about switching to the Republic, thrusting the youngster into an international eligibility saga that dominated local headlines, despite him not having made his competitive debut for the Gunners.

O'Neill represented Northern Ireland at youth level and earned his first two senior caps in friendlies against Guinea and France in June 2026. But that summer, the Republic of Ireland approached him about switching allegiances

‘I've been really impressed with him,’ said Mikel Arteta of O'Neill. ‘For his age, he's really mature, really focused, and he has tremendous quality'

Northern Ireland manager Michael O’Neill met the youngster in London in September before selecting him for the UEFA Nations League. O’Neill earned his third and fourth senior caps against Georgia and Ukraine on September 25 and October 2, effectiely ending the prospect of a switch under FIFA’s eligibility rules – you can’t switch allegiances after representing your country four times at senior level.

With the saga behind him, O’Neill’s focus is now on impressing at Arsenal. After the summer Betis defeat, Arteta praised O’Neill when asked about the player by a throng of excited Irish journalists in the mixed zone.

‘I've been really impressed with him,’ said Arteta. ‘For his age, he's really mature, really focused, and he has tremendous quality. He's a player that we have big hopes with and we just need to develop him in the right way.’

The challenge for O'Neill now is to turn that promise into first-team minutes – and, in doing so, become the clearest sign yet that Arsenal’s post-Brexit recruitment strategy is paying off.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Man Utd make decision for Chelsea as players and staff informed
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney may be in Dubai but he continues to fulfil his duties with The Overlap on their Stick to United podcast.

And he pulled no punches at the squad or owners.

He said: "We're not that Manchester United, look a million miles from the previous winning teams, the fundamentals of the game still have to be there. It's at best a mid-table team but if you look at all the mid-table teams, what do they get? They get players working hard, running, tackling and I keep saying it, going back to the basics. These players think they're better than what they are.

"Unfortunately, what happened when Michael Carrick came in at the start is that it's gave them players and the board false hope that they are get enough. He's done well, stuck together, managed somehow to finish third, then the board are thinking, 'we're a top four team' when in reality they're miles away from it. You knew Luke Shaw wasn't going to play all the games, Harry Maguire and Martinez would struggle with Champions League football, so why on earthy aren't you helping the players?

"Then you could say to Harry Maguire, 'we're going to keep you for the Premier League' and bring someone in to play Champions League football to balance the squad out, they haven't done that. You're deluded if they think the front three are good enough.

"They wanted Premier League players, they've brought lads from Wolves, Brentford, who have done well but for signings to take this Manchester United team to the next level, you're living in cuckoo land if you think they're going to achieve that. The squad is absolutely a million miles away.

"The worst thing for Michael Carrick, he's gave the board a bit of hope when in reality, they needed a big overhaul and have done for years. The midfield, spending that amount on them midfielders, is absolutely crazy.

"I feel for Michael, he's being let down, he hasn't been good enough but the players have let him down massively."

Sports.title: Harry Kane parties at 'London's most exclusive nightclub' after Ballon d'Or triumph
Sports.content:
Harry Kane parties at 'London's most exclusive nightclub' after Ballon d'Or triumph

Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday night and partied at an exclusive Soho nightclub with friends and family as the Bayern Munich and England star further etched his name into the record books

View 3 Images Harry Kane carried his Ballon d'Or celebrations late into the night (Image: katekanex/Instagram)

Harry Kane partied long into the night at one of London's swankiest nightclubs after winning the Ballon d'Or in the capital - becoming the first Englishman to win the award in a quarter of a century.

‌



‌



The Bayern Munich ace enjoyed the best season of his career to date. He claimed another Bundesliga title and German Cup, but fell at the semi-final hurdle in the Champions League and with England at the World Cup. He scored 61 times for the Bavarians.

‌



After his historic moment Kane headed to Cirque Le Soir in Soho to party with family and friends. The Bayern star was greeted by a crowd full of champagne sparklers, and raised his shot glass in appreciation.

‌



His wife, Kate, and brother, Charlie, were with him at the Ballon d'Or ceremony and were by his side as the night went on as they partied on. Kane had security alongside him when he eventually left the shindig in the early hours of the morning.

‌



A host of Kane's former Tottenham teammates also showed up to celebrate his historic moment. The likes of Eric Dier, Ben Davies and Matt Doherty could be seen on the dancefloor at the club.

Kane's backing was clear to see with Bayern having a host of their players and staff travel with him to London, supporting his efforts to win the Ballon d'Or. By scooping the award he became the German club's first winner since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge back in 1981.

‌



The England forward said during his acceptance speech: “Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year, [with] some of the incredible players I was up against – some of my team-mates [and] world class players in the room tonight.

View 3 Images Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or since in 25 years

‌



“Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees, an impressive showing of what hard work and determination can achieve, so well done. My Bayern Munich team-mates – I’ve got a few here tonight, without you it wouldn’t have been possible. The way you guys have pushed me, the way we compete, against Upa [Dayot Upamecano] in training every week, it just makes me want to improve.

“Vincent [Kompany], I know he’s at home, still in the hospital so wishing him very well. Hope this has given you a bit of energy and all the staff, the way we train, the way you push us you’re a credit to yourself."

‌



Kane also recognised his former club Tottenham, where he spent his entire career before leaving for Germany. He added: “I wanna say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur as well. I wouldn’t be where I am today without Tottenham for sure. I was here from 11-years-old.

View 3 Images Harry Kane enjoyed his Ballon d'Or win by doing shots (Image: INSTAGRAM)

‌



“All the guidance, all the coaches. You allow me to live my dream so, for sure, without all those moments together, all the ups and downs along the way from that journey has led me to that journey here today so just want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur.

“To all the fans – Bayern Munich fans, England fans, Spurs fans – and all my fans around the world, a lot of you in this room tonight, the support you give me in the stadiums, around the place, wherever it may be, on social media, I appreciate it all."

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold gets Liverpool return transfer approval as 'Real Madrid don't want him'
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold gets Liverpool return transfer approval as 'Real Madrid don't want him'

Trent Alexander-Arnold has been told it's time to return to Anfield as his Real Madrid troubles continue

View 2 Images Trent Alexander-Arnold has fallen to third-choice at Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher would welcome Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool even if he deserves "plenty of stick" for leaving in the first place. The former Reds defender's difficult spell at Real Madrid is continuing under Jose Mourinho, who returned to the Bernabeu in the summer.

‌



‌



Alexander-Arnold has slipped to third-choice in the right-back pecking order and was an unused substitute in Real's El Clasico victory at Barcelona on Sunday. While Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, has impressed in the position recently, the right side of defence has been a problem area for Liverpool since Alexander-Arnold's departure at the end of the title-winning 2024/25 season.

‌



With the 28-year-old seemingly not wanted by Real and Liverpool needing a quality right-back, Carragher thinks it is time for him to reunite with his boyhood club. On whether the Reds should re-sign Alexander-Arnold, Carragher said on The Overlap: "I'd have him back. Give him plenty of stick, [because] I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake.

‌



"But, as I said, if something benefits Liverpool Football Club going forward… And when you think of the problems Liverpool have in terms of the right-back. Ronnie [Ronald Araujo] has been fantastic, but we do have a problem in terms of full-backs passing. We've definitely missed his creativity."

Real Madrid footage of Trent Alexander-Arnold says it all after Liverpool return verdict READ MORE :

On Alexander-Arnold's situation at Real, Carragher added: "At the moment, he's actually third choice right-back for Real Madrid. They're playing a midfield player [Federico Valverde] at right-back, so even in El Clssico, Denzel Dumfries, the first-choice right-back, comes on as a sub. So when you're third choice at a club, they're obviously wanting you. Move on."

There could be an opening for Alexander-Arnold after Valverde picked up an injury in El Clasico and played through the pain barrier before eventually being replaced by Dumfries. Speaking after the game, the Uruguayan said: "At half-time, the manager asked me if I could continue, so I tried.

"My leg was bothering me a little after a tackle I made. For me, it's very easy to keep playing with these kinds of team-mates who encourage you. It's an honour to share the field with them."

‌



Mourinho was full of praise for Valverde after the game, saying: "There's another name I didn't want to leave out, which is Valverde and playing injured for more than 40 minutes.

"He got injured, he wanted to keep going and push himself to his limits. He gave everything while he was on the field."

It seems Mourinho doesn't hold Alexander-Arnold in such high regard, meaning a return to Anfield cannot be ruled out.

Sports.title: Spanish media react to Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or as Lamine Yamal 'penalised'
Sports.content:
Spanish media react to Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or as Lamine Yamal 'penalised'

Spanish media have explained why Lamine Yamal missed out on the Ballon d'Or to Harry Kane

View 2 Images Lamine Yamal had to settle for third (Image: WireImage)

Spanish media took Harry Kane beating Lamine Yamal to the Ballon d'Or well and offered up reasons why the World Cup winner had missed out on the award. Kane is a popular winner after following in the footsteps of England legends Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

‌



‌



Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Yamal provided strong competition but Kane's 73 goals last season, most of which propelled Bayern Munich to a domestic treble in Germany, made him impossible to overlook.

‌



Despite there being some disappointment from Spanish outlets, there were few complaints. AS's headline read "not Yamal or Mbappe" as if some great travesty had been committed.

‌



But the report itself was gushing in its praise for Kane, saying the award "recognises a career like few others, the career of one of the best strikers, and footballers, in history." It added: "There was no second star this summer, but the English will still feel that 'Football's Coming Home.'"

Another article on the same site argued that the award could have been shared in a year "in a year of imperfect candidates" while praising Kane's "impeccable yet understated career, which deserved recognition."

It said: "Given equal merit, the most prestigious competition of the season should have been granted the tiebreaker." On Yamal, it added: "Lamine was penalised by his lack of brilliance in the crucial moments."

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Catalan title MonEsport agreed, saying Yamal's "discreet role" in the World Cup probably cost him the award. It said: "Having won the League and the Super Cup with Barca and the World Cup with the Spanish national team has not been enough. His discreet role in the World Cup is probably what has condemned him."

‌



SPORT said: "Lamine and Mbappe could have won it, but the jury wasn't influenced by the players' campaigns. It should always be that way, because it's an award earned on the pitch. A sunny day at the beach in London until a hurricane snatched away the gold."

View 2 Images Harry Kane has been praised by Spanish media (Image: Getty)

‌



Marca spotted the trend of a Spain player not winning the award in the year the country won the World Cup. It said: "Once again, it leaves Spain without a Ballon d'Or in the year they won the World Cup, as happened in 2010. On that occasion, Messi beat Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez."

MundoDeportivo focused on Kane's brilliance, saying: "His tremendous goalscoring streak, the second best in history only behind Leo Messi 's in 2011-12 (82 goals), made him one of the top candidates for the award, which he ultimately won."

Sports.title: Andy Murray and wife Kim make big announcement after receiving  major honour
Sports.content:
Andy Murray and wife Kim make big announcement after receiving major honour

Tennis legend Andy Murray and his wife Kim have made a major announcement after winning a coveted award

View 2 Images Andy and Kim Murray will feature in a new documentary (Image: John Phillips, Getty Images)

Andy Murray and his wife Kim have revealed they will star in a new Channel 4 docu-series offering fans a behind-the-scenes glimpse at their transformation of Cromlix. The three-time Grand Slam champion purchased the hotel, located near his hometown of Dunblane, back in 2013.

‌



‌



Since retiring from tennis in 2024, Murray and his wife have been working tirelessly on the property. The new three-part series will document a year-long period of transformation at the hotel, including a new wing with two additional restaurants.

‌



The announcement comes after one of their restaurants, Cradle at Cromlix, received recognition in the Michelin Guide. Titled Our Scottish Hotel, the docu-series arrives on Channel 4 in December.

‌



Andy and Kim Murray open doors of lavish five-star hotel for new Channel 4 series READ MORE :

Andy Murray's return to tennis court confirmed as Rafael Nadal calls out Scot READ MORE :

It will give viewers exclusive behind-the-scenes access as the pair tackle renovations described as "the biggest financial gamble" Murray and Kim have undertaken since purchasing the hotel over a decade ago.

Speaking about the new series, Kim said: "The last couple of years have been really full of change at Cromlix with a huge building project and a totally new direction for fine dining and wellness, and I was really keen to document that as there were so many personal stories and interesting discoveries along the way.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Andy and I haven't worked on anything together before, so that was a fascinating process - and a learning curve! I've loved shaping this building and estate into what's now become a really thriving and much-loved Scottish business. I hope people enjoy watching the show and meeting the team behind the hotel."

Our Scottish Hotel follows the staff at Cromlix as they work hard to keep up their high standards for guests while renovation work takes place throughout the estate. The documentary also follows Murray and Kim's return after the hotel's five-month shutdown, to find out whether their gamble has been worthwhile.

‌



Emily Shields, the Commissioning Editor for Channel 4, said: "Cromlix is a fascinating world to step inside, and this series offers a rare glimpse behind the scenes of a business where no detail is overlooked.

"Kim and Andy are embarking on an ambitious transformation, but at its heart this is a story about people: the team whose hard work brings Cromlix to life, and the shared desire to create something truly special.

‌



View 2 Images Andy and Kim Murray will feature in the new Channel 4 documentary series, Our Scottish Hotel (Image: Verena Wood)

"We're delighted to be bringing viewers this warm, intimate and revealing look at life behind the doors of one of Scotland's most distinctive hotels."

‌



The series consists of three one-hour episodes, produced by Rogan Scotland for Channel 4. James Rogan, co-CEO of Rogan Scotland, said: "It's been such a privilege for Rogan Scotland to be invited into Cromlix at this pivotal time.

"What fascinated us was not simply the scale of the transformation, but how personal every decision became.

Article continues below

"From the food on the plate and the David Shrigley works on the walls to the search for water beneath the estate, the series captures Kim and Andy's contrasting instincts, ambitions and sense of humour.

"Cromlix is also the story of an extraordinary team, responding to each new challenge with ingenuity, pride and a determination to make every guest feel that nothing unusual is happening at all."

Sports.title: Paul Scholes says Man Utd manager candidate is 'miles ahead' despite 'massive warning'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes says Man Utd manager candidate is 'miles ahead' despite 'massive warning'

Manchester United chiefs are considering whether to replace Michael Carrick as manager following a dreadful start to the season and Paul Scholes thinks one candidate stands out

View 3 Images Paul Scholes believes Antonio Conte would be the best available manager for Manchester United (Image: The Good, The Bad & The Football)

Paul Scholes believes that Antonio Conte is "miles ahead" of the other candidates Manchester United are considering to replace Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



Carrick survived crisis talks with the United hierarchy at the club's Carrington training ground on Monday. He is continuing to prepare for United's Premier League game against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, but his position is far from secure.

‌



United have identified Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Conte as possible replacements, with all three managers currently available. There is reportedly some disagreement behind the scenes, with director of football Jason Wilcox preferring Howe, while director of recruitment Christopher Vivell favours Nagelsmann.

‌



Ex-Chelsea and Tottenham boss Conte is interested in the position, but would demand his own backroom staff and control over transfers. The Italian also has a fearsome reputation - something that Scholes believes would be worth it.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick future LIVE: Man Utd announcement imminent with two lead candidates lined up READ MORE :

Eddie Howe's first Man Utd demand clear after job offer collapsed at 11th hour READ MORE :

Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, the United legend said: "You’d have to pick a manager who you think will get us back to being a competitive team for the Premier League. Out of them three, Antonio Conte’s the man, but he comes with a big f***ing massive warning.

‌



"He’s made noises that he wants to come and I’m pretty sure the club would have spoke to all three of them. I can’t understand why he’d want this job because I don’t think the team’s good enough for him, personally."

United also have admiration for Aston Villa boss Unai Emery and Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler, but there is little chance they could tempt them to leave their clubs to take over United, who sit 16th in the Premier League.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with a move to Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Is the answer staring us right in the face in Unai Emery?" Scholes added. "He’s won the Europa League with Aston Villa, do you know what an achievement that is? He gets a new team every single year because they have to sell their best players. and he keeps producing, keeps producing.

"Is everyone put off by his Arsenal and PSG days? Probably, because it’s a big club. But it might be staring us in the face. He’d have to take United over Villa, I think he would.

‌



"I think Conte’s the best one around. When I’m talking best in class and you talk them four, I think Antonio Conte’s miles ahead of all of them. You think Juventus, he went to Napoli and goes and wins the league with them."

View 3 Images Michael Carrick could be sacked soon (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Former United winger Ashley Young disagrees with Scholes, having played under Conte. Speaking on The Overlap, Young said: "I’ve worked underneath him at Inter. He’s crazy by the way, crazy. A lot of talk has been about Man United’s running stats. If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster I think."

He added: "There was a lot that he’d done, the training sessions were a lot of 11 vs 11, at times a little bit boring. Meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking: If we lost a game, we could go in for the meeting and he’d stop literally everything. And you could be in there for three or four hours. It was like ‘come on now, let’s be serious’.

Article continues below

"I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places because it’s not just the players he tries to test mentally, but the board as well, and the owners. I think that people get annoyed with him and think ‘it’s time for you to go’."

Sports.title: Ex-Man City star Samir Nasri aims sly dig at Harry Kane after his historic Ballon d'Or win
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City star Samir Nasri aims sly dig at Harry Kane after his historic Ballon d'Or win

Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday night, but the Bayern Munich star's achievement wasn't welcomed by everyone

View 2 Images Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday night (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Harry Kane did not deserve to be crowned as the best player in the world because he doesn't make the difference in big games, according to Samir Nasri.

‌



‌



Kane won the Ballon d'Or on Monday night at an awards ceremony in London, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to claim the award. The Bayern Munich and England star came out ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal in the voting.

‌



Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last season, leading Bayern to a domestic double and the semi-finals of the Champions League, as well as spearheading England’s run to the World Cup semis.

‌



His moment on stage was widely celebrated as deserved recognition for an extraordinary achievement. But former Manchester City and France midfielder Nasri had a very different reaction.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Harry Kane, Ballon d'Or... OK, the statistics made the difference," he said on Canal+. "He's a fantastic player with so many qualities. But he's never been the player who carried his team somewhere or made his team win in the very big matches. There's often a slight weakness. But he's an extraordinary player."

‌



Asked if he was not excited by Kane's win, Nasri replied: "No, that's an understatement!"

Kane's tally of 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern last season is the most by a player in a single campaign in the German club's history. Including his tally with England, he managed 73 goals and eight assists in 65 matches.

‌



Despite his individual brilliance, Bayern were beaten by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-finals, while England fell at the same stage at the World Cup against Argentina.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Kane beat Kylian Mbappe to the Ballon d'Or (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

France legend Thierry Henry was one of the presenters at the ceremony and had a classy message for Kane after he beat Mbappe to the prize.

‌



“I would always back my fellow Frenchmen but I have to say something about Harry Kane," he said. "I have seen him since the beginning. He had to suffer really hard to achieve what he has achieved. A worthy winner, well done.”

That suffering was touched upon by Kane himself. "Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," he told DAZN.

‌



"I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now.

"I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination. I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better."

Sports.title: Donald Trump backed to join Tyson Fury for Anthony Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Donald Trump backed to join Tyson Fury for Anthony Joshua fight

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will end their decade-long feud later this year, and US President Donald Trump has been offered the chance to be a part of history

View Image Tyson Fury has asked US President Donald Trump to walk him to the ring for his fight with Anthony Joshua

Carl Froch believes US President Donald Trump walking Tyson Fury to the ring for his fight with Anthony Joshua would only add to the monumental showcase.

‌



‌



Fury and Joshua will trade leather in the early hours of December 12 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. With Netflix set to broadcast the all-British bout, the fight could start as late as 2am in a bid to satisfy US audiences. For a while, it looked as if the fight would land at Madison Square Garden in New York.

‌



But Joshua refused and managed to bring the fight to the UK shores. Prior to the official announcement, Fury flew to Washington DC and managed to bump into Trump during his travels. The president had used his position to grant the 'Gypsy King' a visa after he had previously been banned from the country.

‌



And Fury has since asked Trump to be a part of his ring walk later this year. "I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy and we'll see if he's available," he said. "But it's probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States."

Speaking to BetVictor Online Casino, the boxing legend said: "I think it’s a massive move if Donald Trump walks Tyson Fury out. But the chances of it happening are f***ing slim to none.

"He’s such a busy man with a massive schedule. I know he loves UFC and he’s often seen at UFC events with Dana White, but that’s America. The cost, security-wise, would be massive. If he does come, it’ll be last minute and he’ll probably turn up without anybody knowing.
