Sports.title: Red Bull explains why Verstappen and Hadjar's 'silly' problems won't all be fixed in 2026
Sports.content:
Although Max Verstappen once again secured a podium finish, something that seemed to be the maximum achievable for much of this Formula 1 season, there was certainly little satisfaction in the Red Bull hospitality on Sunday evening. Several team members acknowledged in the paddock that Kimi Antonelli's race pace was impossible to match, although both Red Bull drivers were frustrated that the team had failed to extract the full potential from its package in Austin.

This was partly due to problems specific to this race, such as strategic decisions Verstappen was unhappy with – particularly the insistence on sticking with the softer compounds while the harder ones seemed to work better – and inconsistent behaviour from the power unit. But the difficult Sunday afternoon at the Circuit of the Americas was also caused by two problems that have repeatedly cropped up this year: poor starts and technical issues with the team radio.

All of this led to frustration for Isack Hadjar, who summed it up as follows in the media pen:“At the moment, it's the little things we can’t do.

"I have poor radio, I don't even know what's happening. And whenever I drop the clutch, it's going into a nightmare. If we fix these two issues, we might already be on the podium. It seems like we can do the hardest things, but we can’t do the silly things.”

By 'the hardest things', he was naturally referring to the fact that Red Bull has managed to overturn its enormous gap to the front of the field. In Australia, China and Japan, the average deficit in race pace was 1.2 seconds per lap, and making up that kind of ground over the course of a season is certainly no small feat.

At the same time, tackling the start problem and getting the radio issues under control has proved more complicated than expected. When Autosport put those observations to Laurent Mekies, referring to Hadjar's comments, the team principal clarified that the two aspects needed to be treated separately. Yes, the radio problem is unacceptable for a top team and must be resolved before the end of this year, but the start issue is more complex and will remain an obstacle until 2027.

“I guess there are two different ways to answer your question," said Mekies. “I think there is some truth in what Isack is saying, meaning that we are all frustrated to struggle with radio issues for the second race in a row. It's making everyone's lives very difficult, so it is true that it's something that we would like to fix quite quickly, because it's an item that should be working without using too much of our energy.

Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images

“So he's right on that one. The start is a slightly more complex issue to solve.”

As for the radio problems, both drivers were affected in Austin, which was the first time this year for Hadjar. Verstappen has been troubled by them more frequently. In Singapore, his race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase could not hear him, forcing ‘GP’ to resort to coded communication. In Austin, Verstappen could not hear stand-in race engineer Tom Hart – who, according to Mekies, did a great job – which once again made communication difficult.

Red Bull acknowledges that it does not yet fully understand these radio problems, although Mekies believes they should not be overly complex to resolve.

“If we were understanding it, we would have solved it," said the Frenchman. "We don't fully understand why we are being hit by these issues. I have to admit that the competition is doing a better job than us because we can hear everyone's radio and we have been struggling more than what we would have liked to.”

Starts can improve, but hardware changes needed for a proper solution

The start problem is considerably more complex. After the race in Austin, Hadjar said that Red Bull needs to redesign the clutch, arguing that he follows all the procedures correctly but that the clutch is still too sensitive.

Mekies clarified, however, that it is not as simple as that and that the start problem is actually linked to a wide range of different factors.

“The start is a slightly more complex issue to solve, meaning that the start performance is going across pretty much all departments of the company, probably except the aerodynamic department," he said.

Race start Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

“It's engine, it's gearbox, it's clutch, it's many things. And we certainly have seen from the beginning of the season that we are not the benchmark in terms of launch performance.”

A proper solution will therefore require several hardware changes for the 2027 F1 season, involving the interaction between the clutch, gearbox, power unit and turbo.

That said, Red Bull acknowledges that it should be possible to perform somewhat better with its current software and hardware than it is doing at present, and it is also looking at sister team Racing Bulls in that regard. On average, Racing Bulls has made better starts, although Verstappen has said that everything is identical and that the difference can only be made with the procedures.

Mekies acknowledged that there should still be more performance to unlock in that area, although he stressed that Red Bull has already made significant progress compared with Melbourne.

“As much as we have reduced the gap, because you may remember how bad our starts were at the beginning of the year, we are still not the benchmark,” Mekies said.

“And yes, the fact that the car improved a lot in the meantime improved and is fighting closer to the front, makes that deficit even more painful now, because the competition around us is very strong.

“So to your point, on one side I'm confident that we will continue to reduce the gap to the competition from now to the end of the year, because every race we learn. Every race we come up with small ways to close the gap.”

But a genuine, long-term solution will have to wait until next year.

“On the other side, I equally know that we will not be the benchmark before the end of the season," he concluded. "That will require some significant design and hardware changes, and this is something that we will only see next year.”

Sports.title: Why being "very adaptive" gave Norris the edge over Piastri at US GP
Sports.content:
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella has explained the reasoning behind asking Oscar Piastri to wave Lando Norris past in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix.

Piastri and Norris locked out the fourth row of the grid at the Circuit of The Americas, having failed to challenge the Mercedes, Red Bulls and Ferraris in Q3.

However, over the first seven laps of the race, Piastri lost one second per lap to race leader Kimi Antonelli – precisely 0.997s on average, discounting lap one – and couldn’t even keep up with a struggling George Russell, who was pulling away by two tenths a lap.

Norris complained on the radio he was “being held up” by his team-mate; McLaren asked the Australian to let his team-mate through, which he duly did in Turn 1 on lap eight. Norris went on to pull away by four seconds in seven laps.

“We had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar,” Stella detailed. “This is a track in which Lando excels and is one of the tracks in which Oscar instead struggles a little bit more.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Andrea Stella, McLaren Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

“This year, in particular for Oscar, is tricky because Oscar's superpower is to build; once he creates references, he can really effectively build lap after lap. But here every lap is different, so these are the conditions that challenge Oscar and actually are the conditions where Lando uses his own superpower, which is being very adaptive to the conditions, especially as the car slides.

“So, given this context, we discussed before the race that if Lando was behind Oscar, and Oscar could not keep up with the cars ahead, then we could have given Lando a chance or an opportunity to see if we could attack the cars ahead – and that's what we did.”

This meant a lot to McLaren after its drivers collided in the Singapore sprint race. “It's a way of demonstrating that as a team and together with the drivers, we care about the interests of the team, which was always the conversation that we have had,” Stella added.

“And especially after Singapore, we reinforced how much it's important that we all together help McLaren go back to the position that we want to have, which is Oscar and Lando, first row in qualifying, fighting for the win, and then we manage the internal competition. But up to then, all together, we need to sustain the trajectory of McLaren back to the front.”

How Norris fought for the podium

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

McLaren picked a one-stop strategy in a bid to challenge the other top teams on Sunday, with Ferrari duo Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, plus Max Verstappen on two stops. Norris consequently held second place until lap 46, before succumbing to those three drivers – but he still managed to undercut Isack Hadjar and Russell on his way to fifth place, with Piastri likewise beating the Silver Arrow to seventh.

“We tried to deploy the hard tyres, which in practice seemed to be competitive, and we knew that the others were going for the softer side of the tyre allocation,” Stella explained. “Once we saw the first stint and the fact that they were struggling a bit, we got some encouragement that using the hard tyres could have been a good way of catching up.

“So, we were actually catching up compared to the two Ferraris and Verstappen in the second stint. At some stage, we just decided to go for the one-stop, because if we go for a two, we are always going to stay behind. The one-stop gives you the possibility to take advantage of a safety car, which didn't come. We are still waiting for a compensation for what happened in Madrid – it will come,” the Italian added, referring to Norris losing a potential win to an untimely VSC period at Madring.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

“We also attempted to see what's left in the hard tyres, but honestly, we knew that it was very, very unlikely that we could have kept Verstappen and in particular Leclerc behind. With Hamilton, we thought it was more dependent on the final tail of the hard tyres. Nobody could have known, but worthwhile giving it a go.

“We are happy with the strategy execution; we are happy with the fact that we kind of understood which tyres needed to be used today; happy with the fact that the car seems to have improved thanks to the upgrades. But we need to improve our qualifying performance, and we also need to keep improving the car if we want to consistently compete for podiums, but above all for victories.”

McLaren is on a four-round podiumless streak, its worst spell of form by that metric since the last two rounds of the 2023 season and the first two of its title-winning 2024 campaign.

Sports.title: The two recurring issues that hampered Verstappen and Red Bull again at the US GP
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen secured his 10th podium of the 2026 Formula 1 season in Austin, his sixth in succession since his crash at Zandvoort. It is an impressive statistic, although it did little to satisfy him at the Circuit of the Americas.

On Saturday, the pace appeared to be there to take pole position – at least judging by Verstappen's impressive Q2 lap – but he inexplicably lost grip in Q3. Based on the practice sessions, his race pace still appeared good enough to challenge for the win, but according to Verstappen, too many small things went wrong during the race.

"It was pretty frustrating, to be honest, just not a really good race for us," Verstappen said in the post-race press conference.

Why Red Bull's recent strength turned into a weakness in Austin

That frustration stems partly from problems that have been troubling Red Bull for some time and partly from decisions specific to this race that ultimately backfired.

"In hindsight, of course, it’s very easy to say, but for whatever reason, the softer compounds were not really working that well today. Then also, I think the way that we used our tyres was wrong, the order of the stints," the Dutchman added.

"I think at one point, it was quite clear that the people on the harder compounds were finding a lot of grip, so I guess we didn't really react to that. We were probably sticking a bit too much to our belief from the last two races, where the softer compounds were the fastest. But clearly here, that didn't work."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

In recent race weekends, that had been one of the areas where Red Bull made the difference. The RB22 had been particularly good at managing the softer tyres and keeping them alive in the right operating window, but in Austin the opposite proved to be the case, as team principal Laurent Mekies also admitted after the race.

Verstappen also complained over the team radio about issues related to the power unit, to which the team responded with some engine braking suggestions.

"Besides the strategy, we had too many issues with the power unit, where it was just very inconsistent behaviour around the corners. Every lap and every corner, the behaviour was different," Verstappen said.

"You can't build up a rhythm, you can't build any kind of consistency in the car. And then I had a slow pit stop as well, so yeah, too many things today that just didn't go well."

Two recurring problems continue to trouble Red Bull

While the strategy and power unit problems were specific to this race, there are two other factors Red Bull has been struggling with throughout the year: radio communication and poor starts. Regarding the latter, Verstappen explained that his start in Austin was not so much bad as simply in line with Red Bull's average this year – which has been consistently below par.

"I didn't lose a position, so it wasn't that bad. It's normal. My start was normal, just consistently sh**," Verstappen said, stopping short of finishing the final word to avoid swearing during the FIA press conference.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Radio communication has also become a recurring problem. In Singapore, his regular race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase could not hear Verstappen, forcing them to switch to coded communication. Mekies subsequently said Red Bull was taking the problem very seriously and wanted to come up with a "strong solution", but that solution had evidently not yet materialised in Austin.

At the extremely bumpy Circuit of the Americas, both Hadjar and Verstappen experienced communication problems with the team. In Verstappen's case, he could not hear Tom Hart, who was standing in as his race engineer this weekend to begin building their working relationship for the future.

"It's not the second time. It's already, I don't know how many times this year. Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language! It's probably cheaper as well," Verstappen joked.

"But yeah, it’s a disaster. It's really frustrating, to be honest."

Taken together, all these setbacks meant Red Bull was unable to extract the full potential of the RB22 in Texas. Team members acknowledge that Kimi Antonelli also had the upper hand in terms of outright pace, although Verstappen's frustration mainly stems from the fact that Red Bull did not even reach the level it had been aiming for.

Sports.title: Alonso criticises quality of F1 backmarkers after Albon clash at United States GP
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso let rip at Williams' Alex Albon after contact between their cars on the opening lap of the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix. It cost the Aston Martin driver four places in Austin and left him with floor damage, which compromised the AMR26 for the rest of the race.

The two-time world champion lost one position at the start from 12th on the grid as Esteban Ocon surged from 15th to 11th. Albon picked up three places with a clean launch to run 14th and challenged Alonso for position all the way through the Esses on the opening lap.

At Turn 11, Alonso made a bid to pass the squabbling Haas cars on the inside line into the left-hander, but Albon had also launched on a similar trajectory. The Williams was already committed as the gap narrowed, and Albon's front-right wheel crunched into Alonso's left-hand bargeboard and floor edge.

Alonso was pushed onto the outside kerb, losing a further four places. The damage to the Aston Martin's floor was clearly visible from Albon's on-board camera. Alonso recovered to 12th place at the chequered flag, but was clearly disgruntled when he spoke to the media.

"That was the biggest damage," he said. "I think we lost half a second or more [per lap]. The car is destroyed, I saw it in parc ferme. Half of the floor is not there. I don't know how we kept on going and how we were semi-competitive.

"I imagine if the car was in one piece, probably today the points were a strong possibility because we were running P12 with half a car. I lost even further pieces of the floor. I couldn't turn. So we stopped. I thought about retiring the car. I was ready to switch it off.

Alexander Albon, Williams, Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

"But then they put a new front wing and I went out again. Obviously the car was turning ok to the right and not ok to the left for the last 15 laps of the race. But we wanted to finish and collect a little bit more data.

"When you start at the back, there is this risk always. I think the quality of the drivers in the low third of the grid is very low. As we saw today with Alex. So I think we need to improve the car and start a little bit higher up."

The contact wasn't deemed worthy of investigation by the stewards, being a typical consequence of three cars fighting for the same patch of real estate at that corner.

"It felt like there was a car on the right side of Fernando," explained Albon. "And he gave Fernando enough space as if he thought there was only one car on his inside. But then I was on the inside of Fernando.

"So then I think it pinched and I tried to get out of the way and get on the kerb. But I didn't make good of it. So I imagine he got damage. I know I got damaged as we were driving around with a broken wing for the race."

Sports.title: Russell scrambling for answers after "not being quick enough" at US GP
Sports.content:
George Russell is desperately searching for answers after “not being quick enough” at the United States Grand Prix as team-mate Kimi Antonelli closes in on the Formula 1 world title.

Antonelli dominated Sunday’s race at Austin from pole, whereas Russell started sixth but finished eighth, having received a five-second penalty for gaining an advantage by running off-track on the opening lap.

It came on lap one when the Briton was defending from Oscar Piastri heading into Turn 12, where he left the track and rejoined ahead of the McLaren to keep his position.

But that penalty had little impact on his finishing position anyway since, without it, he’d have theoretically finished seventh instead of the Australian with a point gain of just two.

So when asked by Sky Sports what he’s particularly struggling with, Russell replied: “Just not being quick enough, to be honest.

“I need to try and understand why it is. It’s strange when you’re so far off, so hopefully there’s some answers somewhere. But, anyway, I don’t have one.”

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Russell’s result came despite a recently upgraded W17, which he claims has a ‘narrow set-up window’ as evidenced by his up-and-down form since it was introduced in Malaysia.

There, Antonelli finished runner-up to the dominant Max Verstappen while Russell was set to finish third until a late power unit failure caused him to retire.

In Singapore, Verstappen won again with Antonelli third, while Russell took a lowly ninth meaning it is now three grands prix without a podium for the Briton amid a horrid 2026.

Speaking later with the written media in Austin, Russell said: “The pace wasn't good on the first stint.

“But when I came out of the pits on the hard [tyres], I probably did six laps where I was lapping the same pace as Kimi. But then I caught up with Oscar and I just couldn't overtake.

“Six good laps, 50 bad laps. I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint. The penalty was a bit ridiculous as well, but that was at least some of my worries after such a bad weekend.”

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Pierluigi Orsi, Mercedes Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

The results means that Antonelli is likely to become champion in Mexico next weekend, holding a 123-point advantage over Russell with 125 left available ahead of the final five rounds.

Russell is then only one-point above third-placed Lewis Hamilton and sixth ahead of Verstappen in fourth, while Mercedes is set to win the constructors’ title as it’s 133 points in front of Ferrari.

“For me, as long as we win the constructors’ [championship], that's the main thing,” said Russell. “For the team, obviously I'd like to finish best of the rest but P2, P3, P5 is not champion so it doesn't mean anything.”

Sports.title: The maths behind Antonelli becoming F1 world champion at Mexico GP
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has taken another giant step towards becoming Formula 1 world champion by dominating the United States Grand Prix from pole on Sunday.

The Mercedes driver consequently took his ninth victory of the 2026 season and it leaves him with one hand on the championship trophy - though it has been for a while.

So, when will he do it and become F1’s youngest ever world champion?

How many drivers can still win the F1 2026 title?

There were six mathematical contenders heading into Austin - Antonelli, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris - as 139 points separated the drivers with 150 left available pre-Texas.

Three of those - Verstappen, Leclerc and Norris - have now dropped out of contention though, due to them finishing third, second and fifth respectively. All solid results, but it just shows how unlikely world championship glory was for them as it meant their hopes had ended.

For Antonelli to become champion at Circuit of the Americas, he needed to win with Russell finishing ninth or below and Hamilton taking fifth. But as his Mercedes team-mate took eighth and the Ferrari driver, who he succeeded at the Silver Arrows, finished fourth, the fight goes on to next weekend.

How Antonelli becomes world champion at Mexico GP

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

There are now 125 points left available in the 2026 campaign with five rounds remaining - Mexico, Sao Paulo, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - provided the Middle Eastern grands prix go ahead amid the conflict.

Russell is now 123 points behind Antonelli and Hamilton is 124, so the 20-year-old Italian is all-but certain to take the crown at Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. After that race there will be 100 points left on the table, but the other two must be behind Antonelli by 99 or fewer, due to the championship leader having the most wins this season by a comfortable margin - so he would win it on countback.

This means both must outscore Antonelli by 24 and 25 points respectively. So for Russell, that entails him winning and his team-mate finishing no higher than 10th, while for Hamilton, he must also take victory but Antonelli not take any points.

Sports.title: F1 United States GP: Antonelli dominates from pole - but forced to wait for title
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has taken another step towards an inevitable Formula 1 title with a sovereign United States Grand Prix win, defeating Charles Leclerc at Austin's Circuit of the Americas.

From pole, the Mercedes driver warded off a challenge from the Ferrari man and Max Verstappen as he stuck to the Silver Arrows’ masterplan and executed a clean one-stop race.

Antonelli's ninth grand prix win of 2026 wasn't quite enough to secure the title just yet, but the 20-year-old Italian now looks set to become F1's youngest ever world champion at next weekend's Mexico Grand Prix.

Antonelli held onto his lead at the start of the 56-lap race as second-placed Verstappen suffered a poor getaway. That left the Red Bull driver vulnerable to Leclerc, who had picked off Isack Hadjar and then swept past Verstappen with a high commitment move through the Esses.

Lewis Hamilton, starting on used softs, also worked his way past Hadjar. Behind him, George Russell was handed a five-second time penalty for going off the track on lap one while defending his position. As the top of the order settled down, Oscar Piastri was told to let quicker Lando Norris past on lap eight for seventh.

At the front, Antonelli controlled a narrow but sovereign three-second lead on Verstappen. That prompted Red Bull to roll the dice and call the Dutchman in on lap 14 for a second set of soft tyres, putting him on a two-stop race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Mercedes didn't take the bait and kept Antonelli out as it looked determined to stay on a one-stop strategy. Struggling for grip on used softs, Hamilton came in for mediums next, as did his team-mate Leclerc and the two McLarens.

That left a temporary top three of Antonelli, Hadjar and Russell until all came in for what was supposed to be their only pitstop, with Antonelli eschewing the soft tyres entirely to go from mediums to hards on lap 25.

Verstappen didn't enjoy his new-found lead all that long as he started struggling with engine braking issues, calling his Red Bull "undriveable". It forced him into the pits on lap 32 for a second stop for mediums, dropping down to fifth, 18 seconds behind new leader Antonelli.

On the slower hard tyres Antonelli faced a challenge from Leclerc, but both he and Ferrari team-mate Hamilton were yet to stop again as Verstappen remained Antonelli's real challenger. The two Ferraris both moved to hard tyres in the final third, which droppèd them behind Verstappen.

To get to Antonelli, though, Verstappen first had to clear second-placed Norris, who also banked on a one-stop strategy. Verstappen's battle with Norris allowed Leclerc to exploit his fresher tyres and close the gap, with the three cars converging with 10 laps to go.

At the start of lap 47, Verstappen made a late lunge on Norris to the inside of COTA's steep Turn 1 hairpin, snatching second away before Leclerc also found a way through. On much fresher tyres, Leclerc then picked off Verstappen on the back straight on lap 49 to take second.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alex Slitz / Getty Images

Antonelli's win never came under real threat as he led Leclerc by 13 seconds, with Verstappen another four seconds behind in third.

Norris also fell into the clutches of Hamilton as the latter secured fourth from the reigning world champion on lap 51, which also meant the seven-time world champion remained in mathematical title contention until next week.

Hadjar finished sixth ahead of Piastri, who held off Russell for a distant seventh. With Russell needing to avoid finishing ninth or lower to prolong his theoretical title chances, he only just managed to do so after a frustrating weekend.

Liam Lawson continued Racing Bulls' canter to fifth in the constructors' championship by finishing ninth, with the final point going to Alpine's Pierre Gasly. Antonelli is now all but certain to wrap up the championship in Mexico, needing just two points to become the youngest ever title winner aged 20.

Haas driver Oliver Bearman was one of three retirements, the eventual result of first-lap damage from contact with Gasly, which the Briton was handed a 10-second penalty for and provoked a brief VSC period.

Alpine's Franco Colapinto also disappeared from the race, while Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas retired late on with engine trouble, causing the second brief virtual safety car period of the race.

Sports.title: Inside COTA's Turn 1 clubhouse and its plans to build a second track
Sports.content:
For spectators and TV viewers tuning into coverage of Formula 1's United States Grand Prix, it's been hard to miss. Turn 1 of the Circuit of the Americas has a distinctly different look to it this year with the addition of a mammoth multi-storey clubhouse.

Connected to the main paddock area via a cable car that crosses the track, this weekend the new hospitality structure serves as an extension of F1's swanky Paddock Club. From 2 January it becomes a year-round members-only club, dubbed 'The Circuit', as the venue turns private at the start of next year.

"It isn’t an annual membership in the traditional sense," said Parris Mullins, COTA’s Senior Vice President of Motorsports. "It’s much more like a country club. There are annual dues to maintain the facilities and cover staffing, but the initiation fee is a one-time payment that essentially provides a lifetime membership.

"We’ve had more than 50 additional submissions in the past 24 hours, and that was before this race weekend. Before this race weekend, around 600 people had reached out. We’ve had one-to-one conversations with approximately 140 of them, and many have started putting down deposits and signing contracts.

"There will never be more than 300 members. We’re limiting North American membership to 250. The remaining 50 places will be a mix of international and corporate memberships."

A view from COTA's new Turn 1 clubhouse. Photo by: Filip Cleeren

The new facility isn't just COTA president Bobby Epstein's brainchild alone, though. It fits a calendar-wide push by F1 management for races to significantly ramp up their hospitality offerings.

"A lot of our contract renewal was dependent on this as well," Mullins added. "We needed to improve both the members’ experience and the experience for the Paddock Club guests. F1 has made a big commitment to it. The sport has grown, and certain markets demand these kinds of amenities. They have to keep improving what they offer."

Why COTA is building a second circuit

COTA's decision to go private has some side effects, with the venue now no longer available for track days or for regional driving clubs. But there's a solution on the horizon. On an empty plot of land to the north of the existing F1 track, COTA has crafted advanced plans to build a second, shorter circuit designed for both cars and motorcycles.

"A second track will be built, primarily because we recognise that we’re displacing a number of people and organisations that have been partners of ours since the circuit opened," Mullins explained.

"Growing motorsport, particularly in the local area, is very important to us. We’re not going to build another FIA Grade 1 facility because there’s no need for one. Instead, we want to build something that suits the local motorsport community, allows them to continue using a circuit and gives them access at a much lower price point.

"There’s obviously prestige associated with COTA. I know people love being able to say they’ve driven their car on the grand prix circuit, and we’re sorry that this won’t always be possible unless they’re members. But we want to give people somewhere they can drive, enjoy motorsport and continue participating at a grassroots level."

While details remain sparse, the circuit's undisclosed layout has already been defined. COTA is also open to the new circuit, built to FIA Grade 3 standards suitable for touring cars, sportscars and entry-level single-seaters, hosting smaller motorsports series. But by not having to cater to F1 cars, Mullins feels there is an opportunity to come up with a track more suited to high-performance sports cars and the people who drive them.

"We want to create something fun with a different personality from the grand prix circuit," he said. "COTA was built around the requirements of a single major race weekend. I’d like it to have corners we don’t have here. We don’t have a banked corner, for example, so I think the new circuit should have one. It should also have an iconic chicane. We want features that people can enjoy in the kinds of cars they bring to the track. The layout should suit them much better."

Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

When asked about the timelines for the secondary track, Mullins didn't want to commit to a firm date, but there is a sense of urgency not to leave local driving and car clubs without a track for too long.

"We still need to finalise everything and work through the process with the city," he said. "We’re far enough along that we’re comfortable saying we want to get it done sooner rather than later. We don’t want the local motorsport community to go without a facility for too long, but we also need to get the project right."

COTA still sees itself as the "people's race" with its enormous spectator numbers of up to 440,000 across the F1 weekend, and by gradually turning the entire venue into one giant theme park the organisers want to lean into F1's changed demographic in the post-Netflix era. Some of that can be taken quite literally, with the rollercoaster rides of the new COTALAND amusement running alongside the circuit's third sector. But the grand prix also continues its tradition of big-name end-of-day concerts, roping in Austin's popular college sports and food culture.

Earning a new F1 deal to 2034 gives COTA the long-term stability to write off those investments, and turn them into ways to make the circuit a year-round source of revenue alongside hosting the likes of F1, MotoGP, WEC and - from 2027 - Formula E. COTALAND fits into that picture, and so does the exclusive members club and the secondary track.

But COTA hasn't forgotten that its core business is to keep the hordes of F1 fans entertained over a weekend. "Formula 1 provides the on-track action. Our job is to complement that between sessions," Mullins said. "The concerts were the first step. What Bobby did with those was really groundbreaking.

"At the end of the day, this is sport, but it’s also entertainment. We want to entertain people."

Sports.title: Featured Comment: F1’s flawed rules don’t lessen Antonelli’s achievement | Briefs
Sports.content:
With Andrea Kimi Antonelli poised to win the world championship this weekend, has Formula 1’s ruined season diminished his inevitable triumph? Rick disagrees:

I agree with the disappointing season but I don’t think it takes away from soon to be Antonelli’s championship season. In my almost 50 years of watching F1 there have been many unusual situations and this season will just be added to that list.

I find the biggest problem is that the current ownership knows that they can bring in more casual watchers by reducing true racing and making the spectacle more “entertaining” which in turn means more profit. Will that change? I doubt it because to the owners, it’s about the show and how much revenue it generates, not about racing.

I’ve lived in six countries, most of my life in the USA, and I can say with confidence that greed is the driving force in the country. I’m absolutely not against striving for something, working hard and making huge amounts of money. The problem is when you sacrifice the quality of your life for the desire to make more. In my opinion, that attitude is what drives F1 now and until it changes, I doubt we will see true racing.

Rick Gomez (@Rgomez13)

Sports.title: Stats: Russell scored as many points as Hulkenberg in last three rounds | 2026 United States GP stats and facts
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is on the verge of sealing a historic championship triumph following his victory in the United States Grand Prix.

George Russell was Mercedes’ most recent race-winner going into Austin, and this was Antonelli’s first win in over a month. But Russell’s fading championship challenge has collapsed entirely over the last three rounds.

The rot set in with his retirement in Malaysia, which not only left him point-less but prompted a grid penalty in Singapore. He compounded matters there by crashing out of the sprint race while leading.

The upshot is, with only an eighth and a ninth place to count from his last three grand prix weekends, Russell has added just six points to his tally in that time. He has been out-scored by eight of his rivals, including Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson, who picked up three times as many points as Russell over the period.

Underlining just how badly the last three rounds have gone for Russell, his haul of six points matches that of Nico Hulkenberg, who lies 14th in the championship standings.

Antonelli’s ninth career victory last weekend means he has now won more grands prix than his team mate. He has drawn level with rivals Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri – plus Piastri’s manager, Mark Webber.

Thanks to Antonelli’s success this year, and Piastri’s failure to win since last year’s Dutch Grand Prix, Italian drivers now have as many grand prix wins as Australians. Antonelli claimed the 52nd grand prix win for an Italian driver, putting the two nations level in seventh place on the all-time list.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli also scored his seventh pole position, giving him as many as Jacques Laffite. But he missed out on the fastest lap, which Leclerc scored for the second race in a row. It is Leclerc’s 15th fastest lap, matching his Ferrari predecessors Felipe Massa and Clay Regazzoni, plus three-times world champion Jackie Stewart.

Isack Hadjar equalled the best qualifying position of his career with third place. He previously achieved this in the Australian Grand Prix earlier this year.

Unusually, both Red Bull drivers finished lower than they started. However their recent upswing in form continued and they look increasingly likely to avoid finishing outside the top three in the championship for the first time since 2015. They out-scored McLaren for the fifth round in a row, have drawn level with them on 355 points, and are classified ahead of them in third place by dint of their higher finishing positions in races.

However third place for Max Verstappen means he is no longer a championship contender for the first time in almost six years. The last race Verstappen competed in which he could not take the title was the 2020 season finale at Yas Marina. He dropped out of contention for that year’s championship four rounds earlier at Imola.

Finally, Gabriel Bortoleto set a new record for the largest grid drop penalty ever issued to an F1 driver. He collected a total grid drop of 80 places after Audi replaced multiple parts of his power unit during the weekend. As he qualified 13th and started 21st, he only served 10% of the penalty. The record was previously held by Jenson Button, who had a 70-place grid penalty at the 2015 Mexican Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Antonelli will automatically become champion if F1 cancels another race | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is virtually guaranteed to win the world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend.

Carlos Sainz Jnr last weekend expressed doubt over whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix could go ahead due to the ongoing war between Iran and the USA. The war has already forced the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and the relocation of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia.

This reduced the number of rounds this season from 24 to 23. A further reduction remains possible, and should that happen none of Antonelli’s rivals will be able to prevent him taking the championship.

F1 has indicated it is prepared to hold an alternative final race at Imola in Italy if necessary. However if both races in the Middle East are cancelled and only one replacement event is arranged, the total number of championship points available over the remainder of the season will be reduced.

With 125 points currently remaining, George Russell needs to out-score his team mate by 124 to take the title. Lewis Hamilton needs to beat Antonelli by 125 points.

Both scenarios are extremely unlikely as they would essentially involve the championship leader failing to score any points over the remaining five rounds. But another race cancellation with no replacement, reducing the total points available to 100, would make it impossible for Antonelli to be beaten.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Moto GP series is due to hold its rescheduled Qatar round on the weekend after the Mexican Grand Prix. However many riders are demanding reassurances from the event promoters about their security, safety and compensation in the event of any last-minute changes.

Only a few F1 world championship titles have not been decided by the result of a grand prix. Max Verstappen won the 2023 world championship in a sprint race, coincidentally held in Qatar. In 1987 Nelson Piquet clinched the title when team mate Nigel Mansell withdrew from the Japanese Grand Prix after injuring his back in a crash during practice.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Wolff on stewards’ decision to penalise Russell: “It’s legal, here, to smoke” | Briefs
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff indicated he did not agree with the stewards’ decision to penalise George Russell in the United States Grand Prix.

Russell collected a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage while fighting Oscar Piastri for position.

David Coulthard sympathised with Wolff over the penalty call in an interview for Viaplay. “I think the-five-second penalty was… I’m not sure what they were smoking,” said the former Former Formula 1 driver. “This was racing on the first lap so hopefully that gets spoken to the stewards about.”

“It’s legal, here, to smoke so maybe,” Wolff replied.

Sports.title: More radio problems vex Verstappen: “‘Maybe we should use sign language’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen revealed he had yet more problems with his radio during the United States Grand Prix.

The Red Bull driver suffered serious disruption to his pit-to-car communications when he won the previous round in Singapore. He said the radio fault in Austin was “not the second time” it has happened this year.

“It’s already, I don’t know how many times this year,” he said. “Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It’s probably cheaper as well.”

“It’s a disaster. It’s really frustrating, to be honest.”

Verstappen qualified second in Austin but fell to third place in the race as he struggled with his car’s balance. During one radio exchange Verstappen admitted he did not know how to change his front wing angle at his next pit stop.

Afterwards he said Red Bull had not been especially strong or weak anywhere at the Austin track.

“We are balanced as a car,” he said. “We are not the fastest in high-speed, we’re not the fastest in low-speed, and I think maybe here you either need to be very fast in high-speed or you need to be the quickest in low-speed.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“When you’re none of it, you’re just a little bit average, and I think we were just a little bit average in the race.”

However he does believe there was potential for Red Bull to perform better last weekend.

“Of course, if we chose different tyres, probably we could have maybe been second, but that’s always easy to say afterwards. Plus, when you have too many issues with the consistency of your power unit, then that already costs you free lap time.

“So it’s normal that you can’t execute everything to the limit or at least be at your best. There are still a lot of things that we need to look at and do better.”

Sports.title: Antonelli was “concerned” by threat from Verstappen’s early pit stop in Austin | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was concerned to see rival Max Verstappen make an early pit stop in the United States Grand Prix.

Verstappen committed to a two-stop strategy early in the race, pitting on lap 14 for a second set of soft tyres which meant he would have to come in again. Mercedes delayed Antonelli’s first pit stop but the tactics paid off as he was able to reach the end of the race with a single tyre change.

However Antonelli admitted he was “a bit concerned in the beginning” when he stayed out after Verstappen’s pit stop. “But we were able to extend and actually the pace came back with the medium, and we were able to extend without losing too much time.

“So then, as you know, after doing the first stint on the medium, we were like, ‘Oh, right, we’re going to go for one-stop.’ And the hard, to be fair, felt very robust, so I felt pretty confident to go all the way to the end.

“I just didn’t know how much management was required, but it was good, and the car felt very good today.”

Verstappen saved two sets of soft tyres from qualifying which appeared to give him a strategic advantage before the race began.

“We didn’t have much choice, to be fair,” said Antonelli. “We didn’t have any new softs, so the new medium was the only choice we really had, or the hard.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But the medium was not amazing. I think today the best tyre was the hard, just because it was the most resilient tyre. It was quite surprising because in recent races the soft has always been probably the best tyre. So it was a good surprise, and luckily it worked for us.”

Antonelli scored Mercedes’ first win since it introduced a major upgrade for its W17 in Malaysia. He said there is still room for improvement with the car.

“In some places, I would say it’s still not [delivering] as much as we expected, but in other places it is delivering very well,” he said. “I think in the high- and medium-speed [corners] the car is very strong. The balance is good.

“We’re still struggling a little bit in low-speed with front locking. But overall, I feel like the package is finally starting to deliver, and we’re starting to see the results and the improvements from the package.”

Sports.title: On This Day: Shock as Mansell’s tyre blow-out hands title to Prost in final race | Brief
Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. [caption id="attachment_530322" align="alignright" width="470"] The 2025 Formula 1 season started in Australia[/caption]A world drivers’ champion has been crowned every year since the series began. Since 1958 a world constructors’ championship title has also been awarded. The most successful F1 drivers in history are seven-times world champions Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. In 2021 the former became the first and so far only driver to date to win 100 grands prix. While Schumacher retired from F1 at the end of 2012, Hamilton continues to race. His rival world champions in the series are Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso. There are 10 teams active in the championship, each of which field cars for two drivers. Each team is required to design and build the majority of its cars but may source some parts including engines, gearboxes and certain other components. Ferrari has won the F1 constructors’ championship more times than any other team, with 16 titles. It is also the only team which has competed in every championship since the first…

Sports.title: VIDEO: Oleksandr Usyk vs. Vitali Klitschko | FANTASY FIGHT
Sports.content:
What happens when the two most dominant Ukrainian big men in modern prizefighting history collide across 15 grueling championship rounds?

In the fifth installment – and the very first heavyweight edition – of our Fantasy Fight series here at Rummy’s Corner, we examine an ultimate dream matchup: two-division undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk squaring off against former long-reigning WBC heavyweight titlist “Dr. Ironfist” Vitali Klitschko.

Under our standardized neutral ground rules, both fighters enter the squared circle at their absolute physical and tactical peak, competing under unified rules with modern 10-ounce gloves, day-before weigh-ins, and tested across the classic 15-round championship distance. On paper, it pits Usyk’s sublime lateral movement, rapid angles, and relentless southpaw volume against Vitali’s towering 6-foot-7 frame, awkward leans, and suffocating punch output.

Yet, when put to the test across our boxing communities, this dream heavyweight collision ignited one of the most passionate and polarized debates in the history of the series.

To Usyk’s supporters, his peerless conditioning, agile footwork, and surgical combination punching present an impossible stylistic puzzle. Having already proven his ability to disarm and systematically outbox modern super-heavyweight giants, proponents believe Usyk’s continuous feints, angles, and relentless second-half pace would drag the bigger man into deep, uncomfortable waters.

However, writing off Vitali Klitschko in mythical head-to-head territory is dangerous ground. Boasting an iron chin, an 87% knockout ratio, and a resume where he was never knocked down and rarely lost a round, “Dr. Ironfist” was an immovable force of nature. If Vitali establishes his long range-finder jab, dictates the distance, and imposes his crushing 245-pound frame, he could turn the contest into a claustrophobic nightmare for any moving target.

Can Usyk tame the giant with fleet-footed wizardry, or does Vitali break him down over the championship haul?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner breaks down the tactical mechanics, community debate, and official scorecards. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Tests What Canelo Alvarez Has Left
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli in Riyadh with sharp questions hanging over what remains in the Mexican superstar’s tank. Veteran boxing insider Dan Rafael views Alvarez’s mileage, ring age, and recent outings as unmistakable signs that the veteran is drifting further from his peak.

Rafael argues that a prime Canelo would have systematically broken Mbilli down. Heading into Saturday, however, Mbilli brings youth, stamina, and relentless pressure, making the outcome far harder to forecast.

“A lot younger. He’s fresher. I mean, it’s a crapshoot at this stage of Canelo’s career,” Rafael said on About Boxing. “This is the type of guy that in his best days he would completely pick apart and probably just do damage to for 12 rounds or maybe stop him. But the reality is Canelo hasn’t had a stoppage in a long time.”

Rafael pointed to Canelo’s defeat against Terence Crawford alongside his decisions over Jaime Munguia and Edgar Berlanga as clear proof of decline. Alvarez turned pro at 15, and more than two decades in the ring have built up heavy wear and tear.

Canelo hasn’t stopped an opponent since halting Caleb Plant in 2021. While he has managed to keep winning most nights, the emphatic dominance that fueled his run to the top of the sport has largely vanished.

When a fighter has one flat performance, people call it an off night. When it stretches across four straight outings as we’ve seen with Canelo in his last four fights, it is an unmistakable pattern. The public senses it, which explains why the energy around this Riyadh card feels muted.

Mbilli’s relentless work rate presents a serious operational hurdle. Canelo can still punish mistakes off the back foot, and Mbilli’s aggression will present openings. Yet it remains uncertain whether Alvarez can match that output and maintain his gas tank across 36 minutes against a hungry titleholder.

Surviving Mbilli is step one. An emphatic showing keeps Canelo primed for another lucrative main event. Turki Alalshikh could look toward Hamzah Sheeraz next, a fight Alvarez could handle comfortably. It seems doubtful anyone will push him into the ring with a destructive puncher like Osleys Iglesias anytime soon.

A disputed decision on the cards might protect Canelo’s status contractually, but it would hammer his standing with fans. If observers feel Mbilli got robbed, friendly judges will not quiet Rafael’s warnings about the veteran’s fading reflexes.

Mbilli also carries pressure into the ring, looking to rebound after battling Lester Martinez to a draw on the Canelo Crawford undercard. Both enter this meeting off identical layoffs.

Rafael declined to pick the outright upset. Still, he expects Saturday to deliver a clear verdict: Canelo either proves he still belongs at elite championship caliber, or the final bell on his career draws noticeably closer.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury’s 10-Fight Plan Could Lead to More Losses
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury already has his eyes on the future, tossing out the idea of signing another 10-fight contract once his current deal wraps up. That talk might hit a brick wall fast if Anthony Joshua takes care of business on December 11 in Cardiff.

A rough beating at Principality Stadium would leave the 38-year-old stuck in no-man’s-land, stuck weighing genuine ring threats against matchups nobody wants to pay to see.

Walking away does not seem to be anywhere on Fury’s radar. He has walked away and come back enough times that even a lopsided loss might not force his exit.

“I’m going to continue,” Fury told WSVN Miami, brushing off exit talk. He mentioned having two bouts left on his current deal before adding, “I’ll finish the contract off and then probably sign another 10-fight deal. Who knows?”

The Gypsy King tossed in a reality check, noting the cash must make sense and the schedule needs to move fast given his age.

That is a wild roadmap for someone who has logged 39 pro outings, survived a brutal three-bout war with Deontay Wilder, and dropped consecutive decisions to Oleksandr Usyk. He grabbed comeback wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach earlier this year, but Joshua delivers power on a whole different level.

A bad knockout loss would trigger alarms that go way past whether he can hang with top-tier champions. Depending on the damage taken, even a hungry fringe contender who brings steady heat, works the body, and presses the action could become an unnecessary hazard.

Fury spent his prime dominating with slick movement, massive reach, and smothering upper-body weight. Those attributes fade in a hurry when reaction times dip against fresh heavyweights. Joshua owns the raw dynamite to reveal exactly how much punch resistance Fury has left when shots start landing clean inside.

The Fury brand will always sell tickets at home. British fans backed him through long layoffs, fake retirement posts, and the Usyk defeats. A tune-up bout against an easy touch would pull numbers in the short term.

Selling a full ten-round tour against soft touches is an entirely different hustle. The Wach bout worked as a quick warm-up. Stacking up multiple dates against fading veterans or clear underdogs will simply drain fan interest.

Promoters will cut checks as long as Fury wants to put gloves on. The real headache will be finding guys he can handle without boring the crowd to tears.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Shamelessly Pushes for Fighter of the Year Over O’Shaquie Foster
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is continuing his campaign for Fighter of the Year, staying on the attack since last Sunday by taking aim at O’Shaquie Foster’s resume and dismissing his win over Raymond Ford. Foster quickly fired back, asking if Garcia stopping Conor Benn actually tops beating a proven former world champion.

While Garcia praised Foster for handling Emanuel Navarrete on Saturday, he brushed Ford aside as “not a standout fighter.” That remark directly targets half of Foster’s case for the award.

Foster went to X to set the record straight, insisting Ford possesses far more championship pedigree than Benn:

“Ford was a ex world champion, what was Benn other than a big name? Skill for skill he not f***in wit Ray being honest!!! Neither one of your wins compare to mines dude!!”

Ryan made his intentions unmistakable on Sunday, October 25, kicking off a brazen social media campaign for 2026 Fighter of the Year. Responding to talk surrounding O’Shaquie, Garcia flatly declared, “You lost your mind – I’m the fighter of the year,” before posting self-congratulatory notes boasting about wanting to screenshot the faces of critics once the award is handed out.

The sudden push came just twenty-four hours after Foster dominated Emanuel Navarrete. Ryan clearly saw the public momentum swinging toward Foster and decided to counter it by flooding the timeline.

When you place the resumes side by side, it is not particularly close. Foster earned a tough majority decision against Ford in May, then produced a clinic on October 24 against Navarrete. He sent the three-division champion to the canvas twice in round twelve, unifying three major belts at super featherweight.

Garcia picked up the WBC welterweight strap against Mario Barrios before blowing through Benn. Those victories carry weight, yet Foster holds the upper hand on opponent quality, championship hardware, and divisional supremacy. Garcia never referenced Fighter of the Year directly in his latest post, but picking apart the Ford win serves his self-promotion perfectly. Downplaying Foster’s first victory helps clear an easier path to the trophy.

Ryan knows exactly what he is doing by trying to erase the Ford win. If he can convince the casual audience that Foster only had one real fight this year, his own two-fight run looks respectable by comparison. It is shameless PR, but in modern boxing, guys with twenty million followers are used to controlling the narrative regardless of what actually happened in the ring.

Sports.title: Brian Norman Jr. Risks Another Setback Against Abel Ramos
Sports.content:
Brian Norman Jr. could face a dangerous test against Abel Ramos on the December 19 Devin Haney–Liam Paro card, with a loss threatening to undo his progress since surrendering the WBO welterweight title to Haney last November.

Boxing journalist Dan Rafael reports that Top Rank is planning Norman vs. Ramos for the card, which is expected to take place in San Francisco. The bout would be the 25-year-old Norman’s second fight since his defeat to Haney.

Rafael reports that Top Rank also plans to feature welterweights Tiger Johnson and Rohan Polanco. But Norman has the most to lose if the Ramos fight comes together: he’s a former champion trying to regain ground, and his proposed opponent has already shown this year that he can upset a younger fighter’s plans.

Ramos (29-6-3, 22 KOs) is 35 and has six losses on his record, but those numbers don’t tell the whole story. In February, he rallied to defeat previously unbeaten Tahmir Smalls by split decision. Smalls was supposed to be the rising fighter. Ramos turned the fight into a long night and left him with his first loss.

Norman is a more established fighter than Smalls, having already held a world title, but that doesn’t make Ramos a safe opponent. The veteran can pressure, take punishment, and keep working when a younger fighter expects him to fade.

For Norman, the danger is getting drawn into a fight at close range and spending too much time looking for one big punch. He has the power to hurt Ramos, but he’ll need to put his shots together and keep the veteran from setting the pace. If he lets rounds slip away while waiting for a knockout, Ramos could make the scorecards uncomfortable.

The setting would add another layer. Norman lost his WBO title to Haney by decision in Riyadh last November, and now he could return on the undercard while Haney fights Paro in a reported title unification.

That gives Norman a chance to put on a strong performance in front of an audience watching the man who beat him. It also gives him a direct comparison with his former opponent: Haney will be fighting for two belts while Norman takes on a hard veteran to keep his own title hopes moving.

A victory over Ramos would help Norman make his case for another major fight. A loss would be far more damaging, raising questions about where he fits among the leading welterweights after the Haney defeat.

Norman–Ramos remains a planned matchup, according to Rafael, rather than an officially announced fight. If it happens, Norman will have to get past an opponent who has already ruined one prospect’s unbeaten record this year.

Sports.title: Frazer Clarke Agrees To Joseph Parker Fight On Fury vs Joshua Undercard
Sports.content:
Joseph Parker could make his ring return against Frazer Clarke on the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard on December 11 in Cardiff, risking his remaining standing among the heavyweight elite after a lengthy layoff.

Clarke confirmed he agreed to the matchup, though communication has quieted recently and organizers have not officially announced the bout.

Parker has remained inactive since Fabio Wardley stopped him in October 2025. Facing Clarke provides immediate visibility on a massive stage, yet it offers zero margin to shed ring rust.

That defeat to Wardley halted an impressive career resurgence. Parker had forced his way back into title contention through disciplined, mobile performances against Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, frustrating both power punchers over the distance.

Those past achievements offer little protection here. Clarke possesses the size to impose himself physically, alongside an extensive amateur foundation to punish any hesitation if Parker starts slowly.

The central uncertainty centers on Parker’s sharpness. His previous run required sustained concentration across twelve grueling rounds. Following a stoppage defeat and over a year outside the ropes, replicating that form against an ambitious opponent represents a serious hurdle.

Their history stretches back to 2010, when Parker defeated Clarke in the amateur ranks in India. Clarke aims to avenge that loss, calling Parker a huge name and a great fighter in an interview with The Sun.

Clarke recently snapped a two-fight skid with an August stoppage of Lamah Griggs. Upsetting Parker would instantly elevate his profile and secure invitations to major events.

Parker’s time away also involved outside complications, including a backdated three-month suspension following a failed test for a cocaine metabolite. UK Anti-Doping subsequently cleared him for competition.

Fighting in Cardiff delivers the ultimate platform for Parker to re-establish momentum. That spotlight carries severe consequences, because a sluggish showing or another defeat under the eyes of the boxing world could permanently close the door on future world championship opportunities.

Sports.title: Vasily Lomachenko Targets Charly Suarez for Ring Return at 130.
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko is eyeing Charly Suarez for his return at super featherweight, yet defeating the Filipino contender will not settle the core mystery surrounding his comeback: How much elite ability remains after a prolonged absence at age 38?

Suarez is under consideration for his ring return. Lomachenko intends to test his reflexes under real fire prior to chasing premier targets.

“My next step, it will be a fight with a guy, maybe with a guy from the Philippines, Suarez,” Lomachenko said to Fight Hub TV. “It will be my first fight after rest, and after that, we’ll see how I feel.”

Lomachenko has remained inactive since halting George Kambosos Jr. in May 2024. He has not stepped inside the ropes at 130 pounds since 2017, introducing another variable after more than two years on the shelf.

Sharing the ring with Suarez guarantees rounds against an established contender, though any verdict requires scrutiny. Suarez is also 38 years old. Outpointing him offers limited insight into how Lomachenko handles younger, sharper champions across a full championship distance.

Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, spatial control, and split-second precision. He famously pivoted into blind spots, unloading clean punches before opponents could reset. If his reflexes have eroded or his legs can no longer maintain that tempo, fighters who once swung at air might suddenly connect with ease.

Taking on someone like O’Shaquie Foster represents a far steeper hazard. Foster’s slick mobility and sharp counterpunches would force Lomachenko to spend considerable energy establishing range. Looking sharp against Suarez is positive, yet it does not guarantee Lomachenko can cut the ring on Foster or match his pace over 36 minutes.

Lomachenko clearly recognizes the reality in front of him. When questioned regarding matchups with Gervonta Davis or Naoya Inoue, he urged the interviewer to pump the brakes.

“I want to do slowly, slowly, slowly,” Lomachenko noted. “I need to check my body in the real fight.”

Hitting 130 pounds again presents its own physical hurdle. After spending several years up at lightweight, dropping back to a weight class he exited almost ten years ago takes a heavier toll on an older fighter. How comfortably he makes the scale could tell us just as much as his performance under the lights.

The veteran southpaw admitted the ticking clock motivated him to lace up the gloves again instead of letting time slip away.

“One day I wake up and thinking, hey, now I’m 38 years old, and we need to try one more time,” Lomachenko said. “If it will be after two more or three years, then I will be 40, 41 years old. It will be too late.”

His team is scheduled to sit down with Bob Arum to map out the business side of the ring return. Neither a date nor an opponent has been made official.

Suarez offers a workable starting point, though Lomachenko must deliver more than just a victory to prove he still belongs among the division elite. Hand speed, foot mobility, and gas tank over the championship stretch will tell the real story.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Faces Liam Paro In San Francisco
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s new DAZN deal is getting a favorable launch: a welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco, with the Australian traveling to Haney’s home region for the opening fight of that agreement.

Mike Coppinger of The Ring reports that the WBO and IBF titleholders will meet December 19 at Chase Center. The fight has yet to receive an official announcement.

It is a legitimate unification. It also puts Haney in the more comfortable position before either man throws a punch. DAZN gets to introduce its newly signed fighter to a Bay Area audience, while Paro arrives with a belt that could make that investment look better by the end of the night.

Paro’s job is to wreck the launch.

He has done something similar before. In June 2024, he traveled to Puerto Rico and beat Subriel Matias by unanimous decision for the IBF light welterweight title. The champion’s reputation and home support failed to intimidate him.

But using that victory as proof he can beat Haney would overlook the harder comparison. Matias came forward and gave Paro opportunities to land while moving. Haney can force him to become the pursuer, making the Australian create openings rather than wait for an opponent to supply them.

That is where this fight could become frustrating for Paro. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to jab, move and make relatively quiet rounds look like his rounds.

Paro needs to attack the body when Haney moves, work when they get close and avoid letting every clinch become a break from the pressure. He cannot afford to spend the first half studying a target that keeps leaving.

Haney has an obligation here, too. A new broadcast deal and two belts will generate promotion, but they cannot substitute for a performance that makes people want his next fight.

Winning narrowly while limiting the action would collect another title. Taking command against a fellow champion would give DAZN something stronger to sell.

The homecoming is arranged around Haney. Whether the night belongs to him depends on how much fighting Paro forces him to do.

Ghana News.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ licences over $8.38m debt
Ghana News.content:
The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mining leases and prospecting licences of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Ower Mines, citing more than US$8.38 million in unpaid fees and alleged breaches of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703).

In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Commission said it followed the legally prescribed process after the company failed to settle outstanding Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees or remedy other breaches identified by the regulator.

The company has instituted legal proceedings against the State to challenge the termination, according to the Commission.

The Commission said Northern Ashanti Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010.

Under Section 24 of Act 703 and the terms of its lease agreement, the company was required to pay annual mineral right fees.

However, the Commission said the company had accumulated US$8.33 million in unpaid fees relating to its mining leases for the period from 2010 to 2025, alongside US$49,928 owed on prospecting licences covering 2019 to 2025.

On April 14, 2025, the Commission issued Notices to Remedy Breach under Section 68(2) of Act 703 and Regulation 200(3) of the Minerals and Mining Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2176), requiring the company to settle the outstanding amounts.

The Commission said the company failed to comply within the stipulated period.

Beyond the unpaid fees, the Commission said its assessment found that Northern Ashanti Mines had not undertaken meaningful mining operations on the concession for more than two years.

It said this constituted a breach of Section 69(1) of Act 703.

According to the Commission, the company was given an opportunity to regularise its position but failed to remedy the identified breaches.

The Commission said it notified the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources on April 7, 2026, requesting that a notice of termination be served on the company.

The Minister approved the issuance of the notice on April 24, 2026, and the Commission proceeded with the termination process on April 30, 2026.

It maintained that the decision was taken in accordance with the law and that due process had been followed at every stage.

The Commission also rejected suggestions that the company’s status as an indigenous business should exempt it from statutory obligations.

“Once granted, a holder must abide by the rules, whether they are an indigenous company or not, and this includes the payment of statutory fees and the undertaking of meaningful mining operations,” the Commission stated.

The Commission said the terminated mineral rights had reverted to the State, without extinguishing liabilities the company incurred before the termination.

It said it would pursue the recovery of the outstanding fees and take steps to protect the affected assets against encroachment and other unlawful activities.

“The Commission reserves the right and shall pursue the company to pay all the sums it owes to the State,” the statement said.

The Commission confirmed that Northern Ashanti Mines had initiated legal proceedings challenging the termination after acknowledging receipt of the notice.

It criticised the company’s media campaign, arguing that its public statements risked undermining the judicial process while the dispute remained before the courts.

Ghana News.title: Idris Elba launches free AI filmmaking programme for African creatives
Ghana News.content:
African creatives in Ghana and four other countries can apply for a free artificial intelligence (AI) filmmaking programme launched by actor Idris Elba’s Akuna Group in partnership with Google.

The initiative, titled From Script to Screen with AI, aims to equip aspiring and emerging filmmakers with skills in AI-assisted storytelling, alongside mentorship and film production opportunities. Applications opened on Monday, 26 October 2026, and close on 15 November 2026.

Supported by US$1 million in funding from Google.org, the programme’s curriculum was developed by AI filmmaking training company Curious Refuge. It is open to eligible applicants in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Sierra Leone and South Africa.

Participants will undergo a 12-week online academy from February to April 2027, covering the fundamentals of AI filmmaking before choosing a specialist area.

The available pathways are fiction, documentary, animation, advertising and screenwriting, allowing participants to develop their skills across different aspects of visual storytelling.

Following the training, graduates will be invited to submit one-page film ideas. Those shortlisted will form teams and receive four weeks of mentorship from industry professionals and subject experts before pitching their projects to panels comprising representatives from Akuna, Google and the wider film industry.

Selected teams will receive funding to produce their films between July and October 2027, with the completed projects scheduled to be showcased in October 2027.

Sir Idris Elba, chairman of The Akuna Group, said the initiative was intended to widen access to training and enable African creators to tell their own stories.

“For me, this is about learning. This is about access to courses that help educate creators across the continent to tell their stories. Through Akuna Learning, we’re partnering with Google and Curious Refuge on ‘From Script to Screen with AI’, a remarkable training and mentorship programme teaching African filmmakers to use AI tools. Selected projects will receive production funding, and creators will retain control of their work. I’m looking forward to seeing the stories they choose, and how the education leads to employment and self-momentum, but helps shape the narrative of Africa,” he said.

Khaled Gad, chief executive officer of The Akuna Group, said the programme was designed to take participants beyond training and provide a pathway towards producing finished films.

“Training on its own does not build an industry. Creators need a route from the classroom to the screen, and this programme carries them all the way, from their first application to a finished, funded film. It opens on the same day and runs to the same standard in all five countries. You do not need a film school background or any experience with AI to apply. You need finished work that shows what you can do, and your application in by 15 November,” he said.

The programme targets a broad range of visual storytellers, including filmmakers, screenwriters, animators, digital content creators, photographers, designers, editors and visual artists.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old, live in one of the five participating countries and have access to a laptop, reliable internet and consistent electricity. They must also be available for the full 12-week academy and subsequent stages if selected to progress.

No film school qualification or previous AI experience is required. However, applicants must submit existing creative work that demonstrates their talent and commitment. Women are particularly encouraged to apply.

Applications are free, and successful applicants will not pay to participate. Creators will also retain control of their work, with neither the programme nor its partners claiming ownership rights over the films produced.

Interested applicants can submit their applications through Akuna Learning before the 15th November deadline.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian veterinarian leads campaign against proposed African battery cage standard
Ghana News.content:
A prominent Ghanaian veterinarian is leading a continent-wide campaign against a proposed standard from the African Organisation for Standardisation (ARSO) that would approve battery cages for egg-laying hens.

Dr. Daniel Baba Abiliba, founder of the Animal Welfare League (AWL) and a graduate student at the Yale School of the Environment, is speaking out against ARSO's draft standard, CD-ARS 1241:2025(E), which would formally accept the worst form of battery cages as a housing system for laying hens.

"The battery cage system ARSO is endorsing is horrible, and it runs contrary to African ideals," Dr. Abiliba said. "Most Africans interact with animals in one way or another, in our homes, on our farms and in our communities. Also, a large number of us know that chickens are sentient beings; they can feel pain, fear, and distress. The battery cage system has been found to contribute a lot of pain and suffering to chickens. This standard does not reflect who we are."

The Pan-African Campaign

Together with coalition partners, AWL launched a campaign in March 2026 at stoparsobatterycages.org . It calls on all 44 African national standards bodies to reject the draft by signing the petition.

"Treating animals well is not at odds with productivity," Dr. Abiliba said. "Ghanaian farmers know that healthy, well-kept animals are productive animals. We don't have to choose between caring for animals and feeding our people."

Ghana’s Leadership in Animal Welfare

Ghana has demonstrated strong leadership in establishing national poultry welfare standards through the creation of GS 1404:2026 (Farm Animal Welfare – Requirements for Poultry). Dr. Abiliba contributed directly to this effort as part of the technical committee that drafted the standard alongside the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA), the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD), and other key stakeholders.

The GSA has officially adopted both the standard and its accompanying inspection manual as national benchmarks. In line with this, the VSD is currently piloting implementation across over 100 farms nationwide.

"Good animal husbandry has always been part of the African farming tradition. This standard simply puts it into writing and GS 1404 builds on what our farmers already know. ARSO should be learning from Ghana, not moving in the opposite direction," Dr Abiliba said.

A veterinarian with a global record Dr. Abiliba is currently pursuing a Master of Environmental Management at the Yale School of the Environment in the United States. He earned his Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).

He was the first Ghanaian to win the MSD/World Veterinary Association Veterinary Student Scholarship and his exemplary work in rabies prevention has been recognised by the World Health Organization.



The future of animal welfare in Africa depends on collective action. Readers, farmers, and organizations are urged to join the campaign against battery cages by visiting stoparsobatterycages.org and calling on African national standards bodies to reject draft standard CD-ARS 1241:2025(E).
