World.title: Italy’s Young Protesters Return to the Streets
World.content:
Demonstrators across Italy on Saturday protested economic inequality and the political establishment. A heavy police presence throughout the country aimed to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

Young people demonstrated across Italy on Saturday amid a heavy police presence to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

The demonstrations echoed student protests in France that have unleashed a nationwide groundswell of frustration there, sparking the country’s worst rioting in decades.

Italy’s marches on Saturday were largely peaceful, though protesters clashed with the police in Turin, Padua, Bologna and Rome, where a small group of demonstrators stormed the Colosseum. The police arrested just nine people nationwide and reported 87 to prosecutors, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

In Milan, the site of last week’s largest and most violent demonstrations, some 10,000 people hit the streets, the police estimated — five times as many as had marched the previous weekend.

Throngs of young people chanted about their frustration with the high cost of living and Italy’s political establishment. They held hand-drawn signs denouncing low wages, high rents, economic inequality and Italy’s financial support of Israel, whose war in Gaza is deeply unpopular with Italians.

Protesters said that the country’s sluggish job market and a government they saw as more focused on military spending than on investing in young people had set their generation up to fail.

“I look for work abroad every day of my life,” said Ilaria Carrozza, 27, a design engineer. “And that’s not fair: This is my country, I want to stay here. But I can’t live like this.”

Manfredi Cacioppo, a 26-year-old sales assistant from Sicily, said he was demonstrating in solidarity with truckers and farmers in southern Italy, who had recently blockaded roads and ports to protest high fuel prices caused by the war in Iran.

“It all comes from the same issue: money being spent on war,” he said. “That money would be better to invest in health, education, transport, the housing crisis and help for the workers.”

Last weekend’s demonstrations took Italy’s northern cities by surprise. In Milan, groups of masked young people set fires, looted stores and lobbed projectiles at the police, causing an estimated $1.1 million in damage, according to a local business association. Fifty-one people, most of them minors, were arrested.

Milan’s left-wing mayor accused the national police of “having underestimated the moment” and posting too few officers to the scene. Italy’s right-wing interior minister accused the mayor of pandering to the left.

Giorgia Meloni, Italy’s prime minister, called an emergency meeting on Monday and announced tougher penalties for violent protesters. A cabinet member, Matteo Salvini, said that the government would send 500 soldiers to Milan this weekend to “defend” the city against “criminals.”

On Saturday, army vehicles and police vans dotted many of Milan’s main squares, and numerous stores in the city’s shopping district boarded up their windows. Throughout the city, plainclothes police officers stopped groups of young people to check their identification documents.

For many protesters, the first challenge was figuring out where to go.

A social media account that helped organize the protests was supposed to post a meeting place at 2:30 p.m. But shortly before then, the Milan police said they had detained the account’s owner. The announcement never came.

Image Protesters in Rome on Saturday. Credit... Remo Casilli/Reuters

That left many demonstrators unmoored. In bars and online chat rooms, they argued over where, and whether, to show up.

“We were lost and confused,” said Caterina Sironi, a 23-year-old university student. “We ran all over the whole city.”

Ruggero Lorenzi, 19 and a high school student, crisscrossed Milan on three trains and a tram in search of a demonstration. “On Telegram, on Instagram, in metro stations, everyone was fighting over where to go,” he said.

After several false starts — “ten people over here, ten people over there,” he said — he found about 500 protesters gathered near a subway stop in the city center.

As Mr. Lorenzi’s protest snaked through the city to the Politecnico di Milano, Milan’s oldest university, its ranks swelled.

Many protesters said they were eager to keep the demonstration peaceful, hoping their message would be heard. The police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters in other cities on Saturday, but not in Milan, where they reported that there had been no violence or damage.

“We’re trying to emulate the French protests,” said Joshua Flores, 21, who is unemployed. “I hope this protest continues in a positive way.”

World.title: Turnout so far highest in decades as Israelis vote in pivotal election
World.content:
Turnout is at its highest so far in more than four decades, as Israelis vote in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is almost neck-and-neck with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in the race to become prime minister.

But neither of their political blocs are projected to win the 61 seats needed to form a majority government - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead.

The campaign has been shaped by the issues of democracy and security, and the election is widely being seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's rule.

Many leading parties complained on Tuesday morning of alleged irregularities at polling stations across the country - but Israel's Central Election Committee (CEC) says there is no evidence of systematic tampering with ballot slips.

Israel's proportional representation system means governments have always been coalitions - and the race to power can, and has, produced unexpected alliances. But this election looks especially tight - and lines in the sand have already been drawn.

Eisenkot, who leads the newly formed Yashar Party, is the main figure in the so-called "change bloc", a collection of parties who have ideological differences but share the goal of ousting Netanyahu.

Other leaders in the bloc include former prime minister Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman - both right-wingers who take hardline positions on security - and Yair Golan, a left-leaning former general.

For Netanyahu, a titan of Israeli politics who first served as prime minister in 1996, a return to power will hinge on another alliance with the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties that make up his current governing coalition - the most right-wing in Israel's history.

World.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
World.content:
If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula's rival FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, who refused to recognise the result. But Trump was a close ally of FlÃ¡vio's father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro.

When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had "no relationship" with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch-hunt".

Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back â and it paid off.

He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading "Brazil belongs to Brazilians".

His approval ratings jumped.

He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic â a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain.

Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point.

The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again.

Relations then improved.

The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks "very good" and Lula said he left "very satisfied".

Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strong leader.

World.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
World.content:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and a civilian evacuation on Friday.

Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.

Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

There are concerns that the truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity."

Up to 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas, Kyiv believes, with only 1,700 still living in the city itself.

Before the war it was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escape is highly dangerous because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.

No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water for three years.

World.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
World.content:
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.

Syrian health officials told state media five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government. Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.

It comes after a nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.

World.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
World.content:
Federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.

It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump.

Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.

Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

Comey's lawyer, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement that two different teams of prosecutors had investigated the alleged disclosure to the New York Times a decade ago during the first Trump administration.

"Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone," he said.

The attorney said the court filing "purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes that he did not commit".

His legal team has filed a motion to dismiss the charges.

Former federal prosecutor Glenn Kirschner told the BBC that the case may have exceeded the 10-year statute of limitations, giving the motion to dismiss the charges "a very good chance of being granted".

Kirschner said it seemed like the charges against Comey were a "revenge-fuelled attempt by Donald Trump to have his Department of Justice find something that might stick".

Jessica Levinson, law professor at Loyola University in Los Angeles, said that because the charges were still under seal, the details about what federal prosecutors are alleging were slim.

"We do have some examples of the Trump administration and the department of justice going after a variety of people who are his political enemies; we have very different outcomes in some of these cases, though," she told the BBC World Service's Newsday programme.

While other cases involving Comey have not moved forward, cases brought against other Trump adversaries have moved forward, Levinson noted.

World.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
World.content:
Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.

Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game.

"Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement. "Of course, his wife, BeyoncÃ©, will be atop the list."

Next year's Super Bowl LXI will take place on 14 February near Los Angeles.

The hip-hop star will follow in the footsteps of other recent half-time performers including Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.

The musical performance draws global attention while the sport is watched by tens of millions of people in the US.

Kendrick Lamar's 2025 performance was the most watched Super Bowl half-time show in history and won the Emmy award for outstanding music direction.

The announcement was made after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, performed two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played.

The LA shows were part of a tour to celebrate the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt.

"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," said Jay-Z.

"Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he "couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring".

"When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," Goodell said.

The star's accolades include being the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, 25 Grammy awards and being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

World.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
World.content:
Kylian MbappÃ© has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

MbappÃ© had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the programme cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," MbappÃ© said in a statement.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."

Spain's La Liga also apologised, saying it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian MbappÃ©'s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

A few people came out in support of him on Chinese social media, but that is a rare response given China's tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics.

Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like MbappÃ©.

The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview hosted by Real Madrid's AurÃ©lien TchouamÃ©ni first aired. In clips that have been circulating online, MbappÃ© does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.

But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when MbappÃ© refers to "a Chinese dictator".

Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was "unable to translate" his comments because they were "offensive to China and the Chinese people".

Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more.

World.title: Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
World.content:
NPO chair Jet de Ranitz said the organisation had held discussions with broadcasters about participating next year.

"In those discussions, we initially felt there was sufficient support to return. Unfortunately, we were unable to find a suitable format for this.

"As a result, we must conclude that it is currently too early to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027.

"Due to the sensitivities surrounding the themes currently at play, we have decided to take a step back for the time being."

NPO acknowledged that some Dutch fans may be disappointed, but that the contest would still be aired in the Netherlands.

Eurovision Song Contest director Martin Green said he was "deeply sorry" that the Netherlands would not take part, but added that "we understand their decision, and we respect the strength of feeling behind it".

Green added that organisers recognise that opinions about the contest "differ widely, both within countries and between them", adding: "We do not dismiss any of those views.

"At the same time, we believe the Eurovision Song Contest matters in a divided world. It is one of the few moments each year when people from across Europe and beyond come together around music, creativity and shared experience.

"That spirit of unity is what the contest has always stood for, and we are committed to protecting it."

Green said they looked forward to welcoming a Dutch entry again when they "feel the time is right".

World.title: Fallen 33kV power line sparks fire, destroys buildings in Kwara
World.content:
A fallen 33kV electricity transmission line triggered a fire that damaged residential buildings and businesses in Oloje Phase 2, Ilorin, Kwara State, early Tuesday, the state fire service has said.

The fire, which occurred on Lawyer Lambo Street in Ilorin West Local Government Area, destroyed a vehicle and a vulcanising workshop, while several buildings and businesses sustained damage.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Hassan Adekunle, spokesperson for the Kwara State Fire Service, said the agency received a distress call and arrived at the scene at 2:41 a.m.

The fire affected two buildings containing four-bedroom flats each and a third building comprising a room-and-parlour self-contained apartment.

The occupants of the self-contained apartment were rescued by community members, according to the statement.

Three vehicles were in one of the flats when the fire broke out. One was completely burnt, while firefighters saved the other two.

The second four-bedroom flat sustained damage, particularly in its kitchen, where electrical appliances, including a freezer, were affected. Its solar power system was also damaged.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

An adjoining travel and tours office lost its solar power system, four tubular batteries and other electrical appliances. A nearby vulcanising workshop was also destroyed.

Fire follows another incident

The fire service said preliminary findings indicated that a concrete pole supporting a 33kV transmission line collapsed, causing the line to fall onto a vehicle.

“The fallen line also landed on the vehicle that was burnt, and a spark reportedly ignited its tyre before the fire escalated within a short period,” the agency said.

The fallen transmission line also posed a risk to firefighters, prompting the agency to contact the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) control room to request the shutdown of the electricity feeder supplying the affected area.

The Chief Fire Officer, Alabi Muhammed, expressed sympathy with residents, property owners and business operators affected by the incident.

He urged residents to avoid erecting structures beneath high-tension electricity lines and advised property developers to observe safety setbacks around electricity infrastructure.

He also urged residents to report fallen poles, damaged electrical infrastructure and exposed transmission lines to the relevant authorities, warning them not to touch fallen wires or objects in contact with them.

The incident occurred less than 24 hours after another fire destroyed a building comprising three-bedroom flats in Kangile Village, Ilorin South Local Government Area, on Monday.

The fire service did not state whether the two incidents were connected.

World.title: Osinbajo demands justice, accountability to end North-central conflicts
World.content:
Former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo has called for justice, accountability and deliberate reconciliation to address persistent conflicts and social divisions in Nigeria’s North-central region.

He spoke on Monday at a conference organised by the Justice Research Institute, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru in Plateau State.

Mr Osinbajo said lasting peace would require governments, religious leaders, the political elites and civil society organisations to work together to rebuild trust among communities affected by years of violence.

The conference, themed “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North-Central Nigeria: Beyond Tribe and Faith—Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” brought together stakeholders to discuss practical approaches to addressing divisions and restoring peaceful coexistence.

Mr Osinbajo said rebuilding social cohesion required a deliberate change in how people viewed themselves and related to others across ethnic and religious divides.

“Let’s go back to being brothers and sisters again, and that orientation must be an intentional thing,” he said, stressing that uniting divided communities required deliberate government actions.

Citing South Africa and Rwanda as examples, the former vice president said societies that had experienced severe violence could rebuild relationships through determined leadership and sustained reconciliation efforts.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He referred to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, during which hundreds of thousands of people, predominantly Tutsis, were killed, saying the country’s subsequent reconciliation efforts demonstrated the importance of political commitment to rebuilding social cohesion.

“I think there’s a need for deliberate reconciliation and peacebuilding, and that can only be done by the government in collaboration with civil society groups and religious leaders,” he said.

He added that political and religious leaders, as well as civil society organisations, must promote unity, while governments must demonstrate the political will to address the underlying causes of conflict.

Mr Osinbajo also warned that reconciliation would be difficult without justice and consequences for wrongdoing.

He said victims of land grabbing and other forms of dispossession should have their properties restored, while compensation should be provided where necessary.

“For instance, if you look at the land-grabbing situation, the lands have to be returned to those from whom they have been taken. It’s as simple as that,” he said.

He said failure to restore victims’ losses would leave grievances unresolved and undermine efforts to rebuild trust among communities.

“Similarly, there must be penalty for wrongdoing, and our justice system… requires urgent attention,” he added, calling for improvements in the administration of justice.

In his welcome address, the Director-General of NIPSS, Ayo Omotayo, urged participants to approach the discussions with open minds and without prejudice.

Mr Omotayo said the conference should produce practical recommendations to improve relationships and secure a peaceful future for communities across the North-central region.

The conference chairman, the Emir of Lafia, Sidi Bage, a retired justice, also called for discussions that would produce meaningful solutions, promote justice and address the underlying causes of conflicts.

Mr Bage urged participants to embrace new perspectives and recognise their shared responsibility for building peaceful communities.

The co-chairman and Secretary-General of Jama’atu Nasril Islam, Khalid Aliyu, said rebuilding civic cohesion remained challenging in some communities, partly because of misleading messages from some religious leaders.

Mr Aliyu stressed the importance of responsible religious leadership in promoting understanding, tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

The conference focused on ways to counter ethnic and religious polarisation and rebuild trust in the North-central region, which has experienced recurring communal violence and prolonged tensions among communities.

World.title: Army recover two AK-47 rifles after gunfight in Benue
World.content:
Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke have recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items after repelling armed men during an operation in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State.

The troops encountered the armed group on Monday after receiving intelligence that suspected criminals posing as herders had crossed from neighbouring Nasarawa State into Guma, according to the military.

In a statement on Monday, Ahmad Zubairu, the acting media information officer of the task force, said the troops came under gunfire on arrival at the location but responded and forced the armed men to flee.

He said the troops recorded no casualties.

A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number document belonging to Umar Yusuf and ₦20, the statement said.

The Force Commander of Operation Whirl Stroke, Moses Gara, commended the troops for their response and urged them to sustain intelligence-led operations and strengthen collaboration with local communities.

He also called on residents to report suspicious movements and activities to security agencies.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Related incident

The operation came a day after Operation Whirl Stroke troops rescued two kidnap victims along Naka–Ahume Road in Benue State.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on 26 October that the troops encountered suspected kidnappers during a patrol on the road on 24 October. The suspects fled after a gunfight, abandoning their captives.

One of the rescued victims, Mngunengen Ihom, 36, sustained machete wounds and was taken to Naka General Hospital for treatment.

The two incidents highlight continuing military operations against armed groups and suspected kidnappers in Benue State.

World.title: Toluwanisings’ burial dispute deepens as uncle calls for death probe
World.content:
The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji has insisted that his burial must wait until the authorities determine what caused his death.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo” crooner died after he slumped at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State on 15 October.

Since then, the family has faced controversy over his burial arrangements, including whether to bury him in a cemetery, at his residence, or in his hometown.

The singer’s uncle, Lawal “Up Lawal” Ademola, made the family’s position clear during an interview with Dunmininu Kingdom, posted on TikTok on Monday.

Speaking on behalf of the family, he called for a transparent and impartial investigation into the death and warned against any attempt to compromise the investigation.

Up Lawal, a health worker, urged the government, community leaders, and security agencies to prevent interference in the investigation.

The younger brother of the singer’s father said: “The family has decided that Sodiq must not be buried on Wednesday. We have informed the musicians, who have since suspended all arrangements for his burial. The family thanks God, as we believe that He is the giver and taker of life. Since Sodiq’s death, we have accepted it as God’s will. However, the family now needs the support of Nigerians and the government because his death has deeply pained and baffled us.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are calling on the government, Christians, Muslims, and traditionalists to help us investigate the cause of Sodiq’s death. The whole world knows that Sodiq is dead, but to establish the facts and avoid future controversy, we, the Olayemi family, need to know the cause of his death. We are appealing to everyone to help us get answers.”

“No burial till further notice”

Furthermore, Up Lawal said the family had directed that all burial plans for Toluwanisings be suspended, adding that they had already informed their relatives in Ibadan.

He insisted that the family would continue to foot the mortuary bills until investigators completed their work and uncovered the cause of Toluwanisings’ death.

“The government should ensure that the law takes its course and empower the relevant authorities to investigate Sodiq’s death. We do not want to take the law into our own hands. The family is deeply saddened by his death. For this reason, nobody should make further burial arrangements for Sodiq, as we are still grieving and want to know the truth.

“The family has resolved that he must not be buried until the cause of his death is established. We will continue to pay the mortuary fees until the investigation is concluded. Once the cause of his death is established, we will bury him at his house in Ibadan, where his wife currently lives. That is the family’s decision,” said Up Lawal.

Allegations

He also alleged foul play in the singer’s death, claiming that his wife, workers, and others showed no sign of mourning when he visited Toluwanisings’ house with seven family members

“I represented the head of the family. 7 of us travelled from Ikirun to Ibadan, we got there at about 9:30am, and we met the wife’s mother, the wife’s sisters, PA, and Tolu’s aunt. I was devastated when I saw them watching TV and eating. They put food inside takeaway packs. I had to ask the wife if Tolu was truly Tolu dead because there was no sign of mourning. I told the PA to take me to the morgue so I could see Tolu’s body.

“He refused. I had to call the other family members, and they said I should arrest the PA. That was when he agreed to take us there. I then checked his body. I challenged my wife that there was a day Tolu’s daddy called her, that even if Tolu is not checking on me, you should be checking on m,e, but Tolu quickly took the phone from his wife and said, ‘don’t destroy our home,’ but she denied.”

He said he told Toluwanising’s widow, Elizabeth, that the family wanted to bury the late singer in his own house, but she rejected the idea.

“She said she couldn’t bear to see his grave. I then suggested Ikirun, but she complained that it was too far. I told her she had to choose one.

“Paternal grandmother insists Toluwanising must be buried in his house.”

Meanwhile, Toluwanising’s paternal grandmother, Sabitiyu Olayemi, insisted that the late singer should be buried in the house he built rather than beside his late mother’s grave.

She also accused the singer of neglecting her despite her family’s efforts to care for his mother.

She further claimed that Toluwanising hardly gave her money, alleging that he sent her just N10,000 on three occasions after she complained about his failure to visit her.

“It is my wish for him to be buried inside the house he built; they should not come and put him beside his mother’s grave at all. I will not allow it. We took care of his mother very well, like our own, but Toluwanisings doesn’t call me then, and even when I want to call people, they advise me not to. I didn’t even know he had built a house. I just recently learned that he is a popular Christian singer.

“He never gives me money at all, not even one kobo. It’s even one girl around one time ago that I gave his number to help me call him so that I can even hear his voice and he will just greet me and all. Even when I complain he doesn’t come to see me, he will be like ‘oh mummy, I have been very busy with work,’ and after that he only sent 10 thousand just like three times, and that was it,” the grandmother said.

Meanwhile, as the family continues to demand an investigation into his death, a flyer shared on Toluwanisings’ Instagram page on Tuesday announced a night of tributes in his honour at the Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, Ibadan.

The event will begin at 3 p.m., with attendees expected to dress in all white.

World.title: Fewer attacks, more deaths recorded in seven northern states after 2023 election – Report
World.content:
Recorded attacks against civilians declined slightly across seven northern Nigerian states in the six months after the 2023 presidential election, but estimated fatalities associated with those attacks increased, an analysis of conflict records by PREMIUM TIMES has found.

Data supplied by the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) project show that incidents classified as violence against civilians fell from 401 in the six months before the 2023 election to 383 afterwards, a decline of 4.5 per cent. Estimated fatalities, however, rose from 549 to 759, an increase of 38.3 per cent.

Most of the net increase in estimated fatalities was concentrated in Benue, where the figure rose from 111 before the election to 315 afterwards. The state’s increase of 204 accounted for almost all the net rise of 210 across the seven states.

The analysis covered Katsina, Zamfara, Sokoto, Kebbi, Kaduna, Niger and Benue. It also examined comparable periods around the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections and changes in recorded violence outside election years.

The findings describe violence recorded during selected periods. They do not establish that the elections caused the attacks or that the incidents were connected to electoral activity.

Different patterns across seven states

The decline in recorded incidents after the 2023 election was not uniform. Katsina recorded 93 incidents before polling day and 74 afterwards. Zamfara declined from 100 to 86, Kaduna from 72 to 56, and Kebbi from 12 to six.

Other states moved in the opposite direction. Sokoto rose from 38 incidents before the election to 58 afterwards, while Benue increased from 45 to 61. Niger remained almost unchanged, with 41 incidents before polling day and 42 afterwards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Estimated fatalities did not follow the same pattern as incident counts. In Zamfara, they increased from 136 to 154 despite a decline in recorded incidents. Sokoto recorded an increase from 45 to 98, while Benue’s estimated fatalities rose from 111 to 315. A decline in the number of recorded attacks does not necessarily mean fewer people were killed.

ACLED’s fatality figures are estimates derived from reported incidents. They should not be treated as independently verified death counts.

What earlier elections show

PREMIUM TIMES also examined comparable periods around the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections.

In the six months before the 23 February 2019 election, ACLED recorded 83 incidents of violence against civilians across the seven states. The number increased to 147 in the equivalent period afterwards — a rise of 77.1 per cent.

The 2015 comparison showed an increase from 29 to 40 incidents.

Although recorded incidents declined slightly after the 2023 election, their number remained substantially higher than during the corresponding periods around the earlier votes. Across the combined pre- and post-election windows, ACLED recorded 69 incidents around the 2015 election, 230 around 2019, and 784 around 2023.

These comparisons describe changes in recorded events. They do not establish that presidential elections caused the increases or declines. Changes in the availability and sources of conflict reporting over time must also be considered when interpreting differences between election years.

Katsina and Zamfara after 2019

Katsina recorded one of the sharpest increases in the 2019 comparison.

ACLED logged 10 incidents of violence against civilians in the six months before the election and 37 afterwards. Estimated fatalities associated with those incidents rose from 16 to 161.

The post-election incidents were concentrated in three local government areas: Kankara (10), Batsari (9) and Danmusa (6). Together they accounted for 25 of the state’s 37 recorded incidents. In neighbouring Zamfara, incidents increased from 21 to 31, while estimated fatalities rose from 148 to 360. Shinkafi and Kaura Namoda accounted for eight and seven of the post-election incidents respectively.

Violence beyond election periods

The conflict records also show substantial changes outside presidential election years.

In Katsina, ACLED recorded 37 incidents of violence against civilians between 24 February and 24 August 2019. The equivalent 182-day period in 2020 recorded 71 incidents, while the period from 24 February to 23 August 2024 recorded 98.

Zamfara recorded 31 incidents during the 2019 period and 22 in the equivalent period in 2020. The 2024 comparison recorded 130 incidents.

Annual records also show substantially higher incident counts in later years. Across the seven states, ACLED recorded 279 incidents classified as violence against civilians in 2019, compared with 750 in 2023 and 1,192 in 2024.

These figures show that changes in recorded violence were not confined to election periods. However, the number and composition of reporting sources in the dataset also changed over time. Differences in recorded incidents cannot automatically be read as equivalent changes in the underlying level of violence.

While the ACLED records show how violence changed around the elections, reports from INEC and election observers document specific ways insecurity affected voting arrangements in Niger and Katsina states during the 2023 presidential election.

How insecurity disrupted voting

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reported difficulties deploying personnel and materials to Alawa in Shiroro Local Government Area of Niger State. INEC Chairman Mahmood Yakubu attributed the delay to security concerns, according to an election-day report by PUNCH.

In Katsina, the commission reported the seizure of six Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices by thugs in Safana Local Government Area. Three devices were recovered and replacements deployed, Mr Yakubu said, according to Channels Television.

Election observer Yiaga Africa reported that polling units had been relocated in parts of Shiroro, Mariga, Magama and Rafi local government areas of Niger State following attacks. Its election-day situational statement raised concerns about the effect on voters’ access to polling locations.

Voting arrangements for displaced residents

INEC’s Report of the 2023 General Election states that special voting arrangements covered 155,101 registered voters across 323 polling units and 42 registration areas in five local government areas of Niger State affected by banditry and flooding. The commission said voting took place at established camps for internally displaced persons under security protection.

Earlier public statements gave different figures. In March 2022, officials identified 270 affected polling units across Mariga, Shiroro, Rafi and Munya. A February 2023 briefing referred to 247 or 248 units, while the final report recorded 323.

The differences may reflect changes in displacement, coverage or administrative definitions. They cannot be compared directly without the underlying schedules.

The European Union Election Observation Mission, in its report on Nigeria’s 2023 general elections, raised wider concerns about the information available to displaced voters on registration, voter cards, polling locations and the implementation of special voting arrangements.

INEC’s report records the scale of the arrangements but does not establish how many of the 155,101 registered voters were accredited or cast ballots. Determining participation would require the final polling-unit schedule, accreditation records and election results.

How we analysed the data

PREMIUM TIMES examined 17,114 ACLED conflict-event records covering Benue, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto and Zamfara. Of these, 9,354 were classified as violence against civilians.

The incident-level dataset was supplied directly by ACLED on 14 October 2026 following a request submitted on 13 October. The analysis used the event date, state, local government area, event classification and estimated fatality fields. Event identifiers were checked for duplication.

For each presidential election, incidents recorded during the 182 days before polling day were compared with those recorded during the 182 days afterwards. Election days were excluded.

The periods examined were:

2015: 27 September 2014 to 27 March 2015 and 29 March to 26 September 2015.

2019: 25 August 2018 to 22 February 2019 and 24 February to 24 August 2019.

2023: 27 August 2022 to 24 February 2023 and 26 February to 26 August 2023.

Comparable 182-day periods outside presidential election years were also examined. For the 2019 comparison, the period ran from 24 February to 24 August. In the leap years 2020 and 2024, the equivalent periods ended on 23 August to maintain the same number of days.

The analysis describes changes in recorded incidents and associated estimated fatalities. It does not establish that elections caused those changes or that the attacks were election-related.

ACLED’s records depend partly on the availability and quality of conflict reporting. Its fatality figures are estimates compiled from reported events and should not be treated as independently verified death counts.

Source: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), incident-level dataset supplied to PREMIUM TIMES in October 2026.

World.title: Ebola: ₦100,000 weekly allowance for quarantined contacts was unplanned – NCDC
World.content:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has revealed that its decision to pay ₦100,000 weekly to people quarantined over possible exposure to Ebola was an unplanned, temporary measure introduced on compassionate grounds after some threatened to leave the facilities.

The NCDC Director-General, Jide Idris, disclosed this on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, explaining that the agency introduced the payments to address concerns raised by quarantined contacts who said their absence from home was affecting their families and businesses.

Mr Idris said the authorities had taken affected people out of their normal environments for public health reasons, making it necessary to consider their welfare while ensuring they complied with quarantine measures.

“Those people who were in the quarantine area, there are people who never planned to be there. We took them out of their comfort zones to put them there for public health reasons,” he said.

Mr Idris said the agency had taken responsibility for their feeding and accommodation but faced complaints from some quarantined contacts who said they had families to support and businesses to run.

He said some threatened to leave the facilities because of the disruption to their daily lives, a development he described as a potential public health concern.

“If you allow them to leave the place, it’s a public health issue because you don’t know whether they will turn positive or who is ill,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Idris explained that the financial support was introduced to ease tensions and encourage affected people to remain in quarantine for the period health authorities require.

He said the arrangement was temporary and had not been part of the agency’s original budget.

“It’s a temporary thing because it’s not something we’ve done,” he said, adding that the government had to intervene because the expected support from state governments was not forthcoming.

State governments’ responsibilities

Mr Idris said state governments were responsible for providing quarantine facilities and the resources needed to manage people placed under public health restrictions.

He said the NCDC stepped in to address the immediate welfare concerns of the quarantined contacts because the necessary support had not been provided.

The agency’s intervention, he explained, was intended to prevent people from leaving designated facilities before completing the required monitoring period.

Nigeria’s Ebola response

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the NCDC approved a weekly allowance of N100,000 for each person quarantined following possible exposure to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

Speaking on Channels Television on Monday, Mr Idris said the number of identified contacts had increased to 54 after authorities traced an Uber driver who transported the patient to the first hospital where she sought treatment.

The contacts include healthcare workers, the patient’s husband, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples.

They are being monitored for 21 days after their last possible exposure, in line with Ebola’s incubation period.

Nigeria confirmed the imported Ebola case on 20 October, its first since the 2014 outbreak. The patient, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja, was subsequently evacuated to Switzerland alongside her husband.

The woman is receiving treatment in Geneva, while her husband, who had shown no symptoms, remains in isolation in Zurich.

Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation said Nigeria had no remaining confirmed Ebola cases, noting that contact monitoring and other public health measures continue.

World.title: CBD COP17: Nigeria’s environment minister arrives Armenia for biodiversity talks
World.content:
Nigeria’s Minister of Environment, Balarabe Lawal, has arrived in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia, to participate in the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Biodiversity Conference (CBD COP17).

Mr Lawal arrived on Monday, ahead of the high-level segment scheduled for 27 and 28 October, when ministers and other senior government officials are expected to address barriers to implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), adopted in 2022.

According to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Secretariat, approximately 1,500 people, including 140 ministers and deputy ministers of finance and environment, are expected to participate in the high-level segment.

The segment comes as negotiations enter their final stretch, with delegates seeking to translate global biodiversity commitments into concrete action before the conference concludes.

The CBD Secretariat said negotiators made progress during the opening week, adopting four decisions under COP17 on invasive alien species, gender, education and knowledge management.

Eight substantive decisions were also adopted under the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, covering monitoring and reporting, compliance, and the strengthening of national processes for effective implementation.

Additionally, two decisions advancing the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing were achieved, focusing on monitoring and reporting and compliance.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Among other issues, the global review of progress towards the biodiversity framework will consider evidence from the State of Biodiversity Action report, launched by UN Secretary-General António Guterres ahead of COP17. The report found widespread national commitment but significant gaps in ambition and implementation.

“COP17 is enabling a total mobilisation of more than $1.8 billion from all sources — governments, philanthropic organisations and investors — in support of strong biodiversity action,” said COP17 President Hambardzum Matevosyan.

“The first week has shown that cooperation can deliver progress. The second week must demonstrate that political commitment can deliver action.”

Nigeria, Africa’s priorities

Since negotiations began last week, biodiversity financing has remained one of the most contentious issues, particularly for developing countries seeking substantial financial support to implement the global framework.

Discussions have focused on mobilising additional public and private funding, improving access to existing resources and redirecting environmentally harmful subsidies towards activities that support nature conservation.

A major issue is the implementation of the Cali Fund, established following COP16 to support benefit-sharing from the commercial use of digital sequence information (DSI) on genetic resources.

The mechanism seeks to ensure that companies benefiting from the commercial use of such information contribute to biodiversity conservation and its sustainable use.

For African countries, the debate is closely linked to equity, resource ownership and the continent’s capacity to finance conservation.

African negotiators argue that the continent’s rich biological resources support commercial activities worldwide, while the benefits generated from their use do not adequately reach the countries and communities from which those resources originate.

They are pushing for benefit-sharing arrangements that deliver tangible financial resources for biodiversity protection, community development and the implementation of national conservation plans.

Negotiators are also discussing ways to mobilise private investment and redirect environmentally harmful subsidies. The global biodiversity framework calls for at least $500 billion annually in harmful incentives to be eliminated or redirected by 2030.

Upon his arrival at the COP17 venue, Mr Lawal was received by Nigerian delegates and national focal points.

The minister also formally presented certificates for the $50,000 Rapid Deployment Mechanism (RDM) grants won by Nigeria and six other countries to Joseph Onoja, director-general of the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), and members of his team.

PREMIUM TIMES reported earlier that Nigeria and six other countries under the High Ambition Coalition (HAC) for Nature and People won $50,000 seed grants each under the RDM to execute projects aimed at accelerating progress towards their 30×30 conservation targets.

The 30×30 target seeks to ensure that at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and sea areas are effectively conserved and managed by 2030.

Mr Lawal is expected to deliver Nigeria’s national statement during the high-level segment.

Final stretch

As the UN Biodiversity Conference enters its final week, governments face the challenge of resolving outstanding disagreements over biodiversity financing and economic incentives that continue to drive nature loss.

The conference comprises COP17, the 12th Meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and the sixth Meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing. It is scheduled to close on Friday.

The CBD Secretariat said the second week of negotiations must demonstrate that political commitments can translate into action.

Conference organisers said achieving meaningful results would require governments to place biodiversity at the centre of economic and financial decision-making, a priority underscored by the participation of finance ministers.

“Nature is not a luxury we protect when economies can afford it. Nature is what makes economies possible. The arrival of finance ministers at COP17 sends an important signal,” said Inger Andersen, United Nations under-secretary-general and executive director of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

“Biodiversity loss is not simply an environmental problem. It is an economic problem, and the solutions must reach into the heart of economic decision-making.”

The scale of the challenge is reflected in financial incentives that continue to drive biodiversity loss, often undermining investments in conservation and restoration.

“Financing the destruction of nature with 30 dollars against every dollar spent restoring it is like paying 30 people to tear down your house for every one hired to rebuild it,” said Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the CBD.

Ms Schomaker identified three priorities for translating commitments into results: accountability, alignment and acceleration.

Accountability involves using national reports, scientific evidence and the first global review to identify shortcomings and guide stronger action.

Alignment requires ensuring that public budgets, private investments, economic policies and financial incentives support, rather than undermine, global biodiversity objectives.

Acceleration entails moving faster to implement the framework’s 23 targets by 2030.

“The global review showed us where progress is being made and where we are falling behind,” she said. “Yerevan focuses all Parties on closing those gaps.”

However, closing the gaps will require governments to overcome significant differences in the negotiations.

Major questions remain over which countries and stakeholders should contribute to international biodiversity financing, how much funding should be mobilised and the mechanisms through which the resources should be channelled.

Parties also remain divided over language on reducing or phasing out harmful incentives, including agricultural subsidies.

Other unresolved issues include which commercial users of digital sequence information should contribute to the Cali Fund, arrangements for a new permanent body on Indigenous Peoples and local communities under Article 8(j) of the Convention, and how biodiversity action should align with climate commitments and other international obligations.

World.title: Oyebanji seeks Ekiti assembly’s approval to reappoint three ex-commissioners, 10 special advisers
World.content:
Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has sought the House of Assembly’s approval to reappoint three commissioners and 10 new special advisers as he begins his second term in office.

The request comes after Mr Oyebanji’s swearing-in on 16 October for another four-year term, with the governor pledging to sustain ongoing projects, strengthen service delivery and consolidate its achievements.

In a letter addressed to the speaker of the assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye, on Monday, the governor requested the screening and confirmation of Dayo Apata, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Akintunde Oyebode as Commissioner for Finance, and Oyebanji Filani as Commissioner for Health and Human Services.

The governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Olayinka Oyebode, disclosed the requests in a statement on Tuesday.

According to the statement, the proposed appointments are intended to ensure continuity in key areas of governance and enable the administration to settle into its second term.

“The proposed appointments reflect the governor’s intention to constitute key components of his administration early and ensure continuity in critical sectors of governance,” the statement read.

It added that the justice, finance and health portfolios were considered crucial to the effective take-off of the new administration, particularly amid prevailing developments in the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oyebanji also sought the assembly’s approval to appoint 10 new special advisers to support the day-to-day administration of the state. The statement did not disclose their names or specify the portfolios they would oversee.

The requests follow the governor’s recent appointments in the power, road infrastructure and transportation sectors, which were announced last week as part of efforts to organise his second-term administration.

The governor appointed Philip Atere as technical advisor for power infrastructure, Tope Fatukasi as technical advisor for road infrastructure, Sunday Makinde as technical advisor for airport, and Tajudeen Alingbolu as the Director -General, Ekiti State Transport Agency.
