World.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

…As Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report

By Henry Umoru

President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country.

President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio.

Akpabio, who read the letter on Tuesday during plenary, said the request covers the 2026–2027 fiscal period and targets critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security.

Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing was necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects.

In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing would support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy.

“The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said.

According to the letter, the proposed facilities total $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643, and the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments.

“I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said.

The president who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said, “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.”

He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation, adding that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it have made additional external borrowing necessary.

“In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” Tinubu said.

He identified power, transportation and healthcare as among the critical sectors expected to benefit from the proposed financing.

“These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the president said.

Tinubu, who maintained that prompt consideration of the request would enable the government to meet its obligations to Nigerians through timely disbursement of funds and effective execution of the projects, said, “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.”

The President, who noted that legislative approval would enable the government to proceed with the proposed interventions, said, “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.”

The President of the Senate thereafter referred the Communication to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative action to report at plenary within one week.

The Committee is expected to examine the proposal, potentially in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees.

The letter, as presented to the Senate, did not provide a detailed project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the specific financing terms or the amount earmarked for each sector.

The National Assembly’s consideration of the request is expected to focus on the proposed financing and its intended development objectives, including the government’s plan to close infrastructure gaps, stimulate economic activities and improve public services.

The letter titled “Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans, read, ” I write in reference to the above subjects and to submit the attached Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects.

“The 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security, and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others.

“The total facility for the projects and programs under the Borrowing Growing Plan is $20,517,000,000 and €1,045,083,643 respectively and the summary of the breakdown is attached to this presents.

“So, Distinguished colleagues, in light of the removal of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901, and €1,045,083,643.

” I want to emphasize that the projects and programs included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country.

“These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skilled acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.

“The majority of these projects and programs will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall.

“These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others.

“Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilizing the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.

“This will enable the government to fulfill its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.

“This request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, probably in collaboration with the Preparation and Finance, but majorly by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts. And you can report back in one week.”

World.title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
World.content:
Aston Villa’s Senegalese striker #11 Nicolas Jackson (L) watches his shot as Manchester City’s Italian goalkeeper #01 Gianluigi Donnarumma concedes a second goal during the English Premier League football match between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park in Birmingham, central England on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa.

Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games.

Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference.

Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday.

“Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes.

“But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.”

And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi.

“Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest.

“And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.”

Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias.

“After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.”

AFP

World.title: Resign, support Obi, KNN replies RMRDC boss
World.content:
Peter Obi

.Challenges Shettima to explain subsidy savings, rising debt

By Steve Oko

The Kwankwaso National Network, KNN, has challenged the Director-General of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council, RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, to resign his appointment and support the presidential ambition of his kinsman, Mr Peter Obi, rather than campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election based on selfish interests.

KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North.

The group, a support network for Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the position as disappointing, arguing that Nigeria needed leadership capable of addressing economic hardship, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power rather than continuity with policies it blamed for the country’s difficulties.

KNN sought to know how Obi’s emergence as Nigeria’s President in 2027 would disadvantage the South as claimed by Ike-Muonso, asking whether Obi is a Northerner.

The group argued that Obi who had declared his intention to be in office for only one term if elected, will only be completing the turn of the South.

KNN in a statement by its South East Regional Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the 2027 election should be about competence, accountability and national recovery, not merely regional power rotation.

“2027 is not about the continuation of misgovernance and ineptitude; it is about rescuing Nigeria from total collapse,” the group declared.

It described Obi as a credible alternative with national appeal across ethnic and religious divides, urging Nigerians dissatisfied with the current administration to support his presidential project.

KNN also criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima over his reported remark that Obi had nothing to offer beyond statistics.

Shettima made the comment at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he questioned Obi’s economic proposals and his opposition to the restoration of petrol subsidy.

Challenging the Vice President, KNN said he should counter Obi’s figures with verifiable data rather than make sweeping allegations.

The group also demanded explanations for the administration’s borrowing despite its claims of increased fiscal savings following petrol subsidy removal in May 2023.

It challenged Shettima to provide a transparent account of the savings generated, how the funds had been deployed and the tangible benefits Nigerians had received.

KNN further questioned the progress made in rehabilitating Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, demanding clarity on expenditure, operational capacity and timelines for delivering results.

The group argued that Nigerians deserved measurable improvements in living standards, energy security and economic opportunities rather than repeated assurances of recovery.

It warned that political rhetoric would not shield the All Progressives Congress, APC, from electoral rejection if the government failed to address citizens’ concerns.

KNN maintained that the 2027 election should be determined by candidates’ competence, policy proposals and performance, insisting that Nigerians deserved accountability and a government that prioritised their welfare.

World.title: Venus Williams suffers 16th defeat in a row with loss to teenager
World.content:
Venus Williams

Venus Williams suffered her 16th loss in a row in singles tennis as the 46-year-old American icon was defeated by teenager Lilli Tagger in straight sets at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday.

Austria’s Tagger, who is 28 years younger than the former world number one, eased through 6-2, 6-2 in southern China.

Williams, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July last year.

Now ranked 599 in the world, Williams last played at the US Open in August-September, when she lost in the first round in straight sets to Sofia Kenin.

Williams won in the doubles with Indonesia’s Janice Tjen in Guangzhou on Monday.

They will play again on Wednesday.

The 53rd-ranked Tagger faces Magda Linette of Poland in the next round.

AFP

World.title: Niger Miners’ deaths: Panel details roles of NSCDC commandant and four officers
World.content:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

By Ayobami Okerinde

The independent ministerial committee probing the deaths of miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has detailed the alleged roles of the suspended Niger State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and four other officers in the incident.

The committee accused the officials of various acts of misconduct, including unlawful detention, failure to respond to distress signals, poor supervision and attempts to alter the detention facility before an independent forensic examination.

The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja on Tuesday.

In its findings, the panel said Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without adequate planning, approval or oversight, permitted overcrowding and failed to ensure that detainees were held in accordance with lawful procedures.

“The committee found extensive failures of leadership, supervision and professional conduct. State Commandant Suberu Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without proper planning, approval or oversight,” Kure said.

“He permitted overcrowding, failed to ensure lawful detention practices and later issued a false public statement attributing the deaths to a disease outbreak. The committee concluded that his actions reflected gross leadership failure, abuse of authority and serious professional misconduct.”

The committee identified CSC Oluwadare Sunday, head of the Investigation Unit, as another officer whose actions contributed to the failures. It said he facilitated unlawful detention practices, disregarded legal and medical concerns and failed to intervene despite knowing that conditions in the detention facility were deteriorating.

SC Usman Isah Ndamaka was accused of maintaining overcrowded conditions and instructing subordinates not to open the cell. According to the panel, he also failed to respond appropriately to emergency alerts and participated in cleaning and altering the detention area before independent investigators examined it.

The committee further faulted Station Guard ASCI Hassan Mohammed for allegedly failing to open the cell despite repeated distress signals and not adequately escalating the emergency.

Another officer, DSC Sule Garba, was accused of profiling detainees, including minors, without adequately protecting their rights. The panel also said he failed to properly document exhibits.

DSC Musa Marafa was accused of unlawfully arresting and detaining one Emmanuel Emeka over a civil death dispute. The committee said his actions contributed to Emeka’s continued detention until his death alongside other detainees.

Beyond the conduct of the individual officers, the committee identified broader institutional shortcomings within the NSCDC, including inadequate detention facilities, weak custodial oversight, the absence of closed-circuit television monitoring, poor record-keeping and insufficient emergency medical capacity.

Other deficiencies listed in the report included ineffective supervision, weak intelligence reporting arrangements, workforce imbalance and chronic underfunding.

The panel warned that these weaknesses created conditions in which serious violations could occur without timely detection or intervention.

The committee said the investigation also faced challenges that limited aspects of the forensic assessment. It said the detention register for September 16, 2026, was unavailable, while 30 of the 33 deceased persons had been buried before post-mortem examinations could be conducted.

It added that the detention area had been cleaned, disinfected and altered before independent forensic investigators arrived, affecting aspects of the examination.

World.title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
World.content:
Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time.

A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17.

Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added.

The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week.

Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed.

In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty.

He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon.

Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football.

Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football.

tsc/jde/mw/pi

World.title: Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in
World.content:
England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane speaks after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Harry Kane said Tuesday that his Ballon d’Or triumph “feels like a dream” as tributes poured in for the first English winner of the award in a generation.

The England and Bayern Munich forward fended off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to be named the world’s best men’s footballer at the London Palladium theatre late on Monday.

Wembley was lit up to recognise Kane’s achievement, with England’s X account carrying the message: “The home of the world’s best footballer.”

The former Tottenham forward is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

The 33-year-old struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

The England captain, who also picked up the men’s striker of the year award, scored six times as his side finished third at the World Cup in North America.

“It sounds crazy to be honest but it sounds pretty good,” Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday. “What a special night. An incredible feeling. I’m still just trying to take it all in really. It feels really, really like a dream.

“The emotion (when his name was called) was relief, joy, happiness, excitement. There was so much waiting to find out the winner and in that moment it was quite nerve-wracking so to have that kind of release and to be able to share it with everyone there in that theatre was special.”

Prince William, patron of the Football Association, praised the England skipper.

“What a fantastic achievement and so deserved,” he wrote on Instagram.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.”

– Superlatives –

England boss Thomas Tuchel, who was Bayern boss when Kane arrived in Germany in 2023, said the Three Lions were “lucky” to have him as their leader.

“I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world,” he said.

“To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.”

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice described Kane as “incredible” while Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, another international teammate, said he was the “best ever”.

Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer said the award was “a proud day for FC Bayern”.

“Harry Kane can do it all –- and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (as previous Ballon d’Or winners) –- that says everything about our history,” he said.

“The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. We are proud that this all-round outstanding sportsman and person is part of our FC Bayern family.”

Harry Redknapp, former Tottenham manager, described his all-round game as “brilliant”.

“It isn’t just his goalscoring that is good, it is his all-round play, and the way he is and the way he is around the players. He is great as the England captain,” he told the BBC.

“No one could have deserved this more, it has been a brilliant story.”

AFP

World.title: Court Grants $100m Mareva Order in Chappal Energies Dispute, Bars Asset Takeover
World.content:
Wale Igbintade



The Federal High Court in Lagos has issued three interim orders restraining R28 Limited and its Founder, Adebisi Adebutu, from taking over the operational assets of two companies, dealing with financial assets worth up to $100 million and effecting changes to their corporate records.

Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa, in an order issued on October 22, 2026, restrained the two respondents from seizing or interfering with the operational premises, management, physical assets, and commercial equipment of Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited.

The Judge also granted a Mareva order restricting dealings with financial assets up to $100 million or its equivalent in other currencies, while directing the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) to preserve the companies’ corporate records and reject specified changes to their directorship, shareholding and signatory authority.

The orders were made pending the hearing and determination of the applicants’ motion on notice for interlocutory injunction.

The suit, marked FHC/LAG/FR/500/2026, was filed on October 14, 2026, by Ufoma Joseph Immanuel, Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited.

The respondents are R28 Limited, Adebutu, Michael Humphries, the CAC, Zenith Bank Plc, Fidelity Bank Plc, Access Bank Plc, and Rand Merchant Bank.

Under the Mareva order, R28 Limited and Adebutu, whether acting personally or through their agents, privies, representatives, nominees or other persons acting on their instructions, are restrained from transferring, withdrawing, removing, dissipating, assigning, encumbering or otherwise dealing with funds and other financial assets covered by the order.

The restriction applies to monies, deposits and financial assets standing to the credit of accounts maintained in their personal or corporate names, including accounts operated through proxies or shell entities with Zenith Bank, Fidelity Bank, Access Bank or any other commercial bank, financial institution or electronic platform in Nigeria.

The financial restraint is capped at $100 million or its equivalent in other currencies.

The order does not, however, establish that the sum has been recovered, confiscated or identified in any particular account. It is an interim restriction intended to preserve assets pending further proceedings.

On the companies’ operations, Justice Lewis-Allagoa restrained the first and second respondents from entering upon, seizing, taking over or interfering with the operational premises, management, physical assets and commercial equipment of Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited in Nigeria.

The judge also directed the CAC, the fourth respondent, to maintain the status quo in the corporate registers of the two companies and refuse to register changes to their directorship, shareholding or signatory authority submitted by R28 Limited or Adebutu, particularly changes relating to Michael Humphries, the third respondent.

The order followed an ex parte application supported by an affidavit sworn to by Immanuel.

The court made the orders after considering the application and hearing submissions from the applicants’ counsel, comprising K. Braithwaite, Wogu Christian, Olaoluwakitan Braithwaite and Hilda Nwankwo.

In their application, the claimants sought to prevent interference with the companies’ operations and assets, preserve the financial assets covered by the Mareva order and forestall changes to their corporate records pending the determination of their motion for interlocutory injunction.

The latest order is one of a series of legal disputes reportedly involving Immanuel, the founder and managing director of Chappal Energies, and Adebutu over a commercial disagreement centred on control and the allotment of shares in the company, which Immanuel founded in 2022.

Justice Lewis-Allagoa adjourned the matter till December 4, 2026, for further proceedings.

World.title: Nigeria Doesn’t Need Tourist President, Adeyeye Tells Atiku
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale and Hassan Amina in Abuja



The Chairman, Board of Directors of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has declared that Nigeria does not need a tourist president who runs to Dubai whenever there is a crisis.

Adeyeye stated this while addressing a press conference yesterday in Abuja, describing the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar as a “jumper” who had defected to six political parties in 19 years.

He said Atiku could not fix the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) that made him vice president for eight years, asking how would he fix Nigeria of 230 million people?

Adeyeye stated: “My brothers, a man who cannot build a political party cannot build Nigeria of 230 million. PDP to AC to PDP to APC to PDP to ADC. Six parties in 19 years. Small crisis, he runs to Dubai. If he cannot stay to fix PDP that made him vice president, how will he stay to fix Nigeria?

“When Obasanjo wanted to crush him, where did he run to? Bourdillon —to Tinubu. Tinubu gave him AC (Action Congress). Gave him a platform. A man who ran to Tinubu for refuge now wants to challenge Tinubu? Asiwaju is his master in politics and nation building.”

Adeyeye noted that Atiku lives in Dubai, and only comes when election season comes, contests, loses, and runs back, adding that that is not residence, that is tourism and Nigeria does not need a tourist President.

He emphasised that Atiku’s only economic plan is to sell, stressing that as Chairman of the National Council on Privatisation, he sold NITEL, NICON, Ajaokuta steel rolling.

Adeyeye added: “He lives in Dubai, comes only when election comes, loses, runs back. His only plan is to sell. As privatization chairman, he sold NITEL, NICON, Ajaokuta – all died. Now he wants to sell NNPC and our new ports.

“Tinubu built AD (Alliance for Democracy), built ACN (Action Congress of Nigeria), built APC (All Progressives Congress). Built Lagos from N600 million to N51 billion Internally Generated Revenue (IGR). Built a party, built a city, now building a nation.

“Atiku only jumps. Defect, contest, lose, run away. Nigerians must choose: Builder or Jumper? Stayer or Tourist? A President who pays you while alive, or one who lets you die waiting?

“Tinubu has done the painful surgery. Let us allow him to complete the healing.”

Adeyeye revealed that President Bola Tinubu approved the sum of N758 billion to clear pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with 957,045 pensioners paid.

He added that the president reintroduced 100 per cent gratuity under the Exit Benefit Scheme for federal workers in January, ending a 20-year period when retirees went home without gratuity.

He added that the administration also cleared the $3.4 billion International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan inherited on assumption of office, with the IMF confirming zero principal as of April 30, 2025.

The chairman noted that the administration has commenced repayment of the N22.7 trillion Ways and Means securitised to 40 years, with N613 billion paid as of June this year.

He stated: “President Tinubu approved N758 billion to clear pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with 957,045 pensioners paid.

“No president has ever done what Tinubu did. In one decision, he approved N758 billion to clear pension debts from 2007.”

On debt management, Adeyeye said the administration cleared the $3.4 billion IMF loan inherited on assumption of office, with the IMF confirming zero principal as of April 30, 2025, and had commenced repayment of the N22.7 trillion Ways and Means securitised to 40 years, with N613 billion paid as of June this year.

He said removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms led to a surge in Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) disbursements from N14.11 trillion in 2024 to N26.5 trillion in 2025, and N33.27 trillion between January and November 2025 alone.

Adeyeye cited World Bank data showing GDP growth rising from 3.5 percent in first half of 2024 to 4.2 percent in first half of 2026, inflation declining from 27.6 percent in January 2025 to 15.2 percent in December 2025, and foreign reserves growing from $33 billion in 2023 to $53.8 billion.

On governance reforms, he said Tinubu approached the Supreme Court to secure financial autonomy for 774 local governments in a judgment delivered July 11, 2024, and initiated the State Police constitutional amendment, which he said has been approved by 24 of 36 states.

World.title: Tinubu Decries Murder Of Katsina Cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka
World.content:
* Directs relevant security agencies to thoroughly investigate the heinous act

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has condemned the murder of a prominent Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State.

Unknown gunmen killed the duo in a drive-by shooting incident on Monday evening.

The president, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, in a release issued on Tuesday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and sanctity of human life.

Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, as well as the government and people of Katsina State, over the tragic loss.

The president has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice.

Tinubu prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and comfort for all those who mourn their death.

World.title: Katsina Boosts Vocational Skills with N4bn Investment
World.content:
Katsina State Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda, has disclosed that his administration has invested over N4 billion in renovating, upgrading and equipping the Katsina Youth Craft Village (KYCV) to boost vocational skills in the state.

Radda disclosed this on Monday during the graduation ceremony of 1,662 trainees held at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium in Katsina.

He explained that the number of graduates represents a 156.79 per cent increase from the 648 trainees recorded at the institution’s maiden graduation ceremony.

He said the investment was part of his administration’s Building Your Future Agenda, designed to equip young people with practical skills and transform them from job seekers into job creators.

“When this administration came into office, we made a commitment under our Building Your Future Agenda to prioritise youth empowerment, skills acquisition and job creation. We promised to transform our young people from job seekers into job creators,” the governor said.

Radda explained that the government had provided modern machines, tools and equipment at the centre to ensure that trainees acquired industry-relevant skills and could establish viable businesses after graduation.

“We do not believe in simply issuing certificates and sending our graduates home without the means to put their training into practice. That is why we are providing them with start-up tools and equipment to enable them to establish their businesses,” he added.

The governor said the graduates received training in more than 15 trades, including tailoring, welding and fabrication, carpentry, electrical installation, information and communication technology, catering, cosmetology, plumbing and automobile repairs.

He also disclosed that the government had established a modern innovation hub and an innovation desk at the centre to encourage creativity, technological advancement and entrepreneurship.

Describing vocational education as a critical tool for addressing unemployment, Radda announced plans to establish additional training centres across the state’s 34 local government areas.

“Our target is to train and empower more than 5,000 young people through vocational training initiatives before the end of our tenure,” he said.

He further revealed that the Katsina State Enterprise Development Agency had supported more than 60,000 beneficiaries through various enterprise development programmes.

Radda urged the graduates to make productive use of the start-up packages provided by the government rather than sell them.

“I urge you not to sell your start-up packs. Use them to establish your businesses, grow your enterprises and create employment opportunities for others,” he advised.

In his remarks, a former governor of the state, Ibrahim Shehu Shema, recalled that the Katsina Youth Craft Village was established during his administration to equip young people, particularly those from rural communities, with practical and marketable skills.

He stressed that technical and vocational education remained essential to youth self-reliance, entrepreneurship and economic development.

“The importance of technical and vocational education cannot be overemphasised. It provides young people with practical skills to become self-reliant, establish businesses and contribute meaningfully to society,” he said.

Earlier, the Coordinator of the Katsina Youth Craft Village, Kabir Abdullahi Kofar Soro, described the graduation ceremony as a significant milestone in the state’s youth empowerment efforts.

He highlighted the increase in the number of graduates from 648 at the maiden ceremony to 1,662 at the second edition, attributing the achievement to the state government’s support and expansion of the institution.

“This achievement would not have been possible without the direct intervention and support of His Excellency, particularly his commitment to youth development and approval for the expansion of the Katsina Youth Craft Village,” he said.

World.title: Obi Vows to Wage War on Corruption, Promises Nigerians Results From Day One
World.content:
• NDC presidential candidate pledges emergency measures on security, agriculture, education, healthcare, electricity

• Promises 20% of credit to SMEs, primary healthcare centres in every ward within two years

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has vowed to wage an uncompromising war against corruption and ensure the transparent management of public resources, declaring that Nigerians would begin to see measurable improvements in governance from the first day of an NDC administration.

Obi, who is contesting the January 16, 2027 presidential election with former Kano State governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, as his running mate, also promised emergency interventions in security, agriculture, education, healthcare and electricity, insisting that Nigeria could no longer afford leadership that blamed previous administrations for its failures.

He made the commitments in Abuja at a dinner organised to inaugurate the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council and present certificates of return to its candidates, following the unveiling of its new national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja.

The former Anambra State governor said his administration would prioritise problem-solving, accountability and measurable outcomes rather than political excuses, arguing that public officeholders must demonstrate how the country’s resources translate into improved living conditions.

“The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. Kwankwaso and I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible,” he declared.

Obi accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of failing to translate increased government revenues and borrowing into commensurate improvements in Nigerians’ living conditions.

He said the country needed leadership that would respond directly to the challenges confronting citizens, particularly insecurity, hunger, unemployment, poverty and the rising cost of living.

“From my engagements all over Nigeria, Nigerians are looking for new leadership. And we assure you that we will create that new leadership,” he said.

Obi made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his campaign, promising to ensure that public funds served the interests of Nigerians rather than being diverted for private benefit.

He argued that corruption had weakened public institutions, undermined development spending, discouraged productive investment and contributed to the country’s persistent economic difficulties.

Questioning the management of government revenues and borrowed funds under the Tinubu administration, he demanded greater transparency in public expenditure and challenged the Federal Government to account for its spending and development projects.

“We must stop people from stealing public money. We must use public money for the public good. And that will be seen, it will be shown,” he said.

The NDC candidate insisted that public officials found culpable of corruption must be held accountable in accordance with the law.

He also questioned the implementation of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 budgets, alleging that capital expenditure remained below 20 per cent and that contractors were experiencing difficulties receiving payments for completed projects.

Obi challenged the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a detailed account of its expenditure, projects and achievements, arguing that citizens deserved tangible improvements rather than repeated explanations of the country’s problems.

“We don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. It’s only in Nigeria that you hire people, and they start reminding you of what happened in the past.

“No, we don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. We want you to hire us to improve from today,” he said.

On security, Obi promised a more direct presidential response to kidnapping, violent attacks and other threats to lives and property, insisting that the president must demonstrate leadership by visiting communities affected by emergencies.

He argued that the country’s security challenges required urgent action and a leadership willing to engage directly with affected communities rather than remain distant from the realities confronting victims.

“If they say there is a problem in Jos, he will go to Jos,” he said.

Obi pledged to visit communities affected by insecurity in Plateau, Benue, Zamfara, Sokoto and Borno States, among others, and criticised what he described as excessive foreign travel by the president.

He maintained that Nigeria needed a leader who would devote greater attention to domestic challenges and demonstrate solidarity with citizens facing violence, displacement and economic hardship.

The NDC candidate also promised emergency measures to revive agriculture, particularly in northern Nigeria, where insecurity has disrupted farming activities and restricted access to productive land.

He said restoring security in farming communities would enable farmers to return to their fields, increase food production, reduce dependence on imports and strengthen the supply of raw materials to local industries.

“We have vast land in the north. When we secure the north, our farmers must go back and produce what we eat and what we use for our industries,” he said.

He linked agricultural recovery to the broader task of tackling hunger, stabilising food prices, creating employment and moving the economy away from excessive dependence on consumption and borrowing.

Obi also pledged emergency interventions in education, expressing concern over the number of Nigerian children outside the formal school system.

He argued that the country could not achieve sustainable development without investing in human capital and ensuring that children from disadvantaged backgrounds had access to quality education.

Drawing on his experience as governor of Anambra State, he said education should serve as a pathway to opportunity, regardless of a person’s family background or social connections.

“We must create a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said.

On healthcare, Obi renewed his promise to establish a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward within two years of assuming office.

He said the proposed intervention would bring basic medical services closer to communities, improve access to treatment and reduce preventable deaths.

The former governor also pledged emergency measures to address persistent electricity shortages, describing reliable power supply as indispensable to industrial growth, job creation and economic recovery.

“We will declare emergency on generation, transmission, and distribution,” he said.

Obi argued that unreliable electricity had increased operating costs for businesses, burdened households and constrained the productive capacity of Nigerian industries.

He called for the revival of manufacturing establishments across the country, citing the decline of industries in Kano as an example of the economic consequences of inadequate infrastructure and weak industrial development.

He said Nigeria must transition from an economy driven largely by consumption and borrowing to one built on production, investment and job creation.

Small and medium-sized enterprises also featured prominently in Obi’s economic proposals, with the NDC candidate promising improved access to credit, tax relief and incentives to stimulate business growth.

Citing figures indicating that Nigeria has more than 40 million small businesses, he said the sector remained constrained by limited access to bank financing despite its importance to employment and economic activity.

Obi said an NDC administration would work to ensure that more than 20 per cent of credit went to small businesses, arguing that expanding financing opportunities would enable entrepreneurs to grow their operations and employ more Nigerians.

“We will put a mark to it. We will ensure that over 20% of credits will go to small businesses. We will support them,” he said.

He also promised tax holidays and other incentives to support small businesses, while insisting that government policies must encourage production and enterprise rather than impose burdens that stifle growth.

The proposed measures, he said, would form part of a broader economic strategy to expand employment opportunities, strengthen local production and improve household incomes.

Turning to the 2027 elections, Obi urged political actors to respect the rights of opposition supporters and refrain from intimidating citizens engaged in lawful political activities.

He said political competition should centre on ideas, policies and the credibility of candidates rather than harassment or the suppression of opposing voices.

“Humility and civility are not weaknesses. It is a virtue. Good behaviour is not a weakness. It is a virtue,” he said.

The NDC presidential candidate also urged Nigerians to defend the integrity of the electoral process, insisting that the forthcoming election should provide citizens with an opportunity to determine their political future through the ballot.

“The revolution that is coming is a revolution of the ballot,” he declared.

He called for free, fair and credible elections, maintaining that electoral legitimacy remained fundamental to democratic governance and public confidence in political institutions.

Earlier, NDC National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, described the gathering as a significant milestone in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general election, saying its emergence was driven by the determination to offer Nigerians a different approach to governance.

Cleopas said the party had conducted its primaries within a short period and that the dinner provided an opportunity for candidates, party leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen their commitment to a common political agenda.

He identified the inauguration of the National Presidential Campaign Council and the presentation of certificates of return to candidates as major steps in the party’s preparations for the elections.

The national chairman disclosed that the certificates contained security codes, warning against unauthorised claims to candidacy and insisting that the party would maintain order and accountability in its electoral process.

He challenged candidates to regard their nominations as a responsibility to the electorate rather than a personal achievement, warning that the party would not tolerate unfulfilled campaign promises.

Cleopas urged candidates to make realistic commitments and ensure that, if elected, they delivered on their promises to the people.

“If we fail to bring water for you in two years, if we open our mouths to say, vote for us again, please don’t vote for us,” he said.

He described the party’s political mission as an effort to address the country’s challenges and restore public confidence in leadership.

“We are going for a rescue mission; the hope of this country is in NDC,” Cleopas declared.

The party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the new national secretariat as the NDC’s ‘Noah’s Ark’, presenting the facility as a unifying centre for the party as it prepares for the 2027 elections.

The secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative headquarters and provide a central base for strategic planning, organisational activities and coordination of its nationwide presidential campaign.

The unveiling followed the party’s Third National Executive Committee meeting and formed part of a series of activities designed to strengthen its structures ahead of the general election.

The event brought together Cleopas, Dickson, Senator Victor Umeh, who represents Anambra Central in the Senate; Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs; Adamawa State governorship candidate, Senator Aisha Binani and other party leaders and members.

The inauguration of the campaign council and presentation of certificates of return to candidates marked another phase in the NDC’s electoral preparations.

With the establishment of its national headquarters and the inauguration of its campaign council, the party is seeking to build a nationwide campaign around accountability, economic recovery, improved public services, security and a different approach to leadership ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: Licence Issuing Suspension: Investors Ask  CBN  to Refund N100.35m
World.content:
Promoters of Coin Finance Company Limited have demanded the return of N100.35 million paid to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to operate as a finance house, following the suspension of new licence applications.

A representative of the promoters, Mr Christopher Itua, made the demand in a statement, saying the funds had remained with the apex bank for about 15 months without the proposed institution progressing.

According to him, the investors paid N100 million as capital deposit, N100,000 as application fee and N250,000 as licensing fee on July 16, 2025, bringing the total payment to N100.35 million.

The payment was made as part of the requirements for licensing Coin Finance Company Ltd as a finance house. Itua said CBN officials informed the promoters in October 2025 that processing of new finance house applications had been suspended until further notice.

He explained that following the suspension, he wrote the CBN Department of Financial Policy and Regulation on October 15, 2025, requesting the return of the funds with applicable interest.

The promoters later petitioned the CBN Consumer Protection Department on May 18, 2026, and sent a follow-up letter on July 7, but said they had received neither a refund timeline nor a substantive update.

“It has now been over 14 months since the CBN took possession of our capital,” Itua said in his latest appeal to the CBN Governor.

He said the proposed finance house was designed to address a financing gap at the grassroots and strengthen economic activity at the micro level.

“The finance house is meant to boost grassroots empowerment, a sector that is very important to strengthening the micro economy,” he said.

Itua noted inadequate institutions serving small businesses and grassroots entrepreneurs remained a major constraint despite improvements in the broader macroeconomic environment.

“The macro is doing well, but the micro is not. This is the missing link because there are not enough institutions to power that sector,” he said.

According to him, the prolonged retention of the capital had stalled the promoters’ plans to establish the institution and provide financial support at the grassroots.

The investors are asking the CBN to calculate applicable interest on the N100.35 million from July 16, 2025, when the funds were deposited, until the date of release.

“The prolonged silence and structural failure to return capital deposits directly undermines the Federal Government’s ease-of-doing-business initiatives,” Itua said.

The promoters said their payment receipts, transaction documents and previous correspondence had been submitted to support the request.

Itua appealed to the CBN Governor to intervene and resolve the matter administratively, stressing that the promoters had repeatedly used the bank’s established channels.

They said continued inaction could compel them to pursue further administrative and legal channels, although they preferred to resolve the matter without escalation.

The promoters are seeking the immediate return of the N100.35 million, together with applicable interest from July 16, 2025, until the funds are released.

World.title: 2027: NSCDC Warns Personnel against Election Bias, Voter Intimidation
World.content:
. Stakeholders Task INEC to conduct free, fair, credible elections

Michael Olugbode in Abuja and Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja

The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has warned its personnel against voter intimidation, abuse of citizens and partisan conduct ahead of the 2027 general election, stressing that neutrality and professionalism are essential to protecting Nigerian democracy.

The Commandant-General of the Corps, Prof. Ahmed Audi, gave the warning in Abuja while opening a three-day workshop designed to prepare security personnel for election-related duties.

This is just as stakeholders in Kogi State have unanimously tasked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027

Audi cautioned officers and men of the agency against abandoning their duty posts or obeying unlawful orders, insisting that their overriding responsibility must be to the national interest and the protection of citizens’ democratic rights.

The workshop brought together 216 personnel drawn from the 36 state commands, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and 18 zonal Commands to strengthen their understanding of the legal, operational and supervisory responsibilities of security agencies during elections.

Organised in collaboration with Alnas Consulting Limited, the workshop was built on the theme: ‘Role of Security Agencies in the Conduct of the General Elections in Nigeria: Legal, Field Conduct, Supervisory and Operational Perspectives’.

The Commandant-General’s warning came as preparations gather pace for the 2027 elections, with security agencies expected to play a critical role in ensuring that voters can exercise their franchise without intimidation, harassment or undue interference.

In his welcome address, the Chief Responsibility Officer of Alnas Consulting Limited, Prof. Nasirdeen Usman, described the NSCDC as a critical component of Nigeria’s security architecture and urged participants to share the knowledge acquired with colleagues in their respective commands.

The event also featured goodwill messages from representatives of the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, the Controller-General of Corrections, the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service and the Chief Executive Officer of TAF Africa, Dr Jake Ekpelle.

The NSCDC reiterated its commitment to peaceful elections, effective cooperation among security agencies and the protection of the democratic rights of Nigerians.

Meanwhile, stakeholders in Kogi State have unanimously tasked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027.

This was contained in a communique issued at the end of the critical stakeholders’ meeting held at the headquarters of INEC in Lokoja yesterday.

The stakeholders also agreed that INEC shall adequately supply the political parties and their candidates with useful information as far as the 2027 general election is concerned.

On security matters, the stakeholders noted that the police shall treat all the candidates equally as far as elections matter is concerned in Kogi State.

It was pointed out that all the perpetrators of violent attacks recently be brought to book with immediate effect.

They also stated that all candidates and their party leadership shall conduct their political campaigns in accordance with the law and regulations on election matters, and candidates of political parties shall cooperate with INEC and obtain permission from security agencies before going about campaigns.

“Candidates of all political parties shall ensure the safety of all the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members participating in the general election. Each political party shall cooperate with security agencies,” the communique stressed.

Earlier, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Dr. Shehu Wahab, explained that the commission is poised to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027.

Also, the state Commissioner of Police, Naziru Kankafori, stressed that the security agencies would provide enabling environment for the conduct of violence-free elections in Kogi State.

World.title: PAU Alumni President Calls for Stronger Varsity-Industry Partnerships to Drive Nigeria’s Devt
World.content:
The President of the Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association (PAUAA), Dr. Onyebuchi Odianjo, has called for stronger partnerships between universities and industry to drive Nigeria’s development, strengthen professional networks and create opportunities for sustainable economic growth.

Odianjo made the call at the inaugural Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association International Conference, themed ‘The Advantage: Connecting People, Ideas and Opportunities,’ held at the Ecobank Pan African Centre in Lagos.

She reaffirmed the association’s commitment to building a vibrant alumni community that translates shared values and professional relationships into meaningful collaborations, student support and broader economic impact.

“Our goal remains clear: to build an alumni community whose values extend beyond shared memories to meaningful relationships, mutual support and collective progress. What began as a conversation about the potential of our alumni network grew into a vision for a platform where people, ideas and industries could connect, relationships could become partnerships, and ideas could become opportunities,” Odianjo said.

Delivering the keynote address, MD/CEO, Coleman Technical Industries Limited (Manufacturers of Coleman Wires and Cables), George Olutope Onafowokan, stressed that integrity, character and discipline are fundamental to building sustainable businesses and driving long-term economic development.

He identified vision, focus, discipline, integrity and good character as essential principles for professional and corporate success, urging business leaders to prioritise ethical conduct and sustainable business practices.

“Integrity is your biggest weighted gold, not your car, not your house, not your land. Build it from the day you start your life. The entitlement mentality is the greatest killer of integrity. When you build character and integrity, you derisk yourself, and doing business or leading people becomes seamless,” Onafowokan asserted.

He cautioned business founders against establishing enterprises primarily to finance personal lifestyles, noting that businesses are more likely to survive generational transitions when supported by sound governance, sustainable structures and leadership by example.

In her address, the Vice-Chancellor of Pan-Atlantic University, Professor Enase Okonedo, commended the Alumni Association’s executive committee for organising the conference and highlighted the importance of values-driven leadership in national transformation.

She noted that the university’s growth over the past 34 years reflects the potential of education to develop leaders capable of making meaningful contributions to Nigeria.

“We grew from humble beginnings 34 years ago, starting in a living room in Sierra Leone. Today, we sit across expanded campuses with a collective alumni body of 15,000 between the business school and the university. Think about 15,000 well-formed people who can make a difference in Nigeria. You are the ambassadors, and PAU graduates are beginning to stand out not only for their work ethic, but also for their values,” Okonedo stated.

The conference brought together alumni, business leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen professional relationships, foster university-industry collaboration and explore opportunities for innovation, enterprise development and national progress.

World.title: DA candidate killed days before elections
World.content:
Police are investigating the murder of DA Ward 14 candidate Thulani Mbana, who was shot dead at his home in Zamdela, Free State, on Monday, 26 October 2026. Image: X

A Democratic Alliance (DA) councillor and ward candidate has been shot dead at his home in Zamdela, Free State, just days before the local government elections.

Thulani Mbana, the party’s Ward 14 candidate in Metsimaholo, was killed in Taylor Park on Monday night, 26 October.

According to police, two unidentified men approached his residence at approximately 21:40 and called out to him.



As Mbana approached, one of the men allegedly pulled out a firearm and shot him several times at close range.

Both suspects fled on foot. Mbana died at the scene.

POLICE HUNT FOR KILLERS

Free State police commissioner Lieutenant General Thabang Lesia has assigned the Zamdela Trio Task Team and Serious Organised Crime Unit to investigate the murder.

The motive remains unknown, and police have not established whether the attack was politically motivated.

Authorities have urged residents to avoid spreading unverified information that could compromise the investigation.

ELECTION SECURITY UNDER SPOTLIGHT

Mbana’s murder comes ahead of the local government elections on Wednesday, 4 November.



The Free State Provincial Joint Operational and Intelligence Structure (ProvJOINTS) says it is ready to coordinate security operations across the province.

Lesia warned that police would not tolerate violence or criminal activity and pledged to protect communities during the election period.

Anyone with information can contact investigating officer Captain Sandile Dladla on 082 453 6245 or 073 226 6788.

Anonymous tip-offs can also be submitted through Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or the MySAPS App..

World.title: Why poachers are targeting these two indigenous South African plants
World.content:
'Kaneeltjie' has carrot-like leaves and flowers that release a strong, clove-like fragrance at night. Image: Wikimedia

The illegal harvesting of two indigenous plant species has landed a poacher in court after 104 specimens were stolen from a Cape nature reserve.

Ashley Dirkse was convicted in the Kuils River Magistrate’s Court on 21 October for stealing the plants from Bracken Nature Reserve on 20 May 2024.

The poacher’s haul included Drimia elata, known locally as ‘jeukbol,’ and Pelargonium triste, or ‘kaneeltjie.’ The City of Cape Town and CapeNature confirmed that the plants and bulbs were returned to the reserve and replanted.



City authorities welcomed the return of the bulbous plants. Image: CoCT

Why these indigenous plants are in high demand

Both indigenous plants have long histories of use in traditional South African medicine and domestic crafts, mainly because of the potent chemical compounds in their underground bulbs and tubers.

These underground storage organs helps them survive unfavourable conditions, but also makes them vulnerable to poaching.

‘Jeukbol’ (Drimia elata) is a ‘red-list’ bulbous perennial flowering plant. According to the South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) it remains widespread, but is thought to be declining due to medicinal harvesting.

The bulb of D. elata is actually toxic, but contains cardiac glycosides. Is also has antibacterial, antifungal and other pharmacological properties. It is the third most popular bulbous medicinal plant used in South African traditional therapy.

‘Jeukbol’ is a popular medicinal indigenous plant with wide distribution in Southern Africa. Image: Easyscape

‘Kaneeltjie’ (Pelargonium triste), also known as night-scented pelargonium, has a large underground tuber and distinctive, carrot-like leaves. Its pale-yellow/ purple flowers release a strong, clove-like fragrance at night.

The plant’s tannin-rich tubers are used in Namaqualand for tanning leather. It has traditional uses too, and infusions from the tubers are used for treating dysentery and diarrhoea. The Pelargonium genus is a garden-worthy plant that is sought after in the international horticultural trade.



Plant poaching threatens SA’s natural heritage

Dirkse was sentenced to an R80 000 fine or two years’ imprisonment, wholly suspended for five years. He was also barred for three years from obtaining permits to enter protected areas or pick flora in the Western Cape.

“Hopefully, this sends out a strong message to poachers,” said Cape Town’s Deputy Mayor Eddie Andrews, who is also the City’s Mayco Member for Spatial Planning and Environment.

“I want to remind the public that it is a crime to remove any plants, animals, rocks, shells, or any natural specimen from our reserves, coastline, and protected areas.”

The City and CapeNature warn that illegal harvesting can damage habitats and undermine indigenous plant populations.

Members of the public can report suspected biodiversity crime to their nearest police station, CapeNature on 087 087 9262, or Crime Stop on 08600 10 111.

World.title: Government is hoping for a miracle to keep funding NSFAS
World.content:
What is Treasury's plan to limit NSFAS funding. Image: Pexels

Buried in the final few pages of the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS), the National Treasury spotlights its fiscal risks.

One such risk is the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS).

According to Treasury, it doesn’t have enough money to keep funding NSFAS at its current scale.



The government can’t afford to keep funding NSFAS

NSFAS is one of three fiscal risks National Treasury spotlighted in the budget.

The others are the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant and the cost of the government employee wage bill.

Treasury describes the scheme as a “significant risk.”

According to the MTBPS, the scheme’s “spending requirements exceed the resources available within the higher education baseline.”

But Treasury also admits it doesn’t know the extent of the funding problem.

So the measures it’s putting in place will only reduce “immediate funding risks.”



Treasury intends to mitigate the risk by pooling “available surpluses within the skills development system.”

Beneath the program’s threat to the budget is the hope that something extrinsic might happen to reduce the risk.

Beyond a financial miracle, the government only has one option: fewer people become eligible for NSFAS.

In practice, that could mean the government restricts eligibility or fewer South Africans apply for NSFAS.

More South Africans Applying for NSFAS

NSFAS is on track to receive 1 million applications.

By 19 October 2026, 30 days into the NSFAS admission process opening, 868 626 individuals had applied.

This is 66.3% higher than the total number of applicants in 2018, when NSFAS shifted its funding model from a combination of a bursary and a loan to a bursary.

That year, NSFAS also increased the eligibility criteria from R121 000 per annum to R350 000 and paid out R20.6 billion.

What is the plan to reduce the NSFAS fiscal risk?

The data suggests the plan to make NSFAS more affordable could start in primary school.

In 2017, the government budgeted R77.5 billion for higher education, referred to as “Post-school education and training.”

That same year, National Treasury budgeted R243 billion for basic education.

In the 2026 MTBPS, National Treasury budgeted R363.4 billion for basic education.

It budgeted R157.7 billion for higher education.

The basic education budget has increased 49.5% in 9 years.

However, over the same period, higher education’s budget has increased by 103.6%.

Department 2017 Budget 2026 Budget % Change Basic Education R243 billion R363.4 billion 49.5% Higher Education R77.5 billion R157.7 billion 103.6%

Basic education getting less of the education pie appears to coincide with children dropping out of primary and high school.

A Department of Basic Education report shows more primary school children dropping out between 2018 and 2020.

According to the report, departure ratios (the number of children leaving school between grades) first appear for grade 6 learners in 2019.

With each passing grade, the figures worsen.

World.title: South Africa’s best-rated beaches for families
World.content:
Finding the right beach for a family day out can be tricky. Parents may want somewhere scenic and clean, while children are likely to be more interested in sand, space and water.

A new analysis of 162 655 Google reviews across 119 South African beaches has revealed some of the country’s highest-rated coastal spots, and several stand out as particularly appealing options for families.

The analysis, conducted by SEO Backlinks, was based on Google Maps listings collected on 5 October 2026. Only beaches with at least 200 reviews were included.



While a Google rating cannot tell you whether a beach is safe for swimming or whether lifeguards will be on duty, it can provide an indication of how visitors rate their overall experience.

Here are some of the highly rated beaches worth considering for a family trip.

Struisbaai Main Beach

Google rating: 4.75/5

Reviews: 768

Struisbaai Main Beach is one of the strongest options for families on the list. It shared second place in the national ranking with Robberg 5 Beach and Keurbooms Beach, but had substantially more reviews than either.

Its long sandy beach and relatively warm water are among the features praised by visitors. The beach also has parking and nearby facilities, while visitor information describes it as suitable for young children.



For families looking for somewhere to spend several hours rather than simply admire the scenery, this is one of the more obvious choices.

Coney Glen Beach, Knysna

Google rating: 4.73/5

Reviews: 285

Knysna’s Coney Glen Beach came fifth in the national rankings, scoring 4.73 stars.

The beach is known for its attractive coastal setting and has picnic areas and parking, which can be particularly useful when travelling with children.

It offers a combination of scenery and space without requiring visitors to sacrifice basic conveniences.

Sardinia Bay Beach, Gqeberha

Google rating: 4.72/5

Reviews: 1 134

Sardinia Bay is another strong family option, and one of the most heavily reviewed beaches in the national top 10.

The Gqeberha beach scored 4.72 stars from more than 1 100 Google reviews, making it the sixth-highest-rated beach in the country in the analysis.

Its wide coastal setting makes it a popular choice for visitors looking for a traditional beach day.

It is also significant for families travelling along the Eastern Cape coast, as it provides a highly rated alternative to the Western Cape beaches that dominate the national ranking.

Bakoven Beach, Cape Town

Google rating: 4.71/5

Reviews: 1 162

Bakoven Beach may be small, but its Google rating is impressive. It scored 4.71 stars from more than 1 100 reviews, putting it among the country’s top-rated beaches.

The beach’s sheltered setting and large rocks create calmer sections of water, something visitors frequently mention in reviews.

For families, that can make it an attractive option, although parents should always check current conditions before allowing children into the water.

Llandudno Beach

Google rating: 4.71/5

Reviews: 3 003

Llandudno is one of the most heavily reviewed beaches in the national ranking, with more than 3 000 Google reviews.

Despite the large number of reviews, it maintains an impressive 4.71-star average.

The beach is known for its dramatic scenery and granite boulders, while its Blue Flag status for the 2026/27 season and lifesaving services during the relevant season add to its appeal.

Families should note, however, that there is limited shade and some approaches involve steps.

Pringle Bay Beach

Google rating: 4.71/5

Reviews: 898

Pringle Bay rounds out the selection. It recorded a 4.71-star rating from 898 reviews and is known for its broad sandy stretches and mountain and coastal scenery.

The combination of space and scenery makes it worth considering for families looking for a quieter beach outing away from the biggest city beaches.

The ratings are based on the October 2026 analysis and can change as new Google reviews are submitted.

Google ratings are useful for judging the overall visitor experience, but they should not be used as a measure of swimming safety or water quality.

Conditions can change, and families should check current local advisories, look for lifeguarded swimming areas and follow any warnings or signage at the beach.

World.title: Calls for young Sharks star to earn Springbok call-up
World.content:
Teenage prodigy Zekhethelo Siyaya is fast emerging as one of South African rugby’s most exciting young talents, and increasingly making a persuasive case for inclusion in Rassie Erasmus’ Springbok squad for the upcoming end-of-year tour.

Educated at Westville Boys’ High School, the 19-year-old utility back has made a seamless transition through the Sharks’ youth system into senior rugby.

Comfortable at both fullback and wing, Siyaya caught the attention of fans and the national coaches after stepping up to United Rugby Championship duty, with his footwork, security under the high ball, and all-round composure leading to calls for Erasmus to give him a run sooner rather than later.



Springbok door could open for Siyaya

With veterans such as Cheslin Kolbe and Makazole Mapimpi battling with injuries and set to miss the November Tests, it will be interesting to see whether Siyaya could be accelerated into the Springbok squad, even just primarily as a tourist to gain squad experience.

Siyaya’s swift progression led to a call-up to the Springbok alignment camp earlier this season, followed by a bright but brief performance for South Africa ‘A’ against Zimbabwe.

Continuing his strong form into the current Sharks campaign – including impressive performances in Europe – Siyaya has consistently shown that his skill set translates to the physical demands of northern hemisphere conditions.

With the Springboks seeking to expand their backline depth and blood young talent in European test conditions ahead of the next World Cup cycle, Siyaya’s dynamic attacking edge and rapid development could make him an ideal candidate for an international call-up.

World.title: Navi Pillay says Nobel Peace Prize win feels 'lonely'
World.content:
“The rest of the world is throwing out the statues, they have a graveyard for statues,” she says.

Pillay also described her disbelief when she first learnt she had won the Nobel Peace Prize, saying she had received no prior indication from the institution.

“What was I to believe when I was in this conference in the Nuremberg Courtroom 600 where the Nazis were tried?” she says.

She says the audience heard the announcement before she did.

“So it’s social media and I said no, I want to verify first, it might be a hoax,” she says.

It was only after watching footage of the announcement and hearing her six decades of work acknowledged that she accepted the news was genuine. She says the recognition of her work also helped justify the award.

Pillay says she has not yet spent the prize money or even checked how the Norwegian krone converts to the rand. She plans to consult others on how best to use the money to promote and protect human rights.

World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - eNCA reporter Pule Letshwiti-Jones was awarded with the Whistleblower Award in the Investigative Journalist - Broadcast category.

Letshwiti-Jones has worked tirelessly in covering the Madlanga Commission and all rogue characters implicated during the Commission's proceedings.

"I feel honoured, because as a team we have been working hard," he said.

He says the early mornings and late nights, receiving calls from sources, verifying said sources and stories encompassed by long hours has paid off.
