World.title: From anthems to definitions, the WNBA keeps doing dumb things, and the reason for it will leave you speechless
World.content:
Searching for a late snack outside Chase Center on Monday night after the Golden State Valkyries took care of the Atlanta Dream in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals, I found myself rather speechless.

A woman dressed in a lavender Valkyries jersey saw the media credential around my neck, and, as I stood at the counter of a restaurant trying to decide what to order, she offered to pay for my meal.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

As we chatted, she said that she appreciates so much the media coverage that the WNBA gets because she is such a big fan. Buying a meal for a reporter, she explained, was the least she could do.

Speechless. How unexpectedly nice!

I politely declined, of course, and laughed to myself as it occurred to me that, while my newfound friend could see that I was wearing a media badge (I forgot to take it off as I exited the arena), she undoubtedly didn’t see what media organization I work for.

'STAND OR HIDE IN THE TUNNEL' FOR THE ANTHEM, VALKYRIES WNBA FANS SHOW LOYALTY; READY FOR EARLY FINALS GAME 6

Most diehard WNBA fans probably don’t fully appreciate the coverage we give the WNBA here at Fox News Digital/OutKick.

To our credit, we have given the WNBA credit when credit is due. We have pointed out its rise in TV ratings and attendance numbers. We are all over Caitlin Clark’s mind-blowing impact on the league and on the sports world in general. We have fun keeping up with Sophie Cunningham and we have even written favorably on Angel Reese beyond just her "mebounds."

LONG LIST OF EMBARRASSING WNBA INCIDENTS IS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN SPORTS LEAGUES MADE POLITICS THEIR PRIMARY FOCUS

Yet, unlike most media organizations that cover, strike that – coddle, the WNBA, we have also pointed out the lunacy that can be the WNBA, and rightfully so.

This league. Oh, this league. Lately, it too has left me speechless. If I could type the equivalent of the hand-palming-the-forehead emoji, I would.

Prior to coming here, I covered the WNBA for 24 years, starting in its first season. In the early days, players were humble, and genuinely grateful just to have a place in the United States to play. They were extremely conscious of their place as role models for kids, especially young girls.

The league, which represented a long-time-coming for professional women’s team sports, was easy to root for. I felt good taking my young kids to games, especially my daughter. I encouraged the girls on the grade school basketball teams I coached to dream big and aspire to be WNBA players someday.

I can’t say that I would give that same advice today.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Many of the players today seem entitled and bratty, flat-out unlikable.

And over the last three to five years, the WNBA as a league has done so many stupid, self-sabotaging things that it’s hard to even keep track of them all. But I will attempt it.

** Somehow, this league that was created to empower and uplift women cannot define a woman. This is why we have the Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White dilemmas. Those two former NBA players may have generated a lot of headlines with their antics, but they don’t want to play in the WNBA. Obviously. Like many of us, I think they just got sick of the WNBA not using its platform as an advocate for female athletes to take the lead in the fight against men in women’s sports. That should have been a no-brainer for the WNBA. Remember, the W in WNBA does stand for women. Why does the WNBA seem to forget that?

** This league has been out to cook its golden goose from Day 1. It’s beyond comprehension. Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark brought fans and eyeballs and money and deals and interest to the WNBA that was unprecedented. And all she’s gotten in return is grief, both physical and verbal, from her colleagues. These other players have stuck her in the eye, pushed her, pulled her, knocked her down. They’ve disrespected her in awards voting, they’ve spoken of her with disdain. Call it jealousy, or sour grapes, or perhaps reverse racism. Whatever it is, it’s insane that the league hasn’t squashed this madness long ago. Whatever the opposite of smart business is, the WNBA is the poster child.

** The WNBA has alienated large swaths of fans by allowing players to issue damning accusations and engage in bad behavior. Angel Reese has accused Indiana Fever fans of being racist. Ditto for DiJonai Carrington and Alyssa Thomas. Meanwhile, Natasha Cloud, while she was playing in a game, got into a yelling match with Kanter Freedom, who was sitting in the stands. And league MVP A’Ja Wilson stepped towards the baseline seats and yelled at a fan, just because he was yelling something innocuous at her during the course of a game, as fans tend to do. All of this is bad behavior, and a bad, bad look.

** Not all messaging is OK in the WNBA. Only that of the preferred ideologies. Fans who wore XX-XY shirts in support of women’s sports to games in Atlanta and San Francisco were harassed, and in one case asked to cover those shirts. But Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve showed up to coach a nationally televised game in a "Trans Kids Belong" T-Shirt, seemingly in response to Sophie Cunningham speaking up for keeping boys out of girls sports. Back when it was en vogue, the WNBA also fully embraced "Black Lives Matter" with signage on its floors and uniforms.

** And then there’s the self-sabotage du jour, the anthem controversy. While in San Francisco, I covered the latest Finals game in which both teams ran off the court as soon as it was time for the national anthem, and then ran back on as soon as it was over. Five Finals games, five run-offs. Why is this a thing? The only "explanation" we’ve heard is that "it’s part of the pregame routine." Really? Running off the court, disappearing for 60 to 90 seconds, only to run back onto the court to resume what you were doing right before you ran off? That’s a key part of the game prep? Please. This feels so wrong to me. It feels disrespectful, irreverent to skip out on the anthem. Part of our sports culture in this country is the playing of the national anthem prior to events. It’s a tradition, it’s an opportunity for people to come together under one flag and feel united as Americans. It’s an opportunity to honor our country and those who served and died for our freedoms. How can any of that be a bad thing? But for some reason, the WNBA has decided to stick a lightning rod in the national anthem, too.

WNBA WANTS A BIGGER STORY THAN CAITLIN CLARK, BUT TV RATINGS KEEP POINTING BACK TO HER

Without a doubt, the WNBA has gotten more attention than ever lately because of these dumpster fires that inevitably go viral. And while that attention is for, in my opinion, all the wrong reasons, maybe, just maybe, this is all a part of some genius and purposeful marketing plan by the league. A "let’s do and say the craziest things possible" because "there is no such thing as bad publicity."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

And that leads me to what else left me speechless in San Francisco. I interviewed at least 20 fans prior to the Valkyries-Dream game on Monday and I couldn’t believe what most of them were saying. None of them seemed all that bothered by the national anthem issue.

And these were all very nice people, too, all seemingly very normal folks. Just very different in their thinking and their worldviews. They said things like: standing on the floor should be the players’ choice, that not everyone views the anthem the same. One said that the anthem shouldn’t be played before games in the first place.

See? Speechless.

Maybe this is why it seems like the WNBA is constantly doubling down on the madness. It’s not worried.

The league is drawing record crowds. Chase Center was packed to the rafters on Monday.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Within this very divided country of ours, the WNBA, no matter what insanity it unleashes next, might always have just enough fans of a certain persuasion to not only keep the lights on but to leave the rest of us…well, speechless.

Will the WNBA ever stop doing things that alienate half the country? Does it care, so to speak, that "Republicans buy sneakers, too?" Let me know your thoughts at: pbabcockmcgraw@outkick.com.

World.title: Dante Moore won’t quit on Oregon, but concussion will keep star QB out of games moving forward for Ducks
World.content:
The unfortunate 2026 season for the Oregon Ducks continues to get worse by the day, as Dan Lanning announced on Monday that he does not expect quarterback Dante Moore to return this season.

It was during the September 28th game against USC when Oregon's season took a turn, when Moore sustained a concussion after taking a shot to the head by linebacker Desman Stephens as the quarterback was attempting to slide on a run.

LINCOLN RILEY'S USC TENURE COULD END WITH LOSS AGAINST OHIO STATE'S BACKUP QUARTERBACK, WITH $70 MILLION BUYOUT LOOMING

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Over the past few weeks, Moore had returned to practice for Oregon, participating with the team on a daily basis. But, in terms of returning to the field in an uncontrolled environment, Dan Lanning mentioned that he can not be cleared by the Ducks medical team for a return to live action.

"Really got clarity for us over the past week. I think if it was up to Dante in any shape or way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said on Monday. "But unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante, and it's not really up to me. We can control the settting of practice where he's able to do things for us, where that's not always the case in a game.

"You know, we said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to make a full recovery from. That has not changed, I definitely feel that way. But for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not going to happen."

MORE QUESTIONS THAN ANSWERS: ARCH MANNING LIKES THE DISRESPECT, BIG 12'S DISASTER AND A CFP RACE IN DISARRAY

This was not Dante Moore quitting on a three-loss Oregon team

Up until the concussion sustained against USC, Moore had thrown for 925 yards and nine touchdowns, with zero interceptions.

And, for those that think this was a decision Dante Moore made in relation to Oregon currently having three losses and the season being a wash, Lanning made it clear this was not the case, as Moore is currently the scout team quarterback.

"We're getting one of the best scout team looks in practice every week, and he looks good out there," Lanning mentioned. "This isn’t like a selfish decision on Dante's part saying 'I don't wanna come back, the season doesn’t look like theyw ay I want it to look'. That's not at all what this is."

USC LINEBACKER SUSPENDED AFTER VICIOUS HIT ON OREGON QUARTERBACK DANTE MOORE

Oregon moving forward, with Dante Moore now preparing for the NFL

The unfortunate situation for the Ducks quarterback has obviously had an effect over the past month.

After suffering a loss to Oklahoma State, the Ducks were already working at a deficit in the eyes of CFP committee members, not being able to afford two more losses. But, as Oregon worked through two-different quarterbacks in Moore's absence, Dan Lanning has been dealt two additional losses in the process.

Oregon committed seven turnovers in a 17-15 loss to UCLA earlier this month in a loss, and then this past weekend against Illinois could only score ten points in the 21-10 loss on the road.

OREGON HEAD COACH DAN LANNING'S WORDS IMMEDIATELY CAME BACK TO BITE HIM IN AWFUL LOSS TO UCLA

Now, the reality has set in for a football team that has not been able to establish a rushing attack, while dwindling in the passing game behind their backup quarterbacks.

This led to Dan Lanning making the move to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday.

For Dante Moore, his focus will now shift to making a full recovery in preparation what comes next, which is expected to be the NFL Draft.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Oregon quarterback has been projected to be a first-round pick next April, after choosing to return for another season in Eugene this past offseason.

What was once a season full of hope for Oregon has now turned into a disaster with over one month left in the regular season, as the Ducks are currently 4-3 with a very low percentage chance of making the postseason.

There will be a lot of questions to be answered over the next few months before the transfer portal opens and Oregon starts to rebuild its roster for 2027, with Dylan Raiola transferring from Nebraska this past offseason in hopes of one day becoming the full-time starter in Eugene.

World.title: Amid 2028 speculation, Wes Moore urges Marylanders to back him on redistricting
World.content:
BALTIMORE — Maryland Gov. Wes Moore is expected to cruise to re-election on Nov. 3. But he’s sweating the campaign nonetheless.

Moore’s political prowess is being tested at home beyond his own race for a second term, as Maryland voters prepare to take sides on a ballot question that would allow state Democratic leaders to redraw congressional district lines in a way that favors the party even more than the current 7-1 map.

Moore and his allies — including former President Barack Obama — are framing a vote for the ballot question as a vote to fight back against President Donald Trump and Republicans, an argument that might usually be expected to find purchase in a deep-blue state.

But it has become apparent in recent weeks that support for the ballot measure may not be as strong as Moore and other Maryland Democrats had hoped, and a major late effort has ramped up to promote passage of the measure. If it doesn’t pass, it would be a major political setback for Moore amid wide speculation that he’s gearing up for a potential 2028 presidential campaign.

Moore and his allies in Annapolis sought to redraw congressional districts this year, arguing that the Legislature could draw a map with all eight districts favoring Democrats to replace the current map in the wake of GOP redistricting efforts elsewhere.

But the effort was halted by state Senate President Bill Ferguson, a fellow Democrat who claimed that the push didn’t have the support of a majority of lawmakers in his chamber. Ferguson noted that Maryland Democrats tried to draw a more favorable congressional district map in 2021, only for a state judge to toss it out in 2022.

The ballot measure stemmed from that, seeking to address the state constitutional issue that sank the 2021 map first. In August, Ferguson and other Democrats in the Legislature overwhelmingly moved to put a measure before voters to eliminate the requirement that Maryland’s congressional districts obey natural boundaries, like the Chesapeake Bay. The state’s lone GOP U.S. House member, Andy Harris, represents a district concentrated on the state’s Eastern Shore.

After a legal challenge, Maryland’s Supreme Court allowed the question to be put to voters in a form rewritten by state judges.

With Election Day closing in, passage of the ballot question is far from certain.

A poll released this month by the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, found that a majority of likely Maryland voters (53%) planned to vote against the measure. That included 42% of Democrats, 74% of Republicans and 59% of unaffiliated voters who planned to vote no.

“To me, there was a broader underlying, interesting question about democracy. Do people want district lines to favor one party over the other? And most Marylanders don’t like that idea,” Mileah Kromer, the director of the UMBC Institute of Politics, told NBC News.

Kromer’s survey used plain language instead of the legalese that will appear on the ballot defining Question 3 and still found broad opposition from members of both parties and independent voters.

“Certainly there are a lot of Democrats who want to see some fighting back against President Trump but maybe don’t believe that, you know, redrawing congressional district lines just to favor their outcome is the way that they’d like to do it,” Kromer said.

She added that part of the reluctance of Maryland voters in particular is the fact that Democrats would gain only one seat in redistricting efforts. A similar measure that passed in California last year allowed the state to redraw congressional district lines in a way that gained Democrats advantages in five seats, overriding the state’s independent redistricting commission just months after Texas redrew its congressional maps to boost Republicans in an additional five seats.

A national fight over district lines

The two states’ moves last year set off yet more state redistricting efforts this year. A number of red states succeeded in redrawing their maps, while others still face legal challenges.

A longtime Democratic strategist in Maryland also pointed to the fact that Maryland voters are usually especially well-informed about national politics, particularly those who live in counties that border Washington.

“I wonder if there aren’t a lot of people in the state, Democrats in particular, who don’t feel like co-opting the Republican strategy of mid-decade redistricting is the best way to fight back,” said the strategist, who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to speak candidly. “If they heard anything in the news about mid-decade redistricting, it’s about, you know, Republicans or Donald Trump breaking the rules. They may not be that comfortable with that.”

Still, Kromer cautioned that the UMBC survey was conducted before the groups backing and opposing the ballot question began spending heavily on TV, digital and physical advertising.

Maryland’s Democratic voters are “upset about the Trump administration, and the messaging of, like, fighting back against Trump could be a really, really good messaging strategy,” Kromer said. “It might actually knock people more into the attitude of ‘I don’t like it, but it’s necessary.’”

After the poll was released last month, Moore and his allies began spending in earnest to persuade voters to support the ballot measure.

So far this month, Fight Back MD, a group supporting the measure, has spent $550,000 on TV ads urging voters to vote in favor of Question 3, according to AdImpact. Last week, Moore’s campaign decided to switch advertising from promoting his re-election bid to urging voters to support the measure.

But even raising money among Democrats to support the measure has been an uphill battle, with the redistricting divide between Moore and Ferguson still present behind the scenes.

Moore’s campaign released an ad last week featuring some of the state’s Democratic leaders urging voters to support Question 3, which was backed by a $700,000 investment by the campaign. On Monday, the campaign used an additional $500,000 on a TV and digital ad featuring Obama telling voters to support Question 3.

One state leader noticeably absent from the push is Ferguson. While he worked in August to convene a special session to pass a measure to put the redistricting question to voters, he hasn’t publicly or privately committed to pursue redistricting during next year’s legislative session if it passes next month.

Meanwhile, some donors who had expressed interest in the redistricting campaign have shown hesitation to donate this fall because Ferguson refuses to commit to passing new congressional maps, according to an operative familiar with the pro-Question 3 campaign.

Ferguson’s communications director, David Schuhlein, told NBC News that Ferguson “is primarily focused on retaining our Democratic state Senate seats and also trying to build on that and gain one or two more in a couple of districts throughout the state, and that takes an immense effort from him and the rest of our leadership team.”

“That’s where most of his efforts have been focused from the primary till now,” Schuhlein added.

Redistricting on the 2028 campaign trail

Moore in recent years has demurred about his potential presidential aspirations, but his out-of-state travel schedule has fueled speculation.

Last year, he told NBC News’ “Meet the Press,” “Yeah, I’m not running for president,” adding that he was focused on his re-election bid.

But in a gubernatorial debate this month against his GOP opponent, former state Del. Dan Cox, Moore didn’t commit to serve a full term if he’s re-elected this fall.

“Being the governor of Maryland has been the honor of a lifetime,” he told debate moderators when he was asked whether he’d commit to serve a full second term. “And I would not be running for re-election if I was not committed to the people of Maryland.”

Republicans in the state, who oppose Question 3, have accused Moore of pushing redistricting in Maryland to bolster his political aspirations.

A digital video produced by the state’s conservative Freedom Caucus tells viewers that 100% Democratic control of Maryland’s eight congressional districts would be “a trophy for his run at the White House.”

But some of Moore’s allies stressed that even if Moore fails to persuade voters to pass Question 3, it wouldn’t be a stain on a future presidential run.

“I just cannot imagine people caring that much about this” outside Maryland, a national Democratic strategist told NBC News. “He has a great record to talk about on issues people care about. ‘You didn’t knock off Andy Harris’ is not going to be an issue in early [Democratic presidential primary] states.”

“This is not the end-all, be-all for his political aspirations,” the strategist added.

Michael Hanmer, the director of the Center for Democracy and Civic Engagement at the University of Maryland, told NBC News, “The average voter, they’re not going to notice and they’re not going to care in terms of how they think about this when they’re looking at the candidates.”

“The problem in that situation, if it doesn’t pass, is that opponents are going to bring it up, and they’re going to use it as an example. They’re going to say: ‘Look at the makeup of your state. You couldn’t get this? It was just one; you couldn’t flip one?’” Hanmer added.

He predicted that redistricting and how elected officials wield political power in their states could emerge as a wedge between potential 2028 candidates, particularly governors, because of their broad agreements on issues like the economy, foreign affairs and immigration.

“I don’t think that we’re going to see a lot of candidates with massive distance between themselves on policy, right?” Hanmer said.

He added: “Gov. Moore is an extremely skilled politician. He is extremely, I think, quick on his feet and smart. I am sure he will have a response, but I would be surprised if [redistricting] is not something that others — if they were successful and he was not — bring up.”

World.title: Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire goes into effect in Ukrainian town ‘on brink of disaster’
World.content:
The rare humanitarian agreement comes amid renewed pressure from President Donald Trump on Kyiv to agree to a deal to end the war, which began when Russia ⁠invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

Ukraine complained of gaps in intelligence sharing from the U.S. and a slowdown of Elon Musk’s Starlink service, both of which it says have now been restored. It has also said the U.S. is holding up supplies of crucial interceptor missiles.

Earlier this month, Trump also agreed to a deal allowing Russia to supply diesel to the global market, in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the midterm elections. The move, and his later waiving of sanctions, reversed years of American policy and raised alarm in Ukraine and Europe.

But in a rare intervention from the first lady, the White House quoted her as saying last week that Oleshky was “on the brink of disaster” and its remaining population, composed primarily of elderly residents, was in urgent need of medical attention, medicine, food and clean water.

“The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks,” she said. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.”

Civilian representatives from both sides will visit the town, which had a population of around 24,000 people before the war, to determine the level of assistance the remaining residents require, the statement said.

An “impartial American media organization” will document the process to ensure “that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected,” it added.

Both sides blame each other for the crisis in Oleshky.

Kyiv has accused Russian forces of mining nearby roads and using the remaining residents as human shields to prevent Ukraine’s army from conducting offensive operations in the town. Meanwhile, Russia has blamed Ukraine for “laying siege to the town” with drone strikes and preventing humanitarian aid from getting in.

Last month, the Kremlin acknowledged problems with food and medical ​supplies getting into Oleshky, saying its military was working to resolve them.

Ukrainian media has for months been featuring interviews with people who have managed to escape Oleshky and spoken to relatives of those who remain there — an estimated 2,000 people, including children.

Some said the town was on the verge of starvation and residents were relying on homegrown produce to survive. Others had reportedly resorted to eating grass.

With winter looming, fears of famine are growing in the town where communication is difficult because of a severely compromised internet and cellphone service in the area.

The United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, which has been documenting the crisis for months, said there have been no food deliveries to the town since the end of May.

The ceasefire is likely to last several days as the Russian side has to “clear the roads of mines,” Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukraine’s TSN TV channel Sunday, adding that his forces would have to verify the area is clear.

“There is no doubt that Russia will do everything it can to clear the roads of mines so that these people head toward Russia and stay there. They are not going to simply let people go,” he said.

Oleshky, like a large portion of the Kherson region, has been occupied by Russian forces since the early weeks of the invasion.

Drone footage of the town, shared by Ukraine’s 34th Separate Marine Brigade “Borysfen” last month and verified by NBC News, shows the charred ruins of desolate residential and administrative buildings inside the town, in a rare look at the level of destruction.

Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, shared another video earlier this month, geolocated by NBC News, showing residents leaving Oleshky on foot, bicycles and mopeds in what he said was a desperate search for food. He said they faced the impossible choice of being blown up on a mine or dying from hunger.

Their plight received international attention in recent weeks after the Pope directly raised the growing crisis with Putin, and European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno went on a hunger strike, saying “the people of Oleshky cannot be abandoned.”

While both Kyiv and Moscow have unilaterally announced Easter or Christmas ceasefires before, they did not revolve around a humanitarian crisis and have not involved open mediation by the U.S., making the Oleshky ceasefire an unprecedented halting of fire between the two sides.

The ceasefire could serve as a model for similar humanitarian arrangements in other areas, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday, especially given the “highly positive” American involvement, including from the first lady.

Melania Trump has been involved in the humanitarian campaign to bring back Ukrainian children taken by Russia, and the White House statement said she leveraged the “communication channel” established through those efforts to bring about a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky.

World.title: Memes, Mao and Mbappé: Chinese brands drop soccer star in fury over ‘dictator’ joke
World.content:
The Chinese social media platform Xiaohongshu also distanced itself from Mbappé, saying its contract with him had ended after he appeared in a 2024 ad for the platform that went viral. On Tuesday, a note on Mbappé’s Xiaohongshu account, which had more than a million followers, said it had been suspended “for violating community guidelines.”

The companies did not specify Mbappé’s missteps, but the statements came after a clip circulated widely on social media Monday showing an interview last spring with the French online talk show “The Bridge.”

Mbappé is often depicted jokingly online as a dictator because of his outsize presence on and off the field. Fans have created memes comparing him to a number of authoritarian historical figures, including Mao.

In the clip, Mbappé was asked which meme was his favorite.

“A video someone made of a guy… I think he was a Chinese dictator,” he said. The clip then shows Mbappé’s face superimposed on an image of Mao, whom Mbappé did not mention by name.

His comments drew fury in China, where he was accused of insulting a country that has been a lucrative source of income for him.

“Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with a collective boycott by all sectors of Chinese society,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Tuesday at a regular briefing in Beijing.

Foreign athletes have run afoul of Chinese sensitivities in the past, sometimes with profound economic consequences for major sports leagues. NBA games were largely suspended from Chinese broadcast for years in 2019 after a Houston Rockets manager expressed support for anti-government protests in the Chinese territory of Hong Kong, and in 2023 former NBA star Dwight Howard drew controversy when he referred to the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan as a country.

According to a commentary Tuesday by Global Times, a state-backed nationalist tabloid, sporting events and s involving Mbappé have also been suspended from broadcasting.

“Mbappé is not an isolated case. He has now paid the price, and deservedly so,” the commentary said. “His experience should serve as a clear red line for all foreign public figures seeking to enter the Chinese market.”

After reports that broadcasts of the Spanish league, where Mbappé plays for Real Madrid, had been suspended in China, the league distanced itself from the remarks.

“We deeply regret” the comments “that have caused discomfort and offense in China,” La Liga President Javier Tebas said in a post on social media. “We cannot allow an individual’s action to tarnish” La Liga and its clubs’ relationship with China, Tebas said, adding that it was working with its partners in China to “overcome the situation.”

In his own apology, also posted to social media, Mbappé said that “during a recent interview, I reacted to an image of myself. My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.”

He added: “I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”

World.title: Jay-Z to headline Super Bowl halftime show
World.content:
Jay-Z has helped select artists for the last several Super Bowl halftime shows.

Now, the 25-time Grammy winner and mogul will step into the performer role as the headliner for the 2027 show.

The NFL and Apple Music announced the news on social media during Monday night’s game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles, confirming recent reporting about the halftime show from Puck that cited industry sources.

“GOAT’s out of the bag,” read the post, which featured a black-and-white video of Jay-Z in the stands with a goat on his lap as “Allow me to reintroduce myself,” the opening line of his song “Public Service Announcement (Interlude)” plays.

Jay-Z’s entertainment company, Roc Nation, has been a partner with the NFL and produced the halftime show since 2019.

“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

Super Bowl 61 will take place Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, near Los Angeles. The game and the halftime show will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+ and on mobile devices with NFL+.

Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, just wrapped his 30 Tour, which celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” His final two shows were at SoFi.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” he said in a statement Monday. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

During the tour, which featured stops in Paris, London and Jay-Z’s hometown, New York City, he brought up several guests, including his wife, superstar Beyoncé.

It’s unclear whether Bey or any of Jay-Z’s many other famous friends and collaborators will make cameos during the halftime performance.

Many artists who have headlined the event have brought on major stars. But several, including The Weeknd and Rihanna, chose to shine solo when they appeared at the event.

Last year’s game, which was broadcast on NBC and Peacock, featured Bad Bunny as the headliner, with Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin making cameos. The performance was awarded seven Creative Arts Emmys this year, making it the most awarded halftime show in history. It was Bad Bunny’s first Emmy and Jay-Z’s third, with both artists serving as producers last year.

Kendrick Lamar, who headlined the 2025 show, also took home an Emmy after he tackled the gig.

Next year, said Apple’s vice president of music and international content, Oliver Schusser, fans can expect “an incredible show” from Jay-Z, whose “impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable.”

World.title: Ex-luxury real estate brokers and brother to be sentenced on federal sex trafficking charges
World.content:
Two former luxury real estate brokers and their brother are scheduled to be sentenced in a New York City courtroom Tuesday, seven months after they were convicted of drugging and raping women in a sex trafficking ring.

Federal prosecutors are seeking life sentences for Oren and Alon Alexander, a pair of former powerful real estate brokers, and their brother, Tal.

Attorneys for the brothers, who have asserted their innocence, are seeking 15-year sentences for each defendant.

The men were found guilty in March of 10 counts, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking and sex trafficking by force, after a trial that included testimony from 11 women who described being lured, drugged and sexually assaulted over a period of years.

Six of the women were part of the indictment.

Tal Alexander and Oren Alexander in New York in 2016. Sean Zanni / Patrick McMullan via Getty file

In a sentencing memo, prosecutors in New York’s Southern District said more than 70 women came forward with allegations of abuse and accused the brothers of exploiting their wealth, influence and connections to target victims.

At trial, prosecutors said the brothers raped the women after having promised them parties and trips. One woman testified that she lost control of her body after she had a drink with Alon Alexander at a New York City club.

When she awoke, she testified, they were naked on a bed. She kept trying to get up, and he kept pushing her back down, she said.

When she told him that she didn’t want to have sex with him, she testified, he responded, “‘You already did.’”

In a sentencing submission, attorneys for the brothers acknowledged that they sometimes behaved insensitively toward women but categorically denied that any of them had raped or sexually assaulted anyone.

At trial, the attorneys described the sex as consensual and said the women were motivated in part by financial gain.

“All the stories were rehearsed,” Tal Alexander’s attorney, Deanna Paul, said in her closing argument. “They’re looking for money.”

World.title: Convicted murderer escapes prison through fence, steals truck
World.content:
A man serving a life sentence for killing his co-worker four years ago has escaped from a prison in northwest Tennessee by slipping through a fence, authorities said. Investigators have since released surveillance footage that showed him stealing a truck in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Officials realized Jacob Morley, 28, was unaccounted for around 11:30 p.m. Sunday at the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, the Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement.

This booking photo released by the Tennessee Department of Correction on July 24, 2025, shows Jacob Morley. Tennessee Department of Correction via AP

Investigators looked at security cameras and saw Morley escape while wearing his prison uniform, officials said. They did not release any other details, including how Morley got through the fence.

Later, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation released surveillance tape showing Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350, with Tennessee plates and a Lindamood Planting Company logo on the door, at around 1 a.m. local time on Tuesday. The vehicle was stolen from Lake County, which includes Tiptonville, investigators said.

The bureau said Morley remained on its "most wanted" list as of Monday, and officials have offered a reward of up to $2,500 for information leading to his arrest. In a statement, it urged residents of the area from which the car was stolen "to check home security systems, including doorbell cameras and trail cameras, for any sightings of Morley or the stolen truck."

Prison officials said law enforcement throughout the area has searched buildings and other structures near the prison about 90 miles north of Memphis in an isolated, rural area of flat land tucked near a bend in the Mississippi River near Missouri.

Morley is 5-foot-11 and 240 pounds. He has brown hair and green eyes.

Morley was sentenced to life for killing co-worker Cody Birchfield in 2022. Birchfield's body was found in a box under Morley's Carter County home after he had been missing for a few weeks.

Along with first-degree murder, Morley was also convicted of aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, vandalism and evading arrest. When Morley saw deputies at his home in 2022, he led police on a chase that ended in North Carolina, authorities said.

Several violent attacks between inmates and by employees have been reported in recent years at Northwest Correctional Complex. A grand jury in July returned dozens of indictments for five inmate murders, assaults against staff and inmates and other violence.

Northwest Correctional Complex can house 1,776 men and can house minors who have been convicted as adults, according to the Department of Correction. In 2023, an audit of Tennessee prisons found the department was struggling to fill open positions at the prison and had a 61% vacancy rate for correctional officers in that fiscal year.

World.title: Greenhouse gas levels set records again in 2025, U.N. says
World.content:
Geneva — Greenhouse gas concentrations in the atmosphere rose to record highs in 2025, locking in climate impacts that will persist for centuries, the United Nations said on Tuesday.

Levels of the three main greenhouse gases -- the climate-warming carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide -- all rose to unprecedented figures in 2025, the U.N.'s weather and climate agency said.

The World Meteorological Organization said the rise would lead to more long-term temperature increases for the planet.

The WMO's 22nd annual Greenhouse Gas Bulletin comes ahead of the COP31 U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20.

"Another year, another new record," said WMO Deputy Secretary-General Ko Barrett.

"Greenhouse gases are trapping an unprecedented amount of heat in the atmosphere, providing energy for more extreme weather and associated risks to our economies and societies.

"The past 11 years have been the warmest on record and this trend is set to continue. Carbon dioxide (CO2) has a very long life-time and so will affect the global climate not just for years but for decades and even centuries."

El Nino's impact

The bulletin looks at greenhouse gas concentrations -- the amount of those gases in the atmosphere -- rather than new annual emissions amounts as the world burns more coal, oil and gas.

In 2025, carbon dioxide concentrations were at 426.8 parts per million (ppm); methane at 1,948 parts per billion, and nitrous oxide at 339.1 parts per billion.

That takes them, respectively, to 153%, 267% and 126% of the pre-industrial levels witnessed before 1750.

Of the three major greenhouse gases, CO2 accounts for about 66% of the warming effect on the climate.

Around half of the total CO2 emitted each year remains in the atmosphere; the rest is absorbed by the land and oceans.

From 2024 to 2025, the global average concentration of CO2 rose by 2.8 ppm -- smaller than the record surge from 2023 to 2024 of 3.6 ppm.

WMO senior scientific officer Oksana Tarasova said this reflected the "recovery of the land carbon sinks and reduced fire carbon emissions in 2025 after the strong 2023/2024 El Nino," the naturally occurring, climate-warming weather phenomenon.

"However, a 2.8 ppm annual increase is still a substantial addition of carbon to the atmosphere from fossil fuel burning."

It is also above the average growth rate for the past decade of 2.6 ppm -- a figure that stood at 0.8 ppm in the 1960s.

"We can expect to see a further increase in concentrations in 2026 because of fossil fuel burning and the development of a powerful El Nino which will impact land carbon sinks, as it did in 2023/2024," Tarasova warned.

Methane accounts for about 16% of the warming effect on our climate by long-lived greenhouse gases, though it has a much shorter lifetime than CO2.

Around a third of methane emitted into the atmosphere comes from natural sources like wetlands, with the rest from anthropogenic sources such as cattle, rice farming, landfills and biomass burning.

The bulletin said that as countries shift their energy systems toward decarbonization, more attention should be paid to two potent but less abundant trace gases closely related to electricity production and distribution: molecular hydrogen (H2) and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).

SF6 has been rising steadily over the past three decades. It is used primarily as a spark suppressant in electricity distribution.

Why hydrogen levels have increased over the past decade is unknown but it has begun to be used as an energy storage medium.
