World.title: ‘Children first and competitors second’: Esports industry failing young players’ wellbeing, report warns
World.content:
Children’s health and wellbeing are not adequately protected in competitive gaming, according to a new report, “Protecting Child Rights in Esports,” by Save the Children, published on Tuesday.

 

The report calls on the fast-growing esports industry to put children’s rights, enshrined in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), ahead of competitive ambitions.

Young esports players — up to 300 million children worldwide — can face disrupted sleep, musculoskeletal problems, sexism, anxiety, online harassment and depression, while intensive training can leave less time for education, family and friends.

"Esports offers exciting opportunities for children, but participation should never come at the expense of their rights, wellbeing or development,” Theo Toresson, a psychologist at Save the Children and gaming expert, said in a press release.

"As the industry continues to grow, children must be recognised as children first and competitors second,” he added, calling for children's involvement in decision-making and ensuring a future where “every child can participate safely, develop their talents and enjoy the benefits of gaming without being exposed to harm.”

The concern is that children entering structured competitive environments may face expectations associated with professional sport without equivalent safeguards designed around their age and development.

No common standards for healthy competition

Long periods of sitting, inadequate breaks and training schedules that encroach on sleep, physical activity or schoolwork are among the concerns facing young players.

Long sessions and poor posture can also contribute to neck, shoulder and wrist pain, highlighting the need for ergonomic guidance and better-structured training.

Sleep is another concern. Late-night gaming schedules and the demands of competition can disrupt rest, affecting cognitive performance, mood regulation and overall wellbeing, the report says.

A representative of a national esports federation, quoted anonymously in the report, said there were no established guidelines on playing hours or training methods.

“We do talk about screen breaks, healthy diets, sleep, and hydration. But these are practices we've found best from different researchers and brought together ourselves. There isn't yet a centralized body trying to bring this together,” the representative said.

The absence of common standards raises questions about who is responsible for ensuring that competitive gaming remains compatible with children’s physical and psychological development.

The picture is not uniformly negative, however. The report notes that many professional esports players report satisfactory levels of physical activity, with higher-ranking players often placing greater emphasis on fitness. Players may also adopt healthy habits around diet and other aspects of their lifestyles.

Mental health under pressure

The psychological demands of competition are another concern.

“The demanding nature of esports, coupled with online toxicity, can create significant mental health challenges” for Youth Esports Athletes, the report says.

Stress, anxiety and depression can be compounded by intense competition and limited access to appropriate support. This can be further fueled by, for example, sexism and online harassment, as many interact with audiences through in-game chats, Discord communities, livestreaming platforms such as Twitch and YouTube and social media.

These channels can help young players build communities and develop public profiles, but they also expose them to cyberbullying and privacy violations. The report cited an analysis of chatrooms during 302 gameplay segments from the top 20 streamers on Twitch, one of the most popular platforms for esports

and gaming-related streaming, which revealed that 62% of streams included sexist language, 37% included racist language, 84% included ableist language, and 97% included violent language.

Some esports federations and teams require staff to obtain mental health first-aid training, according to the report, but such practices are not widespread across the industry.

The report warns that young players can be thrust into public-facing roles before they have the experience or support needed to navigate online scrutiny, interviews and livestreams.

The report also exposes challenges such as ensuring equal participation, with persisting large disparities based on access, gender, race, LGBTQIA+and disability; children's involvement in decision-making; economic exploitation, as teams, agents, and even parents sometimes exploit young players, taking advantage of non-transparent contracts and unequal power dynamics; and risks at live events without an adequate supervision.

World.title: TikTok parent company founder tops China's rich list amid AI boom
World.content:
TikTok parent company ByteDance's founder Zhang Yiming has reclaimed his position as China's richest person, fuelled by the company's expansion into artificial intelligence.

 

Zhang topped the Hurun Report's rich list with a fortune of $100 billion (€89.4bn), up 43%, “almost all of it on the back of AI,” according to its chairman, Rupert Hoogewerf.

“AI is the biggest single wealth engine on this list: 160 Hurun rich listers — 1 in 10 — now make their money from AI,” he added.

The Hurun Research Institute, which has published the ranking annually since 1999, identified a record 1,529 individuals with fortunes exceeding 5 billion yuan (€645mn), up 6.6% from last year.

China now has 1,176 billionaires, up 155 from last year and 176 more than the US, although still below its 2021 peak of 1,185.

FILE - Zhang Yiming, founder of ByteDance attends the opening ceremony of the 5th World Internet Conference in Wuzhen in east China's Zhejiang province on Nov. 7, 2018. AP Photo

The ranking comes as China's economy grew 4.5% year-on-year in the third quarter, supported by strong exports, while weak domestic demand and a prolonged property downturn continued to weigh on growth.

“This year’s gains were polarised — entrepreneurs in AI, semiconductors and robotics surged ahead, whilst those in consumer, real estate and traditional manufacturing saw their wealth shrink — a two-speed economy,” Hoogewerf said.

The property sector's struggles were also reflected in the ranking. For the first time, no mainland Chinese property developer featured among the 100 richest people, with only Hong Kong property-owning families remaining at the top.

World.title: Dutch chip firm Besi's shares jump as Applied Materials moves to double stake
World.content:
Dutch company BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi), which makes machines used to assemble and package semiconductors, saw its stock climb more than 10% to over €160 per share by early afternoon on Tuesday.

 

The jump came after Applied Materials, one of the world's biggest makers of chipmaking equipment, announced late on Monday that it would increase its holding in Besi to about 20%, from the 9% it has owned since April 2025.

In a statement, Applied said it had signed an accelerated share purchase agreement to buy the additional stock, with delivery depending on a review under US antitrust law.

The California-based group called the stake a long-term investment and said it "currently has no intention to increase its investment in Besi beyond approximately 20%".

Nor will it ask for a place on the Dutch company's board, the firm added.

Prabu Raja, president of Applied's semiconductor products group, said in the same statement that the company was increasing its stake because hybrid bonding and next-generation ways of connecting chips are increasingly becoming critical to energy-efficient AI computing.

"We also look forward to furthering our strategic collaboration with Besi," Raja concluded.

Hybrid bonding and AI

The companies' collaboration on hybrid bonding dates back to 2020.

The technique joins chips directly to one another without tiny solder bumps, allowing them to be stacked more tightly, and is seen as key to the next generation of AI processors and memory.

On 1 October, in a joint statement, they widened the partnership to other packaging technologies, with Besi becoming an "innovation partner" at Applied's new research and development hub in Silicon Valley, known as the EPIC Center.

In that statement, Raja said advanced packaging had become a materials engineering challenge rather than a back-end assembly step.

Besi's CEO Richard Blickman called joining the centre "a natural next step".

Why not a takeover?

Applied's promise to stop at 20% also keeps it well clear of a key threshold. Under Dutch takeover rules, an investor that crosses 30% of a listed company’s voting rights must make an offer for the whole company.

A full deal would also face scrutiny in Beijing.

Both companies sell heavily into China, giving its competition regulator a say over any potential merger.

Roughly 30% of Applied's 2025 revenue came from China, while Besi runs a factory in the Chinese city of Leshan, in Sichuan province.

Applied has been in a similar situation before. In 2021, it abandoned a deal to buy Japanese chip equipment maker Kokusai Electric when Chinese approval failed to arrive in time.

Applied's move also comes after a steep slide in Besi’s share price.

The stock has lost about half its value since peaking at €317 in June, caught up in a wider sell-off in chip stocks.

World.title: Football: Mbappé apologises for 'ill-judged' joke about China's Mao Zedong that led several brands to drop him
World.content:
Kylian Mbappé has lost several of his biggest sponsorship deals in China after a video circulated online in which he appears to joke about Mao Zedong, the founder of the People’s Republic of China, that led to a backlash that he has now apologised for.

 

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement he published in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday.

"I apologise to everyone my words have upset."

Energy-drink maker Dongpeng and dairy group Mengniu both ended their partnerships with the Real Madrid forward with immediate effect.

“Our company is firmly opposed and applies a policy of zero tolerance towards any behaviour that offends national feelings,” Dongpeng said, announcing the end of “all forms of cooperation” with the player.

Mengniu said in its own announcement that it was ending all cooperation with the captain of the French national team in a move that shows how political and national sensitivities can weigh on international brands.

What sparked the backlash?

Mbappé reportedly made the 'insensitive' comment on the French talk show The Bridge, where he was asked about the online memes about him being a 'dictator' and the ones which amuse him the most.

He then said the one that makes him laugh most is a video of a man he thinks is "a Chinese dictator".

Mbappe laughs as the programme cuts to a meme showing his own face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

A woman walks by an  featuring French soccer star Kylian Mbappé in Shanghai, China on June 30, 2026. (Chinatopix Via AP) CHINA OUT Chinatopix

The meme is part of a running joke on social media in which Mbappe is called a "dictator" over his huge influence on and off the pitch.

Why did the video cause such a reaction?

The decision by several brands to drop Mbappe came after the clip spread across China, where jokes about Mao, who died in 1976, are seen as disrespectful.

Both companies’ statements stressed the need to protect national feelings and clearly distanced themselves from Mbappé.

Related Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé breaks silence on Ceuta shirt controversy

The split is a sharp reversal for the 27-year-old, who until now has been hugely popular with Chinese fans and has millions of followers on the country’s social platforms.

During this year’s World Cup, Chinese viewers regularly saw Dongpeng adverts featuring AI-generated images of him drinking the brand’s energy drink.

He is also affectionately known in China as "Guigui", which translates as "turtle", a nickname linked to a meme inspired by the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

World.title: To the moon and beyond: Astronauts Chris Hadfield and Victor Glover on why the 'New Space race matters
World.content:
What does it feel like to be in outer space? And how does the experience affect your outlook on Earth matters and humanity?

 

Just two of the questions Euronews Culture put to former International Space Station commander Chris Hadfield and the record breaking Artemis II pilot Victor Glover during their appearance at the Starmus Festival where Glover and his NASA crewmates were awarded the Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication.

In an extraordinary conversation, the two astronauts explore how their real-life adventures compare with space travel in pop culture and discuss if the 'New Space Race' is creating divisive competition between rival nations or closer collaboration.

World.title: Knives, knuckledusters and a ‘Gucci robbery’: police discover chats linked to Milan riots
World.content:
Youssef Siher exercised his right to remain silent when questioned by preliminary investigations judge Tiziana Landoni in Milan’s San Vittore prison on Tuesday.

 

Investigations into the unrest that rocked the centre of the Lombard capital on 17 and 18 October are proceeding on two separate tracks: messages found by investigators in a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members, and the Milan prosecutor’s inquiry into Siher’s alleged role in organising and spreading content linked to the so-called 17 October Movement.

Chats with threats: “We steal their weapons” and “set fire to a government building”

The Monza and Brianza Digos (General Investigations and Special Operations Division) began investigating after finding a message in a chat in which a user urged others not to put their balaclavas on straight away, to avoid being identified by police.

On 22 October, acting on a warrant from the Milan juvenile prosecutor’s office, investigators searched the home of the teenager believed to have written the message. They found a balaclava and an Under Armour T-shirt thought to have been stolen from a shop looted in Milan. A search of another minor turned up a second T-shirt of the same brand, also believed to have been taken during the looting.

But it was the first boy’s mobile phone that gave investigators their most significant lead, pointing them to a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members. The conversations referred to weapons, knives, smoke bombs and firecrackers, as well as plans to attack officers, snatch their weapons, damage police vehicles and set public buildings on fire.

Messages cited by investigators include “And we steal their weapons”, “Let’s grab one, beat him up and take his weapon” and “Hey guys, if we’re going to protest, let’s set fire to a government building”. Others urged people to get hold of knives, clubs and pepper spray, while some discussed stealing cars and targeting businesses, with references to a “Gucci robbery” and a McDonald’s.

The chats also mentioned further demonstrations planned for 24 October, which risked turning violent. The information gathered helped trigger a nationwide preventive operation.

Knives, knuckledusters and balaclavas: 150 searches

On 24 October, around 150 personal and home searches were carried out in several Italian provinces, coordinated by the Central Directorate of Preventive Police and involving Digos units and Flying Squads from various cities. The main aim was to find illegally held weapons and ammunition.

In Brianza, the checks covered 32 people living in 16 municipalities, including Monza, Seregno, Giussano, Carate Brianza, Limbiate, Nova Milanese and Desio.

Officers seized folding and butterfly knives, a hatchet with “1312” engraved on its blade – a numerical code for the acronym ACAB (“All Cops Are B*****ds”) – knuckledusters, a telescopic baton, two blank-firing pistols missing their red safety caps, glass breakers, balaclavas and other items classed as offensive weapons.

Investigators are continuing to piece together the alleged conduct and identify anyone else responsible.

Siher stays silent

Siher was detained on 24 October and is accused of incitement to commit crimes, aggravated by terrorist intent, and of organised violence during public demonstrations. Prosecutors say he runs the social media channels of the 17 October Movement, which was set up after the clashes in central Milan.

Landoni must now decide whether to validate his detention and grant the request for him to be held in prison pending trial, submitted by chief prosecutor Marcello Viola and prosecutor Francesca Crupi, who attended the hearing. Prosecutors argue there is a risk he could flee or reoffend. A decision is expected by 28 October.

Siher is represented by lawyers Benedetto Ciccarone and Yasmina Abu Sharar, who deny he incited violence or terrorism and have asked for his release.

World.title: The most haunted hotels in Europe you can book a stay in this Halloween
World.content:
A spectre is haunting Europe. No, hang on. Spectres are haunting Europe, and apparently people are willingly sleeping in the same space as them.

 

While I personally would avoid any hotel that claims to be haunted, there are a number of properties across the continent that loudly and proudly shout about their paranormal guests, and with Halloween coming up, we thought it was time to spotlight them.

Here’s where to stay if you want a truly haunted Halloween experience.

Golden Fleece, York, UK

Billing itself as one of the most haunted cities in Europe, practically every street in York has a building with a ghost story attached to it.

The Golden Fleece, a pub on Pavement, claims to be the most haunted in the city, and for those who aren’t satisfied with just enjoying a pint among the spectres, you can also book a night in one of the rooms here.

According to York’s tourism board, paranormal guests you might encounter during your stay include Lady Alice Peckett, the wife of the pub’s owner from the early 18th century, and a British airman who fell out of a window here in 1944.

The Ancient Ram Inn, Gloucestershire, UK

Originally built in the late medieval period, The Ancient Ram Inn has had plenty of time to rack up supernatural figures that wander its halls while guests sleep.

Its owners say it’s the most haunted bed and breakfast in the UK, with some 20 ghosts, including a young girl named Rosie, reports Metro. One ghost hunter even claims to have encountered a female sex demon. Blimey.

The Shelbourne, Autograph Collection, Dublin, Ireland

When it comes to five-star hotels, you tend to have certain expectations: Top-notch service, fantastic bars and restaurants, and preferably a nice wellness area with a spa or swimming pool.

You probably don’t expect to run into the mischievous spirit of a seven-year-old girl named Mary Masters who died of cholera in 1791.

But that’s exactly what you’ll get at The Shelbourne, Autograph Collection in Dublin, according to the Irish Mirror, with sightings as frequent as two or three times a week.

Actress Lily Collins even claimed to have seen the ghost during a stay here while filming The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones.

Hotel Union Øye, Norway

While Mary Masters is supposedly limited to the sixth floor of The Shelbourne, the ghost said to be inhabiting Hotel Union Øye sticks to “The Blue Room”.

The tale goes that a servant girl named Linda started an illicit affair with one of Emperor Wilhelm’s officers, and The Blue Room was where the pair would meet.

It ended in tragedy. Unable to divorce his wife and be with the woman he loved, the officer killed himself. Linda, not wanting to live without him, killed herself by walking into the lake, never to be seen again.

Now, according to Norway’s tourism board, Linda’s ghost is said to be heard weeping in The Blue Room.

Toftaholm Herrgård, Sweden

Another broken-hearted ghost can be found at Toftaholm Herrgård in Sweden.

Servant Mats fell in love with the daughter of a count, who was promptly married off to the son of a nobleman. Upon discovering the news, Mats hung himself in one of the guest rooms of the mansion.

Describing him as a “gentle ghost”, the team behind Toftaholm Herrgård say guests claim to have seen him appearing behind women staying in the hotel, occasionally putting his hand on their shoulder.

World.title: Why should Big Tech know what you’re working on? Scale AI accused of spying on AI trainers
World.content:
A prominent European data protection group said it was filing five legal complaints in Europe against American startup Scale AI over the way its training platform Outlier tracks its workers, infringing on their rights.

 

It comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny in Europe, with the EU’s AI Office opening investigations into OpenAI and Anthropic this month. In the US, meanwhile, President Donald Trump signed an agreement with the six largest American AI firms allowing them to regulate themselves, a sign of growing divisions over how to govern the technology globally.

There are also growing concerns worldwide that AI could take people’s jobs and be used for harmful purposes.

The European Centre for Digital Rights, known as Noyb, is filing two complaints in Austria, one in France, one in the Netherlands and another in Italy, it said in a statement published on Tuesday 27 October, relating to the way workers are trackers and the lack of protections granted by its freelance contract model to recruit staff.

Scale AI’s Outlier AI platform recruits freelancers and subject-matter experts to help train, evaluate and improve artificial intelligence models, using a platform worker model like those used by Uber and food delivery services.

According to Noyb, the platform uses more than 900,000 freelancers to evaluate and correct the responses of AI systems, with customers including Meta, OpenAI, Google and the US government, which the organisation describes as a process in which workers are “effectively giving their expertise to US Big Tech companies”.

Outlier "collects huge amounts of personal data and forces workers to go through an invasive biometric verification to earn money", the NGO said.

"In Europe, this far-reaching workplace surveillance clearly violates the workers’ fundamental right to data protection," it said.

Noyb alleges that while workers are on the Outlier platform, trackers from companies such as TikTok, LinkedIn and Facebook are placed on their devices and given access to their personal data.

This includes IP addresses, contact details and data that can be used for targeted advertising and profiling, the group said.

“Such constant and extensive tracking while working really goes against all reasonable expectations. Why should LinkedIn or Facebook know which tasks you're working on?” said Lisa Steinfeld Leiser, Data Protection Lawyer at Noyb.

It also alleges that Scale AI forces workers to repeatedly go through a biometric verification process carried out by a company called Persona, which includes making video recordings of their face and uploading their ID.

World.title: Denmark's Frederiksen criticizes Finland and Norway for calling Putin without coordinating with allies, despite consultation with Ukraine
World.content:
Finland and Norway have called Putin about ending the Ukraine war, drawing Danish criticism. The dispute highlights divisions over European engagement with Moscow ahead of planned US-led peace talks.

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized Finland's and Norway's leaders Tuesday after they held a joint phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin about ending the war in Ukraine.

The call came ahead of planned US-led peace talks, which European leaders are seeking to join.

Why did Denmark criticize the call?

Frederiksen said that Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store had gone "solo.”

"I'm very sceptical about this Norwegian and Finnish initiative. It hasn't been coordinated with any of the rest of us," she told reporters while attending a meeting of Nordics leaders.

"I honestly don't know what those two countries think they can achieve with this."

"I believe we should keep Europe united, rather than going it alone," Frederiksen said.

Stubb and Store said they had consulted Ukraine before initiating the call.

What should the EU's new Arctic strategy look like? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

They stressed that they represented their own countries and were not speaking on behalf of Europe.

What did the leaders discuss with Putin?

Stubb described the conversation as "frank and substantive." Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the call, the first between the three leaders.

"The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," Stubb said.

Finland and Norway both border Russia and have supported Ukraine throughout the war.

Store said the leaders had emphasized de-escalation.

"The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations," he said.

How was Ukraine involved?

The call followed an October 20 meeting in Oslo involving Stubb, Store, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US envoy Steve Witkoff. US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner joined remotely.

Zelenskyy also spoke with the Nordic leaders after their conversation with Putin.

"Finland and Norway will continue to support Ukraine, and the efforts to find a just and lasting peace," Stubb wrote on social media.

World.title: Jordan acknowledges civilian casualties in Syria airstrike against 'Islamic State'
World.content:
A Jordanian government spokesman has expressed "regret" over civilian casualties in an airstrike it said was targeting "IS" militants.

The Jordanian government admitted on Tuesday that a number of civilians had been killed in airstrikes conducted against so-called "Islamic State" militants in southern Syria on Monday night.

The Jordanian air force carried out the strikes on "terrorist groups" in the region in retaliation for last week's attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox Church in Jordan in that killed nine people, adding the strikes killed more than 20 IS fighters.

However, Syrian authorities contradicted the claim, saying the strikes in the Daraa and Sweida provinces had killed seven people including three children and a woman. Two men who were killed were reportedly elderly.

One resident, Masoud al-Salim, said he lost his wife, son and three grandchildren in one of the strikes that hit his home in the Syrian border village of Al-Tuff.

"I came running and found there was no house anymore, no tent, nothing. I couldn't find anyone," he told the Associated Press, which said he was rummaging through children's schoolbooks and toys in the rubble.

"I started looking under the rubble. I thought they might be buried there."

Jordan admits civilians killed

On Tuesday, Jordanian Communications Minister ​Mohammed al-Momani acknowledged the civilian casualties, which he said the Hashemite Kingdom regretted.

"Jordan always takes all precautions to avoid harming civilians," he said in a post on social media, insisting: "The operations were carried out based on field intelligence to neutralize confirmed threats and terrorist operations against Jordan."

He said the Jordanian air force had inflicted "heavy losses in IS ranks, estimated at more than 20 elements" and destroyed a "massive weapons depot belonging to the organization."

"Jordan refrained from targeting sites where intelligence indicated the presence of civilians and regrets the occurrence of civilian casualties," he added.

Middle East conflicts take toll on Jordan's tourism sector To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Syria condemns 'violation'

Monday's operation sparked anger in Syria, where the Foreign Ministry condemned the strikes as an "unacceptable violation [of] and encroachment [into]" Syrian airspace.

While the Jordanian military claimed the strikes were conducted in coordination ⁠with Damascus, ​the Syrian government said they were carried ​out without prior coordination and announced an investigation.

Jordan and Syria maintained strong bilateral ties following the downfall of the Assad dynasty in December 2024 and the emergence of interim President Ahmad al-Sharaa's Islamist-led government.

Despite Monday's airstrike, Syria asserted that that both countries' leaderships will strengthen security coordination to "obstruct any efforts to destabilize the two countries' security and spill the blood of its people."

No group has claimed responsibility for the initial attack on the Greek Orthodox funeral in Jordan, but Jordanian security forces arrested three men – two brothers and their in-law – following a shootout earlier on Monday.

World.title: DR Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases as the outbreak spreads abroad, with no approved vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo virus
World.content:
DR Congo has reported more than 10,000 Ebola cases and nearly 4,900 deaths. The outbreak involves a virus for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, complicating efforts to contain its spread.

Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported that Ebola cases had risen to 10,060, with 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was identified in mid-May.

The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has described it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

Where else have cases been reported?

Kenya has confirmed nine infections, including two deaths, after a patient traveled from DR Congo through Uganda to the capital, Nairobi.

Nigeria also confirmed an infection in a Swiss woman, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, who fell ill after visiting Uganda. Authorities are investigating where she contracted the virus. She was evacuated to Switzerland.

Why is the outbreak difficult to contain?

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person. It can cause fever, diarrhea and, in some cases, bleeding.

Nigeria on alert after traveler tests positive for Ebola To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Early symptoms can resemble malaria, potentially delaying isolation and treatment.

The lack of an approved vaccine or specific treatment against the Bundibugyo virus further complicates efforts to control the outbreak.

Are vaccines and treatments being tested?

Clinical trials of two antiviral treatment approaches have been underway since July.

Two further trials are investigating whether the Ervebo vaccine can protect against the Bundibugyo virus. The vaccine is currently approved and recommended only against Ebola virus, formerly known as Zaire ebolavirus.

World.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
World.content:
10/27/2026 October 27, 2026 Mercedes cuts outlook for 2026 profit margin

German carmaker Mercedes-Benz has cut its forecast for 2026, with difficult market conditions in China and higher fourth-quarter cost expectations set to negatively impact profits, the company said on Tuesday.

Markets were quick to take note of the announcement, and Mercedes shares dropped 3.4% in trading on Tuesday morning.

The move makes Mercedes the third big German carmaker to lower its outlook for 2026 after BMW and VW took similar steps.

Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius has called on German employees to work more without pay while also expanding manufacturing operations in Hungary, where he said costs are about 70% lower than in Germany.

Mercedes currently expects an adjusted car profit margin of 2% to 3% in 2026, compared to the 3% to 5% in the previous guidance.

Mercedes: A star that's lost its sheen? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Like many German automakers, Mercedes has faced weak sales in China. German carmakers have struggled in the world's largest car market with sluggish demand and increased competition from local manufacturers.

Mercedes vehicle deliveries in China — last year already at their lowest level since 2016 — fell a further 29% in the nine months to the end of September.

Mercedes also released third-quarter figures earlier than planned, which showed that the company generated just €172 million ($191 million) in free cash flow from its vehicle business, down on the €422 million forecast by financial market experts.

Before interest and tax, Mercedes posted an operating profit of €1.77 billion — more than double the €750 million recorded a year earlier, according to the preliminary figures. But last year's stats were significantly impacted by one-time expenses, especially related to job cuts and legal disputes.

Adjusted for one-off items, the operating profit margin in the passenger car business stood at 2.5%, down on the 4.8% recorded a year earlier.

World.title: Two men face UK national security charges following an incident near RAF Fairford, with police suspecting Iranian state involvement
World.content:
British prosecutors have charged two men over an incident near RAF Fairford in September. Police suspect Iranian involvement in the case at a base used for US strikes on Iran.

British prosecutors said Tuesday that two men had been charged under the National Security Act in connection with a September incident near RAF Fairford, an airbase used by US forces to launch strikes on Iran.

US bombers were withdrawn from Fairford on security grounds shortly after the arrests immediately after the incident.

What have police said about the Fairford suspects?

The Crown Prosecution Service charged Mohmed A., 24, of London, with engaging in conduct likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service. Counterterrorism police chief Laurence Taylor said investigators believed the country involved was Iran.

Nouman E., 24, also of London, was charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on August 22. Both men were due to appear in court later Tuesday.

Nouman E. was initially arrested near the Gloucestershire base on September 27 and rearrested on October 20.

UK releases air base plot suspects To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

A separate suspect, a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national also arrested on October 20, was released without charge over the suspected intelligence offense. He remains on bail following an October 1 arrest on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. Five other men also remain on police bail.

How did the Fairford investigation begin?

Armed police responded to reports of three suspicious vehicles near the base on September 27 and arrested five men. Scores of residents were evacuated as police and military bomb-disposal experts searched the area for explosives.

Police have said they consider Iranian state involvement "highly likely."

"We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state," said Laurence Taylor, head of UK counterterrorism policing.

He said police were working with MI5, Britain's domestic intelligence service, to counter the threat and urged the public to report concerns.

Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said it considers bases used to attack its territory legitimate targets.

World.title: Police in northern Germany search for suspects after car ramming overnight injures several
World.content:
A person intentionally drove into a group of people in a northern German town, police have said. Three people have been taken into custody in what police said was likely a gang confrontation.

A BMW was driven ​deliberately ‌into a group of people, leaving ‌four to five of ‌them ​with some serious but not life-threatening injuries in Neustadt am Rübenberge late on Monday night, police said on Tuesday morning.

A police patrol making routine traffic checks in town near Hannover in the state of Lower Saxony, intervened, shooting at the car to stop it.

"The officers witnessed the incident as it happened and opened fire on the vehicle after it had been driven into the group of people," the spokesperson said.

Organized crime suspected

Police announced that they had taken three people into custody at the BMW owner's address.

A police spokesperson added that initial findings indicated the ramming was an act of gang violence between organized crime families, that the individuals involved knew each other and that the perpetrators likely targeted the group of people and were not acting at random.

Forensic analysis of the crime scene was ongoing, a police spokesperson said Image: Moritz Frankenberg/dpa/picture alliance

Several suspects had fled the scene of the ramming on foot, police had said.

"The sequence of events and the exact roles of those involved are still under investigation," the spokesperson said, adding that forensic analysis of the cars and ramming scene was ongoing.

A reporter for the German DPA news agency described several damaged cars, with flat tires, a smashed rear window and bullet holes.

Edited by: Wesley Rahn

World.title: India news: Arunachal sees fresh violence over proposed dam
World.content:
10/27/2026 October 27, 2026 India's east coast braces as cyclone 'Arnab' approaches

Cyclone Arnab originated from the Bay of Bengal which births several severe storms every year Image: Ahamad Shaik/REUTERS

The Indian coastal states of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, took a number of steps including shutting schools, issuing helpline numbers and moving vulnerable people to safety as the severe cyclonic storm "Arnab" approaches.

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) on Tuesday forecast isolated by "extremely heavy rainfall" over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha for Tuesday and Wednesday, adding that nearby Chhattisgarh would experience similar conditions on Wednesday.

Much of the rest of India, including Delhi, will also see moderate weather impacts of winds and rainfall due to the cyclone, the press statement said.

Other eastern states including West Bengal and Jharkhand will also see heavy rainfall over the next three days, it added.

The cyclone which formed over the Bay of Bengal on Monday morning is expected to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday.

Authorities are moving vulnerable residents away from the coast to safer regions ahead of Arnab's landfall Image: Ahamad Shaik/REUTERS

Odisha shut schools and banned fishing and is preparing to evacuate nearly 50,000 people to safer places to prepare for the storm, local media reported.

Andhra Pradesh also implemented similar measures to ensure "zero loss of life and minimal damage to infrastructure."

Train services were also impacted with India's South Coast Railway suspending 53 train services over October 27 and 28 due to the storm.

India's biggest air carriers IndiGo and Air India said flights to and from Andhra Pradesh's capital city of Vishakhapatnam would be impacted on October 27 due to weather conditions brought by the storm.

They advised travelers to check their flight status and book book alternate flights in cases of cancellations.

World.title: Israel election: Israelis vote for 1st time since October 7 terror attack
World.content:
10/27/2026 October 27, 2026 Netanyahu casts ballot, while accusing Arab-Israeli parties of fraud

Benjamin Netanyahu cast his ballot in Jerusalem Image: Yonatan Sindel/REUTERS

Israel's Central Elections Committee said on Tuesday that "there are currently no indications of systematic tampering with ballot slips" after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Arab-Israeli parties of "trying to steal the election."

Netanyahu made the allegation after casting his own ballot in Jerusalem while urging voters to choose his Likud party.

"We know what is at stake ... We cannot leave this battle here in the hands of the left and the Arab parties that want to bring an end to the Jewish state," he said.

Netanyahu has used Arab-Israeli parties throughout the election to stoke fears of a Palestinian state and mobilize voters for Likud.

"So no barbecues, don't go to the beach — go to the polling station and vote Likud."

Netanyahu had said that three senior officials from the opposition Ra'am party, which has an Arab Muslim voter base, had been arrested in southern Israel with envelopes full of cash.

The acting director general of the Central Elections Committee, Dean Livne, referred to the "unusual" incident with the envelopes in a press conference Tuesday morning but said that "police, even before people arrived at the polling stations, caught individuals who tried to bribe voters."

He said the unidentified suspects were not actually at polling stations and were caught near their homes, adding the matter was under investigation.

"There are no similar incidents of this kind across the country," he concluded. "This was a localized case."

Opposition parties, including that of Netanyahu's main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, have also complained that ballot papers were being defaced and stolen at polling stations.

World.title: Comuns acuerda con el PSC retirar sus candidaturas al Senado en Girona, Lleida y Tarragona
World.content:
El acuerdo entre socialistas y la confluencia de izquierdas que lidera Ada Colau para el Senado ha aterrizado este martes en las cuatro provincias catalanas. En sendos comunicados, el PSC y Comuns —que forma parte del Frente Amplio— han explicado que solo competirán en la demarcación de Barcelona. Los de Colau renuncian a presentar candidatura por los escaños de Girona, Lleida y Tarragona, a cambio de que los socialistas les cedan uno de los que tendrán por designación autonómica. El movimiento busca frenar al Partido y Popular y Vox, pero también afecta a Esquerra.

“Es una responsabilidad democrática de las fuerzas progresistas y catalanistas frenar el paso de la derecha y la extrema derecha en el Senado”, justifican los textos enviados por las dos formaciones, que además certifican que esa institución en manos de la mayoría absoluta del PP “se ha convertido en una Cámara de bloqueo para las iniciativas del Gobierno”.

El acuerdo consta solo de dos puntos e implica que PSC y Comuns solo competirán en Barcelona. Los de Ada Colau se comprometen a retirar las candidaturas en las circunscripciones de Girona, Lleida y Tarragona. Allí sí se presentará el PSC . A cambio de esa cesión, los socialistas designarán a un senador autonómico a propuesta de los Comuns.

La decisión llega después de que, en un movimiento inédito, el PP haya renunciado a presentarse en tres provincias para dejar el camino abierto a Vox. Dos de ellas son catalanas: Lleida y Tarragona. En la primera, por ejemplo, los socialistas se hicieron con tres de los cuatro escaños en las últimas elecciones y, con este pacto, por un lado buscan frenar a la derecha pero también aspiran a arrebatarle el otro sillón a ERC.

El acuerdo PSC-Comuns recuerda a la Entesa Catalana de Progrés entre 2000 y 2011. Allí, además de los socialistas e Iniciativa —partido que recaló en la confluencia de Colau— estaban ERC e Esquerra Unida, referente de Izquierda Unida en Cataluña. En su momento, llegó a ser el tercer grupo parlamentario del Senado después del PP y el PSOE.

World.title: Candela Peña desvela lo que no pudo decir a Pedro Sánchez en ‘La Revuelta’ y un deseo: “Daría mi vida por que viniera la Santi”
World.content:
David Broncano presentó este lunes en La Revuelta a Candela Peña como una de las personas en boca de todos tras la entrevista del pasado jueves al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez. El presentador explicó que los excelentes datos de audiencia del programa ese día, con un 33,9% de cuota de pantalla media, crecieron hasta cerca del 50% en el tramo en el que la actriz se unió a la charla, al final de la misma. Este lunes, la colaboradora regresó al espacio de La 1 para comentar la repercusión de aquella breve intervención y desvelar lo que iba a contar aquel día sobre el escenario.

Candela Peña explicó que, tras grabar el programa el jueves, no se había quedado contenta con el resultado, pero que al día siguiente no paraba de recibir mensajes: “Me vibraba el móvil a cascoporro”. Pidió a Broncano que la avise para las próximas entrevistas con políticos: “Daría mi vida por que viniera la Santi”, dijo refiriéndose a Santiago Abascal.

En cuanto a la anécdota que quería contar a Pedro Sánchez partía de una carta que recibió en su hogar y que la felicitaba por haber llegado “a esta edad en la que estás”, misiva que iba acompañada de una compresa para pérdidas de orina. Peña denunció esta campaña de marketing como un insulto hacia sus destinatarias.

Broncano también anunció en La Revuelta la siguiente visita política, la de Irene Montero y Gabriel Rufián, representantes de Podemos y ERC. Aunque en un principio se anunció para este miércoles, finalmente el programa ha comunicado que tendrá lugar hoy martes 27 de octubre “por necesidades de agenda”.

Son otros dos de los políticos que sí han aceptado ya la propuesta para acudir a charlar con Broncano, al igual que lo ha hecho Ada Colau, candidata del Frente Amplio. Sin embargo, según el programa, aún siguen a la espera de respuesta de otros dos candidatos, que por tanto se trataría de los líderes del PP y Vox.

World.title: Meghan Markle vuelve a la televisión australiana como juez invitada de ‘MasterChef Junior’: “No lo dudé ni un segundo”
World.content:
Un día después de desmentirse los rumores de su posible incorporación al reparto de la tercera temporada de la serie ‘The Gentlemen’, la duquesa de Sussex ha confirmado su fichaje en el programa culinario en el que ya apareció el pasado abril

“Meghan Markle podría obtener un papel en la serie de Netflix The Gentlemen de Guy Ritchie”, tituló Deadline un artículo el pasado 21 de agosto que corrió como la pólvora por internet. Apenas 24 horas después de hacerse público el regreso de Enrique de Inglaterra y su esposa al Reino Unido seis años después de su sonada marcha a Estados Unidos, el medio especializado en cine apuntaba como uno de los motivos de su vuelta la posible incorporación de la duquesa al elenco de la tercera temporada de esta ficción ambientada en la campiña inglesa. Sin embargo, ambas partes han negado esta posibilidad. Fuentes cercanas a Meghan Markle acusaron a la plataforma de filtrar esos rumores para ayudar a promocionar la segunda temporada de la serie, estrenada el pasado septiembre. “Es el truco de marketing más viejo del mundo: conseguir que una figura famosa lea un guion y luego filtrar que estás ‘en conversaciones’ con ella”, dijeron a The Telegraph. Por su parte, fuentes internas de la producción insistieron recientemente en The Times sobre la innecesidad de publicidad de The Gentlemen. “Esta no es una serie que necesite recurrir a actores famosos”, aseguraron.

Este lunes, 26 de octubre, The Gentlemen ha confirmado el reparto de la nueva entrega, con incorporaciones como Elijah Wood y Orlando Bloom, pero sin rastro de la duquesa de Sussex. La posibilidad de su regreso a la actuación ha quedado así disipada, al menos por el momento. Pero la exactriz sí que volverá a la pequeña pantalla. Así lo ha confirmado este martes el medio australiano News.com.au, que ha anunciado en exclusiva que se unirá al rodaje de la nueva temporada de MasterChef Junior Australia. “Una fuente cercana a la producción confirmó que el popular programa regresará en 2027, seis años después de su temporada anterior, con Meghan apareciendo junto a la jueza de MasterChef Australia, Poh Ling Yeow”, aseguraba el medio australiano, que apuntaba a la duquesa como presentadora de esta nueva edición que se emitirá en el canal australiano Network 10 el año que viene. La revista People, en cambio, ha confirmado más tarde que será “invitada especial”, tal como se ha anunciado en el perfil de Instagram del programa.

Más información Las revelaciones de la docuserie sobre Matthew Perry: del comienzo de sus adicciones a los siete millones de dólares que gastó en desintoxicarse

Se espera que el rodaje tenga lugar en Melbourne y que dure varias semanas, según detalla The Times. “Enrique y sus hijos, Archie, de siete años, y Lilibet, de cinco, podrían acompañarla, aunque aún no se ha tomado una decisión definitiva”, señala el medio británico. Esta no sería la primera aparición de Meghan Markle en la televisión australiana. El pasado mes de abril, los duques de Sussex visitaron el país insular y ella aprovechó para aparecer como invitada de uno de los programas de MasterChef Australia que se emitió a finales de julio. Durante el rodaje, Enrique de Inglaterra llamó por videollamada desde Canberra, donde estaba reunido con veteranos de guerra, y preguntó: “¿He interrumpido algo importante?”. Su esposa lo saludó con un “Hola, mi amor” y le mostró los platos de los concursantes. Después de que él se despidiera y se disculpara por molestarla, ella dijo: “Es todo un encanto, ¿verdad?”.

Meghan Markle y Poh Ling Yeow durante la participación de la duquesa de Sussex en un capítulo de 'MasterChef Australia' emitido el pasado verano. TNI Press/TwoPointO Media / Cordon Press

Según un comunicado de prensa de los productores del programa, la presentadora Poh Ling Yeow estará acompañada por la duquesa de Sussex, y juntas “ayudarán a guiar a la próxima generación de jóvenes talentos culinarios”. “Lo pasé de maravilla con todo el equipo de MasterChef el pasado abril, así que cuando me propusieron volver a trabajar con este joven grupo de talentos no lo dudé ni un segundo. Me encanta cocinar con mis hijos, así que ver lo que estas jóvenes estrellas crean en la cocina va a ser divertidísimo. ¡Estoy deseando ver qué preparan!”, asegura ella en el comunicado. “Disfruté muchísimo grabando con Meghan a principios de este año, y reencontrarnos será un verdadero placer”, añade Yeow.

Meghan Markle ha aparecido en numerosos programas de cocina a lo largo de los años. Además, sus recetas han tenido un papel destacado en su serie de Netflix, Con amor, Meghan, y anteriormente participó como jueza invitada en el programa infantil de cocina Chopped Junior, de Food Network, en 2016. A su nueva aparición televisiva, se suma el cameo que protagonizó para la película pendiente de estreno Close Personal Friends, aunque en la cinta se interpreta a ella misma.

World.title: Información genética para una medicación más segura y eficiente
World.content:
Con una simple muestra de saliva, la farmacogenética permite el análisis de decenas de genes y cientos de fármacos de uso habitual y revela por qué un simple analgésico quita el dolor a una persona y a otra le produce una reacción adversa

Según estima la Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios, entre el 3% y el 6,5% de la población tiene una variante genética que provoca que su hígado transforme la codeína (un compuesto presente en medicamentos o soluciones tan frecuentes como las pastillas para la tos) en morfina. Este proceso, que se produce a gran velocidad incluso si la dosis administrada es normal, puede desembocar en una sobredosis accidental, que en algunos casos termina en el fallecimiento del paciente.

El ejemplo lo pone Javier Suela, director técnico del laboratorio de genética de Sanitas (Madrid). Él mismo pertenece a este pequeño grupo poblacional de riesgo: “Hay mucha evidencia acumulada de la toxicidad de ciertos medicamentos en ciertos pacientes. Estas reacciones adversas van desde un brote cutáneo hasta la muerte en casos extremos, como este mismo de la codeína”, explica.

Suela trabaja para reducir esa peligrosidad al mínimo. En el laboratorio que dirige, desde el pasado mayo, se extrae el perfil genético de quien lo solicite para “determinar si tiene un componente genético, una proteína, que produce que determinados fármacos se procesen de una forma que no es habitual”, sintetiza.

El perfil genético, en tres pasos 1 Recepción de las muestras e identificación de cada paciente El paciente lleva una muestra genética (basta la saliva, por ejemplo) en un tubo. Este tubo va a una primera máquina que realiza una preanalítica y transforma las muestras en placas que identifican a cada persona: en la posición A1 está la muestra de un paciente concreto y en la B1, otro, y así sucesivamente. 2 Procesado del material genético El material genético de la placa, que contiene muestras de hasta 96 pacientes, se prepara y depura (se corta, se colorea...) en otra máquina para el análisis final. Lo que se obtiene, tras cuatro horas de refinado, es la placa definitiva (en la imagen) que se usará para extraer el perfil genético. 3 Obtención del perfil genético La placa, con el material genético ya refinado, se introduce en un escáner que analiza cada celda, que contiene más de un millón de variables (cada una asociada a un genotipo) que procesar. Cuando este escáner finaliza se obtiene el perfil genético del paciente, el resultado final del proceso.

Esta disciplina se conoce como farmacogenética y en Sanitas está disponible para todos sus asegurados bajo el nombre de Mi Farmagen. “Un ser humano puede metabolizar todos los fármacos, pero en función de ciertas variables genéticas los metaboliza a distintas velocidades; entonces el medicamento puede funcionar demasiado bien o demasiado mal. Esto es lo que da lugar a reacciones adversas o reacciones inexistentes, es decir, cuando el fármaco no funciona”, detalla.

29 genes y 125 fármacos analizados

Mi Farmagen analiza hasta 29 genes y más de 125 fármacos de uso habitual, y ofrece un informe con las reacciones a cada uno de estos medicamentos. Y siempre es útil, tanto si se obtiene antes o después de la prescripción, ya que “permite ajustar la medicación sin perder efectividad, pero evitando posibles efectos adversos y aumentando la seguridad”, incide Suela.

Hay casos en los que un cambio anticipado de medicación puede salvar la vida del paciente, pero también situaciones más cotidianas en las que esta información es de mucha utilidad. Así lo explica Andrea Azcárate, jefe de servicio de Endocrinología del hospital Sanitas de La Moraleja (Madrid): “Es el ejemplo de un paciente con colesterol alto al que le sienta mal un tipo de estatina, que es el tratamiento habitual para esta patología. Para corroborarlo, se le hace la prueba farmacogenética. A partir de ahí, probablemente escojamos otro tipo de estatina que vaya a tolerar mejor”. Sin embargo, cada caso, en opinión de Azcárate, no es blanco o negro: “Lo que el análisis nos da es una predisposición de respuesta, una información probabilística que nos permite individualizar el tratamiento”, puntualiza.

0:00 ANDREA AZCÁRATE, jefe de servicio de Endocrinología del hospital Sanitas de La Moraleja (Madrid)

Azcárate y Suela inciden, precisamente, en la importancia de la interpretación facultativa de esta información, que por sí sola vale poco. “Es fundamental la interpretación y el ajuste, algo que siempre se ha hecho: la medicación, en función de las características clínicas del paciente, las casuísticas y las edades, se individualiza”. Y eso mismo se hará a partir de ahora, subraya: “Ajustaremos caso a caso, pero con más información. Es una herramienta más, muy buena y útil, pero hay que tener prudencia a la hora de incorporarla”.

En esa misma línea se expresa Suela: “El informe son páginas de metabolización, nada más. No vale de nada sin facultativo detrás que las interprete. Y, sobre todo, hay que combinar toda la información: igual tienes un paciente del que el análisis dice que el fármaco le va a sentar muy bien, pero esa misma persona tiene unas condiciones físicas complicadas o es un paciente polimedicado, en el que es fundamental medir las interacciones entre fármacos”. Es una cuestión de personalización, como dicta la tendencia actual en la medicina, pero con un conocimiento más preciso.

Así funciona Mi Farmagen Mi Farmagen analiza cómo las variantes genéticas influyen en la respuesta a determinados medicamentos.
