World.title: Pärnu property prices unaffected by Rail Baltic delay
World.content:
Real estate agents have said the postponement of the Rail Baltic deadline until 2032 is still too recent to be reflected immediately in Pärnu's real estate market. Projects already underway are continuing as planned.

This is not the first time that the completion deadline has been pushed back, and entrepreneurs and residents hope they will be able to travel on the track from Tallinn to the summer capital Pärnu by 2032.

Ingmar Saksing, a real estate agent at LVM Kinnisvara, said investors have factored this into their plans.

"Today we can talk about growing interest in the area where a terminal will be built, as in Ülemiste in Tallinn. Following the same logic, it is clear that property prices in this area and interest in the area are higher than before," he said.

The Part spa hotel will be completed by next autumn, adding 450 hotel beds to Pärnu. Sari Sopanen, head of the major development project, said the railway delay has not changed the hotel's development plans, but the completion of Rail Baltic would certainly help increase the number of customers.

Rail Baltic Estonia's map indicating travel times between potential stops on the railway. Source: Rail Baltic Estonia

"If Pärnu were connected to two international airports, Tallinn and Riga, then of course that would be a very, very big advantage for our industry and for us as well," Sopanen said.

"We believe in Pärnu, our location is ideal, it is a very good spot on Pärnu beach," she added.

Property prices in the summer capital have been steadily rising by two to three percent annually over the past decade, including inflation. The delay in Rail Baltic's completion has not caused any major jumps in prices, in either direction.

"People consider other reasons much more when deciding to change their place of residence, plus the fact that the arrival of the railway in Pärnu does not mean that everyone will want to move to Pärnu. Perhaps they will just come during the day and travel back home in the evening," said Terje Võrk, a real estate agent at Arco Vara.

In recent years, new real estate developments have sprung up in several parts of the city. Saksing said this is welcome, because when supply emerges, demand will follow.

"In total, 400 apartments are under construction and on offer, and at the current pace it will take up to two years to sell them, assuming no more are added," Saksing said.

World.title: Online casino tax cut brings no extra revenue, but culture picks up the bill
World.content:
The promised extra revenue from Estonia's online casino tax cut has not materialized for this year, making next year's culture budget €6–7 million smaller than hoped.

The Finance Ministry says only two new license applications have appeared following the cut, which was a pledge of the coalition Eesti 200 party, and one of those applications has been declined.

The tax cut, to apply to online casinos licensed in Estonia, was meant to make everyone happy. A lower rate would, it was argued, make Estonia a casino mecca; the state would have amassed more revenues, and culture – gambling tax revenues are a major source of funding for the sector — would finally stop struggling,

"This law isn't built on dreams. Together with the Foresight Center we modeled the entire potential tax take — how much market share would move to Estonia if the tax fell, how much tax revenue would come from that share, what the growth in receipts would be and how we could use it for extra funding for culture and sport," Eesti 200 leader Kristina Kallas had said last December.

A scenario accompanying the cut illustrated these hopes: online casino tax revenues rising to €95 million by 2029. Advocates turned a blind eye warnings at the time which found that not enough new companies might arrive to offset the lower rate. Yet this is what has materialized, though a finance ministry spokesperson rejected claims this had come as a surprise.

"Only two new license applications have come in. One is in process, one has been refused — so there hasn't been a great rush for Estonian licenses. Nor did we expect there to be one. So it went more or less as we thought," said Evelyn Liivamägi, deputy secretary general with the Ministry of Finance.

The Cultural Endowment (Eesti Kultuurikapital) which disburses culture funding to major projects is preparing to tighten its belt, with next year's budget must be made €6–7 million smaller than was projected just a couple of years ago, directly as a result of the tax break.

"The lion's share of that reduction will come from the gambling tax cut, and a very large part of the gambling tax cut comes from the fact that the gambling tax rates have been lowered," said Margus Allikmaa, head of the Cultural Endowment.

Margus Allikmaa. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

The under-construction new ERR TV house, the "Siuru" Tartu Downtown Cultural Center, and the Tallinn Film Wonderland development are among the projects receiving Cultural Endowment money; should tax revenues come in lower than expected, however, the funding payment schedule stretches out. This in turn will mean a greater reliance on loans, and consequently higher interest payments. In the case of the new TV house, this could translate into less funding for new equipment.

"Indeed, if money has to be spent on loan interest instead, it could mean a couple of million less for new television equipment, and we would have to bring equipment over from the old TV house — which we are anyway trying to do as much as possible — but which isn't really very high quality or particularly viable any more," said Erik Roose, ERR board chair.

Current law provides for the online casino tax cut to go ahead in increments, however, reaching 4 percent by 2029.

Allikmaa, Roose's predecessor as ERR chief, said he wants the cuts stopped. "I have proposed that the sensible thing is to end the gambling tax cut as a matter of urgency. The worst thing would be to do nothing," he said.

Finance Minister Jürgen Ligi (Reform) too considers the online casino tax cut bad policy, yet despite this, the government is not planning reverse the tax decision, noting it passed a Riigikogu vote.

"We didn't initiate it and we won't reverse the Riigikogu's choice. But if the Riigikogu does so itself, we'll take an understanding view," Ligi said.

Tax policy must be predictable. Tax rises, or abandoning tax cuts, must be announced at least six months in advance, Ligi added.

The current Reform-Eesti 200 administration is now a minority government, and a general election is taking place in March 2027.

World.title: Baghdad court sentences seven French ISIS operatives to life and 15 years
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Baghdad’s Karkh Criminal Court sentenced seven French nationals on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to life imprisonment and a 15-year prison term after convicting them of membership in the ISIS terrorist organization, in a hearing attended by their defense counsel and representatives from the French Embassy in Iraq.

According to a formal statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council’s media office, the court handed down life sentences to six convicts, while the seventh received a 15-year custodial sentence under federal anti-terrorism statutes.

Judicial authorities classified the individuals as highly dangerous elements, citing their role in threatening Iraqi national security, destabilizing border areas across Iraq and Syria, and inciting terrorist attacks in other countries.

The judicial authority confirmed that the seven convicts were part of a wider contingent of 47 French nationals transferred into Iraqi custody last year from detention camps across northeastern Syria.

Following their repatriation to Baghdad, the First Karkh Investigation Court led preliminary interrogations and evidence processing before referring the defendants to the competent criminal court for trial under Iraqi statutory procedures.

World.title: Iraq’s dollar reserves rebound to $80 billion as cash inflows continue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) announced on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves rebounded to approximately $80 billion across September and October, recovering from a recent low of $73 billion.

The monetary authority offered assurances to the public regarding the ample availability of physical greenbacks, confirming that scheduled cash shipments from the United States are proceeding as planned.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Mahmoud Dagher, adviser to the CBI Governor and official spokesperson for the central bank, detailed that the aggregate dollar reserves—held across CBI accounts and federal government repositories at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York—gained significant ground, while sovereign gold reserves held firm at 170 metric tons.

Dagher attributed the reserve replenishment to recent monthly oil export revenues reaching near $6 billion, describing the inflow as acceptable given current regional market pressures. He noted that reserve health is measured by import coverage rather than absolute figures. When oil shipments faced disruptions earlier this year between April and June, Iraq’s reserve buffer contracted from 12 months of import cover to roughly nine months, before recovering back toward prior benchmarks. Dagher emphasized that the Ministry of Finance must accelerate structural diversification to reduce sovereign dependency on central bank foreign assets for operational budget financing.

Addressing physical liquidity, Dagher confirmed that Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi is personally monitoring incoming cash flights, with each air consignment carrying roughly $500 million. Two cargo aircraft loaded with physical banknotes have already arrived in Baghdad, with additional shipments slated to land in the coming days. The surplus of cash liquidity enabled the central bank to raise individual traveler allowances from two quotas up to six quotas per year. However, Dagher noted that the pace of upcoming cash consignments remains tethered to regional security stability, as armed flare-ups or active conflict could complicate cargo transport logistics and transit insurance.

On the placement of Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves, Dagher affirmed that maintaining primary sovereign holdings with the U.S. Federal Reserve is governed by financial logic, technical prudence, and sovereign asset protection rather than political preferences. He explained that pending foreign legal claims against Iraqi state banks continue to restrict custodial options, making Federal Reserve custody vital for legal immunity. While Iraq maintains diversified secondary reserves across Switzerland (Basel), European centers, the United Arab Emirates, and China, the Federal Reserve remains the anchor repository safeguarding Iraqi sovereign wealth.

World.title: Iraqi court sentences Oil Products Chief Hussein Talib to 8 years, orders 55B IQD restitution
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An Iraqi court sentenced Hussein Talib, Director General of the Oil Products Distribution Company (OPDC), to eight years in prison after convicting him of illicit profiting from commercial contracts associated with the North Refineries Company (NRC), while ordering him to reimburse 55 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $36 million).

In a formal statement obtained by the 964 Network on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Federal Integrity Commission confirmed that the judicial ruling issued an eight-year custodial sentence against Talib for using his executive authority to unlawfully benefit from North Refineries contracts, alongside the mandatory restitution of the 55-billion-dinar sum misappropriated in the scheme.

The conviction follows Talib’s arrest in Baghdad on Wednesday, July 8, 2026, by a specialized security force executing a judicial warrant linked to public corruption investigations.

The detention occurred hours before Talib—a senior figure affiliated with the National Wisdom Movement (Hikma)—was scheduled to take the constitutional oath in the Council of Representatives as a substitute lawmaker replacing Ammar Moussa under the National State Powers Coalition list for Baghdad Governorate.

Following his arrest in July, the National Wisdom Movement issued a statement backing state anti-corruption enforcement, emphasizing that legal accountability is strictly personal and affirming the judiciary’s sole authority in adjudicating the case.

The investigation and sentencing form part of an expanded anti-graft drive launched under Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi’s administration, targeting current and former senior state officials implicated in financial wrongdoing across federal ministries.

World.title: US dollar exchange rates stabilize across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar held largely steady across parallel trading desks in major commercial centers on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, with wholesale purchase transactions settling around the 168,000 dinar threshold per $100.

According to morning monitoring reports, exchange bureaus in Baghdad maintained steady levels, quoting selling prices at 168,500 dinars against buying bids of 167,500 dinars per $100.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters listed selling rates at 168,000 dinars alongside buying offers of 167,350 dinars. Across the southern commercial hub of Basra, foreign exchange desks registered selling prices at 168,100 dinars per $100, while purchase bids stood at 167,750 dinars.

The prevailing market rates continue to reflect a wide gap compared to the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory exchange rate, which remains pegged at 152,000 dinars per $100 (1,520 dinars per dollar).

The relative stability follows days of minor downward adjustments after prime ministerial assurances regarding upcoming physical dollar cash shipments aimed at cooling parallel market premiums.

World.title: Iraqi PM reiterates Iraq’s support for the Palestinian people
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reiterated on Monday Iraq’s principled and steadfast support for the Palestinian people.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas in the Jordanian capital, Amman, during his official visit to Jordan.

The high-level talks focused on regional security, bilateral coordination, and the humanitarian crisis in the Palestinian territories, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

President Abbas renewed his congratulations to al-Zaidi on assuming office earlier in the year, wishing him success in his new leadership role.

Al-Zaidi stressed the necessity of regional and international coordination to restore the Palestinians’ full historical rights.

Abbas commended Iraq’s tangible assistance, including its political backing at the United Nations, financial support for UNRWA, medical care provided to injured Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, and its hospitality toward Palestinian refugees living in Iraq.

The two leaders discussed reactivating the joint Palestinian-Iraqi committee to deepen long-term collaboration across political, economic, cultural, and educational sectors.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of al-Zaidi’s broader diplomatic trip to Amman, where he met with Jordan’s King Abdullah II and Prime Minister Jafar Hassan and signed nine bilateral cooperation agreements.

World.title: Mbappe dropped by Chinese brands for ‘offending national sentiments’
World.content:
Beijing – Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football superstar apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong.

In China jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”.

Adverts showing AI-generated images of the 27-year-old France captain drinking a Dongpeng sports drink were regularly shown in China during this year’s World Cup.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward, who until this incident was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme.

“With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement.

“Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures.

The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check.

“Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.

One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable”.

Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles.

Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people” and “have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people”.

– China furore –

Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator, in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

“There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said.

“Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people — well, I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life,” he said.

The furore in China came a day after Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.

Global sports stars that have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there.

Former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s vice president and current president Lai Ching-te, sparking fury on Chinese social media.

Beijing claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.

World.title: Cavs edge T’Wolves in overtime despite superb Edwards
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Cleveland Cavaliers ended the Minnesota Timberwolves’ perfect start to the NBA season, winning 127-125 in an overtime thriller despite 47 points from Anthony Edwards.

Donovan Mitchell and James Harden led the scoring for the victorious Cavs, with 26 and 19 points apiece, as Cleveland moved to 2-1.

“Tough win for us, especially early in the season,” said Harden, who added four rebounds and nine assists.

The Timberwolves, having won their opening three games, led for much of the night, with a 15-point advantage in the first half.

Edwards, only cleared to play late after being listed as questionable with a right knee injury, had made an electric start, with 11 points in the first quarter.

But the Cavaliers rallied to pull level in the third quarter, and then had to come from behind again after slipping to a seven-point deficit in the fourth.

Harden’s driving floater with 10 seconds remaining tied the game, and a blocked Edwards layup with four seconds left sent it to overtime at 113-113.

With just a minute left in overtime, Edwards tied the game again with a trey so close to the arc that a video replay was required.

But Mitchell re-established Cleveland’s lead with a go-ahead midrange jumper, and when Minnesota’s Jonathan Kuminga missed a free throw with 30 seconds left, the Cavaliers pulled clear.

Harden made two more free throws, leaving the Timberwolves requiring three points, but Edwards’ clutch effort bounced off the rim.

Peyton Watson poured in two more free throws for Cleveland to bury the contest.

“We made a lot of mistakes on both ends of the basketball in that first half… second half, we did a better job,” said Harden.

Elsewhere, the Oklahoma City Thunder improved to 4-0 with a hard-fought 125-114 win over the Phoenix Suns.

Ajay Mitchell led the scoring with a career-high 30, supported by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who added 26.

“This league is about winning games, and that’s all that matters,” said Gilgeous-Alexander.

“We were just ready to go. Guys were ready to go. Guys were ready to step up,” added the reigning NBA Most Valuable Player.

– ‘Perfect night’ –

The Houston Rockets also stayed perfect with a 120-110 win over the Atlanta Hawks.

It is their first 4-0 start since 2014, with star Kevin Durant rested for the entire fourth quarter in an ultimately comfortable win.

Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded his first triple-double with new team Miami even as the Heat (0-4) suffered a 113-109 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.

Antetokounmpo, a two-time league MVP who left the Milwaukee Bucks this summer, scored 29 points with 14 rebounds and 11 assists.

Mavericks teen star Cooper Flagg also scored 29, with 11 assists, six rebounds and a career-high five steals.

The Grizzlies also improved to 4-0 with a 110-105 win over the Utah Jazz, while Brandon Miller scored 39 points as the Charlotte Hornets beat the Washington Wizards 110-103.

And the Golden State Warriors earned their first victory of the season with a 134-114 triumph over the Denver Nuggets.

Stephen Curry made 8-of-8 field goal attempts for 24 points.

“Just staying patient. We’ve been working on some offensive approach where I know I get a lot of attention, trying not to force things,” he said.

“I didn’t know it was going to be a perfect night like that, but glad it all came together.”

World.title: Tech firms track Wall St rally on mixed day for Asian markets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Tech firms rallied Tuesday following a healthy run-up on Wall Street as traders welcomed AI titan Anthropic’s IPO filing that revived optimism over the sector after stuttering in the second half of the year.

However, the main gains were concentrated in South Korea and Japan, with other Asian stock markets putting in a mixed performance as traders gear up for a slew of key earnings and central bank decisions this week.

In submitting its plans to list its shares, Anthropic, one of the world’s leading artificial intelligence companies, reported first-half revenue surged about 1,300 percent year-on-year, but also flagged safety risks.

The sale is seen as a crucial test of whether the AI boom can deliver profits, and a disappointing reception could dent enthusiasm further, with traders already questioning the vast sums invested in the sector as well as several companies’ financial positions.

The filing lays out risks specific to an industry that has faced a string of reports in recent months of AI systems behaving in unexpected and harmful ways.

“If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse,” the firm’s business could suffer, it said.

Still, Wall Street-listed tech firms rallied, pulling the Nasdaq and S&P 500 higher along with the Dow.

Seoul briefly jumped more than four percent, thanks to strong gains in chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, while Tokyo added around two percent on the back of spikes in Kioxia, Advantest and SoftBank.

“Sentiment towards technology has improved as investors assess Anthropic’s IPO filing at the start of a week packed with corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve’s rate decision,” wrote Fiona Cincotta at FOREX.com.

“Anthropic revealed steep losses and impressive revenue growth in its filing… laying out ambitions to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy, even at a high cost.

“The listing plan remains in place, even as other firms have stepped back owing to recent market volatility.”

There were also gains in Sydney, Taipei and Manila, but Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Wellington and Jakarta all retreated.

Investors are now awaiting earnings this week from Magnificent Seven members Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon as well as SK hynix and Samsung.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates on hold when it announces its decision on Wednesday, though CME Group’s FedWatch tool says there is a 70 percent chance of a hike when it meets in December.

Oil prices extended Monday’s drop as senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iran in an attempt to stop the Middle East war from reigniting, with Tehran saying the discussions were “very good”.

Officials from the three Mecca pact countries flew to Iran as part of efforts to “de-escalate between the parties to the current crisis”, a Saudi foreign ministry statement said.

The talks followed warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could restart in the eight-month war, with some observers suggesting the period between next Tuesday’s US midterm elections and the new Congress taking office was particularly fraught.

Also in view are elections in Israel, where voters will deliver their verdict on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift.

World.title: The AI social paradox: Better at communicating, worse at connecting?
World.content:
A text from a family member. An email from the boss. A friend seeking advice after an argument. These are ordinary moments that are part of everyday interactions. Yet, increasingly, there is another participant in these conversations, one that neither feels emotions nor has any personal stake in the relationship - artificial intelligence.

For generations, people learnt social etiquette, understood different perspectives and navigated relationships through actual interactions. They often said the wrong things, misunderstood intentions and learnt from those experiences.

Now, with AI offering an instant answer to every social dilemma, some of that effort can be outsourced.

So, why has replying to an ordinary message become something we might need assistance with? Also while AI may make us more articulate, polite and confident, does that necessarily make us better at connecting?

A 'social animal' with AI?

Humans have long been described as social animals. Relationships are shaped not merely by what one says, but by how they listen, react, disagree and adapt to one another.

AI, however, offers something human relationships rarely can: immediate attention, endless patience and responses tailored to specific concerns. There is no awkward silence, no raised eyebrow and seemingly no fear of embarrassment.

This was highlighted by Shailesh K Nevatia, founder director of Grandeavour Communication, having spent nearly 25 years in the communication industry but described himself as shy when it comes to open communication concerning himself.





He said AI helps him navigate differences of opinion, offering perspectives he might otherwise overlook. "With humans we may have certain opinions, views, or thoughts, while with AI, the most valuable thing it offers is not the right answer but a different perspective than us," he said.

"AI can be a guide"

Nevertheless, he maintained that the emotional depth, vulnerability and shared experiences of human relationships cannot be replicated by a chatbot.

When the robot does the talking

The concern with AI-assisted communication is not just that people are using it to find the right words, but that repeated reliance on it could weaken their confidence in finding those words themselves.

For instance, Riddhi turns to ChatGPT almost instinctively when responding at times. Whether she needs to sound polite yet firm in a professional email or find a way to decline plans with friends, AI helps her navigate the interaction.

"It's not like I can't reply without AI, but having someone to proofread the convos is better than just listening to how they sound in my head," she said.

Yet, the reassurance comes with a trade-off for her. "AI has such a grasp on my writing that I am not very confident even while writing this, and that is, without being said, one of the biggest disadvantages." She also called to embrace AI but be careful.

Now that AI has become a new normal, its not possible to go back to the non-AI era, but its also important to not let it become the master of ourselves. Riddhi

Her experience pointed to a potential paradox: a tool intended to make communication easier can also leave users less confident about communicating independently.

The stakes may be higher when AI is used not just to frame a response, but to interpret another person's intentions. Consider someone who turns to a chatbot after an argument and asks who was at fault. The response can sound

but it is based on the account presented to the system, which may omit details or reflect the user's own biases.

In that context, Reshmithaa Nair, counselling psychologist at SPARSH Hospital, Hennur Road, warned that such interactions can reinforce confirmation bias, making people more convinced of their existing interpretation rather than open to another perspective.

That matters because disagreements are also opportunities to develop social skills. Understanding another person's point of view, managing uncomfortable emotions and responding to unexpected reactions require practice, not simply a well-worded reply.

"Social skills are learned in actual situations that involve emotions, misunderstanding, conflict, and sometimes rejection," Nair explained.

Repeatedly delegating these situations to AI could reduce opportunities to develop empathy, emotional intelligence and the ability to navigate uncertainty.

A person may learn to phrase a difficult message more effectively without necessarily becoming better at handling the conversation that follows.

The missing human touch

A message is not simply a collection of sentences. Its meaning can change with the relationship between the people involved, their shared experiences and even the pauses between words.

Ritu Mehrotra, Founder and CEO of Shunya Labs, a voice AI company, pointed out that natural communication involves much more than language.

"Communication is not only about words, itâs also about tone, pauses, context, emotion and all the things we communicate without explicitly saying them."

Advances in voice AI are making it possible for technology to interpret language, intent and context with greater sophistication, including across different accents and communication styles. Yet, recognising emotional signals is not the same as experiencing emotions.

"And as AI is becoming a part of more and more personal conversations, we have to realise that understanding emotion is not feeling it. Trust, privacy, and transparency must be fundamental," she said.

AI should help people connect with one another, not replicate human empathy or replace human relationships. Ritu Mehrotra, Founder & CEO, Shunya Labs

A chatbot may recognise expressions of sadness or affection and produce an empathetic-sounding response. But recognising emotional patterns is different from sharing the emotional responsibility of a human relationship. For ex, an AI chatbot was asked to give advice to reply on a (hypothetical) "text to a friend who was laid off"

Response of AI

While the response was considerate, it was also generic. It offered comfort without knowing the friend's emotional state, personality or the nature of the relationship.

Even a seemingly caring question like âAre you OK?â may fall flat when the person is looking for encouragement rather than a question whose answer seems obvious. A more personal response might acknowledge the setback while affirming the friend's abilities: âOMG, that's awful.

I know the job market is tough, but you're talented. You'll land on your feet.â

The difference is not simply about choosing warmer words. It is about understanding what a particular person might need in that moment, something a chatbot may struggle to judge without sufficient context.

There is also the question of authenticity. When a message is carefully constructed by AI, it may communicate the intended information effectively. But does it still sound like the person sending it?

In this example, of AI removing the human touch, another chatbot was asked "Someone close to me is grieving. I don't know what to say, and I'm afraid of making things worse. What should I tell them?". It gave a response, which is not wrong but is too robotic. "I am here with you. I care about your pain. Speak if you wish; silence is acceptable." Perfect words but not someone who is comforting says in such "rigid tone"

The little hesitations, imperfect expressions and familiar phrases that characterise someone's communication can disappear beneath polished language.

A message can become more grammatically correct while feeling less personal.

What aI can't do when comes to social interactions

Not all bad

Dismissing AI as a threat to social skills, however, would overlook how it can help people who struggle to express themselves.

For Pooja, a college student who hesitates to speak up in front of the entire class or repeatedly ask friends to explain something, AI offers a space where she can ask questions without worrying about others' reactions.

She uses it to understand complicated topics and brainstorm ideas, sometimes asking ChatGPT to explain something as though she were a 10-year-old.

What I love most is that I can ask the dumbest questions without feeling embarrassed. But I also feel it's very easy to become too dependent on it. Pooja

Yet, she recognises the possibility of becoming overly reliant on it. "AI can give you answers in seconds, but actually understanding and learning something is still on us."

For others, AI serves as a sounding board before difficult conversations. It can also help people become more mindful of how their words might affect others.

It can suggest more inclusive language, flag potentially insensitive phrasing and help users consider perspectives they might otherwise overlook. For someone unsure how to communicate across differences, this can offer a starting point for more thoughtful interactions.

But knowing which words are considered appropriate is not necessarily the same as understanding why they matter. Genuine inclusivity requires empathy and a willingness to understand experiences different from one's own, qualities that must extend beyond the words suggested by a chatbot.

Also, in such cases, might not give you the perfect answer, but may help you think in the right direction and give you options that you may not have thought about. In another hypothetical test, a chatbot was asked how to support a family member struggling with their mental health without pushing them away. While its response was not fully correct, it offered different approaches to consider, giving the person a starting point for thinking about how to respond.

AI bot's advice giving suggestions on comforting a family member

Thus, the value, then, may not lie in AI providing the perfect answer, but in helping someone see possibilities they had not considered. The important distinction is whether people use these suggestions to develop their own judgement or simply follow them without question.

As Shruti Rajan Kappil, clinical lead, excellence and quality at a mental health care platform Amaha, explained, that while the need to feel heard and supported is fundamental to human relationships, not every concern feels safe to share.

Shame, embarrassment and fear of judgement often prevent people from opening up, particularly where stigma remains prevalent.

"AI offers space"

AI offers an alternative, but Kappil pointed to an important distinction. "Good support often needs honest disagreement or gentle challenge with a different point of view. AI tends to be agreeable more often than not, and being agreed with is easily mistaken for being helped."

She also noted that repeatedly seeking AI's approval before sending a message can become a form of reassurance seeking.

While it offers immediate relief, constantly checking whether one's words are "correct" may gradually undermine confidence in one's own judgement.

Shristi Chaudhari, senior executive, regulatory intelligence and market research at Bureau Veritas, uses AI almost daily to condense regulatory updates. Increasingly, she also turns to it for interpersonal communication.

From identifying emotional undertones to making messages warmer and more polite for colleagues and professional contacts, AI has become a useful sounding board.

While AI can refine written communication, help us anticipate reactions and interpret conversational nuances, it cannot replace the soft skills, verbal cues and lived experiences that shape genuine human connections. Shristi Chaudhari

These experiences suggest AI can help people prepare for conversations, overcome language barriers and articulate thoughts they might otherwise struggle to express.

Perfect talks, weaker bonds?

Communication is one of the ways human beings establish connection. But effective communication and meaningful connection are not necessarily the same thing.

What AI can and can't do

One involves expressing something clearly. The other requires understanding, trust, emotional involvement and vulnerability.

Tanvi Mankodi, assistant professor at SPJIMR, believes the deeper concern is not whether AI will replace human relationships, but what excessive dependence might do to our ability to participate in them.

"For me, the essence of human relationships is about our vulnerabilities, about our imperfections, and about how we try to relate with each other with our discomforts and uncertainties," she said.

Misunderstandings, difficult conversations and moments when people struggle to find the right words are also experiences through which patience, compassion and empathy develop.

"Rather than worrying about AI replacing human relations, I am more worried about how if we use AI in a way that we are dependent on it, it might reduce our ability to be vulnerable and to be human," she added.

Impact of AI-dictated communications

Her concern captures the paradox: in trying to eliminate the discomfort of human interaction, we may also remove experiences that make relationships meaningful.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Of course, not every AI-generated message weakens a relationship, and the long-term effects of outsourcing everyday communication are still being understood. AI may help some people overcome barriers to social participation while encouraging others to avoid interactions through which confidence develops. But, the concern is can it address the individuality and complexity of human behaviour?

However, using AI to prepare for a difficult discussion is one thing.

Allowing it to decide how we interpret another person's intentions and what we say in every interaction is another.

The point is not whether AI can offer thoughtful, nuanced or well-structured answers to human dilemmas. It is whether those answers can replicate the emotional understanding, vulnerability and lived experiences through which we learn to navigate relationships and grow socially. After all, relationships are not assignments to be completed with perfectly structured answers. They evolve through disagreement, compromise and sometimes saying something imperfectly but sincerely.

Perhaps the real challenge is not learning how to communicate better with AI, but ensuring that, in the process, we do not forget how to connect without it.

World.title: 'Won't rest till puppet Gyanesh is removed': Cong claims denied permit for mock CEC impeachment; Delhi Police clarifies
World.content:
Delhi Police denies charges

Delhi Police's 'terms and conditions'

Poll Vote & Share your view Are the measures imposed by the police for the rally fair? Completely fair Somewhat fair Unfair Not applicable to my opinion 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Congress on Tuesday accused the Centre of denying permission for an event where INDIA bloc parties planned a "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, ahead of their November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan.Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said the government-run Ashoka Hotel had initially allowed the event to be held on its premises but later denied permission following police intervention."The day before yesterday, our people came to construct the infrastructure here and the police stopped them. We don't know what the reason is," Venugopal said."This means it is not the Delhi Police's decision. It is the decision of PM Modi and Amit Shah, and they are protecting their puppet Gyanesh Kumar," he alleged.In a social media post on X, Venugopal also accused the Delhi Police of stopping the party doing the set up for the event at Ramlila Maidan."How many permissions will you deny, Mr. Amit Shah? How many people will you stop? 21 parties of the INDIA bloc had planned a Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar as a curtain raiser to the Nov 1st Mega Rally and March - first at Hotel Ashoka, where permission was denied, and then at Ramleela Maidan, where despite already having all the requisite permissions, Delhi Police stopped us from doing the set up for the event.First they destroy the electoral system, and now they are trying all kinds of tricks to silence those who fight to save our democracy," Venugopal said."Let it be very clear, come what may, we will not rest until Modi-Shah's puppet Gyanesh Kumar is not removed. If they stop us here, we will go to Amit Shah's house, PM Modi's house, and stage a massive dharna there. But we will fight to the finish, and until our mission is accomplished," he added.The proposed event is part of a series of protests by the Congress and other opposition parties demanding Kumar's resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged electoral irregularities.Meanwhile, Delhi Police said it had not withdrawn permission for the Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan, adding that there had been no change in the earlier approval.On the proposed mock Parliament event at Ashoka Hotel, police sources said the matter rested with the hotel, as the premises were privately owned."With respect to the Ashoka Hotel mock Parliament, Delhi Police says it depends on the hotel since it's their private premises," Delhi Police sources told news agency ANI.Earlier, Delhi Police had confirmed that a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued to the Congress for booking Ramlila Maidan from October 25 to November 3. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said the Congress had approached the police after obtaining a venue availability certificate from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD).Delhi Police has also laid down a list of "terms and conditions" for the Congress rally on November 1, including installing high-definition CCTV cameras at strategic locations, ensuring the event concludes by 5pm and prohibiting speeches that could disturb communal harmony.In its communication to the Congress, police said there was "no objection" to the rally from a law-and-order perspective, subject to prior permission from the land-owning authority and compliance with the stipulated conditions.The organisers have been asked to install cameras at "all the strategic points including entry/exit gates, stage, all surrounding areas of Ram Lila Ground and sitting enclosures", along with a monitoring system with "atleast 5 screens" and a CCTV control room.They have also been directed to provide "sufficient numbers of water tankers and toilet blocks (separate for female participants)" and deploy volunteers wearing "identical dress or bear common Badges" to ensure the smooth conduct of the rally.The rally must conclude at 5pm on November 1, after which "the dispersal will start and under no circumstance will it be extended". Overnight stays by participants at Ramlila Maidan, either before or after the rally, have also been prohibited.Police has further directed the organisers to ensure that "no speakers would speak anything about caste/creed/colour that can disturb the public harmony, peace and tranquility of the area".If any "instigating/intimidating speech" is made, "the PA system will be switched off immediately", followed by the removal of the speaker from the stage by the organisers.

World.title: TOI Youth Icons Summit: CM Yogi highlights UP’s push on jobs, startups and MSMEs, says state now has 25,000 startups
World.content:
âEarlier, districts had mafias; now, we have the One District, One Product scheme,â CM Yogi said.

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday highlighted the state's initiatives to create employment opportunities for young people, promote startups and strengthen industries while addressing the TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards â UP Chapter in Lucknow.Thanking The Times of India for recognising young achievers, CM Yogi said, âI would like to thank The Times of India for honouring youth icons who have done something new in their respective fields.âReferring to the changes in Uttar Pradesh over the years, the chief minister said the state had previously faced several challenges, including security concerns, mafia activity and difficulties for girls in accessing education. He contrasted this with the state's present focus on promoting products from individual districts.âEarlier, districts had mafias; now, we have the One District, One Product scheme,â he said, referring to the state's initiative to promote distinctive products from each district.âEvery district has a unique product that is gaining recognition both nationally and internationally, and lakhs of young people are getting employment opportunities,â he added.Highlighting the state's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector, the CM Yogi said Uttar Pradesh had 96 lakh MSME units, with the state government providing each unit with insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh.âThe MSME sector in Uttar Pradesh is providing direct employment to 3.25 crore people, creating a new story of self-reliance,â he said.Speaking about government jobs, the chief minister said appointment letters had been issued for 9.5 lakh government jobs over the past nine-and-a-half years. He said recruitment had been based on merit, without special references or discrimination.âIn the next six months, I will provide another one lakh government jobs to the youth of Uttar Pradesh,â he said.CM Yogi also outlined the state's plans for Agniveers after they complete four years of service under the scheme. He said the government had announced that they would have opportunities for direct recruitment in various state departments, including the police, fire services and forest department.The chief minister also highlighted employment opportunities for sportspersons, saying athletes who win medals for India would be eligible for government jobs in Uttar Pradesh.âWin a medal and get a post,â he said, referring to the policy while mentioning Prachi Chaudhary, Parul Chaudhary and Rajkumar Pal, who became deputy superintendents of police (DSPs).He added that nearly 1,400 athletes had received government job appointment letters in the state. The initiative, he said, was intended to provide athletes with a career pathway and allow them to focus on sports without worrying about their future employment.Highlighting the growth of the startup ecosystem, CM Yogi said Uttar Pradesh had moved from having 120 startups before 2017 to 25,000 currently, with lakhs of young people working in them.âThe youth of Uttar Pradesh are no longer job seekers; they have become job creators,â he said, adding that the state government had established a Rs 1,000 crore fund to support startups.He also outlined plans to develop centres of excellence across the state, including a drone centre in Kanpur and a robotics centre in Noida. The government was also working towards developing centres of excellence for medical technology (MedTech) and deep technology (deep tech), he said.Under the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana, the state provides interest-free, collateral-free loans to one lakh young people every year, according to CM Yogi.âAmong young people, the scheme is popularly known as CM YUVA. It is the government's own Shark Tank,â he said.The chief minister also highlighted employment opportunities in defence manufacturing, recalling a proposal he received from the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) during the 2020-21 Covid period to develop the BrahMos missile in Uttar Pradesh.He said the state offered free land in Lucknow and assured the organisation of the necessary facilities, while asking it to consider recruiting people from the state's institutions.âEventually, 500 young engineers were selected for defence manufacturing projects through campus recruitment conducted by Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Technical University,â he said.CM Yogi added that the state was developing hyperscale data centres and global capability centres, while work was also underway to develop Lucknow as an artificial intelligence (AI) city.Speaking about women's participation in the workforce, the chief minister said the government had ensured that women could work safely during night shifts.He linked the expansion of employment opportunities for young people with the state's economic growth and improvements in connectivity.The TOI Youth Icons Summit & Awards â UP Chapter brought together achievers, emerging leaders and influential voices to celebrate young Indians shaping the country's future. The awards recognised outstanding achievers from Uttar Pradesh across categories including enterprise, sports, society, culture and social media.The summit also focused on Uttar Pradesh's transformation over the years, including developments in employment opportunities, safety and connectivity, with an emphasis on young people whose ambition, ideas and achievements are shaping India's future.

World.title: Is Jagan Reddy's 'regret' message a calculated alliance pitch for Congress?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Is YSRCP supremo

signalling a drift towards the Congress-led INDIA bloc? Or is he trying to break free from the image of being soft on the

?

The former Andhra Pradesh chief minister has provided issue-based support to the BJP-led NDA government on several key legislations in Parliament while he was in power in the state.

However, he has stayed away from joining any alliance till now. So, when Jagan Reddy recently regretted his âmistakeâ of supporting the 2023 NDA legislation for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner, it fuelled speculation about his future political moves.

"We regret supporting the process under which the ruling party nominates the Chief Election Commissioner at the Centre. Neither the CEC nor the SEC should be appointed by the ruling party.

The selection committee should comprise the Prime Minister, the leader of the opposition and the Chief Justice of India (CJI), with all three exercising their voting rights," the YSRCP chief said recently, calling the current selection system "flawed.

"

The timing and context of Jaganâs remarks are significant. So, is he rethinking his âsoloâ politics? And if yes, will the Congress be ready to tango with him in Andhra Pradesh? After all, alliances with regional parties have been the Congressâs biggest Achilles heel across states.





Jaganâs support for NDAâs key Bills

Jagan Mohan Reddyâs MPs backed the Modi government several times between 2019 and 2024, both in Lok Sabha and in Rajya Sabha, on many important legislations. However, when it came to stitching an alliance for the 2024 elections, the BJP ignored Jaganâs help and joined hands with his arch-rival Chandrababu Naidu. Together, TDP and BJP swept the polls in Andhra Pradesh, winning 164 out of 175 seats in the assembly and 21 out of 25 seats in Lok Sabha.

The YSRCP was reduced to 11 seats in the assembly and 4 in Lok Sabha.

Despite being spurned by the BJP and his partyâs shock defeat, Jagan Mohan Reddy remained confident about his BJP ties. After all, he still had 15 MPs (4 in Lok Sabha and 11 in Rajya Sabha) to provide the much-needed support to the BJPâs minority government at the Centre. Jagan even announced that his MPs would extend issue-based support to the NDA government in matters concerning national and state interest.

But with the BJP heavily dependent on Chandrababu Naiduâs support for survival of its government at the Centre, there was little room for the saffron party to accommodate Jagan Reddy. Nearly two and a half years down the line, Reddy seems to have accepted this harsh reality and is perhaps gearing up to chart a new path for the next political challenge in 2029.

Jagan vs Congress

However, for any successful alliance with the INDIA bloc - the YSRCP and the Congress will have to be on the same page.

And that perhaps would be the biggest challenge for Jagan Mohan Reddy.

Jagan Mohan Reddy had a bitter parting from the Congress in 2010, a year after the death of his father YS Rajasekhara Reddy. YSR Reddy was in his second term as the chief minister of Andhra Pradesh when he died in a helicopter crash on September 2, 2009. Jaganâs supporters, who were many in number, lobbied hard with the Congress high command for the top post, but Sonia Gandhi did not budge and made K Rosaiah the chief minister.

The Congress leadership did not approve of Jaganâs Odarpu Yatra, which was part of his announced plan to meet the families of many people who had sacrificed their lives after his fatherâs death.

That set the stage for his eventual exit from the Congress, which he announced on November 29, 2010 in an open letter to Sonia Gandhi carefully written to ensure there was enough public sympathy for his second phase of political career.

In the 2014 assembly elections, the YSRCP made an impressive debut and won 67 out of the 175 seats with a vote share of 44.46%, while the Congress could manage only a vote share of 2.8%. The Congress decision to bifurcate the state and create Telangana played a huge role in the partyâs declining political fortunes in the state.

On November 6, 2017, Jagan embarked on the Praja Sankalpa Yatra and covered 3,648 km in 341 days, crossing 134 assembly constituencies.

The Yatra, from YSR Ghat at Idupulapaya to the northeastern tip of Ichchapuram, powered Jagan Mohan Reddy to a historic mandate of 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in the 2019 elections. The Congressâs vote share was reduced to less than 1%.

The Congress, since then, has been making efforts to reclaim its lost political space in the state. It roped in Jagan Reddyâs sister Y S Sharmila as part of the partyâs revival plan.

Sharmila, who started her political career with her brother Jagan Mohan Reddy eventually drifted towards the Congress and was appointed president of Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee in January 2024.

However, both Jagan Mohan Reddy and his sister Y S Sharmila failed to make an impact in the 2024 elections. The 2024 elections saw a dramatic collapse of Jaganâs electoral fortunes, and his party was reduced to only 11 seats.

The Congress once again failed to make its presence felt.

The 2029 challenge

And that brings us to the 2029 elections - a do-or-die challenge for both Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress. Jaganâs remark on backing the CEC appointment Bill is his first open âregretâ for backing the BJP.

But does this âopen regretâ mean an olive branch for the Congress?

Former Congress leader and senior political commentator Sanjay Jha strongly feels that Jagan and Congress should come together, though he admits that this may not be easy.

âPolitics is the art of the possible and I'm sure Jaganmohan Reddy is aware that Chandrababu Naidu has been an extremely close alliance partner of the Modi government. While the Congress doesn't have a base in Andhra like it used to have once upon a time. The support base of Jaganmohan Reddy is basically the Congress vote which moved away from the traditional Congress to the Congress that Jaganmohan Reddy, branded as the Congress of his father.

So, if the merger were to happen, it would, frankly speaking, give them a huge advantage because then both the Central Congress and the Jaganmohan Congress could be on the same page,â Sanjay Jha says.

However, he accepts that merger of the two parties could be a difficult process while stitching an alliance may be easier. âOnce a political party becomes independent and has power, they don't like to give it up in a hurry.

The TMC or the NCP are good examples. In which case it could be an alliance,â Sanjay Jha adds.

The third option, according to Sanjay Jha, is for the Congress to resurrect itself on its own strongly in Andhra by capturing both the anti-incumbent votes against Chandrababu Naidu and winning back the loyalist voters of the Congress who had moved over to Jaganmohan Reddy.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

This is easier said than done. The Congress has a poor track record when it comes to winning back states it has lost.

We have seen several states across the country where the Congress has lost its government and eventually its support base but does little to reclaim it.

In Andhra Pradesh, Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP are going all out to consolidate their position. Naiduâs call for greater cooperation and coordination among southern states at a recent conference is perhaps an effort to keep his importance and relevance intact. We saw DMKâs MK Stalin make similar moves before he lost power to Vijayâs TVK in the last assembly elections.

Jagan Mohan Reddy and the Congress face an uphill electoral battle in 2029. It will be interesting to see if they can agree to an alliance to take on Chandrababu Naidu and the BJP.

World.title: New Rs 1,000 note with temple design? PIB Fact Check debunks viral claim
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Press Information Bureauâs (PIB) Fact Check unit on Tuesday debunked claims about a new Rs 1,000 currency note. The clarification came after images and videos of a purported yellow-coloured note featuring a temple motif went viral on social media, with some posts claiming it had been issued or would enter circulation on the 15th.

PIB Fact Check clarified that the

(RBI) has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 banknote.

In a post on X, PIB Fact Check said, âSeveral social media posts claim that a new Rs 1,000 note has been issued. This claim is fake.â

The agency added, âThe @RBI has made no announcement regarding the issuance of a new Rs 1,000 note.â It also urged people to âVerify information through official sources and do not share unverified claims.â

The clarification came after the purported note appeared in posts shared across platforms including Instagram, X and Telegram.

The Rs 1,000 denomination was withdrawn from circulation during the demonetisation announced on November 8, 2016, when the government withdrew the legal tender status of the old Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

New Rs 500 notes were subsequently introduced, while the RBI brought in Rs 2,000 notes as the highest-denomination banknotes in the new currency series.





In May 2023, the RBI announced the withdrawal of Rs 2,000 notes from circulation, while clarifying that they would continue to be legal tender.

Banknotes in denominations of Rs 10, Rs 20, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 200 and Rs 500 remain in circulation under the RBIâs Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series.

PIB Fact Check has urged people to verify currency-related announcements through official sources and avoid forwarding unverified claims.

The viral posts should not be treated as confirmation of a new denomination unless the RBI issues an official announcement.

World.title: Open, check, store: What changes once a packaged food is opened
World.content:
âQuick hacks for common kitchen staples.â

â

What the numbers tell us about food safety at home

60% of global food waste happens at home: According to the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) Food Waste Index Report [1] , households account for over 60% of all food wasted worldwide, equivalent to over 600 million tonnes of food per year. Misinterpreting date labels and letting opened food spoil prematurely are two primary drivers.

According to the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) Food Waste Index Report , households account for over 60% of all food wasted worldwide, equivalent to over 600 million tonnes of food per year. Misinterpreting date labels and letting opened food spoil prematurely are two primary drivers. 1 in 10 people fall ill annually: Estimates from the World Health Organization (WHO) [2] highlight that roughly 1 in 10 people worldwide fall ill every year from consuming contaminated food. A common contributor in domestic kitchens is improper temperature control and cross-contamination after packages are unsealed.

Estimates from the World Health Organization (WHO) [2] highlight that roughly 1 in 10 people worldwide fall ill every year from consuming contaminated food. A common contributor in domestic kitchens is improper temperature control and cross-contamination after packages are unsealed. The âbest beforeâ confusion: Data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) shows that 30% to 40% of the food supply is lost or wasted [3] . A significant portion stems from consumer confusion surrounding unopened "Best Before" dates versus actual post-opening shelf life.

What happens when you break the seal?

Air enters (oxidation): Oxygen in the air reacts with fats, oil and certain vitamins. Overtime, this can cause food to become rancid, colours to fade and flavours lose their punch.

Oxygen in the air reacts with fats, oil and certain vitamins. Overtime, this can cause food to become rancid, colours to fade and flavours lose their punch. Moisture changes: Dry foods, such as chips or cookies, can absorb moisture from the air and lose their crispness. Other foods may lose moisture and gradually become dry or stale.

Dry foods, such as chips or cookies, can absorb moisture from the air and lose their crispness. Other foods may lose moisture and gradually become dry or stale. Microorganisms are introduced: Mold spores, yeasts, and bacteria naturally present in the environment can come into contact with the food. Given the right conditions, these microorganisms may grow and contribute to spoilage.

The simple open-check-store checklist

Step Action The goal 1. Check the label Look beyond the âBest Beforeâ date for instructions, such asâRefrigerate after opening and consume within 3 days.â Once opened, follow the manufacturer's guidance, as expiration dates generally apply to unopened products. Ensures the produce is stored and consumed as intended. 2. Seal it tight Transfer opened foods to airtight glass or BPA-free containers or reseal the packaging using bag clips or other closures. Helps maintain freshness and protects against moisture and contaminants. 3. Chill fast Refrigerate perishable foods promptly after opening, ideally (below 4Â°C) promptly. Slows bacterial growth and helps preserve quality and safety. 4. Serve clean Always use dry, clean spoons, forks or scoops. Avoid handling food directly with hands or using utensils that have already been used. Reduces the risk of cross-contamination.

Quick hacks for common kitchen staples

Sauces & dips: Some condiments, such as ketchup, can remain shelf-stable until opened, but mayonnaise, pesto, and cream-based dressings belong in the fridge the second they are opened. Always check the label for storage instructions.

Some condiments, such as ketchup, can remain shelf-stable until opened, but mayonnaise, pesto, and cream-based dressings belong in the fridge the second they are opened. Always check the label for storage instructions. Canned goods: Have leftover tomatoes, beans or other canned foods? Never leave them in an open metal can in the fridge. Transfer them into a clean glass or food-grade plastic container before refrigerating. This helps preserve quality and prevents unwanted flavour changes.

Have leftover tomatoes, beans or other canned foods? Never leave them in an open metal can in the fridge. Transfer them into a clean glass or food-grade plastic container before refrigerating. This helps preserve quality and prevents unwanted flavour changes. Dairy & milk: Store opened milk and dairy products on the inner shelf of the refrigerator where temperatures are more consistent. Avoid storing them on the door shelves which experience greater temperature fluctuation.

Avoid storing them on the door shelves which experience greater temperature fluctuation. Grains & spices: Store spices, flour, rice and cereals into sealed glass jars to keep pantry pests and humidity away.
